e2|20.title: Albert Einstein
paras: My name is Albert Einstein. Many people know about the great things I’ve accomplished. But I had many barriers before I became famous.

I was born in Germany. When I was in elementary school, I already knew about math and statistics. When I was a boy, I pretended to be a great scientist. I loved school, but my life at home was hard. My father lost his job, so my family lived in poverty. We could not pay the rent in Germany. We became immigrants and went to Italy. I finished high school and went to college in Switzerland. After college, I began writing about science. I did not reach success in an instant, though. At first, other scientists did not approve of my work. They thought I was a failure. Rising to the rank of an admired scientist was a gradual process. Soon, people started to notice that I was right. At last, I began to get some recognition.

I showed how to find the approximate size of very big things, like stars. I also detected and explained the movement of very small things, like atoms. And for fun, I made a machine that could refrigerate food by inserting heat. I never retired. It was my duty to keep working. I overcame many hard times, and I will be remembered for my important works.

qs.q: What is this story about?
o: Why Einstein was a failure at first
How Einstein got past barriers to accomplish many great things
Why Einstein pretended to be sick while in elementary school

qs.q: Why did Einstein’s family become immigrants?
o: They were unhappy about new developments in math and statistics.
They couldn’t pay their rent in Germany and had to leave.
His parents didn’t want him to stay in school.
They wanted Einstein to go to college in Switzerland.

qs.q: Why was Einstein’s rise in the ranks of scientists gradual?
o: Einstein did not write down his ideas.
Einstein’s ideas could not be proven.
Other scientists already knew about his ideas.
Other scientists didn’t approve of his ideas at first.

qs.q: According to the passage, all the following are true about Einstein EXCEPT
o: he found the approximate size of stars
he refrigerated food by inserting heat as a power source
he had a duty to retire
he detected the movement of atoms

e2|21.title: From the Earth to the Stars
paras: Jeremy was from a family of miners. Like them, he worked underground during the day. His job was to gather raw minerals and jewels. Each night after work, he lay awake in an open field. With his telescope, he looked at the stars. He was amazed by the scale of space. He wished someday he might travel there. One day there was an accident in the mine. Water poured into the mine. Everything was dark. Jeremy stretched out and grabbed a piece of wood. It kept him from sinking. Jeremy felt a presence nearby.
“I am an angel,” said a voice.
“What?” Jeremy exclaimed.
“You must never come underground again. Have the courage to make your wishes come true.”
For a long time he floated in silence. Then he heard other voices. The other miners were coming to rescue him.

The next day Jeremy skipped work. He decided to become an astronaut. For the next two years, he studied hard. One day, he was given permission to participate in a mission to space. His wish had been granted.
His spaceship left the ground. It went higher until there was no more gravity. He saw satellites floating next to the ship.
Then Jeremy saw a beautiful angel outside his spaceship. It smiled at Jeremy. For some minutes, Jeremy could not speak. Finally, he said, “Thank you.”

qs.q: What is this story about?
o: Why a telescope is a useful thing
How a miner became an astronaut

qs.q: Why did Jeremy stop going underground?
o: It kept him awake all night long.
He could not find any jewels or minerals.
An angel told him to stop working there and make his dreams come true.
He stopped having the courage to skip work.

qs.q: In the second paragraph, we can infer that Jeremy___.
o: did not know how to float
felt the presence of the workers

qs.q: According to the passage, all the following are true EXCEPT___.
o: Jeremy was granted permission to leave the mine
Jeremy used a telescope to watch the stars
Jeremy stretched out to grab the wood
Jeremy was amazed by the scale of space

tr: Jeremi konchilar oilasidan edi.

e2|22.title: The Farm Festival
paras: Once there was a farm. Many animals lived there. One day, they had a contest in the yard. They were going to race from the barn to the farmer’s garage. The barn and the garage were far apart. It would be a long race. The winner qualified to win a bag full of apples as an award.

But the race did not start well. The cart with all the apples was not stable, and the animals had to repair it. Then the pup knocked over the apples. The pig yelled, “We are going to slip! We must clean up this mess.” The pup felt bad, and she began to cry. The dog gave her a tissue to wipe her tears.

Then the race resumed. But the duck tried to rob them and take all the apples. The cat said, “I will have you arrested!” The duck said, “You can’t convict me! You can’t prove I took it.” The race stopped yet again.

The animals tried to race one more time. Then they heard an alarm coming from the barn. There was a fire! They got buckets of water to put out the fire. A journalist came to write a story about the festival and the race. The horse told her, “I am a special breed of horse. I would have won the race easily.” The pig said, “It was somewhat hard to have the race. But we had fun. That is what’s important.”

qs.q: What is this story about?
o: How a special breed of racehorse would’ve won the race
Why animals have to repair things on a farm
How animals had trouble during a race

qs.q: When the cart with the apples fell over, why did the animals stop running?
o: Because they did not want to slip on the apples
Because they had to find tissue
Because they did not want to resume the race
Because the yard was far apart

qs.q: What did the duck do wrong?
o: He was arrested and convicted of stealing a bag of money.
He tried to steal the award.
He set the garage on fire.

qs.q: According to the passage, all the following are true EXCEPT
o: the alarm sounded when there was a fire
a journalist wrote about the festival

G'olib mukofot sifatida bir qop olma yutib olish huquqini qo'lga kiritardi.

e2|23.title: The Clever Thief
paras: A new king inherited a lot of gold. He loved his gold very much. He even wanted to keep it after he died. Therefore, he had a large tomb built for himself and his riches.

However, the tomb’s builder had a plan. Most of the stones were solid, but he put one special stone on the roof. It was made of a lighter substance. When the tomb was done, the king moved in his stock of gold. One night, the builder went to the tomb. His excitement mounted. Because all the stones looked alike, he had left a distinct mark on the artificial block. The mark helped him distinguish the difference in the architecture.
The builder lifted the stone. Using a chain, he climbed into the tomb. He filled his pockets with gold.
The builder followed this manner night after night. Soon, the king noticed a shortage in his gold. This annoyed the king.

At last he hired a guard to hide inside the tomb. When the builder entered the tomb, the guard wounded him. He climbed a pole to the roof. The builder left drops of blood in the dust. The guard followed them and caught him.
When the builder healed, he explained to the king that he didn’t keep any of the gold. He had given it all away to the poor.

qs.q: What is this story about?
o: The manner in which a king inherited his riches
How a builder tricked a king
Why a tomb had a large pole

qs.q: What distinguished the artificial block from the real blocks?
o: A distinct mark on one of the blocks
The different color of its substance
The amount of dust on it
The solid gold pieces in it

qs.q: How did the king know his gold was missing?
o: He found a chain in the tomb.
There was a hole in the roof.
There was a shortage of guards.
His stock of gold had decreased.

qs.q: The builder was caught because
o: he and another man looked alike
he stopped to heal the king’s wound

e2|24.title: The Doctor’s Cure
paras: James Fry was a fantastic doctor. His surgeries helped many disabled people overcome their injuries. He also wrote for a popular medical journal. James was very busy. His son, Steve, rarely saw him.
One day, James was walking and inspecting a patient’s file. There was water all over the floor. James slipped on the liquid and fell. He fell on a broken glass tube. He was hurt.
Steve came to visit him in the hospital. James said, “It will be tough for me to stay in bed. But I can hardly bend my legs.”
“Then let’s watch a movie.” Steve said. It made them laugh together. Steve said, “I have to leave, but here’s some fiction to read.”

James started to recall fun parts of life. He marveled at small things, like food. He was too busy to notice them before. “Steve,” he said, “you get more nutrients when you chew slowly. But I think it makes food taste better, too!”
Weeks later, James said, “Steve, I haven’t spent enough time with you. I regret this. Even my soul feels better when you visit. But I have spent sufficient time here. We should go home.”
Outside, there was a warm breeze. James watched a flag blow.
Finally, James said, “I’m not ready to work. I’m going to take a long bath. And then we’ll watch a movie together.”

A doctor who recalls fun things

He slipped on liquid after a bath.

qs.q: What does James do when he leaves the hospital?
o: He shows Steve that he can bend his legs.
He watches a flag blow in the breeze.
He marvels at the taste of food.

e2|25.title: The Criminal
paras: A man had been in jail because he stole things. The criminal never felt bad. One day, he escaped and ran into the woods. He found a cabin with a fence. The cabin was very neat. Inside, the criminal found a bowl of fruit, a bottle of milk, and a dozen eggs. He ate the fruit and drank the milk. But the eggs smelled funny, so he put them in the trash bin. Soon, he heard the sound of a vehicle’s motor.

An old man came in and saw the criminal. The old man yelled, “Why are you in my house?” The criminal lied, “I am a policeman.” The old man replied, “I am your elder. You cannot fool me. You are the criminal.” The criminal’s facial expression became very sad.

He admitted that he was a criminal. He said, “I’m sorry. It was rude for me to come into your home. Please take the cash from my wallet. It is a mere amount, but it will settle our problem.” The old man said, “I do not want your money. I just want to inspire you to be good. There will be no penalty for taking my food.” On this occasion, the criminal realized that he had been bad. He listened to the old man and never stole from anyone ever again.

o: Why elders are smarter than young people
How a criminal changed and learned to be good
Why you should not go to places with fences
Why you should admit when you are rude

o: He found a stranger in his house.

qs.q: What did the old man do with the criminal at the end of the story?
o: The old man reported the criminal’s penalty to the police.
The old man made an occasion to be bad.
The old man convinced the thief to never steal again.
The old man took the criminal’s money.

qs.q: According to the passage, the criminal did all of the following EXCEPT
o: he ate the fruit that was in the bowl
he drank the milk that was in the bottle
he heard the motor from the vehicle

e2|26.title: The Two Captains
paras: Once there were two ships. Both ships carried cotton. The captains were very different. Thomas was strict. He made his crew engage in difficult tasks. “Make sure the ship’s deck is firm and that nothing falls! Put more fuel in the tank!” he said. His ship was very plain, but he never had a problem with it.

The second captain, William, was not serious. He had a grand ship, and he loved having fun. His crew amused him by singing and dancing. But his crew never fixed anything on the ship. They just wanted to surf.

One day, Thomas saw a hurricane ahead. He knew that his ship needed to turn around. But he was sure William did not see the storm. He adjusted the dials on the radio and called his friend. Thomas said, “You’ll hit the reef. It’s made completely of coral. Turn around to ensure that you do not crash.” William said, “We will go under the deck and shut the door. We will dance and sing until we are past the danger zone.”

When William’s ship got to the hurricane, the wind blew it into the reef. The ship crashed, and water flowed below the deck. William’s crew accused him of being a bad captain. The loss of the ship taught William a lesson. There are times to have fun, but there are also times to be serious.

o: How Thomas is too strict to be a captain
Why people should be serious sometimes
Why hurricanes form over the ocean

He wanted to go to the reef.

He wanted to engage in other activities.

o: William did not go into the storm’s danger zone.
William caused the loss of the ship.
He did not succeed in getting the cotton to its destination.
He ensured his crew that they would not crash.

qs.q: According to the passage, all of the following are true about Thomas EXCEPT
o: he told his crew to put fuel in the tank
he had his crew make sure the deck was firm
he adjusted the radio dial to call William
he sang and danced to songs from an opera

tr: Bir paytlar ikkita kema bor edi.

e2|27.title: The Duke and the Minister
paras: A mean duke grew tobacco, and his cardinal rule was to always keep the plants healthy. The duke’s top minister was his twin brother. They closely resembled each other. One day, the tobacco plants started to die. He hired men to watch the fields. Soon, the men brought a woman to him and said, “We captured a witch!”
The Duke asked, “How do you know?”
“She sang magic words. I can’t pronounce them. She has cursed us. The death of the plants is a symptom of her curse,” the men said.
“I am just an ordinary woman. I was singing a song in a different language,” the woman protested.
The duke didn’t listen. “You are guilty. You will go to jail.”

The minister thought that she was innocent. He needed to expose the truth. He asked the duke to loan him one of his plants. He looked at it closely. He saw hundreds of small bugs eating it! Then the minister went to the jail and did something bold.
“Let this woman go,” he said.
The guards thought he was the duke. They let her go. The minister said, “I owe you an apology.”
“Thank you. I thought my stay in jail was permanent,” the woman answered. The minister thought the duke would punish him. But he didn’t. The duke was too busy trying to preserve his plants.

qs.q: What is this story about?
o: Why the duke was afraid of witches
How a minister did what was right
Why the duke loaned his brother a plant
How a woman was captured and taken to jail

qs.q: Why did the duke hire the men to watch the fields?
o: They had a bold plan to preserve the tobacco.
The tobacco plants were being destroyed.
He needed them to expose the truth.
He wanted permanent guards to watch the farmers.

qs.q: Who or what was destroying the tobacco plants?
According to the passage, all the following are true EXCEPT
o: the duke and the minister are twins
the minister pretended to be the duke
the duke gave an apology to the innocent woman
the guard said the woman pronounced magic words

tr: Bir yovuz gersog tamaki yetishtirardi va uning asosiy qoidasi o'simliklarni doim sog'lom saqlash edi.
Gersogning bosh vaziri uning egizak ukasi edi.
Ular bir-biriga juda o'xshashardi.
Bir kuni tamaki o'simliklari quriy boshladi.
U dalalarni qo'riqlash uchun odamlar yolladi.
Tez orada odamlar uning oldiga bir ayolni olib kelib: «Biz jodugarni tutdik!» deyishdi.
Gersog so'radi: «Qayerdan bilasizlar?»
«U sehrli so'zlarni kuylardi.
Men ularni talaffuz qila olmayman.
U bizni qarg'agan.
O'simliklarning nobud bo'lishi uning qarg'ishining alomati», dedi odamlar.
«Men oddiy ayolman.
Boshqa tilda qo'shiq aytayotgan edim», deb e'tiroz bildirdi ayol.
Gersog quloq solmadi.
«Sen aybdorsan.
Qamoqqa tushasan».
Vazir ayolni aybsiz deb o'yladi.
U haqiqatni fosh qilishi kerak edi.
U gersogdan o'simliklaridan birini vaqtincha berib turishni so'radi.
U unga diqqat bilan qaradi.
U uni yeyayotgan yuzlab mayda hasharotlarni ko'rdi!
Keyin vazir qamoqxonaga borib, jasoratli ish qildi.
«Bu ayolni qo'yib yuboringlar», dedi u.
Soqchilar uni gersog deb o'ylashdi.
Ular ayolni qo'yib yuborishdi.
Vazir dedi: «Men sizdan kechirim so'rashim kerak».
«Rahmat.
Qamoqda abadiy qolaman deb o'ylagandim», deb javob berdi ayol.
Vazir gersog uni jazolaydi deb o'yladi.
Lekin u jazolamadi.
Gersog o'simliklarini saqlab qolish bilan juda band edi.

e2|28.title: The Fisherman
paras: Every day, a fisherman sat on a bridge. He ate apples and spit the seeds into the water. He had a simple way to catch fish. He cut a branch off of a tree and tied a line to it. He put a sharp hook on it and made a tight knot. Then he whispered, “Come here fish.” Like magic, the fish bit the hook. He put them in a big net and took them home to make big pots of fish soup from them.

One day, another man walked up to him. He said, “My name is George. I am staying at the inn. I bet that I am a better fisherman than you. I will accompany you today. I dare you to prove your skill!” The fisherman cast his line. George had a lot of electronic tools. One machine gave him the virtual locations of fish. His rod even weighed fish.
At the end of the day, George subtracted his fish from the fisherman’s. The fisherman had beaten him by forty-seven!

George asked, “How do you catch fish with only a branch and a bare line? I have many different sorts of tools.” The fisherman told George, “My philosophy is simple. I am patient, and I believe in myself. Take a breath, and try it my way.”

qs.q: What is this story about?
o: How a man’s philosophy was a good match for fishing
Why George did not like the fisherman

qs.q: What did the fisherman do with the fish?
o: He sold them to a restaurant.
He made all sorts of food.

qs.q: What did the fisherman do every day at the bridge?
o: He would cast his line into the water.
He would take a breath then jump into the river.
He would accompany George from the inn.
He would eat a virtual pot of fish soup.

qs.q: According to the passage, all the following are true about the fisherman EXCEPT___.
o: he used a bare line with a tight knot
he used an electronic rod to weigh fish

tr: Har kuni bir baliqchi ko'prikda o'tirardi.
U olma yeb, urug'larini suvga tupurardi.
Uning baliq tutishning oddiy usuli bor edi.
U daraxtdan bir shoxni kesib olib, unga ip bog'ladi.
U unga o'tkir ilmoq taqib, mahkam tugun qildi.
Keyin u: «Bu yoqqa kel, baliq», deb pichirladi.
Xuddi sehrdek, baliqlar ilmoqni tishlardi.
U ularni katta to'rga solib, katta qozonlarda baliq sho'rva qilish uchun uyiga olib ketardi.
Bir kuni uning oldiga boshqa bir odam keldi.
U dedi: «Mening ismim Jorj.
Men mehmonxonada turibman.
Garov o'ynayman, men sendan yaxshiroq baliqchiman.
Bugun men sen bilan birga bo'laman.
Mahoratingni isbotlab ko'r-chi!»
Baliqchi qarmog'ini tashladi.
Jorjda ko'plab elektron asboblar bor edi.
Bir mashina unga baliqlarning virtual joylashuvini ko'rsatardi.
Uning qarmog'i hatto baliqlarni tortardi ham.
Kun oxirida Jorj o'z baliqlarini baliqchinikidan ayirdi.
Baliqchi undan qirq yettitaga ko'p tutgan edi!
Jorj so'radi: «Qanday qilib faqat shox va oddiy ip bilan baliq tutasan?
Menda turli xil asboblar ko'p». Baliqchi Jorjga dedi: «Mening falsafam oddiy.
Men sabrliman va o'zimga ishonaman.
Nafas ol-da, mening usulimda urinib ko'r».

e2|29.title: Osiris and the Nile
paras: Long ago, Osiris was the king of Egypt, and Isis was the queen. They ruled the fertile land by the Nile River. They had great intelligence, and they shared their abstract ideas with everyone. Osiris taught the Egyptians how to make wheels and furniture. Isis taught them how to make things from clay and cloth. The people thought they deserved a gift. So they built Osiris and Isis a pyramid. Everyone loved Osiris except his brother, Set. Set wanted to be king. Osiris made his annual trip around Egypt and led religious events. The villages gave him beautiful shells and colorful feathers as gifts. When Osiris returned, Set brought a beautiful wooden box from behind a curtain.
“If someone fits inside this box, I will give it to him or her,” Set said. Osiris got in it. It was an ideal fit!
Suddenly, Set closed the box and threw it into the river. “Now I will be king!” Set said.
The box washed up on a foreign shore after a flood. Isis brought his body home and obtained a grave for him in Egypt. The Egyptian gods thought Isis had done something very romantic.
Because of her love, the gods made him the god of the underworld. Osiris returned every spring to help the farmers. Even nowadays, people say Osiris keeps their crops alive.

qs.q: What is this story about?
o: Why Osiris built a pyramid for Isis
How Set created a grave for Osiris
How Osiris died and returned to make Egypt fertile
Why the gods thought Isis’ actions were romantic

qs.q: What happened each spring?
o: Osiris returned to help the farmers.
Set hid a box behind a curtain.

qs.q: In the last paragraph, we can infer that___.
o: the shore is the ideal home for Osiris
Set had greater intelligence than the gods
the gods felt that Isis did a good deed
nowadays, the Egyptians don’t use Osiris’ abstract ideas

qs.q: According to the passage, all the following are true EXCEPT

tr: Qadim zamonlarda Osiris Misr qiroli, Isida esa malika edi.
Ular Nil daryosi bo'yidagi serhosil yerlarni boshqarishardi.
Ular juda aqlli edilar va o'zlarining mavhum g'oyalarini hamma bilan baham ko'rishardi.
Osiris misrliklarga g'ildirak va mebel yasashni o'rgatdi.
Isida ularga loy va matodan buyumlar yasashni o'rgatdi.
Odamlar ularni sovg'aga loyiq deb o'ylashdi.
Shuning uchun ular Osiris va Isidaga piramida qurib berishdi.
Ukasi Setdan boshqa hamma Osirisni yaxshi ko'rardi.
Set qirol bo'lishni xohlardi.
Osiris har yilgi Misr bo'ylab safariga chiqib, diniy marosimlarni boshqardi.
Qishloqlar unga sovg'a sifatida chiroyli chig'anoqlar va rang-barang patlar berishdi.
Osiris qaytganida, Set parda ortidan chiroyli yog'och quti olib chiqdi.
«Kim bu qutiga sig'sa, uni o'shanga beraman», dedi Set.
Osiris unga kirdi.
U unga ayni o'lchamda edi!
To'satdan Set qutini yopib, daryoga uloqtirdi.
«Endi men qirol bo'laman!» dedi Set.
Toshqindan keyin quti begona sohilga oqib chiqdi.
Isida uning jasadini uyiga olib keldi va unga Misrdan qabr joy oldi.
Misr xudolari Isida juda ishqiy ish qildi deb o'ylashdi.
Uning muhabbati tufayli xudolar Osirisni yer osti dunyosining xudosi qilishdi.
Osiris har bahorda dehqonlarga yordam berish uchun qaytib kelardi.
Hatto hozir ham odamlar Osiris ekinlarini hayot saqlaydi deyishadi.

e2|30.title: The Taxi Driver
paras: Peter’s job was driving a taxi downtown. He made a small salary. But he liked his job because it wasn’t dull. Every day, he saw new things that appealed to him. Peter was practical about the future. “Maybe I can get a scholarship to college,” he thought. “I could learn mathematical formulas and get a job at a bank. I could help clients invest their money.”
Peter stopped to pick up a passenger. “Where to?” he asked.

“Go to the Fourth Street Bank. And don’t talk to me. I’ve had a rough day,” the man said. Peter was angry, but he had a peaceful philosophy. When they stopped, the man’s fare came to $10.25. He put his hands in his pockets. “I can’t find my wallet!” he said. “I can’t pay the fare!”
Peter said, “Maybe I’ll give you a temporary loan. You can borrow ten dollars and a quarter from me.”

The man was embarrassed, saying, “I was mean to you, but now I want to help you. I founded this bank. I want to give you one thousand dollars.” That much money was like a treasure to Peter. The man urged him to take the money, but he didn’t.
“You’re an honest person,” the man said. “I assumed you would take it. I want you to work for me.”
The next day, Peter started his job at the bank. He was happy to be done with his former job.

qs.q: What is this story about?
o: How a poor taxi driver got a new job by being kind
Why a dull job with a high salary appeals to people
How to get a scholarship to go to college
Why it is important not to borrow money

qs.q: What does Peter do downtown?
o: He drives people around for a quarter.

qs.q: Why does the man give Peter a job?
o: He assumes that Peter is practical.
He didn’t want to give Peter a treasure.
Peter showed that he was honest.
Peter loaned him twenty five cents.

qs.q: Why does Peter like his job?
o: He invested a lot of money in it.
It is only a temporary job.
He can embarrass other people by being rude.
It is never dull and he meets many people.

tr: Piterning ishi shahar markazida taksi haydash edi.
U oz maosh olardi.
Lekin u ishini yaxshi ko'rardi, chunki u zerikarli emasdi.
Har kuni u o'ziga yoqadigan yangi narsalarni ko'rardi.
Piter kelajakka amaliy qarardi.
«Balki kollejga stipendiya olarman», deb o'yladi u.
«Matematik formulalarni o'rganib, bankka ishga kirishim mumkin.
Mijozlarga pullarini sarmoya qilishda yordam berardim».
Piter bir yo'lovchini olish uchun to'xtadi.
«Qayerga?» deb so'radi u.
«To'rtinchi ko'chadagi bankka bor.
Va men bilan gaplashma.
Bugun kunim og'ir o'tdi», dedi odam.
Piterning jahli chiqdi, lekin uning tinch falsafasi bor edi.
Ular to'xtashganida, odamning yo'l haqi 10 dollar 25 sent bo'ldi.
U qo'llarini cho'ntaklariga soldi.
«Hamyonimni topa olmayapman! — dedi u. —
Yo'l haqini to'lay olmayman!»
Piter dedi: «Balki sizga vaqtincha qarz berarman.
Mendan o'n dollar va chorak qarz olishingiz mumkin».
Odam xijolat bo'lib dedi: «Men senga qo'pollik qildim, lekin endi senga yordam bermoqchiman.
Men bu bankni asos solganman.
Senga ming dollar bermoqchiman».
Shuncha pul Piter uchun xazinadek edi.
Odam uni pulni olishga undadi, lekin u olmadi.
«Sen halol odamsan, — dedi odam. —
Olasan deb o'ylagandim.
Men uchun ishlashingni xohlayman».
Ertasi kuni Piter bankdagi ishini boshladi.
U avvalgi ishini tugatganidan xursand edi.

e3|1.title: The Real St. Nick
paras: At Christmas, children wait for St. Nicholas to bring gifts down the chimney. But it’s not just a story. St. Nicholas was a real person.

A long time ago, a man named Marcus occupied a house with his family. He was not modest. He always told everybody he was the strongest man in the province. He worked hard, but he could barely sustain his family. He wanted to save money and prosper. Still, he could never earn a penny more than he needed.

One day, Marcus made an agreement with a blacksmith. The blacksmith had a lot of work to do. But he couldn’t do it all by himself. Marcus wanted to help him forge iron. The blacksmith agreed to compensate him with a lot of money.

In the same town, there was a man named Nicholas. At an early age, Nicholas started preaching. But he also believed that he should be humble and charitable. He learned that helping people gave him even more satisfaction than preaching. One day, Nicholas encountered Marcus. Marcus told Nicholas about his agreement with the blacksmith. “I worked hard for him,” Marcus said, “but a problem arose. Even though I worked for him, he didn’t pay me.”

Nicholas wanted to help Marcus. That night, he went back to Marcus’s house. He brought a bag of gold. It exceeded the amount that Marcus needed. Nicholas climbed up a ladder and dropped the bag of gold down the chimney. Marcus thanked his benefactor.
Soon, people found out about Nicholas’s gift. He became well known and loved. Even today, people still give secret gifts to children. And we say they are from St. Nicholas.

qs.q: Which of the following is true about the job Marcus did?
Why didn’t Nicolas tell people that he gave money away?
o: He didn’t want to be modest
He wasn’t popular in the province.

qs.q: What was dropped down the chimney?
Why did Marcus want more money?

tr: Rojdestvoda bolalar Avliyo Nikolayning mo'ri orqali sovg'a tushirishini kutishadi.
Lekin bu shunchaki ertak emas.
Avliyo Nikolay haqiqiy odam bo'lgan.
Qadim zamonlarda Markus ismli bir odam oilasi bilan bir uyda yashardi.
U kamtar emasdi.
U hammaga doim o'zini viloyatdagi eng kuchli odam deb aytardi.
U qattiq ishlardi, lekin oilasini zo'rg'a boqardi.
U pul jamg'arib, farovon yashashni xohlardi.
Shunday bo'lsa ham, u hech qachon keragidan bir tiyin ham ortiq pul topa olmasdi.
Bir kuni Markus bir temirchi bilan kelishuv tuzdi.
Temirchining ishi juda ko'p edi.
Lekin u hammasini yolg'iz o'zi qila olmasdi.
Markus unga temirga ishlov berishda yordam bermoqchi edi.
Temirchi buning evaziga unga ko'p pul to'lashga rozi bo'ldi.
O'sha shaharda Nikolay ismli bir odam bor edi.
Nikolay yoshligidanoq va'z o'qiy boshlagan edi.
Lekin u kamtar va saxiy bo'lish kerakligiga ham ishonardi.
U odamlarga yordam berish unga va'z o'qishdan ham ko'proq qoniqish berishini bildi.
Bir kuni Nikolay Markusni uchratib qoldi.
Markus Nikolayga temirchi bilan qilgan kelishuvi haqida gapirib berdi.
«Men uning uchun qattiq ishladim, — dedi Markus, — lekin bir muammo chiqdi.
Uning uchun ishlaganimga qaramay, u menga pul to'lamadi».
Nikolay Markusga yordam bermoqchi bo'ldi.
O'sha kechasi u Markusning uyiga qaytib bordi.
U bir xalta oltin olib keldi.
Bu Markusga kerak bo'lgan miqdordan ham ko'p edi.
Nikolay narvonga chiqib, oltin xaltasini mo'ridan pastga tashladi.
Markus o'z homiysiga rahmat aytdi.
Tez orada odamlar Nikolayning sovg'asidan xabar topishdi.
U mashhur va sevimli bo'lib qoldi.
Hatto bugun ham odamlar bolalarga yashirincha sovg'a berishadi.
Biz esa ular Avliyo Nikolaydan deymiz.

e3|2.title: The Shepherd and the Wild Sheep
paras: Once there was a shepherd. Every night he counted and gathered his sheep. He was sure never to overlook any of them. One night, he saw some wild sheep had joined his herd. He hoped to acquire the newcomers.

It snowed that night. In the morning, the shepherd couldn’t take his sheep out of his lodge. Instead, he had to feed them inside. He gave a small amount of wheat to his own sheep. But he gave more of the food to the wild sheep. He thought the extra wheat would discourage them from leaving.
It snowed for several days. During that time, the shepherd’s sheep ate very little. The wild sheep, however, ate very well.
At last, the snow melted, and they ventured outdoors. As soon as he opened the door of his hut, the wild sheep started to run away.
“Wait! This is how you repay me? After I treated you so kindly, why do you run away?” the shepherd asked. His voice was full of hatred.
The wild sheep stopped and turned toward the shepherd.

“We’re leaving because you fed us better than your own sheep,” one of the wild sheep replied. “You tried to deceive us with your ridiculous plan. Yesterday you treated us kindly, but tomorrow you might be different. If more wild sheep joined your herd, you would treat us as inferior sheep.”

As the wild sheep ran away, the shepherd understood his offense. He knew this awkward situation was his own fault. He had not been a satisfactory caretaker. He was a fake friend to the wild sheep. Because of this, he had neglected his own herd.

qs.q: What was the shepherd’s hope for the wild sheep?
o: That they would feel hatred for him

qs.q: How did the shepherd hope to discourage the wild sheep from running away?
o: By locking them in his hut

qs.q: All of the following describe what kind of caretaker the shepherd was EXCEPT ___
What was the shepherd’s offense?
o: He never acquired the wild sheep.
He trapped the sheep in his lodge
He did not care for his own sheep.

tr: Bir paytlar bir cho'pon bor edi.
U har kecha qo'ylarini sanab, yig'ib olardi.
U ularning birortasini ham e'tibordan chetda qoldirmaslikka harakat qilardi.
Bir kecha u podasiga bir nechta yovvoyi qo'y qo'shilganini ko'rdi.
U yangi kelganlarni o'ziniki qilib olishga umid qildi.
O'sha kechasi qor yog'di.
Ertalab cho'pon qo'ylarini qo'tondan olib chiqa olmadi.
Buning o'rniga u ularni ichkarida boqishiga to'g'ri keldi.
U o'z qo'ylariga ozgina bug'doy berdi.
Lekin yovvoyi qo'ylarga ko'proq ovqat berdi.
U qo'shimcha bug'doy ularni ketishdan qaytaradi deb o'yladi.
Bir necha kun qor yog'di.
Bu vaqt ichida cho'ponning qo'ylari juda kam ovqat yedi.
Yovvoyi qo'ylar esa juda yaxshi ovqatlandi.
Nihoyat, qor eridi va ular tashqariga chiqishdi.
U kulbasining eshigini ochishi bilan yovvoyi qo'ylar qochib keta boshladi.
«To'xtanglar!
Menga shunday qaytaryapsizlarmi?
Sizlarga shunchalik yaxshi munosabatda bo'lganimdan keyin nega qochyapsizlar?» deb so'radi cho'pon.
Uning ovozi nafratga to'la edi.
Yovvoyi qo'ylar to'xtab, cho'pon tomonga o'girilishdi.
«Biz ketyapmiz, chunki sen bizni o'z qo'ylaringdan yaxshiroq boqding», deb javob berdi yovvoyi qo'ylardan biri.
«Sen kulgili rejang bilan bizni aldamoqchi bo'lding.
Kecha bizga yaxshi munosabatda bo'lding, lekin ertaga boshqacha bo'lishing mumkin.
Agar podangga boshqa yovvoyi qo'ylar qo'shilsa, sen bizga past darajadagi qo'ylardek munosabatda bo'larding».
Yovvoyi qo'ylar qochib ketayotganda, cho'pon o'z aybini tushundi.
U bu noqulay vaziyatga o'zi aybdor ekanini bildi.
U qoniqarli qarovchi bo'lmagan edi.
U yovvoyi qo'ylar uchun soxta do'st bo'lgan edi.
Shu sababli u o'z podasiga e'tiborsizlik qilgan edi.

e3|3.title: The Boy and his Sled
paras: Mike was the smallest child in school. Another boy, Joe, always teased Mike. Joe had a large scar on his face from fighting other children. One day, Joe offended Mike when he made fun of Mike’s valentine, Jane. Mike felt disgrace, but he didn’t know how to make Joe stop.

That day, Mike walked home down an alley. He found a bunch of wood boards next to a pine tree. He thought to himself, “I could build a decent sled from this. If I let Joe use it, he will be nicer to me and Jane.” He took the wood home.

Mike got an ax and cut the wood. He used nails to make sure that the pieces were not loose. As he worked, he bumped his elbow on the boards. The painful sensation made him want to cry. It was a hard chore, but he persisted. He worked overnight. By morning, the sled was finished.
Mike called Joe on the telephone. He said, “Hi Joe. Come over to my house right away.”

Joe didn’t know why Mike wanted him to come over. When Joe arrived, Mike told him, “Joe, it irritated me the other day when you said mean things about my card to Jane. You weren’t kidding when you said those mean things.
But I’m not like you. I just built this sled, and I’ll let you ride it with me if you are nice.”
They became friends, and Joe was grateful.

qs.q: Which item did Mike NOT use when building the sled?
At the end of the reading, Joe ___.
o: was grateful that Mike was nice
did not get to ride on the sled

qs.q: Why did Mike feel a painful sensation?
o: Joe teased him with the hammer.
He got a scar on his face.
He bumped his elbow on the boards.

qs.q: According to the reading, when did Mike build the sled?

tr: Mayk maktabdagi eng kichkina bola edi.
Boshqa bir bola, Jo, doim Maykni masxara qilardi.
Joning yuzida boshqa bolalar bilan urishganidan qolgan katta chandiq bor edi.
Bir kuni Jo Maykning yoqtirgan qizi Jeynni masxara qilib, Maykni xafa qildi.
Mayk sharmandalik his qildi, lekin Joni qanday to'xtatishni bilmasdi.
O'sha kuni Mayk tor ko'cha orqali uyiga piyoda qaytdi.
U qarag'ay daraxti yonida bir dasta yog'och taxtalarni topdi.
U ichida o'yladi: «Bundan durustgina chana yasashim mumkin.
Agar Joga undan foydalanishga ruxsat bersam, u menga va Jeynga yaxshiroq munosabatda bo'ladi».
U yog'ochni uyiga olib ketdi.
Mayk bolta olib, yog'ochni kesdi.
U bo'laklar bo'sh qolmasligi uchun mixlardan foydalandi.
Ishlayotganda u tirsagini taxtalarga urib oldi.
Og'riqli tuyg'u uni yig'latib yuborishiga sal qoldi.
Bu og'ir yumush edi, lekin u bo'sh kelmadi.
U tun bo'yi ishladi.
Ertalabga kelib chana tayyor bo'ldi.
Mayk Joga telefon qildi.
U dedi: «Salom, Jo.
Hoziroq uyimga kel».
Jo Mayk nega uni chaqirayotganini bilmasdi.
Jo kelganida Mayk unga dedi: «Jo, o'tgan kuni Jeynga bergan otkritkam haqida yomon gaplarni aytganingda jahlim chiqdi.
O'sha yomon gaplarni aytganingda hazillashmagan eding.
Lekin men senga o'xshamayman.
Men hozirgina shu chanani yasadim va agar yaxshi bo'lsang, men bilan birga uchishingga ruxsat beraman».
Ular do'st bo'lib qolishdi va Jo minnatdor edi.

e3|4.title: Tiny Tina
paras: In a distant land, there was a kingdom where fairies lived. Tina was a fairy. She had yellow curls and wore a dress made of wool. She always moved with grace. However, because of her compact size, she was scared of mankind.
One day, there was an eclipse of the sun. The fairies didn’t know what was happening. They were scared, so they ran away.

Tina looked for a place to hide. She found a garden with flowers blooming. Tina had a passion for flowers. She decided to hide there. She became sleepy and made a pillow with some leaves. She whistled happily as she worked, and she fell asleep. Suddenly, somebody sneezed. The sound woke Tina up. She saw a very big face looking at her! Tina was so scared that she couldn’t move. She could feel her pulse going very fast.
The big woman went into her house. When she came back, she gave Tina a cup.
The woman sat on the ground among some decaying leaves. Tina dipped a finger in the cup and tasted it. It was tea with all kinds of delicious spices in it. Tina felt refreshed after drinking the tea.
“I’m Wilma,” the lady said. “I spend all my leisure time in my garden cutting flowers. Would you like some dessert?”
Tina said yes. She was hungry, and she wasn’t frightened anymore. She took a bite of cake and relaxed. “How did you get to my garden?”
Tina told Wilma how she got lost.
“That’s terrible! Let us take you home.”
“Actually, I think that I want to stay with you,” Tina said. She wasn’t scared of big people anymore. Wilma and Tina lived happily ever after.

qs.q: Why did Tina suddenly wake up?
All of the following describe Tina EXCEPT ___.
o: she had curls in her hair
she did not like tea with spice

qs.q: What does Wilma do with the flowers?
Where did Tina live before she met Wilma?
o: On a street with big cars

tr: Uzoq bir yurtda parilar yashaydigan qirollik bor edi.
Tina pari edi.
Uning sariq jingalak sochlari bor edi va jun ko'ylak kiyib yurardi.
U doim nafislik bilan harakatlanardi.
Biroq jussasi kichkina bo'lgani uchun u insoniyatdan qo'rqardi.
Bir kuni quyosh tutildi.
Parilar nima bo'layotganini bilishmadi.
Ular qo'rqib, qochib ketishdi.
Tina yashirinadigan joy qidirdi.
U gullar ochilib turgan bir bog'ni topdi.
Tina gullarni juda yaxshi ko'rardi.
U o'sha yerda yashirinishga qaror qildi.
Uning uyqusi keldi va bir nechta bargdan yostiq yasadi.
U ishlayotganda xursand bo'lib hushtak chalardi va uxlab qoldi.
To'satdan kimdir aksirdi.
Ovoz Tinani uyg'otib yubordi.
U o'ziga qarab turgan juda katta yuzni ko'rdi!
Tina shunchalik qo'rqib ketdiki, qimirlay olmadi.
U yuragi juda tez urayotganini sezdi.
Katta ayol uyiga kirib ketdi.
U qaytib kelganida, Tinaga bir piyola berdi.
Ayol chirib borayotgan barglar orasida yerga o'tirdi.
Tina barmog'ini piyolaga botirib, tatib ko'rdi.
Bu har xil mazali ziravorlar qo'shilgan choy edi.
Choyni ichgandan keyin Tina tetiklashdi.
«Men Vilmaman», dedi xonim.
«Butun bo'sh vaqtimni bog'imda gul kesib o'tkazaman.
Shirinlik yeysanmi?»
Tina ha dedi.
U och edi va endi qo'rqmasdi.
U tortdan bir tishlab, yengil tortdi.
«Mening bog'imga qanday kelib qolding?»
Tina Vilmaga qanday adashib qolganini aytib berdi.
«Bu dahshat-ku!
Keling, seni uyingga olib boramiz».
«Aslida men siz bilan qolishni xohlayman», dedi Tina.
U endi katta odamlardan qo'rqmasdi.
Vilma va Tina shundan keyin baxtli yashashdi.

e3|5.title: Trick-or-Treat!
paras: Many different cultures have had traditions about the dead. People in places like Ireland, China, Egypt and Mexico believed that souls needed food. They thought the food nourished them on their journey from cemeteries to heaven. People had to put out good things for souls to eat. However, if the food rotted or spoiled, the soul got mad. The wicked soul might curse the family and make them starve during the winter.

In other places, people begged for food on a holiday that remembers the souls of dead saints. People wore disguises with hoods that covered their faces. If they did not get food, they played a trick on the home. For this reason, the activity is known as “trick-or-treating.” Shortly after people first began trick-or-treating, parents started sending their children to beg on that day. Housewives gave the children food if they performed a song or a dance. When people moved to America from all over the world, they brought this tradition with them.
Inhabitants of villages started trick-or-treating in the early 1900s. In 1939 a children’s publication acquainted the whole country with the tradition. It became very popular.

Today, trick-or-treaters are not begging for food, and they are not scared of souls. They just enjoy the thrill of dressing up like creatures and getting candy. Ghosts and skeletons are favorite costumes. But some children wear fancy disguises, like pirates. They carry flashlights instead of fires. In some places, children still perform songs or riddles to get candy. But most of the time, they just say “Trick-or-Treat!”

qs.q: Which of the following is the most popular disguise?
Why did souls need food?
o: For their long journey to heaven

qs.q: What did the souls do when they left cemeteries?
Why do children perform riddles when they trick-or-treat?

tr: Ko'plab turli madaniyatlarda o'liklar haqida an'analar bo'lgan.
Irlandiya, Xitoy, Misr va Meksika kabi joylardagi odamlar ruhlarga ovqat kerak deb ishonishgan.
Ular ovqat ruhlarni qabristondan jannatga boradigan yo'lida quvvatlantiradi deb o'ylashgan.
Odamlar ruhlar yeyishi uchun yaxshi narsalarni qo'yib qo'yishlari kerak edi.
Biroq agar ovqat chirib yoki buzilib qolsa, ruhning jahli chiqardi.
Yovuz ruh oilani qarg'ab, ularni qishda ochlikdan qiynashi mumkin edi.
Boshqa joylarda odamlar vafot etgan avliyolar ruhini yod etadigan bayramda ovqat so'rab yurishardi.
Odamlar yuzlarini yopadigan qalpoqli niqob kiyishardi.
Agar ovqat olishmasa, o'sha uydagilar ustidan hazil-mutoyiba qilishardi.
Shu sababli bu mashg'ulot «trick-or-treat» («shirinlik ber, bo'lmasa hazil qilaman») deb nomlanadi.
Odamlar bu odatni boshlaganidan ko'p o'tmay, ota-onalar o'sha kuni bolalarini ovqat so'rashga yubora boshlashdi.
Uy bekalari bolalar qo'shiq aytsa yoki raqs tushsa, ularga ovqat berishardi.
Dunyoning turli joylaridan Amerikaga ko'chib kelgan odamlar bu an'anani o'zlari bilan olib kelishdi.
Qishloq aholisi 1900-yillar boshida bu odatni boshlashdi.
1939-yilda bolalar nashri butun mamlakatni bu an'ana bilan tanishtirdi.
U juda mashhur bo'lib ketdi.
Bugun bu odat bilan yurganlar ovqat so'rashmaydi va ruhlardan qo'rqishmaydi.
Ular shunchaki maxluqlardek kiyinib, konfet olishning hayajonidan zavqlanishadi.
Arvoh va skelet eng sevimli liboslardir.
Lekin ba'zi bolalar qaroqchilar kabi chiroyli liboslar kiyishadi.
Ular olov o'rniga qo'l chiroq ko'tarib yurishadi.
Ba'zi joylarda bolalar hali ham konfet olish uchun qo'shiq aytishadi yoki topishmoq aytishadi.
Lekin ko'pincha ular shunchaki «Trick-or-Treat!» deyishadi.

e3|6.title: The Senator and the Worm
paras: A rich senator lived in a big house. He had more money than anyone in his district. One day, he was sitting on a chair listening to a radio broadcast. As he listened to the news bulletin, a worm crawled from underneath the chair and onto his head. His cook was in the kitchen stirring some spaghetti sauce. Suddenly, a cry from the senator alerted him. He ran to the rear of the house where the senator was sitting. The cook looked and saw the worm. He tried to console the senator. “I’ll take it off right away,” he said.
“No!” shouted the senator. “I want you to kill it.”
“But it’s only a worm,” the cook said. “Why should we execute it? It hasn’t committed a crime.”

The senator could not endure the worm on his head. “Hurry!” he shouted. The cook looked through several drawers, but found nothing. Then he ran to the closet and took out a pipe. He returned to the senator and lifted the pipe over his head. He knew he couldn’t just tap the worm. He was going to hit it hard. He grasped the pipe tightly.
“What are you waiting for?” said the senator. “Kill it!”
The cook swung the pipe at the senator’s head.
“Oh, no,” the worm said. “He’s going to chop me in half.” It jumped off the senator’s head.
There was a tremendous noise. “Owww!” cried the senator.
A bump rose upon his skull. Meanwhile, the worm crawled outside.
“That was close,” said the worm. “Instead of being nice, he wanted to hurt me. Now, that man has a big bump on his head.”

qs.q: What was the senator doing when the worm crawled onto his head?
Which of the following did the cook NOT do?
Why did the senator tell the cook to hurry?
o: He was hiding in the rear of the house.
He knew he had to alert the cook
He couldn’t endure the worm on his head.
He had heard a tremendous noise.

qs.q: After the cook hit the senator, where did the worm go?

tr: Bir boy senator katta uyda yashardi.
Uning okrugidagi hammadan ko'proq puli bor edi.
Bir kuni u stulda o'tirib, radio eshittirishini tinglayotgan edi.
U yangiliklar xabarini tinglayotganda, stul ostidan bir chuvalchang chiqib, uning boshiga o'rmalab chiqdi.
Uning oshpazi oshxonada spagetti sousini aralashtirayotgan edi.
To'satdan senatorning qichqirig'i uni xavotirga soldi.
U senator o'tirgan uyning orqa tomoniga yugurdi.
Oshpaz qarab, chuvalchangni ko'rdi.
U senatorni tinchlantirmoqchi bo'ldi.
«Hoziroq olib tashlayman», dedi u.
«Yo'q!» deb qichqirdi senator.
«Uni o'ldirishingni xohlayman».
«Lekin u shunchaki chuvalchang-ku», dedi oshpaz.
«Nega uni qatl qilishimiz kerak?
U jinoyat qilmagan-ku».
Senator boshidagi chuvalchangga chiday olmadi.
«Tezroq!» deb qichqirdi u.
Oshpaz bir nechta tortmani qaradi, lekin hech narsa topmadi.
Keyin u shkafga yugurib, bir quvur olib chiqdi.
U senatorning oldiga qaytib, quvurni uning boshi uzra ko'tardi.
U chuvalchangga shunchaki sekin urib qo'ya olmasligini bilardi.
U qattiq urmoqchi edi.
U quvurni mahkam ushladi.
«Nimani kutyapsan? — dedi senator. —
O'ldir uni!»
Oshpaz quvurni senatorning boshiga qarab siltadi.
«Voy, yo'q, — dedi chuvalchang. —
U meni ikkiga bo'lib tashlamoqchi».
U senatorning boshidan sakrab tushdi.
Dahshatli shovqin eshitildi.
«Voy!» deb qichqirdi senator.
Uning bosh suyagida g'urra paydo bo'ldi.
Bu orada chuvalchang tashqariga o'rmalab chiqib ketdi.
«Sal qoldi-ya», dedi chuvalchang.
«Yaxshilik qilish o'rniga u menga ozor bermoqchi bo'ldi.
Endi o'sha odamning boshida katta g'urra bor».

e3|7.title: Patsy Ann
paras: A long time ago in Alaska, a dog named Patsy Ann watched the horizon. Every day, she waited by the bay for ships returning from an expedition.

Patsy Ann was a brilliant dog, and she was very unique. She was deaf. She couldn’t bark, either. But she used all of her other senses to know when a ship was near. Patsy Ann lived on the streets. Her owners did not want her because she could not hear. So they abandoned her. She found refuge in a fancy hotel. Guests rubbed her back and scratched her chin. Many people gave her food. She became quite overweight.

She became very famous. Visitors to Alaska were enthusiastic about meeting her. They brought presents for her. They liked seeing her and the feeling was mutual. The mayor said Patsy Ann should be called the town’s greeter.

The people in town loved Patsy Ann, too, even though she lived on the streets. They were willing to fight to keep her. A new law made all dogs wear a collar and get shots. The mayor received many complaints. People wanted Patsy Ann to be able to stay. One ambitious sailor got people to help. Together, they paid for Patsy Ann to go to the veterinarian. She got her shots and collar. She could stay.

When Patsy Ann died, everyone missed the town’s loyal greeter. So the mayor hired someone to make a statue of Patsy Ann. He restored the town’s greeter. Now, she sits at the dock forever, waiting for ships to come home.

qs.q: What could Patsy Ann NOT do?
What was the sailor who helped Patsy Ann?
Why did Patsy Ann go to the hotel?
Why was the dog abandoned?
o: Because the veterinarian didn’t like her
Because she was mean to them

tr: Ancha yillar oldin Alyaskada Patsi Enn ismli it ufqqa tikilib turardi.
U har kuni ko'rfaz bo'yida ekspeditsiyadan qaytayotgan kemalarni kutardi.
Patsi Enn juda aqlli it edi va u juda noyob edi.
U kar edi.
U hura olmasdi ham.
Lekin u kema yaqinlashganini bilish uchun boshqa barcha sezgilaridan foydalanardi.
Patsi Enn ko'chada yashardi.
Egalari u eshitmagani uchun uni xohlashmagandi.
Shuning uchun ular uni tashlab ketishgan edi.
U hashamatli mehmonxonadan panoh topdi.
Mehmonlar uning orqasini silab, iyagini qashlab qo'yishardi.
Ko'p odamlar unga ovqat berishardi.
U ancha semirib ketdi.
U juda mashhur bo'lib ketdi.
Alyaskaga kelgan mehmonlar u bilan tanishishga ishtiyoqmand edilar.
Ular unga sovg'alar olib kelishardi.
Ular uni ko'rishni yaxshi ko'rishardi va bu tuyg'u o'zaro edi.
Shahar hokimi Patsi Ennni shaharning mehmon kutib oluvchisi deb atash kerakligini aytdi.
Shahar aholisi ham Patsi Ennni yaxshi ko'rishardi, garchi u ko'chada yashasa ham.
Ular uni saqlab qolish uchun kurashishga tayyor edilar.
Yangi qonunga ko'ra barcha itlar bo'yinbog' taqishi va emlanishi kerak edi.
Hokim ko'plab shikoyatlar oldi.
Odamlar Patsi Enn qolishini xohlashardi.
Bir g'ayratli dengizchi odamlarni yordamga undadi.
Ular birgalikda Patsi Ennning veterinarga borishi uchun pul to'lashdi.
U emlandi va bo'yinbog' oldi.
U qolishi mumkin edi.
Patsi Enn o'lganida, hamma shaharning sodiq mehmon kutib oluvchisini sog'indi.
Shuning uchun hokim Patsi Ennning haykalini yasash uchun odam yolladi.
U shaharning mehmon kutib oluvchisini qayta tikladi.
Endi u kemalarning uyga qaytishini kutib, abadiy iskalada o'tiradi.

e3|8.title: The Anniversary Gift
paras: Joe was a carpenter. He built houses in the highlands. Joe’s wife Stella used a needle and thread to sew elegant clothing. She only used beautiful fabric to make clothes.

Since they didn’t have a lot of money, they lived in an old shed. Water dripped in when it rained. They had broken chairs instead of a couch. But they had coal for heat, and flour from the mill for bread. Together, they trimmed the bushes to make their house look nice. Joe and Stella were poor, but not ashamed. They were happy. Sometimes in the evening, they walked downtown. They looked in store windows and dreamed. Stella wanted a hairbrush with an ivory handle. She pulled her hair upwards every day because she didn’t have a brush to make it nice. Joe wanted to fix his grandfather’s watch.

For their anniversary, Stella wanted to get Joe what he wanted. But then she did the arithmetic. It would take at least six months to save enough money. Then she had an idea. She cut off all of her hair and sold it.
Meanwhile, Joe knew that he could never fix his watch. So he polished it and sold it. He made enough to buy the brush.

On their anniversary, the door burst open. Joe was excited to give Stella his gift. But first, Stella gave him the money to fix the watch. When he saw his wife without any hair, he smiled. “I sold my watch to buy you something,” Joe said. He gave her the brush, and she laughed. They were both willing to give up something very special to make each other happy.

qs.q: Where were the houses that Joe worked on?
What did Joe do with his watch?
o: Lifted it upward to see it

qs.q: What did Stella make?
What did Stella do for Joe on their anniversary?

tr: Jo duradgor edi.
U tog'li hududlarda uylar qurardi.
Joning xotini Stella igna va ip bilan nafis kiyimlar tikardi.
U kiyim tikish uchun faqat chiroyli matodan foydalanardi.
Ularning puli ko'p bo'lmagani uchun eski shiyponda yashashardi.
Yomg'ir yog'ganda ichkariga suv tomardi.
Ularda divan o'rniga singan stullar bor edi.
Lekin isinish uchun ko'mirlari va non uchun tegirmondan kelgan unlari bor edi.
Ular uylarini chiroyli ko'rsatish uchun birga butalarni qirqishardi.
Jo va Stella kambag'al edilar, lekin bundan uyalmasdilar.
Ular baxtli edilar.
Ba'zan kechqurun ular shahar markaziga sayr qilishardi.
Ular do'kon vitrinalariga qarab, orzu qilishardi.
Stella dastasi fil suyagidan bo'lgan soch cho'tkasini xohlardi.
Sochini chiroyli qiladigan cho'tkasi bo'lmagani uchun u har kuni sochini yuqoriga tortib turmaklardi.
Jo bobosining soatini tuzatmoqchi edi.
To'y yilligiga Stella Joga u xohlagan narsani olib bermoqchi edi.
Lekin keyin u hisob-kitob qildi.
Yetarlicha pul yig'ish uchun kamida olti oy kerak bo'lardi.
Keyin uning xayoliga bir fikr keldi.
U butun sochini kesib, sotdi.
Bu orada Jo soatini hech qachon tuzata olmasligini bilardi.
Shuning uchun u uni yaltiratib, sotdi.
U cho'tka sotib olishga yetadigan pul topdi.
To'y yilligi kuni eshik birdan ochildi.
Jo Stellaga sovg'asini berishga intiqib turardi.
Lekin avval Stella unga soatni tuzatish uchun pul berdi.
Xotinini sochsiz ko'rganida u jilmaydi.
«Men senga bir narsa olish uchun soatimni sotdim», dedi Jo.
U unga cho'tkani berdi va u kulib yubordi.
Ikkalasi ham bir-birini baxtli qilish uchun juda qadrli narsasidan voz kechishga tayyor edilar.

e3|9.title: Dalton vs. the Bully
paras: Dalton was a nice boy, but sometimes the other boys made fun of him because he was so tall and skinny. Dalton’s biggest problem was Mitch. He was a bully who boasted about his strength. He quarreled with the other boys. Sometimes, if boys gave Mitch their lunch money, he would have mercy and leave them alone.
One day, the boys learned about a special Middle School Olympics. Their gym class was going to be in it. Many kids were excited. But Dalton thought it sounded like torture.

That morning, Dalton ate plenty of carbohydrates for breakfast. He entered the gym and looked at the dial on the clock. It was time to begin. The teacher asked if they were ready. Everyone nodded, except Dalton.
“I got stung by a bee. I need to see the nurse.” said Dalton. He made it up so he wouldn’t have to play.
“I don’t believe you. Get ready to play,” responded the coach.
First, they wrestled. Then they jumped, crawled and played other games. But Mitch was dominant in every event.

They strained all morning to defeat him. By lunch, they were sore. Their entire bodies ailed them. They thought about how to win. They knew the last game of the day was volleyball. Kids who used to be Dalton’s rivals became his allies. They wanted him to help them beat Mitch. Dalton was going to be Mitch’s opponent.

The game started. Every time Mitch tried to hit the ball over the net, Dalton stopped it. Finally, Mitch used all of his strength. But the ball bounced off Dalton’s hands and back into Mitch’s face! Finally Mitch was defeated.

qs.q: Which of the following was NOT part of their Olympics?
What did boys give Mitch so he would have mercy on them?
Where did the Olympics happen?
What did the boys want to do to Mitch?

tr: Dalton yaxshi bola edi, lekin u juda uzun va ozg'in bo'lgani uchun ba'zan boshqa bolalar uni masxara qilishardi.
Daltonning eng katta muammosi Mitch edi.
U kuchi bilan maqtanadigan bezori edi.
U boshqa bolalar bilan janjallashardi.
Ba'zan bolalar Mitchga tushlik pullarini berishsa, u rahm qilib, ularni tinch qo'yardi.
Bir kuni bolalar maxsus O'rta maktab Olimpiadasi haqida bilib qolishdi.
Ularning jismoniy tarbiya sinfi unda qatnashmoqchi edi.
Ko'p bolalar hayajonda edi.
Lekin Dalton bu qiynoqdek tuyuldi.
O'sha kuni ertalab Dalton nonushtaga ko'p uglevod yedi.
U sport zaliga kirib, soatning siferblatiga qaradi.
Boshlash vaqti bo'lgan edi.
O'qituvchi ular tayyormi deb so'radi.
Daltondan boshqa hamma bosh irg'adi.
«Meni ari chaqib oldi.
Hamshiraning oldiga borishim kerak», dedi Dalton.
U o'ynamaslik uchun buni to'qib chiqardi.
«Senga ishonmayman.
O'ynashga tayyorlan», deb javob berdi murabbiy.
Avval ular kurash tushishdi.
Keyin ular sakrashdi, emaklashdi va boshqa o'yinlar o'ynashdi.
Lekin Mitch har bir bellashuvda ustun edi.
Ular uni yengish uchun ertalab bo'yi zo'r berishdi.
Tushlikka kelib ularning badani og'riy boshladi.
Butun tanalari zirqirardi.
Ular qanday g'alaba qozonish haqida o'ylashdi.
Ular kunning so'nggi o'yini voleybol ekanini bilishardi.
Ilgari Daltonning raqiblari bo'lgan bolalar uning ittifoqchilariga aylanishdi.
Ular Mitchni yengishda Dalton yordam berishini xohlashardi.
Dalton Mitchning raqibi bo'ladigan bo'ldi.
O'yin boshlandi.
Mitch har safar to'pni to'r ustidan urmoqchi bo'lganda, Dalton uni to'xtatdi.
Nihoyat, Mitch butun kuchini ishlatdi.
Lekin to'p Daltonning qo'llaridan qaytib, Mitchning yuziga borib tegdi!
Nihoyat Mitch mag'lub bo'ldi.

e3|10.title: Anna the Babysitter
paras: Since her parents got a divorce, Anna has had to help her mother. In her mother’s absence, Anna takes care of Grace, the baby. At first, Anna thought it was an easy job. One afternoon, Anna played with Grace. She meowed like a cat and Grace imitated her. In fact, Grace reproduced every sound that Anna made. She took her sister outside. She put Grace in the wagon, but there was nowhere for them to go. So they went back inside.

Anna put the infant on the floor and went into her room. But when she came back, Grace had vanished! Anna looked everywhere, but she could not find her sister. Maybe the baby had been kidnapped! “Where are you?” Anna called aloud.

The situation was becoming urgent. She wanted to call her mom, but she didn’t want her to think Anna couldn’t do the job. Anna sat down. What was she going to do? But then, Anna heard something. It was coming from her room. “Grace?” She got down on her knees and looked under the bed. She could see Grace’s bald head. Grace had followed Anna into her room and crept under the bed.
“What a relief!” Anna cried.
She picked up her sister and patted her on the head. Her head was soft and had no wrinkles. Grace was sucking on her thumb and looked tired. So, Anna wrapped her in a blanket and sang rhymes for her.
Then she put Grace in bed for a nap.
After that afternoon, Anna knew that taking care of Grace wasn’t an easy job. It takes a lot of work to take care of a baby!

qs.q: What did Anna feel when she finally found Grace?
How did Grace get under the bed?
o: Anna put her there for her nap.
Anna carried her in the blanket.

qs.q: Which is NOT something Anna did with Grace?
Why did Anna wrap Grace in a blanket?
o: So she could take a nap
To keep her from sucking her thumb

tr: Ota-onasi ajrashganidan beri Anna onasiga yordam berishiga to'g'ri kelmoqda.
Onasi yo'qligida Anna chaqaloq Greysga qaraydi.
Avvaliga Anna buni oson ish deb o'yladi.
Bir kuni tushdan keyin Anna Greys bilan o'ynadi.
U mushukdek miyovladi va Greys unga taqlid qildi.
Aslida Greys Anna chiqargan har bir tovushni takrorladi.
U singlisini tashqariga olib chiqdi.
U Greysni aravachaga o'tqazdi, lekin ularning boradigan joyi yo'q edi.
Shuning uchun ular yana ichkariga kirishdi.
Anna chaqaloqni polga qo'yib, xonasiga kirdi.
Lekin u qaytib kelganida, Greys g'oyib bo'lgan edi!
Anna hamma yoqni qaradi, lekin singlisini topa olmadi.
Balki chaqaloqni o'g'irlab ketishgandir!
«Qayerdasan?» deb Anna baland ovozda chaqirdi.
Vaziyat jiddiylashib borardi.
U onasiga qo'ng'iroq qilmoqchi edi, lekin onasi uni bu ishni uddalay olmaydi deb o'ylashini xohlamadi.
Anna o'tirdi.
U nima qiladi endi?
Lekin keyin Anna nimadir eshitdi.
U uning xonasidan kelayotgan edi.
«Greys?»
U tiz cho'kib, karavot ostiga qaradi.
U Greysning taqir boshini ko'rdi.
Greys Annaning ortidan uning xonasiga kirib, karavot ostiga emaklab kirib olgan edi.
«Voy, yengil tortdim!» deb qichqirdi Anna.
U singlisini ko'tarib, boshini silab qo'ydi.
Uning boshi yumshoq va ajinsiz edi.
Greys bosh barmog'ini so'rib o'tirardi va charchaganga o'xshardi.
Shuning uchun Anna uni adyolga o'rab, unga she'rlar kuylab berdi.
Keyin u Greysni uxlashi uchun to'shakka yotqizdi.
O'sha kundan keyin Anna Greysga qarash oson ish emasligini bildi.
Chaqaloqqa qarash ko'p mehnat talab qiladi!

e3|11.title: Peter and the Dwarf
paras: Peter was a hunter. One day, he was in pursuit of a deer and became lost. He usually carried a compass with him when he went into the wilderness, but that day he left it at home.
As he walked, the forest began to look different. He didn’t see any bamboo. Instead, there were bushes with long leaves. The ecosystem was now very abnormal. Peter knew he was in the Magic Marsh.
Now he was tired and thirsty. He was afraid. Being lost in the marsh could be fatal. When people entered it, they never came out.

At last, he found a pond. Flowers grew around it. The blossoms smelled like the best perfume. He felt relaxed so he drank some water and fell asleep. When he awoke, he saw an evil dwarf staring at him.
“What are you doing here?” it asked. The dwarf spoke in a strange dialect. “I’m lost,” said Peter. “Can you help me?”
“Yes,” it said, but Peter didn’t know it was dishonest.

The dwarf took an old manuscript from his pocket. It was a magic map. “Just recite the words at the bottom,” the dwarf explained. “It will show you how to get home.” “Good,” Peter said. He was impatient and quickly grabbed the map.
He recited the magic words, and a line appeared on the map. He walked for many days but never left the marsh. Finally, the map led him back to the pond. He walked in a circle!
The dwarf was still there. “Here’s a proverb for you to think about,” it said, “When you rush, you lose your way.”

qs.q: Why was Peter in the wilderness?
o: He was in pursuit of a deer.
He was looking for the Magic Marsh.

qs.q: How did Peter know he was in the Magic Marsh?
o: There was a lot of bamboo.

qs.q: What did the dwarf have that could help Peter escape the marsh? | a. A bottle of perfume ___.
Why was Peter afraid of the Magic Marsh?
o: Being lost there could be fatal.
There was an evil dwarf in it.

tr: Piter ovchi edi.
Bir kuni u kiyikni quvib ketib, adashib qoldi.
U odatda yovvoyi tabiatga borganda yonida kompas olib yurardi, lekin o'sha kuni uni uyda qoldirgan edi.
U yurgan sari o'rmon boshqacha ko'rina boshladi.
U birorta ham bambuk ko'rmadi.
Buning o'rniga uzun bargli butalar bor edi.
Endi ekotizim juda g'ayritabiiy edi.
Piter Sehrli botqoqlikda ekanini bildi.
Endi u charchagan va chanqagan edi.
U qo'rqib ketdi.
Botqoqlikda adashib qolish halokatli bo'lishi mumkin edi.
Odamlar unga kirsa, hech qachon chiqib kelishmasdi.
Nihoyat, u bir ko'lmakni topdi.
Uning atrofida gullar o'sardi.
Gullardan eng zo'r atirdek hid kelardi.
U yengil tortib, bir oz suv ichdi va uxlab qoldi.
Uyg'onganida u o'ziga tikilib turgan yovuz pakanani ko'rdi.
«Bu yerda nima qilyapsan?» deb so'radi u.
Pakana g'alati shevada gapirardi.
«Men adashib qoldim, — dedi Piter. —
Menga yordam bera olasanmi?»
«Ha», dedi u, lekin Piter uning yolg'onchi ekanini bilmasdi.
Pakana cho'ntagidan eski qo'lyozmani oldi.
Bu sehrli xarita edi.
«Shunchaki pastdagi so'zlarni o'qib ber, — deb tushuntirdi pakana. —
U senga uyga qanday borishni ko'rsatadi».
«Yaxshi», dedi Piter.
U sabrsiz edi va xaritani tez tortib oldi.
U sehrli so'zlarni o'qidi va xaritada chiziq paydo bo'ldi.
U ko'p kun yurdi, lekin botqoqlikdan hech chiqa olmadi.
Nihoyat, xarita uni yana ko'lmak oldiga olib keldi.
U aylana bo'ylab yurgan ekan!
Pakana hali ham o'sha yerda edi.
«Mana senga o'ylab ko'rishing uchun bir maqol, — dedi u. — Shoshgan odam yo'lidan adashadi».

e3|12.title: The Ice Cream Cone Explosion
paras: One day, John walked to his uncle’s ice cream shop. When he reached the sidewalk, he caught the scent of ice cream cones and anticipated eating some ice cream. Sam opened the door. Uncle John had a new, steel machine. “What is that?” “It’s a cone maker. I built it from a kit. You take flour from the barrel and put it in this pan,” Uncle John said. “Then add water and sugar here and stir it so the sugar dissolves. Next, you fasten down the beam.” Uncle John wanted to look casual, but he was excited. He made a few swift motions and turned it on. There was a puff of smoke, and then cones came out the other end.
“Is it hard to use?” Sam asked.
“On the contrary. It’s easy to use. Want to try?”

Sam washed his hands with caution. He made a deliberate attempt to keep germs out of the dough. Soon, Sam had his first cone. He smiled in triumph! Uncle John tried to turn the machine off, but it just kept making cones. Sam and Uncle John put them on the counter, then on chairs. Before long, cones scattered all over the floor.
They tried everything to stop it, but it wouldn’t stop!
“What are we going to do?” he said.
“Kick it!” yelled Sam. Uncle John lifted his foot and gave the machine a kick. It made a funny noise and exploded. They were both covered with dough.
Uncle John laughed when he knew Sam was OK. He tossed Sam a rag to clean his face and smiled. “I guess we have enough cones now!”

qs.q: Why did Uncle John toss a rag to Sam?
What did Sam anticipate?
What did the machine do?
What did Uncle John say about the machine?

tr: Bir kuni Sem amakisi Jonning muzqaymoq do'koniga piyoda bordi.
U yo'lakka yetganida muzqaymoq vafli qadahlarining hidini sezdi va muzqaymoq yeyishni kutib qoldi.
Sem eshikni ochdi.
Jon amakining yangi, po'latdan yasalgan mashinasi bor edi.
«Bu nima?»
«Bu qadah yasaydigan mashina.
Men uni to'plamdan yig'dim.
Bochkadan un olib, mana bu idishga solasan», dedi Jon amaki.
«Keyin bu yerga suv va shakar qo'shib, shakar erishi uchun aralashtirasan.
So'ng to'sinni mahkamlab qo'yasan».
Jon amaki o'zini oddiy tutmoqchi edi, lekin u hayajonda edi.
U bir necha chaqqon harakat qilib, uni yoqdi.
Bir puf tutun chiqdi, keyin narigi tomondan qadahlar chiqa boshladi.
«Undan foydalanish qiyinmi?» deb so'radi Sem.
«Aksincha.
Undan foydalanish oson.
Sinab ko'rasanmi?»
Sem qo'llarini ehtiyotkorlik bilan yuvdi.
U xamirga mikrob tushmasligi uchun ataylab harakat qildi.
Tez orada Sem birinchi qadahini yasadi.
U g'alaba bilan jilmaydi!
Jon amaki mashinani o'chirmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin u qadah yasashda davom etaverdi.
Sem va Jon amaki ularni peshtaxtaga, keyin stullarga qo'yishdi.
Ko'p o'tmay, qadahlar butun polga sochilib ketdi.
Ular uni to'xtatish uchun hamma narsani qilib ko'rishdi, lekin u to'xtamadi!
«Endi nima qilamiz?» dedi u.
«Tepib yuboring!» deb qichqirdi Sem.
Jon amaki oyog'ini ko'tarib, mashinani tepdi.
U g'alati ovoz chiqarib, portlab ketdi.
Ikkalasi ham xamirga belanib qolishdi.
Jon amaki Semning sog'-salomat ekanini bilgach, kulib yubordi.
U Semga yuzini artishi uchun latta otdi va jilmaydi.
«Menimcha, endi qadahlarimiz yetarli!»

e3|13.title: Sheriff Dan
paras: Dan was the evil sheriff of Oceantown. Dan was as cruel as the devil. He worshipped money. Dan was a millionaire, but he paid his police officers almost nothing. The police were very bitter, but Dan didn’t care. He only cared about his money.

Every person who inhabited Oceantown disliked him. Dan enforced cruel laws. Once, Dan even put his own brother in jail for throwing a coin into a fountain! Sometimes he pointed his gun into the air and pulled the trigger. He didn’t want the bullets to hit anyone. He just wanted to scare people with the loud sound.

Finally, the people of Oceantown decided that they had to get rid of Sheriff Dan. With their understanding, the crowd sought to unify the town. They marched to Dan’s house. He was startled by the sight when he ran to the door. When he opened the door, the crowd jumped on him. They used a rope to tie him to a chair. Dan yelled, “Get your hands off of me! I’ll put you all in jail for the rest of your lives!”
The crowd didn’t listen. They carried Dan to the harbor and put him aboard a vessel. Dan was so scared that he began to sweat. He begged, “If you let me go, I will give you all my money!”

The crowd said back, “Sheriff, we don’t care about your money. We know you will never change. We’re sending you on a voyage to the middle of the ocean.” The boat drifted out of the port, and Dan was never seen again. The people voted for a new sheriff who was kind and fair.

qs.q: Where did the crowd take Dan?
At the end of the reading, Dan ___.
Why did Dan put his brother in jail?
o: He tied Dan to a chair.
He tossed a coin in a fountain.

qs.q: According to the reading, why did the crowd send Dan away?
o: The police were bitter towards Dan.
Dan was a devil to them.

tr: Den Oushentaunning yovuz sherifi edi.
Den shaytondek shafqatsiz edi.
U pulga sig'inardi.
Den millioner edi, lekin politsiyachilariga deyarli hech narsa to'lamasdi.
Politsiyachilar juda alamzada edilar, lekin Denga baribir edi.
U faqat pulini o'ylardi.
Oushentaunda yashovchi har bir odam uni yomon ko'rardi.
Den shafqatsiz qonunlarni joriy qilardi.
Bir safar Den hatto favvoraga tanga tashlagani uchun o'z akasini qamoqqa tiqqan edi!
Ba'zan u qurolini havoga qaratib, tepkini bosardi.
U o'qlar hech kimga tegishini xohlamasdi.
U shunchaki baland ovoz bilan odamlarni qo'rqitmoqchi edi.
Nihoyat, Oushentaun aholisi Sherif Dendan qutulish kerak degan qarorga kelishdi.
O'zaro hamjihatlik bilan olomon shaharni birlashtirishga intildi.
Ular Denning uyiga qarab yurishdi.
U eshikka yugurib kelganida, ko'rgan manzaradan cho'chib ketdi.
U eshikni ochganida, olomon uning ustiga tashlandi.
Ular uni arqon bilan stulga bog'lab qo'yishdi.
Den qichqirdi: «Qo'llaringizni tortinglar mendan!
Hammangizni umrbod qamoqqa tiqaman!»
Olomon quloq solmadi.
Ular Denni bandargohga olib borib, kemaga chiqarishdi.
Den shunchalik qo'rqdiki, terlay boshladi.
U yolvordi: «Agar meni qo'yib yuborsangiz, hamma pulimni beraman!»
Olomon javob berdi: «Sherif, sizning pulingiz bizga kerak emas.
Biz sizning hech qachon o'zgarmasligingizni bilamiz.
Biz sizni okean o'rtasiga sayohatga jo'natyapmiz».
Qayiq portdan suzib chiqib ketdi va Denni boshqa hech kim ko'rmadi.
Odamlar mehribon va adolatli yangi sherifga ovoz berishdi.

e3|14.title: The Helpful Apprentice
paras: There was once a small restaurant. People said that the best chef in the world worked there. But the chef was a horrible person to work for. He was impolite and scolded his workers all the time.

The chef had a young apprentice. The apprentice’s first priority was to make the best food in the world. He was happy to have a good teacher, but he didn’t like the chef. The boy was a diligent worker, but the chef scolded him more than anyone else. Then one day, the chef got great news. The emperor wanted to have dinner there that night. He was very excited. He was working very fast, and he made a mistake. He cut his hand with a knife, and it started to bleed. The apprentice gave him a bandage, but the chef still couldn’t cook.

The chef started to panic. The apprentice tried to assure him. “Everything will be OK,” he said. But the chef was still afraid. Then they started to work together. They began to bond. The chef told the apprentice what to do. The boy cooked a great meal. As soon as they finished, the emperor arrived. He wore a beautiful robe made of soft fibers. He also had a massive crown. Everyone in the restaurant kneeled when the emperor came in. The chef and the boy brought out his food. The emperor was used to luxuries. Would he like the food?
The emperor loved the food. After his departure, the chef was very proud and very thankful to his new friend, the apprentice.

qs.q: Why was the restaurant famous?
o: The best chef in the world worked there.

qs.q: Why did the chef panic before the Emperor arrived?
o: The apprentice assured him things were good.
He wanted to bond with the apprentice.
The Emperor was a horrible person.
He cut himself and couldn’t cook.

qs.q: What was the apprentice’s first priority?
o: To fill the restaurant with luxuries
To make a meal for the Emperor

qs.q: Why was the chef a bad person to work for?
o: He was the best chef in the world
He often cooked for the Emperor
He wanted everyone to be diligent.

tr: Bir paytlar kichik bir restoran bor edi.
Odamlar u yerda dunyodagi eng zo'r oshpaz ishlaydi deyishardi.
Lekin oshpazning qo'l ostida ishlash juda og'ir edi.
U qo'pol edi va ishchilarini doim urishib berardi.
Oshpazning yosh shogirdi bor edi.
Shogirdning birinchi maqsadi dunyodagi eng zo'r taomni tayyorlash edi.
U yaxshi ustozi borligidan xursand edi, lekin oshpazni yoqtirmasdi.
Bola tirishqoq ishchi edi, lekin oshpaz uni hammadan ko'ra ko'proq urishardi.
Keyin bir kuni oshpaz ajoyib xabar oldi.
Imperator o'sha kechasi u yerda kechki ovqat qilmoqchi edi.
Oshpaz juda hayajonlandi.
U juda shoshib ishlayotgan edi va xato qildi.
U pichoq bilan qo'lini kesib oldi va qon keta boshladi.
Shogird unga bint berdi, lekin oshpaz baribir ovqat pishira olmasdi.
Oshpaz vahimaga tusha boshladi.
Shogird uni tinchlantirmoqchi bo'ldi.
«Hammasi yaxshi bo'ladi», dedi u.
Lekin oshpaz hamon qo'rqardi.
Keyin ular birga ishlay boshlashdi.
Ular bir-biriga yaqinlasha boshladi.
Oshpaz shogirdga nima qilishni aytib turdi.
Bola ajoyib taom pishirdi.
Ular tugatishlari bilan imperator kelib qoldi.
U yumshoq tolalardan tikilgan chiroyli to'n kiygan edi.
Uning ulkan toji ham bor edi.
Imperator kirganida restorandagi hamma tiz cho'kdi.
Oshpaz va bola uning taomini olib chiqishdi.
Imperator hashamatga o'rganib qolgan edi.
Taom unga yoqarmikan?
Imperatorga taom juda yoqdi.
U ketgandan keyin oshpaz juda faxrlandi va yangi do'sti — shogirdiga juda minnatdor bo'ldi.

e3|15.title: Why Monkey Has No Home
paras: For five years, there was a famine. The farmers asked people to bless them and finally, they had a good harvest. Since there was now plenty of food, the pharaoh decided to have a party. The party was a happy affair. For five days they had a huge feast.
Monkey was very happy. Because of the famine, he was very slim. He wanted to eat a lot of food.
When he arrived at the feast, hundreds of long tables were filled with food. There were nuts, bowls of cereal, and ripe fruit. He could also smell hot roasted meat cooking on the stove.
The assembly of animals was merry. However, during the feast, Monkey thought of a scheme to exploit the pharaoh’s kindness. He decided to steal some of the food and then eat it at home.
All the animals were cheerful. They didn’t notice that monkey was hiding food. After the feast, Monkey took the food to his house and ate it. He repeated this routine every day for four days.

But on the fifth day, the pharaoh had a surprise. He was going to give all the animals a home. Monkey was very excited. But when he arrived at the pharaoh’s home, he could not get through the door. The diameter of his waist was wider than the doorway. He was too fat!
Monkey asked the pharaoh to forgive him for his theft. But the pharaoh said no. “Pardon?” asked the monkey. He didn’t understand why the pharaoh was being unkind.
“Everybody else will have a home now, but not you. Now you know that greed gets you nothing,” explained the pharaoh.

qs.q: The pharaoh gave a party for all the animals because ___.
o: he wanted to exploit the animals

qs.q: What did Monkey do with the food?
o: He hid it under the table.
He took it to his house.
He gave it to the pharaoh.
He cooked it in the stove.

qs.q: The tables were full of all of the following EXCEPT ___.
What stopped Monkey from entering the party on the fifth day?

tr: Besh yil davomida ocharchilik bo'ldi.
Dehqonlar odamlardan ular uchun duo qilishni so'rashdi va nihoyat yaxshi hosil olishdi.
Endi ovqat mo'l bo'lgani uchun fir'avn bazm o'tkazishga qaror qildi.
Bazm quvonchli tadbir bo'ldi.
Besh kun davomida ular katta ziyofat qilishdi.
Maymun juda xursand edi.
Ocharchilik tufayli u juda ozib ketgan edi.
U ko'p ovqat yemoqchi edi.
U ziyofatga kelganida, yuzlab uzun stollar ovqatga to'la edi.
U yerda yong'oqlar, kosa-kosa yorma va pishgan mevalar bor edi.
U pechkada pishayotgan issiq qovurilgan go'shtning hidini ham sezdi.
Hayvonlar yig'ini xushchaqchaq edi.
Biroq ziyofat paytida Maymun fir'avnning mehribonligidan foydalanish uchun hiyla o'ylab topdi.
U ovqatning bir qismini o'g'irlab, uyda yeyishga qaror qildi.
Hamma hayvonlar quvnoq edi.
Ular maymunning ovqat yashirayotganini payqashmadi.
Ziyofatdan keyin Maymun ovqatni uyiga olib borib yedi.
U to'rt kun davomida har kuni shunday qildi.
Lekin beshinchi kuni fir'avnning bir syurprizi bor edi.
U barcha hayvonlarga uy bermoqchi edi.
Maymun juda hayajonlandi.
Lekin u fir'avnning uyiga kelganida, eshikdan o'ta olmadi.
Uning belining aylanasi eshik o'rnidan kengroq edi.
U juda semirib ketgan edi!
Maymun fir'avndan o'g'rilik qilgani uchun uni kechirishni so'radi.
Lekin fir'avn yo'q dedi.
«Nima dedingiz?» deb so'radi maymun.
U fir'avn nega shafqatsizlik qilayotganini tushunmadi.
«Endi hammaning uyi bo'ladi, lekin seniki emas.
Endi ochko'zlik hech narsa bermasligini bilding», deb tushuntirdi fir'avn.

e3|16.title: Matthew Learns a Lesson
paras: Matthew was a sensible boy. He always kept his room tidy and had a natural literary aptitude. One day, he hoped to have a career in journalism. The adolescent spent much of his time reading and liked having privacy. But his quiet personality hindered his ability to make friends.
One day, Matthew went to the pharmacy to pick up some pills for his grandmother. He saw some boys leaning against a pole outside. One of the boys complimented Matthew. “I like your jacket.”
Another boy asked, “Do you want to go to Nate’s Restaurant?”
“Sure!” Matthew said.

The boys walked to the restaurant. They were going to have slices of pizza. They ordered their food and drank soda with straws. They ate until their bellies swelled up. Matthew was having so much fun.
One of the boys said, “Let’s leave without paying.”
Suddenly, the waiter yelled, “Stop!” The two other boys ran, leaving Matthew there alone.

Soon, the police arrived. “Leaving without paying for your meal is the same as stealing,” said the police officer. “The restaurant wants justice. So next week you have to go to court and let a jury decide your punishment.”
When he went to court, the judge asked, “Do you have anything to say, Matthew?” He said, “I feel sorrow for what I’ve done. Now I know that real friends won’t ask you to do something illegal.”
The jury then let him have his liberty. But they made Matthew pick up trash as punishment.
Much to Matthew’s surprise, he ended up meeting some new friends.

qs.q: Why was Matthew at the pharmacy?
Which of the following is NOT a word used to describe Matthew?
Why did Matthew try to leave the restaurant without paying for his meal?
o: He presumed his friends would like him.

qs.q: Why did Matthew get to keep his liberty at the end of the story?
o: He persuaded the jury he had learned his lesson.
He picked up trash as a punishment
He hindered the jury from making a decision.

tr: Metyu aqlli bola edi.
U xonasini doim ozoda tutardi va tabiatan adabiyotga qobiliyatli edi.
U qachondir jurnalistikada ishlashni orzu qilardi.
O'smir vaqtining ko'p qismini kitob o'qib o'tkazardi va yolg'iz qolishni yoqtirardi.
Lekin uning kamgap fe'li do'st orttirishiga xalal berardi.
Bir kuni Metyu buvisi uchun dori olish maqsadida dorixonaga bordi.
U tashqarida ustunga suyanib turgan bir nechta bolani ko'rdi.
Bolalardan biri Metyuni maqtadi.
«Kurtkang menga yoqdi».
Boshqa bir bola so'radi: «Neytning restoraniga borishni xohlaysanmi?»
«Albatta!» dedi Metyu.
Bolalar restoranga piyoda borishdi.
Ular bir necha bo'lak pitstsa yemoqchi edilar.
Ular ovqat buyurtma qilishdi va somonchalar bilan gazli suv ichishdi.
Ular qorinlari shishib ketguncha yeyishdi.
Metyu juda maza qilayotgan edi.
Bolalardan biri dedi: «Keling, pul to'lamasdan ketamiz».
To'satdan ofitsiant qichqirdi: «To'xtanglar!»
Qolgan ikki bola qochib ketishdi va Metyuni yolg'iz qoldirishdi.
Tez orada politsiya yetib keldi.
«Ovqat uchun pul to'lamasdan ketish o'g'rilik bilan barobar», dedi politsiyachi.
«Restoran adolat talab qilmoqda.
Shuning uchun keyingi hafta sudga borib, jazoingni hakamlar hay'ati hal qilishiga yo'l qo'yishing kerak».
U sudga borganida, sudya so'radi: «Aytadigan gaping bormi, Metyu?» U dedi: «Qilgan ishimdan qayg'uryapman.
Endi bilaman, haqiqiy do'stlar seni noqonuniy ish qilishga undamaydi».
