Shundan so'ng hakamlar hay'ati uni ozod qildi.
Lekin ular Metyuga jazo sifatida axlat terishni buyurishdi.
Metyuni hayratga solib, u yerda bir nechta yangi do'st orttirdi.

e3|17.title: The Magic Cup
paras: Paul and John were brothers. They fought all the time because they both wanted to be leaders of the agency they both worked at.

There was a superstition in their town about a magic cup. People said the cup was in a volcano located far away. Anyone who retrieved the cup would have their wish come true. John and Paul both wanted to find it. Then they could become the leader. They both left to find the cup. Before their trip, their mother said they should work together. They dismissed that idea. Even though their trips originated from the same house, each wanted to travel alone.

They were both miserable during the trip. They had to navigate small boats across shallow rivers and climb difficult slopes. Their journey spanned many days. When they finally got close to the volcano, the ground began to vibrate and the volcano erupted. Ash filled the sky and lava covered everything. John climbed to the top of a hill to keep from getting burned. A few moments later, his brother went up the same hill. They were confined to the hill until the lava cooled down.
They talked about the things they had seen while wandering around the country. They felt more sympathy and affection for each other than ever before. They decided that fate had brought them together.

The next day they left to finish the remainder of the trip together. Everything seemed much easier. When they finally found the cup, they learned that it didn’t make wishes come true. It was only an ordinary cup. But the trip to reach the cup taught them to work together and love each other.

qs.q: Why didn’t the boys travel together?
o: Their trips originated from different places.
They had to navigate boats across shallow rivers.

qs.q: Why were the boys always fighting?
o: They had very little food to eat.
There was a hole beneath the tree.
They both wanted to be leaders of the agency.

qs.q: Why did fate bring the boys together?
o: To show that stories about the tree weren’t true
So they could complete the remainder of the trip together
So they could return home together
So their trip could span many days

qs.q: What was surprising about the cup?
o: It was only an ordinary cup.
It had their names written on it.

tr: Pol va Jon aka-uka edilar.
Ular doim janjallashishardi, chunki ikkalasi ham o'zlari ishlaydigan agentlikning rahbari bo'lishni xohlashardi.
Ularning shahrida sehrli kosa haqida bir xurofot bor edi.
Odamlar kosa uzoqdagi bir vulqonda deyishardi.
Kim kosani olib kelsa, uning orzusi ushalarkan.
Jon ham, Pol ham uni topishni xohlashdi.
Shunda ular rahbar bo'la olishardi.
Ikkalasi ham kosani topish uchun yo'lga chiqishdi.
Safardan oldin onasi ular birga harakat qilishlari kerakligini aytdi.
Ular bu fikrni rad etishdi.
Ularning safari bir uydan boshlangan bo'lsa ham, har biri yolg'iz sayohat qilishni xohladi.
Safar davomida ikkalasi ham juda qiynalishdi.
Ular kichik qayiqlarda sayoz daryolardan suzib o'tishlari va qiyin qiyaliklarga chiqishlari kerak edi.
Ularning sayohati ko'p kunga cho'zildi.
Nihoyat vulqonga yaqinlashganlarida yer titray boshladi va vulqon otildi.
Osmonni kul qopladi va lava hamma narsani bosib ketdi.
Jon kuyib qolmaslik uchun tepalik cho'qqisiga chiqib oldi.
Bir necha daqiqadan keyin akasi ham o'sha tepalikka chiqdi.
Lava sovumaguncha ular tepalikda qamalib qolishdi.
Ular mamlakat bo'ylab kezib yurganlarida ko'rgan narsalari haqida gaplashishdi.
Ular bir-birlariga avvalgidan ko'ra ko'proq hamdardlik va mehr his qilishdi.
Ular taqdir ularni birlashtirdi degan qarorga kelishdi.
Ertasi kuni ular safarning qolgan qismini birga yakunlash uchun yo'lga chiqishdi.
Hamma narsa ancha osonroq tuyuldi.
Nihoyat kosani topishganda, u orzularni ushaltirmasligini bilishdi.
Bu shunchaki oddiy kosa edi.
Lekin kosaga yetib borish safari ularni birga ishlashga va bir-birini sevishga o'rgatdi.

e3|18.title: The Knight’s Plan
paras: A town was fighting for their independence from another country. Several rebels started a revolution. However, they were afraid of an invasion from a lot of troops. They didn’t have enough warriors to stop them, so they asked a knight for help. The knight made a plan. A tall mountain was outside the town. The road near the top was very narrow. Cliffs rose on both sides of it.
“We must trick the enemy. They have to follow us up the mountain,” the knight explained. “On the narrow path, only a few can attack us at one time.” The people agreed with the knight’s plan.
The knight put on his armor, and the warriors got their spears. When the enemy attacked, the knight and warriors acted as if they were afraid. They quickly withdrew toward the mountain.
The enemy troops followed them up the steep path. Soon, the enemy became tired.

At the summit, the knight and his troops stopped. The enemy was close behind them. But now they were tired. Also, only a few could attack because the path was narrow. The knight and the warriors fought the enemy. But there were too many troops.
The knight was afraid. If the warriors yielded the path to the enemy, the town would be lost.

A storm suddenly came over the mountain. There was strong wind and rain. Thunder boomed. Lightning struck some trees near the enemy. The trees blazed. The flames scared the enemy and they retreated. They ran down the mountain, out of the town, and never returned.
The knight explained, “With a little luck, a good plan beats even a big army.”

qs.q: Why was the narrow path important to the knight’s plan?
o: Few soldiers could attack from it.
It led to a high cliff.
It was a safe place to hide.
The enemy troops were afraid of it.

qs.q: After they withdrew to the mountain, where did the knight and warriors stop?
Why didn’t the enemy think there was a trap?
o: They thought the soldiers were scared

qs.q: All of the following happened after the storm came EXCEPT ___.

tr: Bir shahar boshqa bir davlatdan mustaqillik uchun kurashayotgan edi.
Bir nechta isyonchi inqilob boshladi.
Biroq ular ko'plab qo'shinlarning bostirib kirishidan qo'rqishardi.
Ularni to'xtatish uchun jangchilari yetarli emasdi, shuning uchun ular bir ritsardan yordam so'rashdi.
Ritsar reja tuzdi.
Shahar tashqarisida baland tog' bor edi.
Cho'qqiga yaqin yo'l juda tor edi.
Uning ikki tomonida qoyalar ko'tarilib turardi.
«Biz dushmanni aldashimiz kerak.
Ular bizning ortimizdan tog'ga chiqishlari kerak, — deb tushuntirdi ritsar. —
Tor yo'lda bir vaqtning o'zida faqat bir nechtasi bizga hujum qila oladi». Odamlar ritsarning rejasiga rozi bo'lishdi.
Ritsar sovutini kiydi, jangchilar esa nayzalarini olishdi.
Dushman hujum qilganida, ritsar va jangchilar o'zlarini qo'rqqandek ko'rsatishdi.
Ular tezda tog' tomon chekinishdi.
Dushman qo'shinlari ularning ortidan tik yo'ldan yuqoriga chiqishdi.
Tez orada dushman charchab qoldi.
Cho'qqida ritsar va uning qo'shinlari to'xtashdi.
Dushman ularning ortidan yaqin kelayotgan edi.
Lekin endi ular charchagan edilar.
Bundan tashqari, yo'l tor bo'lgani uchun faqat bir nechtasi hujum qila olardi.
Ritsar va jangchilar dushman bilan jang qilishdi.
Lekin qo'shinlar juda ko'p edi.
Ritsar qo'rqib ketdi.
Agar jangchilar yo'lni dushmanga bo'shatib berishsa, shahar qo'ldan ketardi.
To'satdan tog' ustiga bo'ron keldi.
Kuchli shamol esib, yomg'ir yog'di.
Momaqaldiroq gumburladi.
Chaqmoq dushman yaqinidagi bir nechta daraxtga urildi.
Daraxtlar lovullab yonib ketdi.
Alanga dushmanni qo'rqitdi va ular chekinishdi.
Ular tog'dan pastga, shahar tashqarisiga qochib ketishdi va boshqa hech qachon qaytishmadi.
Ritsar tushuntirdi: «Ozgina omad bo'lsa, yaxshi reja hatto katta qo'shinni ham yengadi».

e3|19.title: The Magic Pear Tree
paras: It was a cool morning, and the grass was covered in mist. The market was full of people. A mean farmer named Jack yelled, “Pears for sale!” He sat on a bench, plotting how he could trick people. Then an orphan came to his cart. “Can you spare a pear?” she asked.
Jack felt rage. He replied, “You don’t have any money!” “Please, I haven’t had supper in days.”
“No!” shouted the farmer.
The orphan sighed. However, a pregnant lady heard the dispute and confronted Jack. “Just give her a pear,” she said. Jack had no shame and said no. Finally, a man bought a pear for the girl.
The girl quickly ate it, but she saved the seed. She wanted to get revenge.
She told Jack, “I know a way to get hundreds of pears in one day. I’ll show you how.”

He watched the girl dig a hole. She dropped the seed into the ground. Then she spread the dirt over it. “Watch closely,” she said. “In a few minutes, a stem will grow. It’ll turn into a tree that’s full of pears!”
Jack stared at the dirt, but nothing happened. The only objects there were a few daisies. He looked for the girl, but she had snuck away.
Then he looked at his cart in horror. It was empty!
He suddenly realized that the orphan had tricked him.

While Jack was waiting for the tree to grow, the people had taken the pears from his cart. They all laughed while they were eating the tender fruit. The farmer felt ashamed. The incident taught him to be kinder.

qs.q: What object did the girl keep after she ate the pear?
What was the dispute between the orphan and the farmer about?
o: The girl wanted a spare pear.
The farmer felt rage about the girl
The girl sat on his bench.
The farmer’s pears were too expensive.

qs.q: What did the girl do immediately after she put the seed in the ground?
o: She asked the farmer to watch closely.
She spread the dirt over it.

qs.q: What happened to the farmer’s pears at the end of the story?
o: They were stolen by the crowd.
They were taken by the girl.

tr: Salqin tong edi va o'tlarni tuman qoplagan edi.
Bozor odamlarga to'la edi.
Jek ismli bir yovuz fermer: «Nok sotiladi!» deb qichqirardi.
U skameykada o'tirib, odamlarni qanday aldash haqida reja tuzardi.
Keyin uning aravasi oldiga bir yetim qiz keldi.
«Bitta nok bera olasizmi?» deb so'radi u.
Jekning g'azabi qo'zidi.
U javob berdi: «Sening pulingning o'zi yo'q-ku!»
«Iltimos, bir necha kundan beri kechki ovqat yemadim».
«Yo'q!» deb qichqirdi fermer.
Yetim qiz xo'rsindi.
Biroq homilador bir ayol bahsni eshitib, Jekka qarshi chiqdi.
«Unga bitta nok bering-da», dedi u.
Jek uyalmay, yo'q dedi.
Nihoyat, bir odam qizga nok sotib oldi.
Qiz uni tezda yedi, lekin urug'ini saqlab qoldi.
U o'ch olmoqchi edi.
U Jekka dedi: «Men bir kunda yuzlab nok olishning yo'lini bilaman.
Qanday qilishni sizga ko'rsataman».
U qizning chuqur kovlayotganini kuzatdi.
Qiz urug'ni yerga tashladi.
Keyin uning ustiga tuproq sepdi.
«Diqqat bilan qarang, — dedi u. —
Bir necha daqiqada poya o'sib chiqadi.
U nokka to'la daraxtga aylanadi!»
Jek tuproqqa tikilib turdi, lekin hech narsa bo'lmadi.
U yerdagi narsalar faqat bir nechta moychechak edi.
U qizni qidirdi, lekin qiz sekin ketib qolgan edi.
Keyin u dahshat bilan aravasiga qaradi.
U bo'm-bo'sh edi!
U birdan yetim qiz uni aldaganini angladi.
Jek daraxt o'sishini kutayotganda, odamlar uning aravasidan noklarni olib ketishgan edi.
Ular yumshoq mevani yeb, hammalari kulishardi.
Fermer uyalib ketdi.
Bu voqea unga mehribonroq bo'lishni o'rgatdi.

e3|20.title: Little Wolf and Mother Wolf
paras: Mother Wolf was a magnificent animal. She had all the traits of a terrific hunter. She was very strong and fast. She knew how to hide and how to seize prey. Mother Wolf was the forest’s supreme creature. Her skills were evident to all the other animals. Mother Wolf lived in a den beneath a tree with her cub, Little Wolf. At dawn, Little Wolf and Mother Wolf were eating breakfast. Little Wolf looked sad. Mother Wolf said, “What is wrong, my cub?”
Little Wolf said, “I want to be big like you. You can run and leap better than anyone. You can howl so loudly. Being big is a necessity, and I am so small.”
Mother Wolf said, “Don’t be dissatisfied with your size. Being small can be very useful.”

Just then, rain and hail began to fall. The tree was hit by lightning. It fell on the wolves’ den. Little Wolf was scared. The wolves knew that escaping the den was vital. Mother Wolf said, “Little Wolf, I can not move the heavy pile of branches. But you can escape with ease. You can get out and find help!”

Little Wolf crawled out of the den and called all the large animals for help. They went to the den and pulled away the branches. Mother Wolf came out and said, “Thank you Little Wolf! You saved my life!” She softly squeezed Little Wolf and kissed her. Little Wolf smiled. She said, “Mother, this outcome has taught me a profound lesson. Even though I’m small, I’m still important.”

qs.q: Which is NOT a trait of a terrific hunter like Mother Wolf?
Little Wolf was scared because ___.
o: a hunter came to the den
a tree fell on the den

qs.q: Why did Little Wolf feel sad?
o: She could leap like her mother.
She wanted to howl at the animals
She was dissatisfied with her mother

qs.q: According to the reading, why did Mother Wolf squeeze her cub?

tr: Ona Bo'ri ajoyib hayvon edi.
Unda zo'r ovchining barcha xislatlari bor edi.
U juda kuchli va tez edi.
U qanday yashirinishni va o'ljani qanday tutib olishni bilardi.
Ona Bo'ri o'rmondagi eng oliy maxluq edi.
Uning mahorati boshqa barcha hayvonlarga ayon edi.
Ona Bo'ri bolasi Kichik Bo'ri bilan daraxt ostidagi uyada yashardi.
Tong otganda Kichik Bo'ri va Ona Bo'ri nonushta qilishayotgan edi.
Kichik Bo'ri g'amgin ko'rinardi.
Ona Bo'ri dedi: «Nima bo'ldi, bolajonim?»
Kichik Bo'ri dedi: «Men ham sizdek katta bo'lishni xohlayman.
Siz hammadan yaxshi yugurasiz va sakraysiz.
Siz juda baland uvillay olasiz.
Katta bo'lish zarur, men esa juda kichkinaman».
Ona Bo'ri dedi: «O'lchamingdan norozi bo'lma.
Kichkina bo'lish juda foydali bo'lishi mumkin».
Aynan shu payt yomg'ir va do'l yog'a boshladi.
Daraxtga chaqmoq urdi.
U bo'rilarning uyasi ustiga qulab tushdi.
Kichik Bo'ri qo'rqib ketdi.
Bo'rilar uyadan chiqib ketish hayotiy muhim ekanini bilishardi.
Ona Bo'ri dedi: «Kichik Bo'ri, men og'ir shoxlar uyumini qimirlata olmayman.
Lekin sen osonlikcha chiqib keta olasan.
Chiqib, yordam topib kel!»
Kichik Bo'ri uyadan emaklab chiqdi va barcha katta hayvonlarni yordamga chaqirdi.
Ular uyaga borib, shoxlarni tortib olishdi.
Ona Bo'ri chiqib, dedi: «Rahmat, Kichik Bo'ri!
Sen mening hayotimni saqlab qolding!»
U Kichik Bo'rini mehr bilan quchoqlab, o'pdi.
Kichik Bo'ri jilmaydi.
U dedi: «Ona, bu voqea menga chuqur saboq berdi.
Garchi kichkina bo'lsam ham, men baribir muhimman».

e3|21.title: The Old Man with a Bump
paras: An old man had a large bump on his face. He went to the best physician in town. He gave the old man tragic news: “I can’t do anything. You’ll have to get accustomed to it.” One day, the old man went into the forest. Suddenly, the light became dim. It was going to rain. So he found a hollow tree to sit under. It leaked a little, but there was no other place he could wait.

When the rain stopped, his joints felt stiff from sitting. Suddenly, he heard a tune coming from far away. Many fables said monsters lived in the forest. No one could affirm that the stories were true, though. Still, his instincts told him that there was something out there. He walked farther into the forest. Then he saw a fire glowing. He was astonished to see a clan of monsters. They were having a great feast and banging on drums.
He stood behind a tree, spying on them. Then the leader asked, “Who’s the best dancer here?”

“Me!” the man yelled, coming from behind the tree. He started to dance. When he was finished, the leader said, “I want you to dance every night. In order to make sure you return, I’m going to keep something you love.”
“Please don’t take my bump,” he begged. “I can’t sacrifice it. It’s good luck!” He exclaimed, pointing at it for emphasis.

The monsters agreed that they had to take his bump. After they did, the man stroked his face to make sure it was gone. He had tricked them! He never went back, and he never had to worry about his bump again.

qs.q: What advice did the doctor give the old man?
Why did the man have to wait inside a hollow tree?
Why did the old man come out from behind the tree?
Why does the old man stroke his face at the end of the story?
o: To make sure the bump is gone
To affirm that the bump is there

tr: Bir cholning yuzida katta g'urra bor edi.
U shahardagi eng zo'r shifokorning oldiga bordi.
Shifokor cholga achchiq xabarni aytdi: «Men hech narsa qila olmayman.
Unga ko'nikishingizga to'g'ri keladi».
Bir kuni chol o'rmonga bordi.
To'satdan yorug'lik xiralashdi.
Yomg'ir yog'adigan bo'ldi.
Shuning uchun u ostida o'tirish uchun ichi kovak daraxt topdi.
Undan biroz suv o'tardi, lekin kutish uchun boshqa joy yo'q edi.
Yomg'ir to'xtaganda, o'tiraverganidan bo'g'imlari qotib qolgan edi.
To'satdan u uzoqdan kelayotgan kuyni eshitdi.
Ko'p ertaklarda o'rmonda maxluqlar yashaydi deyilardi.
Lekin hech kim bu hikoyalarning rost ekanini tasdiqlay olmasdi.
Shunday bo'lsa-da, sezgilari unga u yerda nimadir borligini aytardi.
U o'rmonning ichkarisiga qarab yurdi.
Keyin u yonib turgan gulxanni ko'rdi.
U bir to'da maxluqni ko'rib hayratda qoldi.
Ular katta ziyofat qilib, nog'ora chalishayotgan edi.
U daraxt ortida turib, ularni kuzatdi.
Keyin boshliq so'radi: «Bu yerda eng zo'r raqqos kim?»
«Men!» deb qichqirdi chol daraxt ortidan chiqib.
U raqs tusha boshladi.
U tugatganida, boshliq dedi: «Har kecha raqs tushishingni xohlayman.
Qaytib kelishingga ishonch hosil qilish uchun sen yaxshi ko'radigan bir narsani o'zimda olib qolaman».
«Iltimos, g'urramni olmang», deb yolvordi u.
«Men undan voz kecha olmayman.
U omad keltiradi!» deb qichqirdi u, ta'kidlash uchun unga barmog'ini nuqib.
Maxluqlar uning g'urrasini olish kerak degan qarorga kelishdi.
Ular olib bo'lgach, chol g'urra yo'qolganiga ishonch hosil qilish uchun yuzini siladi.
U ularni aldagan edi!
U boshqa hech qachon qaytib bormadi va g'urrasi haqida boshqa hech qachon tashvishlanmadi.

e3|22.title: The Circus
paras: Ben was unhappy. He lived on a ranch near a small town, and he didn’t have many friends. Then one day a messenger came to the ranch. He showed the headline in the town newspaper. The circus was coming to the town. It even coincided with Ben’s birthday!
Ben was very excited as his father steered the car through the town. The circus couldn’t accommodate all the people who wanted to see the show, but Ben had a ticket.

Ben peered at the activity around him. He watched people of both genders dance all around. They wore funny costumes, and their hair was dyed many different colors. Also, tame tigers with stripes on their fur did tricks. Outside, people could commission an informal portrait. They posed in front of a funny picture while an artist quickly drew them. Ben couldn’t believe it. He was happier than he had ever been before.

That day, Ben knew what he wanted to do. He loved the circus to such an extent that he wanted to have his own circus when he grew older. Seeing the circus was like a dose of medicine for him. He wasn’t unhappy anymore. He felt special. He inquired about what he needed to do to have his own circus. He studied hard and learned about business.

Ben worked very hard, and one day, he had his own circus. It was a great circus. People told him that he could be very rich. But he wasn’t tempted by money. He just wanted to make children happy. He knew the circus had changed his life, and he wanted to do the same thing for others.

qs.q: Why did Ben like the circus to such an extent?
o: He inquired about getting his own circus
He took a dose of special medicine.

qs.q: What good news did the messenger bring?
What did Ben’s dad do on his birthday?
o: He taught Ben how to drive.
He steered around town looking for the circus

qs.q: Why wasn’t Ben tempted by money?
o: He wanted other kids to like him.
He only wanted to make people happy.

tr: Ben baxtsiz edi.
U kichik shahar yaqinidagi rancho'da yashardi va uning do'stlari ko'p emasdi.
Keyin bir kuni ranchoga bir xabarchi keldi.
U shahar gazetasidagi sarlavhani ko'rsatdi.
Shaharga sirk kelayotgan edi.
U hatto Benning tug'ilgan kuniga to'g'ri kelardi!
Otasi mashinani shahar bo'ylab haydab borarkan, Ben juda hayajonda edi.
Sirk tomoshani ko'rmoqchi bo'lgan hamma odamni sig'dira olmasdi, lekin Benning chiptasi bor edi.
Ben atrofidagi harakatlarga tikilib qaradi.
U har ikki jinsdagi odamlarning har tomonda raqs tushayotganini tomosha qildi.
Ular kulgili liboslar kiyishgan va sochlari turli ranglarga bo'yalgan edi.
Bundan tashqari, terisi yo'l-yo'l qo'lga o'rgatilgan yo'lbarslar fokuslar ko'rsatardi.
Tashqarida odamlar oddiy portret buyurtma qilishlari mumkin edi.
Ular kulgili rasm oldida turishardi, rassom esa ularni tezda chizib berardi.
Ben bunga ishonolmadi.
U hech qachon bunchalik baxtli bo'lmagan edi.
O'sha kuni Ben nima qilishni xohlashini bildi.
U sirkni shunchalik yaxshi ko'rib qoldiki, katta bo'lganida o'z sirkiga ega bo'lishni xohladi.
Sirkni ko'rish u uchun bir doza doridek edi.
U endi baxtsiz emasdi.
U o'zini alohida his qildi.
U o'z sirkiga ega bo'lish uchun nima qilish kerakligini so'rab-surishtirdi.
U qattiq o'qidi va biznesni o'rgandi.
Ben juda qattiq mehnat qildi va bir kuni o'z sirkiga ega bo'ldi.
Bu ajoyib sirk edi.
Odamlar unga juda boy bo'lishi mumkinligini aytishardi.
Lekin pul uni vasvasaga solmadi.
U faqat bolalarni xursand qilishni xohlardi.
U sirk uning hayotini o'zgartirganini bilardi va boshqalar uchun ham shunday qilishni xohladi.

e3|23.title: Lazy Hans
paras: Hans was lazy. He seldom helped his mother with anything. He didn’t cook and he never mowed the lawn. He didn’t even shave! He spent the daytime gambling with his mother’s money. One day, his mother realized that her money was gone from her purse. “You’re banned from my house!” she shouted. “Don’t come back until you’ve learned your lesson!”
Hans went to live in the forest like an outlaw. But it was cold, and Hans couldn’t find food. He went to a cottage to ask for a meal.
An Aborigine answered the door. “Can I stay here please?” Hans asked.
“You can stay if you work,” the man replied.
Hans liked the prospect of food and warmth, so he agreed.
The man pointed to a field. “Take this rod and plant it over there. I am a wizard, and this magic rod will bring us food.”
The field was far away. Hans knew it would be hard to walk there. So he just threw the rod behind the cottage and sat by the river. When daylight faded, he returned to the cottage and went to sleep.
The next morning, the old man looked very fierce. “You didn’t take the rod to the field!” he shouted.
“No,” confessed Hans, “it was too far!”
“Because of you we have nothing to eat!” replied the man.
Hans was terrified that the man would punish him.
So he ran home. “Mama!” he cried, “I’m desperate to come back!” His mother was cautious.
“Do you promise to work?” she asked.
“Yes!” said Hans, “I’ll never be lazy again!”

qs.q: At the beginning of the story, what did Hans do during the daytime?
Why did Hans’s mother ban him from her house?
o: He didn’t listen to the wizard.

qs.q: What did Hans confess to doing?
o: Throwing the rod behind the cottage

qs.q: How did Hans’s mother feel when Hans returned home?

tr: Hans dangasa edi.
U onasiga kamdan-kam yordam berardi.
U ovqat pishirmasdi va hech qachon maysa o'rmasdi.
U hatto soqolini ham olmasdi!
U kunduzlari onasining puliga qimor o'ynardi.
Bir kuni onasi hamyonidagi puli yo'qolganini payqadi.
«Uyimga kirishing taqiqlanadi! — deb qichqirdi u. —
Saboq olmaguningcha qaytib kelma!»
Hans qonundan tashqari odamdek o'rmonda yashashga ketdi.
Lekin u yer sovuq edi va Hans ovqat topa olmadi.
U ovqat so'rash uchun bir kulbaga bordi.
Eshikni bir tub aholi vakili ochdi.
«Iltimos, shu yerda qolsam bo'ladimi?» deb so'radi Hans.
«Ishlasang, qolishing mumkin», deb javob berdi odam.
Hansga ovqat va issiqlik istiqboli yoqdi, shuning uchun u rozi bo'ldi.
Odam bir dalani ko'rsatdi.
«Mana bu tayoqni olib, o'sha yerga ek.
Men sehrgarman va bu sehrli tayoq bizga ovqat keltiradi».
Dala uzoqda edi.
Hans u yerga piyoda borish qiyin bo'lishini bilardi.
Shuning uchun u tayoqni shunchaki kulba orqasiga uloqtirib, daryo bo'yida o'tirdi.
Kun yorug'i so'nganida u kulbaga qaytib, uxlashga yotdi.
Ertasi kuni ertalab chol juda g'azabnok ko'rinardi.
«Sen tayoqni dalaga olib bormading!» deb qichqirdi u.
«Yo'q, — deb tan oldi Hans, — u juda uzoq edi!»
«Sen tufayli yeydigan hech narsamiz yo'q!» deb javob berdi odam.
Hans odam uni jazolashidan dahshatga tushdi.
Shuning uchun u uyiga yugurib ketdi.
«Onajon! — deb yig'ladi u. — Qaytib kelishni juda-juda xohlayman!»
Onasi ehtiyotkorlik qildi.
«Ishlashga va'da berasanmi?» deb so'radi u.
«Ha! — dedi Hans. — Boshqa hech qachon dangasalik qilmayman!»

e3|24.title: The Bremen Town Musicians
paras: Larry the cow, Harry the rooster and Lester the duck lived on a widow’s farm. They dreamed of playing music in a parade.
One day, the widow went to the lawn where her herd of cattle was grazing. “I’ll eat him tomorrow,” she said, pointing to Larry.
Larry wanted to flee, but he didn’t have the nerve to go by himself. Then his friends Lester and Harry showed him a poster.
“It’s for a parade in Bremen. We’ll go with you, and we can perform our symphony there,” Lester said.

The animals put together a small bundle that held a drum, a flute and a portable microphone. Then they took their baggage and initiated their long journey. They walked down a paved lane all day. That night, they looked in the window of a house. They saw a group of thieves. They were eating a large dinner and telling stories about their greed and the people they stole from.
Lester was an optimist. He said, “I think we can scare them away!”

Soon, the animals came up with a plan. Harry flew inside and knocked over the lamp. “What was that?” screamed a thief as the bulb broke. They could barely see now. Then Larry stood on two feet, and Lester flew to the top of his head. They looked very big. All three of the animals made scary noises. The thieves tried to hit the animals. But Harry flew over them and scratched them.
“It’s a phantom!” yelled one thief.
The thieves ran away. The animals ate and rested. The next morning, Larry said, “Why go to Bremen? We can stay here and make music!” And so they remained there and made music together.

qs.q: Where did the cattle graze at the beginning of the story?
How did Larry, Harry and Lester find out about the parade?
What were the greedy thieves doing when the animals arrived at the house?
o: Planning to steal from the widow

e3|25.title: How Did Greenland Get Its Name?
paras: The nation of Greenland isn’t very green. The sun’s rays don’t shine there for three whole months. As a result, it’s covered with snow, ice and frost. Then how was the name derived? It started with a Viking named Erik the Red. Erik had many merits. However, there was an underlying problem... he got angry easily. People were scared of him. However, he was married to the niece of a very powerful man. So everybody tried to be nice to him.
One day, Erik fought with his neighbor and killed him. His consequent punishment was to leave Iceland.
Many stories circulated about a land west of Iceland. But only a fraction of the people in Iceland believed them. Still, Erik wanted to find it.

Erik sailed toward the land via the Atlantic Ocean. His marine knowledge was good, but the trip was hard. Some of his men drowned. Erik’s lieutenant wanted to resign from his position. Others thought about committing suicide.
Suddenly, Erik thought he saw something.
“I don’t believe it,” said Erik. “It must be an illusion.” But it was no trick—it was the new land!

Erik trembled in the cold polar air. He saw that there was ice everywhere. He realized that the ice could keep enemies out. Not even the best navy could invade the new land. He could start a new dynasty in his name. But how could he convince people to live here?
“I’ll call it ‘Greenland,’” he said. Erik’s plan worked. Within two years, over a thousand people moved to Greenland. In the end, Greenland got its name all because of a trick.

qs.q: According to the story, what was Erik’s underlying problem?
o: He circulated stories that weren’t true.

qs.q: All of the following happened to people on Erik’s ship EXCEPT ___.
What did Erik think he was looking at when he first saw Greenland?
Why did Erik want to bring more people to Greenland?
o: So he could set up a dynasty
To protect them from the Vikings

tr: Grenlandiya mamlakati unchalik yashil emas.

Shuning uchun hamma unga yaxshi muomala qilishga harakat qilardi.
Bir kuni Erik qo'shnisi bilan urishib, uni o'ldirib qo'ydi.

Erik qutbning sovuq havosida qaltirab ketdi.
U hamma yoqda muz borligini ko'rdi.

«Men uni "Grenlandiya" (Yashil yurt) deb atayman», dedi u.

e3|26.title: Everyone is Special
paras: When I was young, everything that went wrong in my house seemed to be my fault. Once, my brothers tried to make cookies. They blended flour and ginger and made a disgusting paste. Then they tried to wash it down the drain, but it got all over the floor. Later, my brothers said that I did it and I had to wipe it up.

I worried that my parents liked them more than me. One autumn day, I was sure I would make my parents proud. I bought a model rocket. After I put it together, I invited everybody to watch it. I wanted my brothers to envy my technical knowledge. I lit the fuse, but nothing happened.
“Looks like your fireworks don’t work. I hope you kept the receipt so you can return them,” my brother said.
“It’s not fireworks!” I screamed. They were making fun of me again.

I didn’t know what went wrong. I hadn’t altered anything. I quickly moved the wires on the bottom, hoping that would help. Suddenly, the rocket flew up. We stood aside as it curved through the lawn and ran straight into the mailbox. Then the mailbox collapsed. The rocket was crushed.
Embarrassed, I ran inside and hid. A few minutes later, my mom asked, “Are you OK?”
“I just wanted them to be jealous of me for once. Now I see why you and Dad don’t love me as much as them,” I said.
“That’s not true!” said my mom. “See my fingers... each one is different. You kids are like my fingers: all are different, but I love them all the same.”
I embraced her. Now I know that my parents love me just as much as my brothers.

qs.q: All of the following happened when the brothers tried to cook EXCEPT ___.
o: they tried to put the paste down the drain

qs.q: The girl thought that putting together the model rocket proved her ___.
Why does her brother say that he hopes she kept the receipt?
o: He wants to buy her a new rocket
He wants her to save money.
He thinks she should return the rocket.

qs.q: The mother tells the girl that her children are like her fingers because ___.
o: they all are different but loved

tr: Men yoshligimda uyimizda bo'lgan har bir noxush voqea mening aybimdek tuyulardi.
Bir safar akalarim pechenye pishirmoqchi bo'lishdi.

Keyinroq akalarim buni men qildim deyishdi va men uni artishimga to'g'ri keldi.
Ota-onam ularni mendan ko'proq yaxshi ko'radi deb xavotirlanardim.
Bir kuz kuni men ota-onamni faxrlantirishimga amin edim.

Akalarim mening texnik bilimlarimga havas qilishini xohlardim.
Men pilikni yoqdim, lekin hech narsa bo'lmadi.
«Mushakbozlig'ing ishlamaydiganga o'xshaydi.

Ular yana meni masxara qilishayotgan edi.
Nima noto'g'ri bo'lganini bilmasdim.
Men hech narsani o'zgartirmagan edim.
Foydasi tegar degan umidda pastdagi simlarni tez qimirlatdim.
To'satdan raketa yuqoriga uchib ketdi.
U maysazor ustidan egilib uchib, to'g'ri pochta qutisiga borib urilganda, biz chetga chiqib turdik.
Keyin pochta qutisi qulab tushdi.
Raketa ezilib qoldi.
Xijolat bo'lib, men ichkariga yugurib kirib, yashirindim.
Bir necha daqiqadan keyin onam so'radi: «Yaxshimisan?»
«Men faqat bir marta bo'lsa ham ular menga hasad qilishini xohlagandim.

e3|27.title: Pizarro and the Inca Gold
paras: According to rumors, there’s lots of precious gold hidden in the jungles of Peru. It got there when the Spanish conquered parts of South America. The Spanish noble, Francisco Pizarro, arrived in Peru in the 1500s. He found a group of people called the Incas. The Incas believed that their leader, Atahualpa, was both a king and a god. But “It is a sin for a man to think he is God!” he said to Atahualpa.

Atahualpa thought Pizarro was insulting his heritage. He thought the blonde Spanish men held prejudices against the Incas. But Atahualpa was a kind man and didn’t want to fight the Spaniards. He said, “If I give you a room full of gold, will you leave my country in peace?”

Pizarro was suspicious. He thought Atahualpa was exaggerating. But a few days later, Pizarro returned to the Inca palace with his ambassadors. He saw a room filled with stacks of gold. There were golden necklaces, cups, plates and vases. It was a great spectacle. He acknowledged that Atahualpa had told the truth. But after seeing the gold, he wanted all of Peru’s gold. So he didn’t leave the country.

The Spanish soldiers stayed in Peru and grabbed all the gold they could find. But the Inca people tricked the Spaniards. They mixed the gold with tin so that it was poor quality. They gave this gold to the Spaniards. Meanwhile, they hid the good gold. They stuffed it into sacks and dragged it deep into the jungle. The Spanish conquerors never found the gold. People think it is still there today.

qs.q: Which of the following did NOT appear in the room with gold?
Which adjective describes Pizarro?
What do the rumors say?
o: There is a lot of gold in the Peruvian jungle.
The Spanish arrived in Peru in the 1500s.

qs.q: Who went to the room of gold with Pizarro?

e3|28.title: The Boy Who Saved the Town
paras: Marcus lived in a small suburb near the sea. He was a stubborn boy, and he only cared about himself. His father worked as a chemist for an institution and wanted Marcus to get a job there. Instead, the boy delivered milk. Each morning he took dairy products to the grocers.

One day, Marcus was jogging down the street with a gallon of milk to give to a merchant. He didn’t want to be late. He ran down a path beside a large canal. A wall there kept water from coming into the town during high tide. But Marcus saw a small hole in the wall. Marcus knew that if the wall broke, it would be a tragedy for the town. At first, he hesitated. He had to choose between helping him self and helping the town. There was only one way to save the town. It seemed crazy to him, but it was the only thing he could do. He poked his finger into the hole. This didn’t fix the problem forever, but it did postpone the tragedy.

His finger ached. He felt the chill of the arctic water as it splashed him. There was no one else around. He knew he had to wait until the tide descended. It was very difficult, but Marcus stayed there and saved the town.

Once the tide had descended, Marcus told everyone what happened. A group of people went to the wall. They saw the hole and fixed it. Everyone was very happy with Marcus. The local congress even gave him a gift for saving the town. He was a hero.

qs.q: Why was Marcus jogging down the street with a gallon of milk?
o: He liked to run beside a large canal.
He had to give it to the grocer soon.
He had to make it home before the tide descended.

qs.q: Why did Marcus hesitate to poke his finger into the wall?
o: He didn’t know who to save, himself or the town.
He didn’t want to get in trouble.
He didn’t want a gift from congress
The arctic water was so cold.

qs.q: What was Marcus’s job?
o: He was a grocer in the suburb.
He did things to help the town.
He took dairy products to merchants in town.

qs.q: Why did Marcus’s finger ache?
o: He knew he would be in trouble.

e3|29.title: An Interesting Life
paras: A man looked through some boxes with his grandson. They were filled with old photographs and objects that portrayed important events from the grandfather’s life. He wished to share the circumstances behind each event with his grandson. The grandson, however, thought his grandfather’s stories were boring. The grandfather coped with this. He ignored his grandson’s criticism.
He took a photo from the box. “That’s the submarine I was on during the war,” he explained. The grandson gazed at it.
The grandfather glanced at the next picture and frowned. It showed a row of coffins. His grandson noticed the grief in his grandfather’s face.
“What is it?” the boy inquired.
“This was after a nuclear bomb was dropped,” the grandfather answered. “It devastated a city.”
Next the grandfather pulled a toy microscope from the box and rotated it in his hand. “Where did you get that?” the grandson asked.

“This is a souvenir I bought at the science museum,” the grandfather said. Now the boy was really interested. He started to understand that his grandfather was telling him a larger story. It was the story of his grandfather’s life. He got another photo. It showed a young bride and groom. They were very happy. A certificate was attached to the photo. The boy couldn’t read it, but he traced his finger over paper.
“What’s this from, Granddad?” he asked.
“That’s my marriage license from the day I married your grandmother,” the grandfather said.
“Wow!” said the boy. “Granddad, now I know all about your life!”

o: the grandfather rotated it in his hand
the grandson only glanced at it
the grandfather bought it at a museum

Nevarasi unga tikilib qaradi.

e3|30.title: The Kitten and the Caterpillar
paras: Katie the kitten liked to play. One day, Cory the caterpillar emerged from a hole in the wall while Katie was playing in the living room.
“Hey!” Katie yelled. “Do you want to play with me?”

Cory was reluctant. He said, “I’d rather not play with you. I have several handicaps. My body is very delicate. Your claws are as sharp as hooks. You might cut me. Plus, I have no bones, not even a spine. You could easily hurt me.”
“I swear that I won’t hurt you,” Katie said.
“No, I don’t want to,” he said again. He hopped from the wall, but Katie pursued him.

Cory ran into the kitchen and into the cupboard, but Katie chased closely behind. Katie knocked appliances to the floor. Plates fell into the sink and broke in the basin. Then he ran into a bedroom. Some laundry was on the floor. Cory hid under a shirt, but Katie saw him. She jumped on the shirt. Her paws left stains on the cloth, and her claws ripped the sleeves into strips.
However, Cory escaped. He utilized a small crack in the floor to hide. But Katie saw him.
“Now you are trapped!” said Katie.

Cory tried to avoid Katie’s claws. He moved his body as far into the hole as possible. Just then, Katie’s owner came home. She saw that the house was a mess. She took a broom and swung it at Katie. She chased Katie out of the house.
Cory was safe, and Katie was left outside because she didn’t listen to the wishes of others.

qs.q: Which is NOT a reason that Cory was reluctant about playing with Katie?
Where was Katie playing when Cory emerged from the wall?
Katie did all of the following damage EXCEPT ___.
o: rip the sleeves of a shirt into strips

qs.q: What did Katie’s owner swing at her?

tr: Mushukcha Keyti o'ynashni yaxshi ko'rardi.

Tanam juda nozik.
Sening tirnoqlaring ilmoqdek o'tkir.
Meni kesib qo'yishing mumkin.
Buning ustiga, mening suyaklarim yo'q, hatto umurtqam ham yo'q.
Menga osongina ozor berishing mumkin».
