Keyti maishiy jihozlarni polga ag'darib yubordi.
Likopchalar rakovinaga tushib, tog'orada sinib ketdi.
Keyin u yotoqxonaga yugurib kirdi.
Polda kir kiyimlar yotardi.
Kori ko'ylak ostiga yashirindi, lekin Keyti uni ko'rib qoldi.
U ko'ylak ustiga sakradi.
Uning panjalari matoda dog' qoldirdi, tirnoqlari esa yenglarni tasma-tasma qilib yirtib tashladi.
Biroq Kori qochib qoldi.
U yashirinish uchun poldagi kichik yoriqdan foydalandi.
Lekin Keyti uni ko'rdi.
«Endi qopqonga tushding!» dedi Keyti.
Kori Keytining tirnoqlaridan qochishga harakat qildi.
U tanasini teshikka iloji boricha chuqurroq kiritdi.
Aynan shu payt Keytining egasi uyga keldi.
U uyning ostin-ustin bo'lib ketganini ko'rdi.
U supurgini olib, Keytiga qarab siltadi.
U Keytini uydan quvib chiqardi.
Kori omon qoldi, Keyti esa boshqalarning xohishiga quloq solmagani uchun tashqarida qoldi.

e4|1.title: The History of Chocolate
paras: Many people believe that chocolate originally came from Europe. However, chocolate, called the “food of the gods,” was first made in the Americas. The first chocolate was very different from contemporary chocolate.

Wild chocolate trees can grow easily in the humid Amazon rainforest. Clusters of flowers growing on these trees turn to seeds. About 20 to 60 cacao beans can be found in the seeds. Cacao beans are the ingredient needed to create sweet, soothing, and delicious chocolate treats.

The Mayan and Aztec cultures both thought that chocolate trees were brought from paradise by gods. The Mayans and Aztecs used the beans from this divine tree to create a special beverage with a very pleasant odor. Surprisingly, the Aztecs believed that it would be toxic to women and children.

In the 1500s, the Spanish explorer Cortes met the Aztecs. Cortes became quite interested in the plantations where the Aztecs cultivated chocolate trees. When he returned to Europe, he took cacao beans with him. He introduced the people of Spain to the Aztecs’ chocolate beverage.

Over the next 100 years or so, kings, queens, and members of the upper class enjoyed drinking chocolate. They enjoyed it even more once they learned to add sugar to the beverage! Soon, chocolate had spread all across Europe. New machines allowed chocolate makers to perfect their products and produce them at a very rapid rate. Preparing the beans in special ways brought out the aroma of chocolate. The beans were combined with condensed milk to give the chocolate a smooth texture.

Today, contemporary chocolates with subtle flavors fill the shelves of expensive chocolate shops. The different types of chocolate available today vary widely. True chocolate lovers can tell which is best, though. They will tell you that the flavor of high quality chocolate stays on the palate long after you finish it.

qs.q: Which word is NOT used to describe chocolate in the reading?
Which of the following did NOT consume chocolate as a beverage?
Which group of people believed that chocolate was toxic to women and children?
What allowed chocolate to be produced at a rapid rate?

tr: Ko'p odamlar shokolad asli Yevropadan kelgan deb ishonishadi.
Biroq «xudolar taomi» deb ataladigan shokolad ilk bor Amerika qit'asida tayyorlangan.
Birinchi shokolad hozirgi shokoladdan juda farq qilgan.
Yovvoyi shokolad daraxtlari nam Amazon tropik o'rmonida oson o'sadi.
Bu daraxtlarda o'sadigan gul to'plamlari urug'ga aylanadi.
Urug'lar ichida 20 tadan 60 tagacha kakao donasi bo'ladi.
Kakao donalari shirin, tinchlantiruvchi va mazali shokolad shirinliklarini yaratish uchun kerakli tarkibiy qismdir.
Mayya va atsteklar madaniyatida shokolad daraxtlarini xudolar jannatdan olib kelgan deb hisoblashgan.
Mayyalar va atsteklar bu ilohiy daraxt donalaridan juda yoqimli hidli maxsus ichimlik tayyorlashgan.
Ajablanarlisi shundaki, atsteklar u ayollar va bolalar uchun zaharli bo'ladi deb ishonishgan.
1500-yillarda ispan sayyohi Kortes atsteklar bilan uchrashdi.
Kortes atsteklar shokolad daraxtlarini yetishtiradigan plantatsiyalarga juda qiziqib qoldi.
U Yevropaga qaytganida, o'zi bilan kakao donalarini olib ketdi.
U Ispaniya xalqini atsteklarning shokoladli ichimligi bilan tanishtirdi.
Keyingi 100 yilcha davomida qirollar, malikalar va yuqori tabaqa vakillari shokolad ichishdan zavqlanishdi.
Ichimlikka shakar qo'shishni o'rganganlaridan keyin esa undan yanada ko'proq zavqlanishdi!
Tez orada shokolad butun Yevropaga tarqaldi.
Yangi mashinalar shokolad ishlab chiqaruvchilarga mahsulotlarini mukammallashtirish va ularni juda tez sur'atda ishlab chiqarish imkonini berdi.
Donalarni maxsus usullarda tayyorlash shokolad xushbo'yligini yuzaga chiqardi.
Shokoladga mayin tuzilish berish uchun donalar quyultirilgan sut bilan aralashtirildi.
Bugun nozik ta'mli zamonaviy shokoladlar qimmat shokolad do'konlarining javonlarini to'ldirib turadi.
Bugungi kunda mavjud shokolad turlari bir-biridan juda farq qiladi.
Biroq haqiqiy shokolad ixlosmandlari qaysi biri eng yaxshi ekanini ajrata oladi.
Ular sizga yuqori sifatli shokoladning ta'mi uni yeb bo'lganingizdan keyin ham uzoq vaqt og'izda qolishini aytishadi.

e4|2.title: Monkey Island
paras: In the middle of the ocean, there is a small island shaped like an arc. Here, monkeys play on the beach and in the trees. But how did the monkeys get there?

Once, an English admiral was exploring Africa when he found hundreds of monkeys. The admiral’s character was mean. He thought, “I could sell these monkeys and become very rich! I’m going to take them to England.”

So the admiral set traps to catch the monkeys. He put stakes in the ground, tied string around them and made loops in the string. When the monkeys ran through the forest, their feet got caught in the loops, and they couldn’t escape. Then the admiral put the monkeys in cages on his ship and sailed away.

The cages were small and uncomfortable. There was no soft hay for the monkeys to sleep on. Instead, they slept on branches with sharp thorns that cut into the monkeys’ flesh. For dinner, he gave them tiny pieces of sour grapefruit to eat. The monkeys grew hungry and weak.
But one day, the admiral hired a new steward. He was a kind man with a good conscience. He was horrified to see the thin monkeys in the cages. So one night he let them out.

The monkeys ran and played all over the ship! They attacked the admiral and the steward and ate their food. They completely wrecked the ship. One monkey ran into a kerosene lamp, and it fell over. The ship caught fire and began to sink! The whole crew was lost except for the monkeys.

After the accident, the monkeys jumped onto a raft. They floated away from the fiery blaze of the ship. In the morning, they saw a little island in the distance. The monkeys used a piece of wood as a paddle, and they went toward it. They found the island shaped like an arc. They felt so happy to find a new home, and they still live there today.

qs.q: Which adjective describes the admiral’s character?
Where did the admiral plan to take the monkeys?
What did the monkeys eat while they were in the cages?
What shape was the island that the monkeys found?

tr: Okean o'rtasida yoy shaklidagi kichik orol bor.
Bu yerda maymunlar sohilda va daraxtlarda o'ynashadi.
Lekin maymunlar u yerga qanday kelib qolgan?
Bir paytlar bir ingliz admirali Afrikani o'rganib yurganida, yuzlab maymunlarni topdi.
Admiralning fe'li yomon edi.
U o'yladi: «Bu maymunlarni sotib, juda boy bo'lishim mumkin!
Ularni Angliyaga olib ketaman».
Shunday qilib, admiral maymunlarni tutish uchun tuzoqlar qo'ydi.
U yerga qoziqlar qoqdi, ularning atrofiga ip bog'ladi va ipda halqalar yasadi.
Maymunlar o'rmon bo'ylab yugurganlarida, oyoqlari halqalarga ilinib qolar va ular qochib qutula olmasdi.
Keyin admiral maymunlarni kemasidagi qafaslarga solib, suzib ketdi.
Qafaslar kichik va noqulay edi.
Maymunlar uxlashi uchun yumshoq pichan yo'q edi.
Buning o'rniga ular maymunlarning etiga kirib ketadigan o'tkir tikanli shoxlar ustida uxlashardi.
Kechki ovqatga u ularga mayda-mayda nordon greypfrut bo'laklarini berardi.
Maymunlar och va holsiz bo'lib qolishdi.
Lekin bir kuni admiral yangi styuard yolladi.
U vijdoni toza, mehribon odam edi.
U qafaslardagi ozg'in maymunlarni ko'rib dahshatga tushdi.
Shuning uchun bir kecha u ularni chiqarib yubordi.
Maymunlar butun kema bo'ylab yugurib, o'ynashdi!
Ular admiral va styuardga hujum qilishdi va ovqatlarini yeb qo'yishdi.
Ular kemani butunlay vayron qilishdi.
Bir maymun kerosin chiroqqa urilib ketdi va u ag'darildi.
Kema yonib, cho'ka boshladi!
Maymunlardan boshqa butun ekipaj halok bo'ldi.
Halokatdan keyin maymunlar solga sakrab chiqishdi.
Ular kemaning lovullab yonayotgan alangasidan uzoqlashib suzib ketishdi.
Ertalab ular uzoqda kichik orolni ko'rishdi.
Maymunlar bir parcha yog'ochni eshkak qilib, unga qarab suzishdi.
Ular yoy shaklidagi orolni topishdi.
Yangi uy topganlaridan juda xursand bo'lishdi va ular hozir ham o'sha yerda yashashadi.

e4|3.title: The Young Man and the Old Man
paras: A proud young man was looking for a new pastime. He heard about people hiking in the national parks and decided to try it for himself. As he started his stroll, an old man walked up to him.
“Don’t go this way,” the old man said. “Beware. The paths are not clear. It’s easy to become lost.”

But the young man disagreed with the old man and bragged that he had a perfect understanding of the park. “I studied maps of this area,” he told him. “I believe I have a thorough knowledge of these trails. I won’t become lost.”
The old man listened to the young man and then admonished him for his pride. “I have walked these trails my entire life,” he said. “If you think you will be safe, then go ahead.”
The young man ignored the old man and started along the trail.

Whenever he had to choose between an easy or difficult route, he always chose the more difficult option. In addition, he was not conscious of which direction he was going. After a while, he decided to return home. Because his course through the wilderness was so indirect, he had no idea where he was.
He looked at his map but could not pinpoint his location. He walked one path after another but soon realized he was lost.

The sun was going down, and sudden strong winds gave a hint that it might rain. Immense clouds filled the sky. Awesome sounds of thunder were audible from all directions. It echoed off the mountains. The thought of the eventual storm tormented the young man. He hurried in one direction, but soon switched out of confusion. Luckily, it led him out of the park.
When he arrived home, he knew that he had acted like an idiot. He realized he was lucky to be alive. He decided to listen to people with more experience than himself.

qs.q: What did the young man choose as his new pastime?
Why did the old man admonish the young man?
o: The young man bragged that he was perfect.
The young man’s route was too indirect.
The young man chose difficult trails.

qs.q: Why did the young man become lost?
o: He was not conscious of where he went.
He pinpointed his location on his map.
He did not switch to an easier trail.
He listened to the old man’s advice.

qs.q: Which of the following gave a hint of an eventual storm?
o: The sparse clouds in the sky
The lightning flashing in the sky

tr: Bir mag'rur yigit yangi ermak qidirayotgan edi.
U milliy bog'larda piyoda sayr qilayotgan odamlar haqida eshitdi va buni o'zi ham sinab ko'rishga qaror qildi.
U sayrini boshlaganida, uning oldiga bir chol keldi.
«Bu tomonga borma, — dedi chol. —
Ehtiyot bo'l.
Yo'llar aniq emas.
Adashib qolish oson».
Lekin yigit chol bilan kelishmadi va bog'ni mukammal bilishi bilan maqtandi.
«Men bu hududning xaritalarini o'rganganman, — dedi u unga. —
Bu so'qmoqlarni puxta bilaman deb ishonaman.
Adashib qolmayman».
Chol yigitni tinglab, so'ng uni mag'rurligi uchun koyidi.
«Men butun umrim bu so'qmoqlarda yurganman, — dedi u. —
Agar xavfsiz bo'laman deb o'ylasang, unda boraver».
Yigit cholga e'tibor bermay, so'qmoq bo'ylab yo'lga tushdi.
Har safar oson yoki qiyin yo'l o'rtasida tanlash kerak bo'lganda, u doim qiyinroq yo'lni tanlardi.
Bundan tashqari, u qaysi tomonga ketayotganini anglamasdi.
Bir muncha vaqtdan keyin u uyga qaytishga qaror qildi.
Yovvoyi tabiat bo'ylab yo'li juda aylanma bo'lgani uchun u qayerda ekanini umuman bilmasdi.
U xaritasiga qaradi, lekin joylashuvini aniq topa olmadi.
U bir so'qmoqdan keyin boshqasidan yurdi, lekin tez orada adashib qolganini angladi.
Quyosh botayotgan edi va to'satdan esgan kuchli shamol yomg'ir yog'ishi mumkinligidan darak berardi.
Osmonni ulkan bulutlar qopladi.
Har tomondan dahshatli momaqaldiroq ovozlari eshitilardi.
U tog'larda aks-sado berardi.
Yaqinlashib kelayotgan bo'ron haqidagi fikr yigitni qiynardi.
U bir tomonga shoshildi, lekin tez orada sarosimada yo'nalishini o'zgartirdi.
Baxtiga, bu yo'l uni bog'dan olib chiqdi.
U uyga yetib kelganida, ahmoqona ish qilganini bildi.
U tirik qolgani omad ekanini angladi.
U o'zidan tajribaliroq odamlarga quloq solishga qaror qildi.

e4|4.title: The Tricky Fox
paras: There was a fox that lived in the forest. Fox loved to play mean tricks on the other animals. One day, he used the sharp rim of a bottle to dig a pit in the ground. He hid in a tree until Rabbit came to the pit’s edge. Then, he jumped out and pushed Rabbit into the pit. Fox laughed and ran away. The angry Rabbit climbed out and told the other animals what happened.

The others said, “That is typical behavior for Fox. He does mean things all the time. Sometimes, he is completely immoral. We all disapprove of his actions, so we should teach him a lesson. Tomorrow, we’ll push Fox into that pit.”

The next day, all of the animals hid near the pit and waited for Fox. Fox was oblivious to the hidden animals. He walked up to the pit to see if Rabbit was still trapped. Just then, the other animals ran up to Fox and pushed him in. All the animals laughed and cheered, except Fox, of course.

Fox couldn’t get out! The walls of the pit were covered in damp ivy. It was too slippery for him to climb out. He was utterly helpless. He moaned and began to weep. At last, he saw Eagle watching him from her roost. He yelled, “Eagle, please help me! If I don’t get out of here, I will perish!”
Eagle said, “You may think your tricks are trivial, but you hurt others when you do mean things. I’ll help you if you promise to be nice.”
Fox said, “I promise!”
Eagle began her flight to the bottom of the pit. She picked up Fox with her beak and soared out of the pit. She dropped Fox safely on the ground.
Fox thanked Eagle and kept his promise. He was nice to the other animals. The other animals were happy, and they all became friends.

qs.q: How did Rabbit fall into the pit?
o: Fox pushed him into the pit.

qs.q: Why did Fox thank Eagle?
o: She did not let Fox perish.
She gave Fox some rope to climb out.

qs.q: Why did Fox moan and weep?
o: The animals taught him a lesson
He saw Eagle in her roost

qs.q: What happened after Eagle’s flight to the bottom of the pit?
o: She got stuck in the pit.
She made Fox promise to leave the forest.
She picked up Fox with her beak.

tr: O'rmonda bir tulki yashardi.
Tulki boshqa hayvonlar ustidan yomon hazillar qilishni yaxshi ko'rardi.
Bir kuni u shishaning o'tkir cheti bilan yerda chuqur qazidi.
U Quyon chuqur chetiga kelguncha daraxtda yashirinib turdi.
Keyin u sakrab chiqib, Quyonni chuqurga itarib yubordi.
Tulki kulib, qochib ketdi.
G'azablangan Quyon chuqurdan chiqib, boshqa hayvonlarga nima bo'lganini aytib berdi.
Boshqalar dedi: «Bu Tulkiga xos xatti-harakat.
U doim yomon ishlar qiladi.
Ba'zan u butunlay axloqsiz bo'ladi.
Hammamiz uning qilmishlarini qoralaymiz, shuning uchun unga saboq berishimiz kerak.
Ertaga Tulkini o'sha chuqurga itarib yuboramiz».
Ertasi kuni barcha hayvonlar chuqur yonida yashirinib, Tulkini kutishdi.
Tulki yashiringan hayvonlardan bexabar edi.
U Quyon hali ham qamalib qolganmi-yo'qmi, bilish uchun chuqur oldiga keldi.
Aynan shu payt boshqa hayvonlar Tulkiga yugurib kelib, uni itarib yuborishdi.
Barcha hayvonlar kulib, xursand bo'lishdi, Tulkidan tashqari, albatta.
Tulki chiqa olmadi!
Chuqurning devorlari nam pechak bilan qoplangan edi.
U chiqib olishi uchun juda sirpanchiq edi.
U mutlaqo ojiz edi.
U ingrab, yig'lay boshladi.
Nihoyat, u Burgutning o'z qo'nim joyidan unga qarab turganini ko'rdi.
U qichqirdi: «Burgut, iltimos, menga yordam ber!
Agar bu yerdan chiqmasam, halok bo'laman!»
Burgut dedi: «Sen hiylalaringni arzimas narsa deb o'ylashing mumkin, lekin yomon ish qilganingda boshqalarga ozor berasan.
Yaxshi bo'lishga va'da bersang, senga yordam beraman».
Tulki dedi: «Va'da beraman!»
Burgut chuqur tubiga qarab parvozini boshladi.
U Tulkini tumshug'i bilan ko'tarib, chuqurdan uchib chiqdi.
U Tulkini yerga eson-omon tushirdi.
Tulki Burgutga rahmat aytdi va va'dasida turdi.
U boshqa hayvonlarga yaxshi munosabatda bo'ldi.
Boshqa hayvonlar xursand bo'lishdi va hammalari do'st bo'lib qolishdi.

e4|5.title: The Magic Computer
paras: I had a difficult geography project to finish by the end of the semester. My teacher wanted it to be typewritten, so I went to the school computer room. But when I got there, all the computers were turned off. Apparently there was a recent problem, and technicians were fixing it.

I knew of some private study rooms downstairs. They were small and dark, and the computers were very old, but I had no choice. At least the computers were operating correctly. I typed and highlighted the assignment’s title: “Evaluate the Government’s Response to Global Warming.” But I didn’t know what to write in my essay. Finally I decided to find a book to help me. I went to the library, checked the book indexes and eventually found a useful book. Then I returned to the computer.

When I looked at the screen, I saw something so weird that I nearly fainted! The essay was complete! Had somebody in cyberspace written it? I didn’t know, but I was very happy. I printed it out and handed it in. I got an “A.”

After that, I used the computer for all my assignments. I’d type the title, wait awhile, and the computer would do it. Every assignment was perfect; I never had to edit anything. I stopped paying attention to my teacher’s lectures and spent my extra time in the gymnasium. And my grades got better and better.
A month later, I was walking into class when my friend said, “Are you prepared for the test?”
“What test?” I asked.
“The geography test!” he replied. “I hope you studied. It’s worth seventy percent of our final grade!”

I failed the test, of course. I was completely ignorant about the subject. After that, I made a resolution never to use the magic computer again. The moral of this story is that if you cheat at school, you won’t learn anything.

qs.q: How did the teacher want the project to be written?
What was the project about?
What did the student NOT have to do in order to use the magic computer?
Where did the student spend his free time?

tr: Semestr oxirigacha tugatishim kerak bo'lgan qiyin geografiya loyihasi bor edi.
O'qituvchim uni kompyuterda terilgan holda topshirishimni xohladi, shuning uchun maktabning kompyuter xonasiga bordim.
Lekin u yerga borganimda, barcha kompyuterlar o'chirilgan edi.
Aftidan, yaqinda bir muammo chiqqan va texniklar uni tuzatishayotgan edi.
Men pastki qavatdagi bir nechta alohida o'quv xonalarini bilardim.
Ular kichik va qorong'i, kompyuterlari esa juda eski edi, lekin boshqa ilojim yo'q edi.
Hech bo'lmasa kompyuterlar to'g'ri ishlayotgan edi.
Men topshiriq sarlavhasini terib, belgilab qo'ydim: «Hukumatning global isishga munosabatini baholang».
Lekin inshomga nima yozishni bilmasdim.
Nihoyat, menga yordam beradigan kitob topishga qaror qildim.
Men kutubxonaga borib, kitob ko'rsatkichlarini tekshirdim va oxiri foydali kitob topdim.
Keyin kompyuterga qaytdim.
Ekranga qaraganimda, shunchalik g'alati narsani ko'rdimki, sal qoldi hushimdan ketishimga!
Insho tayyor edi!
Uni kibermakonda kimdir yozdimikan?
Bilmasdim, lekin juda xursand edim.
Men uni chop etib, topshirdim.
«A» (a'lo) baho oldim.
Shundan keyin barcha topshiriqlarim uchun o'sha kompyuterdan foydalandim.
Sarlavhani terib, biroz kutardim va kompyuter uni bajarib qo'yardi.
Har bir topshiriq mukammal edi; hech narsani tahrir qilishimga to'g'ri kelmasdi.
Men o'qituvchimning ma'ruzalariga e'tibor bermay qo'ydim va ortiqcha vaqtimni sport zalida o'tkazdim.
Baholarim esa tobora yaxshilanib bordi.
Bir oydan keyin darsga kirib kelayotganimda do'stim: «Imtihonga tayyormisan?» dedi.
«Qanaqa imtihon?» deb so'radim.
«Geografiya imtihoni! — deb javob berdi u. —
O'qigan bo'lsang kerak, deb umid qilaman.
U yakuniy bahomizning yetmish foizini tashkil qiladi!»
Albatta, men imtihondan yiqildim.
Men bu fan haqida mutlaqo hech narsa bilmasdim.
Shundan keyin sehrli kompyuterdan boshqa hech qachon foydalanmaslikka ahd qildim.
Bu hikoyaning ma'nosi shuki, agar maktabda ko'chirmachilik qilsang, hech narsa o'rganmaysan.

e4|6.title: Jack Frost and the Pudding
paras: Every winter, a magical boy with a wild spirit named Jack Frost arrives in town. He wears a white cape, and his role is to cover everything with frost and ice. But Jack Frost also gets pleasure from playing tricks on common folks.
One dark winter evening, he was sitting on the rail of a fence near a river, pointing at some trees. When he did so, there was a pop, and the trees were evenly covered in frost.

Then old Tom Muggins came along the path. He was carrying a basket of ingredients for his wife’s cake recipe. “I’ll have some fun with him!” said Jack Frost. He pointed, and suddenly there was a patch of ice on the path. Poor Tom slipped and fell into the river. The bags of flour, fruit and sugar fell open and got wet. A couple of eggs broke, and a stick of butter shrank in the water. Tom gathered the ingredients and climbed out of the river. The food made an absolute mess of the path. “Alas!” he cried. “There’ll be no cake for me!” Jack Frost laughed at poor Tom because his nice suit got soaked as well. “Are you cold?” he said. “Don’t worry, I’ll make you warm!” He pointed at the mess in Tom’s basket. Suddenly, there was a spark. What was left of the food caught fire! Jack Frost ran off laughing. Poor Tom sat by the fire. He could only envision how angry his wife would be. He wished he had been more attentive and noticed that Jack was around.

Suddenly, a pleasant smell came from the basket. Tom looked inside. The butter was melting and the eggs were starting to cook! Even the fruit began to simmer. Soon there was a fat, brown pudding in the basket! Tom tasted it. It was delicious! He happily took it home for dessert. Although Jack Frost had tried to make Tom’s life difficult, Jack had actually made Tom a wonderful pudding!

qs.q: Tom Muggins likes playing tricks on folks.
Jack Frost was sitting on the rail of a fence.
Jack Frost’s role is to cover everything with fire.
Tom wished that he had been more attentive.
Tom said “Alas!” because he knew he wouldn’t have any cake.
When Jack Frost set fire to the food, the eggs started to melt.

tr: Har qishda shaharga Jek Frost ismli yovvoyi ruhli sehrli bola keladi.
U oq yopinchiq kiyadi va uning vazifasi hamma narsani qirov va muz bilan qoplashdir.
Lekin Jek Frost oddiy odamlar ustidan hazil qilishdan ham zavq oladi.
Bir qorong'i qish oqshomida u daryo yaqinidagi panjaraning to'sinida o'tirib, bir nechta daraxtni ko'rsatayotgan edi.
U shunday qilganida «pip» degan ovoz chiqdi va daraxtlar bir tekis qirov bilan qoplandi.
Keyin so'qmoq bo'ylab keksa Tom Magins kelib qoldi.
U xotinining tort retsepti uchun masalliqlar solingan savat ko'tarib kelayotgan edi.
«U bilan bir maza qilaman!» dedi Jek Frost.
U barmog'ini nuqidi va to'satdan so'qmoqda muz qatlami paydo bo'ldi.
Bechora Tom sirpanib, daryoga yiqildi.
Un, meva va shakar xaltalari ochilib, ho'l bo'lib ketdi.
Bir-ikkita tuxum sindi va bir bo'lak sariyog' suvda kichrayib qoldi.
Tom masalliqlarni yig'ib, daryodan chiqdi.
Ovqatlar so'qmoqni butunlay bulg'ab tashladi.
«Voy, attang! — deb qichqirdi u. —
Endi menga tort yo'q!» Jek Frost bechora Tom ustidan kuldi, chunki uning chiroyli kostyumi ham shilta ho'l bo'lgan edi.
«Sovqotyapsanmi? — dedi u. —
Xavotir olma, seni isitib qo'yaman!»
U Tomning savatidagi bulg'anchiqni ko'rsatdi.
To'satdan uchqun chaqnadi.
Ovqatdan qolgan narsa alangalanib ketdi!
Jek Frost kulib qochib ketdi.
Bechora Tom olov yonida o'tirdi.
U faqat xotinining qanchalik jahli chiqishini ko'z oldiga keltira olardi.
U ehtiyotkorroq bo'lib, Jekning atrofda ekanini payqamaganiga afsuslandi.
To'satdan savatdan yoqimli hid kela boshladi.
Tom ichiga qaradi.
Sariyog' erib, tuxumlar pisha boshlagan edi!
Hatto meva ham qaynay boshladi.
Tez orada savatda qalin, jigarrang puding paydo bo'ldi!
Tom uni tatib ko'rdi.
U juda mazali edi!
U uni shirinlik uchun xursand bo'lib uyiga olib ketdi.
Jek Frost Tomning hayotini qiyinlashtirmoqchi bo'lgan bo'lsa ham, aslida Tomga ajoyib puding tayyorlab bergan edi!

e4|7.title: The Architect’s Plan
paras: An architect wanted to build a new office building. He selected some land that seemed perfect. He planned to cut down the trees to make room for the building. But there was a problem... a big problem. The land was actually the habitat of several types of birds. Some nature lovers were very upset with the architect. First, they held a rally and told others about the issue. Then, they decided to take legal action because the architect didn’t respect the animals’ rights. To resolve the problem, they asked a judge to intervene.
The judge could not call any witnesses for the nature lovers, so he first asked the architect to tell his side of the story.

“Why are you going to destroy the birds’ habitat?” the judge asked. The architect replied, “I have the deed to the land. I want to make a great building there. As you may know, all my buildings become memorable landmarks.” Then one of the nature lovers spoke. “We believe that there’s no reason to destroy all the trees. We just want to protect the birds.” Then the judge made his decision. “I proclaim that the office building should be built,” he said. “It is not a crime to remove those trees. I can not give you a sentence for any offenses, but I feel obliged to make one request. I will only allow you to use half of the land. The other half will remain free, so the birds have a place to live.”
The nature lovers could not conceal their gratitude. All of the people cheered.

The architect said, “I have an idea. I will volunteer my time and efforts to design a new type of building. It will provide bushes on the roof where birds can live. There are enough resources in my company’s bank account to create the best building ever made.”
The architect did exactly as he promised. He built this new type of building, which was loved by everyone.

qs.q: Why did the group have a rally?
Which of the following about the land did the architect NOT tell the judge?
o: He wanted to make a great building.
He had a deed for the land.
His building would be a memorable landmark.

qs.q: What did the group do in order to resolve the problem with the architect?
o: Move the birds to a new habitat
Sell the land to the architect

qs.q: What did the judge decide to give the architect as a sentencing?
o: He gave him five years in prison.
He had to pay the nature lovers money.
He could not build any more buildings.
He was not given a sentence.

tr: Bir me'mor yangi ofis binosi qurmoqchi edi.
U mukammal tuyulgan bir yer tanladi.
U bino uchun joy ochish maqsadida daraxtlarni kesib tashlashni rejalashtirdi.
Lekin bir muammo bor edi... katta muammo.
Bu yer aslida bir necha turdagi qushlarning yashash joyi edi.
Ba'zi tabiat ixlosmandlari me'mordan juda norozi bo'lishdi.
Avval ular miting o'tkazib, boshqalarga bu muammo haqida gapirishdi.
Keyin me'mor hayvonlarning huquqlarini hurmat qilmagani uchun sudga murojaat qilishga qaror qilishdi.
Muammoni hal qilish uchun ular sudyadan aralashishni so'rashdi.
Sudya tabiat ixlosmandlari uchun birorta guvoh chaqira olmadi, shuning uchun avval me'mordan o'z fikrini aytib berishni so'radi.
«Nega qushlarning yashash joyini yo'q qilmoqchisiz?» deb so'radi sudya.
Me'mor javob berdi: «Menda yerning hujjati bor.
U yerda ajoyib bino qurmoqchiman.
Bilsangiz kerak, mening barcha binolarim esda qolarli diqqatga sazovor joylarga aylanadi».
Keyin tabiat ixlosmandlaridan biri gapirdi.
«Biz barcha daraxtlarni yo'q qilishga hech qanday sabab yo'q deb hisoblaymiz.
Biz faqat qushlarni himoya qilmoqchimiz».
Keyin sudya o'z qarorini chiqardi.
«Ofis binosi qurilishi kerakligini e'lon qilaman, — dedi u. —
U daraxtlarni olib tashlash jinoyat emas.
Men sizga hech qanday qoidabuzarlik uchun hukm chiqara olmayman, lekin bitta iltimos qilishga o'zimni majbur his qilaman.
Men sizga yerning faqat yarmidan foydalanishga ruxsat beraman.
Qolgan yarmi bo'sh qoladi, toki qushlarning yashaydigan joyi bo'lsin».
Tabiat ixlosmandlari minnatdorliklarini yashira olishmadi.
Hamma odamlar xursand bo'lib qichqirishdi.
Me'mor dedi: «Mening bir fikrim bor.
Men yangi turdagi binoni loyihalash uchun vaqtim va kuchimni ixtiyoriy ravishda sarflayman.
Uning tomida qushlar yashashi mumkin bo'lgan butalar bo'ladi.
Kompaniyamning bank hisobida hozirgacha qurilgan eng zo'r binoni yaratish uchun yetarli mablag' bor».
Me'mor aynan va'da qilganidek qildi.
U hamma yaxshi ko'rgan bu yangi turdagi binoni qurdi.

e4|8.title: Janie and the Music Player
paras: Janie had constant thoughts about getting a music player. One day, she was late to class. She hurried down the hall but halted when she saw a backpack on the floor. She looked inside and found nothing but some books. She reached inside the bag and felt a small object at the bottom. It was a music player enclosed in a black case! Janie tended to be honest, and she had no valid reason to take the device. However, her desire for the player influenced her decision. Janie was being sly. She put the device into her own backpack. When she arrived at class, she gave her teacher the bag. “I found this,” she said.

Ms. Johnson asked, “Does this backpack belong to anyone?” A girl named Linda claimed the bag. Linda looked inside and yelled, “My music player is missing! Janie took it!” Janie answered, “I did not.” Linda responded, “You were the only one that had access to it! If your version of the story is true, you’ll let Ms. Johnson check your bag.” Janie started to perspire as she realized the impending trouble she was in. She gripped her bag tightly.
Ms. Johnson took the bag from Janie. Inside she found the player. “Janie, I never expected this kind of conduct from you,” she said. “You’ve always been such a good student.”

Ms. Johnson gave Linda the player. Linda said, “Ms. Johnson, look!” There was a crack along one side. She turned it to the “on” mode, but it wouldn’t work. It must’ve snapped while Janie was holding onto the bag so tightly.
Ms. Johnson called Janie’s parents. They were very upset.

“Stealing is illegal. You have no respect for the law whatsoever,” they said. “We bought you a music player, but we’re giving it to Linda. It will replace the one you broke.” In the end, Janie got nothing at all.

qs.q: What did Janie find enclosed in the black case?
The reading explains that Janie lied to her teacher about what?
o: The reason she snapped the player
How the player got a crack

qs.q: What did Ms. Johnson NOT expect from Janie?
Janie’s parents said she had no respect whatsoever for what?

tr: Jeyni doim musiqa pleyeri olish haqida o'ylardi.
Bir kuni u darsga kechikdi.
U yo'lak bo'ylab shoshildi, lekin polda ryukzakni ko'rib to'xtadi.
U ichiga qaradi va bir nechta kitobdan boshqa hech narsa topmadi.
U qo'lini xalta ichiga tiqdi va tubida kichik bir narsani sezdi.
Bu qora g'ilofga solingan musiqa pleyeri edi!
Jeyni odatda halol edi va qurilmani olishga hech qanday asosli sababi yo'q edi.
Biroq pleyerga bo'lgan istagi uning qaroriga ta'sir qildi.
Jeyni ayyorlik qilayotgan edi.
U qurilmani o'z ryukzakiga solib qo'ydi.
Darsga kelganida, u o'qituvchisiga xaltani berdi.
«Buni topib oldim», dedi u.
Missis Jonson so'radi: «Bu ryukzak kimnikidir?»
Linda ismli qiz xaltani o'ziniki deb aytdi.
Linda ichiga qarab, qichqirdi: «Musiqa pleyerim yo'q!
Uni Jeyni olgan!» Jeyni javob berdi: «Men olmadim».
Linda javob qaytardi: «Unga faqat sen yaqin bo'lgansan!
Agar sening aytganing rost bo'lsa, Missis Jonsonga xaltangni tekshirishga ruxsat berasan».
Jeyni boshiga tushayotgan muammoni anglab, terlay boshladi.
U xaltasini mahkam ushladi.
Missis Jonson xaltani Jeynidan oldi.
Ichida u pleyerni topdi.
«Jeyni, sendan bunday xatti-harakatni hech kutmagandim, — dedi u. —
Sen doim juda yaxshi o'quvchi bo'lgansan».
Missis Jonson pleyerni Lindaga berdi.
Linda dedi: «Missis Jonson, qarang!»
Uning bir tomoni bo'ylab yoriq bor edi.
U uni «yoqish» rejimiga o'tkazdi, lekin u ishlamadi.
Jeyni xaltani shunchalik mahkam ushlab turganida u sinib qolgan bo'lsa kerak.
Missis Jonson Jeynining ota-onasiga qo'ng'iroq qildi.
Ular juda xafa bo'lishdi.
«O'g'irlik qonunga zid.
Sen qonunni umuman hurmat qilmaysan, — deyishdi ular. —
Biz senga musiqa pleyeri sotib olgan edik, lekin uni Lindaga beryapmiz.
U sen sindirgan pleyerning o'rnini bosadi».
Oxir-oqibat Jeyni hech narsa olmadi.

e4|9.title: Growing to be Great
paras: When George was just a boy, he didn’t have any parents. The rumor was that they died in a car accident. Many bad things could have happened to George, but he was lucky. He was sent to live alongside other children without parents. There were kind people to assist George and help him go forward with his life. However, he was a pessimistic and mean little boy.

George was often outraged. He told mean rumors about the other kids. He smashed furniture and even slapped other boys. He defied anyone who tried to help him, and soon it was difficult for them to forgive him. But George did display a love for one thing. He loved to play baseball. Whereas he was lazy in school and liked neither the subjects nor the teachers, he was lively and happy when he played baseball.

One of George’s teachers noticed his talent. He began to work with the boy. At first they only talked about baseball. The teacher watched George play. He was a very efficient hitter. He almost never missed the ball. The teacher thought that George looked majestic when he played. When George hit the ball, it flew through the breeze as if it would never come down. In time, they began to talk about other things. They talked about George’s family and his dreams for the future. They developed a very good relationship. As George got older, he began to grow. His appetite was huge. He ate and ate. He got stronger. Soon the other boys and even the teachers looked small and feeble next to him. Everyone thought that this heralded the start of a great baseball career.

When George got his first job as a baseball player, he gave most of his wages to the people who had helped him as a boy. He hoped that other children would also find a way to live happy, successful lives.

qs.q: George grew up alongside other children who didn’t have parents.
George looked majestic when he played baseball.
George was a feeble boy with a small appetite.
When George grew up, he gave some of his wages to the people who had assisted him.
George was a lively student who liked many subjects.
George smashed things and slapped other boys when he was outraged.

tr: Jorj hali kichkina bola bo'lganida, uning ota-onasi yo'q edi.
Mish-mishlarga ko'ra, ular avtohalokatda vafot etgan edi.
Jorjning boshiga ko'p yomon narsalar tushishi mumkin edi, lekin unga omad kulib boqdi.
Uni ota-onasiz boshqa bolalar bilan birga yashashga yuborishdi.
U yerda Jorjga yordam beradigan va hayotda oldinga borishiga ko'maklashadigan mehribon odamlar bor edi.
Biroq u tushkun va yovuz kichkina bola edi.
Jorj tez-tez g'azablanardi.
U boshqa bolalar haqida yomon mish-mishlar tarqatardi.
U mebellarni sindirar va hatto boshqa bolalarga shapaloq tushirardi.
U unga yordam bermoqchi bo'lgan har qanday odamga qarshi chiqardi va tez orada ular uchun uni kechirish qiyin bo'lib qoldi.
Lekin Jorj bir narsaga muhabbatini namoyon qilardi.
U beysbol o'ynashni yaxshi ko'rardi.
Maktabda u dangasa bo'lib, na fanlarni, na o'qituvchilarni yoqtirgan bo'lsa ham, beysbol o'ynaganda jonli va xursand bo'lardi.
Jorjning o'qituvchilaridan biri uning iste'dodini payqadi.
U bola bilan shug'ullana boshladi.
Avvaliga ular faqat beysbol haqida gaplashishardi.
O'qituvchi Jorjning o'yinini kuzatardi.
U juda samarali zarba beruvchi edi.
U deyarli hech qachon to'pni o'tkazib yubormasdi.
O'qituvchi Jorj o'ynaganda ulug'vor ko'rinadi deb o'ylardi.
Jorj to'pni urganda, u go'yo hech qachon tushmaydigandek shabada bo'ylab uchib ketardi.
Vaqt o'tib, ular boshqa narsalar haqida ham gaplasha boshlashdi.
Ular Jorjning oilasi va kelajakdagi orzulari haqida gaplashishdi.
Ular o'rtasida juda yaxshi munosabat shakllandi.
Jorj kattalashgan sari o'sa boshladi.
Uning ishtahasi juda katta edi.
U yeyaverdi, yeyaverdi.
U kuchliroq bo'ldi.
Tez orada boshqa bolalar va hatto o'qituvchilar ham uning yonida kichkina va zaif ko'rinib qolishdi.
Hamma bu buyuk beysbol karyerasining boshlanishidan darak beradi deb o'yladi.
Jorj beysbolchi sifatida birinchi ishiga kirganida, maoshining katta qismini bolaligida unga yordam bergan odamlarga berdi.
U boshqa bolalar ham baxtli, muvaffaqiyatli hayot kechirish yo'lini topishlariga umid qilardi.

e4|10.title: Anton’s Great Discovery
paras: Anton Van Leeuwenhoek was a Dutch cloth merchant. His life began to change after he got his first microscope in 1653. It was a very simple microscope. It had a lens in an upright stand. It could make small things look large. It was handy for looking closely at cloth.
Soon, Anton felt a longing to build a more powerful microscope. He dreamed of using it to make an important scientific discovery. He wanted to become famous. Three decades later, he did.

For many years, Anton experimented with microscopes and lenses. Eventually he constructed a very powerful microscope. If he had sold the concept to others, it would have made him very rich. However, Anton refrained from surrendering his secret to anyone. Instead, he wanted to use it to become famous. So he used his secret microscope to study the natural world.

One day he was looking at saliva from his mouth with the microscope. In the saliva, he saw numerous tiny particles. Some of them were moving! He thought that the particles were tiny organisms. So he isolated them from each other and studied each one carefully. Then he classified them into different categories. Some were round. Others were long and had tails. All were alive.

Anton was so excited. He knew he could become famous now. He was the first person to see these tiny organisms. So he drew diagrams of the organisms and sent them to a group of scientists in London. The scientists were sophisticated men who did not believe tiny, animate organisms could live in our mouths. Anton made a plea for them to come to Holland to see the organisms with their own eyes. The men took a ferry to Holland and met Anton. They performed a careful review of his work, and they conceded that he had made a worthwhile discovery. Anton Van Leeuwenhoek had discovered bacteria. After decades of hard work, he had become famous.

qs.q: Which is true about Anton’s discovery?
o: It isolated him from his work.
It was handy for his business.
It took him three decades to make it.

qs.q: Why was Anton’s first microscope handy?
o: It helped him look at cloth.

qs.q: What was Anton’s plea to the scientists?
o: To see the particles with their own eyes

qs.q: Why didn’t Anton sell his concept of a powerful microscope?
o: He didn’t want to surrender his secret.
Scientists needed to review it first.

tr: Anton van Levenguk gollandiyalik gazlama savdogari edi.
Uning hayoti 1653-yilda birinchi mikroskopini olganidan keyin o'zgara boshladi.
Bu juda oddiy mikroskop edi.
Unda tik turgan tagliqqa o'rnatilgan linza bor edi.
U kichik narsalarni katta qilib ko'rsatardi.
U gazlamani yaqindan ko'rish uchun qulay edi.
Tez orada Anton kuchliroq mikroskop yasashni orzu qila boshladi.
U undan foydalanib muhim ilmiy kashfiyot qilishni orzu qilardi.
U mashhur bo'lishni xohlardi.
O'ttiz yildan keyin u bunga erishdi.
Ko'p yillar davomida Anton mikroskop va linzalar bilan tajribalar o'tkazdi.
Oxir-oqibat u juda kuchli mikroskop yasadi.
Agar u bu g'oyani boshqalarga sotganida, u juda boyib ketardi.
Biroq Anton o'z sirini hech kimga bermaslikka harakat qildi.
Buning o'rniga u undan mashhur bo'lish uchun foydalanmoqchi edi.
Shuning uchun u o'zining maxfiy mikroskopidan tabiat olamini o'rganish uchun foydalandi.
Bir kuni u mikroskop orqali og'zidan olingan so'lakka qarayotgan edi.
So'lakda u son-sanoqsiz mayda zarrachalarni ko'rdi.
Ulardan ba'zilari harakatlanayotgan edi!
U zarrachalarni mayda organizmlar deb o'yladi.
Shuning uchun u ularni bir-biridan ajratib, har birini diqqat bilan o'rgandi.
Keyin ularni turli toifalarga ajratib tasnifladi.
Ba'zilari dumaloq edi.
Boshqalari uzun bo'lib, dumlari bor edi.
Hammasi tirik edi.
Anton juda hayajonlandi.
U endi mashhur bo'lishi mumkinligini bilardi.
U bu mayda organizmlarni ko'rgan birinchi odam edi.
Shuning uchun u organizmlarning chizmalarini chizib, Londondagi bir guruh olimlarga yubordi.
Olimlar mayda, tirik organizmlar og'zimizda yashashi mumkinligiga ishonmaydigan bilimdon odamlar edi.
Anton ulardan organizmlarni o'z ko'zlari bilan ko'rish uchun Gollandiyaga kelishlarini iltimos qildi.
Ular parom orqali Gollandiyaga borib, Anton bilan uchrashishdi.
Ular uning ishini sinchiklab ko'rib chiqishdi va u arzigulik kashfiyot qilganini tan olishdi.
Anton van Levenguk bakteriyalarni kashf etgan edi.
O'n yillab qilingan mashaqqatli mehnatdan keyin u mashhur bo'ldi.

e4|11.title: How a Singer Helped Win the War
paras: Sometimes famous people are vain. They only care about themselves. But Josephine Baker was an exception. In the 1930s and 1940s, Baker was one of the most famous women in France. She was a big part of the new jazz genre and culture and had a diverse group of fans. The French people especially loved her. And she loved France. So when World War II started, she wanted to help the nation that had given her so much. In 1940, armed German troops entered Paris. When this happened, some French people formed a secret alliance. It was called the French Resistance. The group worked for the defense of France. It helped the European and American armies fight the Germans.

Baker was an important member of the Resistance. She had three jobs. The first was to carry messages to and from other members. The messages were written in code on her sheets of music. The second was to provide shelter and supply goods to Resistance members. It would have been dangerous if the Germans found them.
Baker’s third job was the most important. Baker held concerts for European politicians and army members.
She lured them in, promising an entertaining show.
She enchanted them with her singing and dancing and got lots of applause.

But Baker was always equipped with a small notebook at these concerts. She listened for details about the war and wrote them down. Baker sorted the details and gave authoritative reports to the Resistance.

Some thought Baker’s fame would be an obstacle. The Germans knew who she was, but they didn’t think she was smart enough to work for the Resistance. So she could get information from the Germans easily. This helped the Resistance and the French army save lives and win the war.
Baker had a big impact on the Resistance’s work. She got many awards for her help. When she died, the army had a special ceremony to thank her again for her bravery.

qs.q: Which genre of music was Josephine Baker famous for?
o: She was famous for jazz music.
She was famous for blues music.
She was famous for rock music.
She was famous for country music.

qs.q: What happened when the Germans entered Paris?
o: Baker lured them back to Germany.
The French formed a secret alliance.

qs.q: What was Baker’s most important job?
o: To have a diverse group of fans

qs.q: What happened when Baker died?
o: The army had a special ceremony.
Baker had an impact on France
The Resistance found her secret codes.

tr: Ba'zan mashhur odamlar manman bo'lishadi.
Ular faqat o'zlarini o'ylashadi.
Lekin Jozefina Beyker bundan istisno edi.
1930–1940-yillarda Beyker Fransiyadagi eng mashhur ayollardan biri edi.
U yangi jaz janri va madaniyatining katta qismi edi va uning turli xil muxlislari bor edi.
Ayniqsa fransuzlar uni yaxshi ko'rishardi.
U ham Fransiyani yaxshi ko'rardi.
Shuning uchun Ikkinchi jahon urushi boshlanganida, u o'ziga shuncha ko'p narsa bergan xalqqa yordam bermoqchi bo'ldi.
1940-yilda qurollangan nemis qo'shinlari Parijga kirdi.
Shunda ba'zi fransuzlar yashirin ittifoq tuzishdi.
U Fransuz qarshilik harakati deb ataldi.
Guruh Fransiyani himoya qilish uchun ishladi.
U Yevropa va Amerika qo'shinlariga nemislarga qarshi kurashishda yordam berdi.
Beyker Qarshilik harakatining muhim a'zosi edi.
Uning uchta vazifasi bor edi.
Birinchisi, boshqa a'zolarga va ulardan xabarlar yetkazish edi.
Xabarlar uning nota varaqlariga shifr bilan yozilardi.
Ikkinchisi, Qarshilik a'zolariga boshpana berish va ularni kerakli narsalar bilan ta'minlash edi.
Agar nemislar ularni topib olishsa, bu xavfli bo'lardi.
Beykerning uchinchi vazifasi eng muhimi edi.
Beyker Yevropa siyosatchilari va harbiylari uchun konsertlar berardi.
U qiziqarli tomosha va'da qilib, ularni jalb qilardi.
U qo'shig'i va raqsi bilan ularni sehrlab, ko'p olqish olardi.
Lekin bu konsertlarda Beyker yonida doim kichik daftarcha bo'lardi.
U urush haqidagi tafsilotlarga quloq solib, ularni yozib olardi.
Beyker tafsilotlarni saralab, Qarshilik harakatiga ishonchli hisobotlar berardi.
Ba'zilar Beykerning shuhrati to'siq bo'ladi deb o'ylashardi.
Nemislar uning kimligini bilishardi, lekin u Qarshilik uchun ishlaydigan darajada aqlli deb o'ylashmasdi.
Shuning uchun u nemislardan osongina ma'lumot ola olardi.
Bu Qarshilik harakati va fransuz armiyasiga odamlar hayotini saqlab qolishga va urushda g'alaba qozonishga yordam berdi.
Beyker Qarshilik ishiga katta ta'sir ko'rsatdi.
U ko'rsatgan yordami uchun ko'plab mukofotlar oldi.
U vafot etganida, armiya uning jasorati uchun yana bir bor minnatdorlik bildirish maqsadida maxsus marosim o'tkazdi.

e4|12.title: The Sun and the North Wind
paras: The Sun and the North Wind were talking to each other in the sky. The North Wind was saying that he was better than everyone else. The Sun listened as the North Wind talked with enthusiasm about how powerful he was and how he could push something from one continent to another with one breath. He said, “I am the strongest thing in the sky.” “Really?” asked the Sun. “How do you know that you are more powerful than the stars, or the rain, or even me?”

The North Wind laughed with disrespect. He yelled, “You? That’s a joke!” This hurt the Sun. He was usually timid and did not want to cause conflict. Today he decided that he should teach the North Wind a lesson.

In the meantime, a man began walking along the avenue down on Earth. When the Sun looked down on the terrain below, he saw the man. He pointed down to the Earth and said, “Do you see that man walking below? I bet I can get his jacket off of him. Can you?”
“Of course!” the North Wind replied as he took a deep breath and filled his lungs with air. He used all of his muscles in his face and belly to blow winds at his target in succession.

The harsh air currents made the man cold. The man pulled his jacket more tightly around him. It did not come off. The Sun decided to rescue the man from the mischief of the North Wind. He said, “May I try?” Then he sent down sunlight that made the man warm. The man leaned against a tree. He took off his jacket and enjoyed the nice weather.

“You are very powerful,” the Sun said to the North Wind, “but you use violence in your bid to appear strong. You should think of an alternative. The strongest people don’t use force to get what they want.”

qs.q: Why was the North Wind so full of enthusiasm?
o: He was going on a date.

qs.q: Why did the North Wind fill his lungs with air?
o: To find an alternative to violence
To blow air at his target

qs.q: How was the North Wind causing mischief?
o: By blowing harsh wind at the man

qs.q: What happened in the meantime while the Sun and the North Wind were talking?
o: The man felt the cold air currents
The man took off his jacket.
The man began walking along the avenue.

U qichqirdi: «Senmi?
Bu hazil-ku!»

U nishoniga ketma-ket shamol esdirish uchun yuzi va qornidagi barcha muskullarini ishga soldi.
Qattiq havo oqimlari odamni sovqotirdi.
Odam kurtkasiga yanada mahkamroq o'ralib oldi.
U yechilmadi.

e4|13.title: The Big Race
paras: Alex woke up scared because of a nightmare. In it, he was running a race. Just before he reached the finish line, he fell. Alex thought that it was a subconscious way that his brain was trying to warn him about something. He was going to run in a race that day. Did the dream mean he was going to lose? He became irritable.

“Good morning,” said Alex’s mother. “I brewed some coffee and made you a special breakfast.” Alex didn’t want it. It had too much sugar. He needed something nutritious. So he prepared a meal that contained a lot of protein to maximize his energy for the race. Then his father asked, “Do you want help packing your stuff?” “No,” replied Alex. He wanted to make sure that he had all of his equipment for the race.

Alex’s family got in their van and drove to the track. When they arrived, a boy ran toward Alex. “Can I have your autograph?” asked the boy. Alex had many fans. He usually charmed everybody he spoke to. However, today Alex refused to give the boy his signature. He needed to think about his race.

He took his jump rope from his bag and started his usual workout. Maybe exercising would help him forget about the nightmare. “The race is about to start,” said the coach. Beads of sweat formed out of Alex’s sweat glands. All he could think about was his terrible dream. He thought it might be his destiny to become a loser. While he was thinking, he didn’t hear the horn that meant the race had started.

The runners zoomed toward the finish line. By the time Alex started, he lagged far behind everyone. He couldn’t run fast enough to catch up to the others. He had lost the race! He shouldn’t have let the nightmare affect him. He should have stayed focused on the race.

qs.q: What did Alex think his destiny might be?
What did Alex’s father offer to help him do?
What did the boy at the track ask Alex for?
What was Alex so affected by that he lost the race?

e4|14.title: The Brothers and the Bread
paras: Two brothers wanted to go outside and play. However, because the only bread in the house was stale, their mother told them they needed to bake fresh bread.
“I have to have the car repaired,” she said. “When I return, if the bread is ready, you can play.”

The brothers hurried to prepare the bread, but not carefully. They didn’t sift the flour. They were careless and sprinkled too much salt into the mixture. The dough needed to be soft and flexible, but the salt made it into a lump that was as hard as a brick.
The younger brother uttered a sigh. “Now we have to start again,” he said. “No, we don’t,” the older brother replied. “I’ll fix it. I just need to make the dough flat again and add water to it.”

He decided to hit the ball of dough with his fist to make it flat. But he hit it so hard that it flew right off of the table and knocked over a glass, which shattered. The dough then crashed into the kitchen window’s shutters and crumbled. Luckily, the brothers were not injured, but they did make a huge mess.
A slight mistake now became a major problem. The brothers had ruined the kitchen. Just then their mother returned. She saw the mess and became flushed with anger.
“Now you can’t play,” she said. “Instead, you have to clean the kitchen. I want this kitchen to be so clean that it may sparkle!”

The brothers cleaned the floor and expressed their sorrow to their mother. Soon, they were reconciled. But there was no bread, and it was too late to play. They realized that trying to do something quickly often makes more work.

qs.q: What made the dough into a hard lump?
What happened when the older brother hit the dough with his fist?
o: The dough flew into the oven.
The dough crumbled in his hand.

qs.q: Why was the mother flushed with anger? | a. The dough was hard. I c. The brothers sighed ___.
When were the brothers reconciled with their mother?
o: When she returned from the store

Aka-ukalar nonni tayyorlashga shoshilishdi, lekin ehtiyotkorlik bilan emas.
Ular unni elashmadi.
Ular beparvolik qilib, aralashmaga juda ko'p tuz sepib yuborishdi.
Xamir yumshoq va egiluvchan bo'lishi kerak edi, lekin tuz uni g'ishtdek qattiq bo'lakka aylantirib qo'ydi.
Kichik uka xo'rsindi.

Lekin u shunchalik qattiq urdiki, xamir stoldan uchib ketib, stakanni ag'darib yubordi va stakan chil-chil sindi.
Keyin xamir oshxona derazasining darchalariga borib urildi va ushalib ketdi.
Baxtiga, aka-ukalar jarohat olishmadi, lekin ular katta tartibsizlik qilib qo'yishdi.
Kichik xato endi katta muammoga aylandi.
Aka-ukalar oshxonani vayron qilishgan edi.
Aynan shu payt onalari qaytib keldi.

e4|15.title: Laika, the Space Dog
paras: One of the world’s most beloved space travelers was also the furriest. Laika was a little dog living on the streets of Moscow, Russia. She matured on the streets because no one would give her a home. She had to learn how to live without eating much. She found ways to keep warm in a very cold climate. Scientists thought a tough dog like Laika would do well in a project they were putting together.

In a prior launch, Russia had put the first man-made object into space. Now, scientists wanted to see if a living thing could go to space. Although many facts about space had been learned, they weren’t enough to help send humans to space safely.

Laika and two other dogs were chosen to help scientists with their research. The animals were used in a variety of tests. In the end, though, only Laika would go to space. On November 3,1957 the Sputnik 2 spaceship was due to leave Earth.

Scientists carefully applied wires to Laika’s skin to measure her body’s reactions once she got into space. Laika also wore a special leash. Without it, she would float around in the spaceship. Soon after, Laika left the planet. Scientists on Earth awaited information from the ship.

But in the midst of so much excitement, something very sad happened. Scientists were able to tell that Laika was under a lot of stress. The trip confused and scared her. Laika’s entire ship had become as hot as a furnace. Scientists were powerless to help the dog in her misery. After about five hours, Laika died. Some have complained that the little dog should never have been used in the mission. Scientists knew that she would not survive the trip. Laika was never buried, but a memorial has been established in Moscow. There are many songs and books about her, too. It seems that Laika became a hero to many people.

o: She was a beloved space traveler.

qs.q: Why did scientists apply wires to Laika’s skin?
o: To take her for the entire trip

e4|16.title: Gwen’s New Friends
paras: Gwen walked into the gym for her next class. Coach Peeves said, “Today, we’re playing basketball. The custom is to let you choose your own teams. However, we’re going to do things differently.”

The coach assigned each girl to a team. There were six girls per team. Gwen glimpsed at her teammates. She didn’t know any of them. All of her friends were on the other teams. She couldn’t believe her misfortune.

“I feel sick. May I go to the nurse?” asked Gwen. The coach could foresee Gwen’s excuses. It wasn’t the first time Gwen tried to leave class. With a stern voice, the coach said, “No.” Gwen was vehement. “I don’t know any of these girls! Let me play on another team. Please!” she pleaded.
“Gwen, don’t be disobedient. I don’t want to hear any more negative comments from you.”

Gwen had no choice. Then a girl smiled at her. “Hi, I’m Stephanie. I was in your English class last year,” she said. Gwen remembered her. “For the sake of the team, please try your best. I know you’re a good player,” said Stephanie.
When the game started, Gwen played as best as she could. She took a long shot. The ball sailed through the air and went right through the hoop!
“That was awesome!” said one of her teammates. Later, Gwen fell with a loud thump.
“Are you OK?” asked her teammates. They were worried.
She had ripped her jeans. She had scraped her knee and had a small bruise.
Gwen told her teammates, “My knee is fine, and I can stitch my pants later. Let’s keep playing!”

By the end of the game, Gwen forgot altogether that she hadn’t wanted to play, and her team won! The victory bound Gwen’s team together. She had made a lot of new friends, and they were a source of happiness for her for many years.

qs.q: Why did Coach Peeves speak to Gwen in a stern voice?
How did Gwen know Stephanie?
o: They had an English class together.

qs.q: What happened after Gwen’s shot went through the hoop?
o: Her teammate said it was awesome
She forgot about the rules altogether.

qs.q: How were the girls on Gwen’s team bound together?

e4|17.title: Kara Goes Camping
paras: “Kara, would you like to go camping with my family?” asked Tracy. Kara had never been camping before, but she decided to go anyway. That weekend, they drove to Estes Park. When they arrived, Kara looked around. She felt so far from civilization.

After they set up the camp, they went for a walk. Tracy’s father, Mr. Grieves, showed them the native plants and animals. “Look,” he said, “that’s a fox’s den. Do you see that bunch of mushrooms next to it? Don’t touch them. They contain poison.” Kara was bored. She didn’t care about nature.

As the day went on, mighty clouds soon loomed in the distance. “It looks like stormy weather,” said Tracy. “We should go back.” It suddenly began to rain. They used an umbrella to shield them from the rain. Back at the camp, they ate cold sandwiches for dinner and went to sleep.

By morning, the rain had stopped. It was a drastic change from the previous day’s weather. They folded their sleeping bags and put them in a box. Tracy closed the lid and told Kara, “Today will be fun, I promise!” Kara didn’t believe her. She missed her convenient life in the city. She was used to an urban lifestyle.

After breakfast, they went for a walk. The grass was covered with dew, and it gleamed in the sunlight. Finally, they reached a lake. Kara and Tracy waded into the water. The reeds swayed in the wind, and a flock of birds flew above. Kara felt very peaceful. That night, they made a fire. They sat around it while Mr. Grieves told scary stories. Kara had a lot of fun. Camping was a good way for friends to spend time together, she realized. The next day, it was time for them to leave. She felt sad while they exited the park. She didn’t like camping at first, but she learned how fun it could be over the weekend.

What does Kara miss about her urban lifestyle?
