Ko'p odamlar quyosh energiyasida ishlaydigan avtomobillar yechim deb o'ylashadi.
Bu turdagi transport haqida ko'proq bilish uchun universitetlar va korporativ tashkilotlar jamoalari har ikki yilda Avstraliyada quyosh mashinalari poygasi uchun yig'ilishadi.
Poyga «Jahon quyosh musobaqasi» deb ataladi.
Bu turnir ishtirokchilari o'z mashinalarini o'zlari loyihalashlari kerak.
Jamoalar barcha rejalarini sir saqlashadi.
Ular boshqa jamoalar bilan muloqot qilishmaydi, chunki poyga juda raqobatli.
Bu mashinalar oddiy mashinalarning shunchaki takomillashtirilgan va o'zgartirilgan versiyalari emas.
Ular butunlay boshqacha.
Mashinalarda faqat bir kishilik joy bor va ichi juda oddiy — hatto haydovchi o'tirishi uchun yostiqcha ham yo'q.
Bu mashinalar oddiy mashinalardan pastroq va ancha yassiroq.
Eng muhimi, mashinalarning tashqi tomoniga bir-biriga parallel joylashgan quyosh panellari o'rnatilgan.
Bu panellar quyosh nurini qabul qilib, uni elektr energiyasiga aylantiradigan materiallardan yasalgan.
Ular shu tariqa harakatlanadi.
Bu mashinalar Avstraliya hududlari bo'ylab 3000 kilometrdan ortiq masofada poyga qilishadi.
Haydovchilar qat'iy qoidalarga amal qilishlari kerak.
Ular batareyalarini quvvatlash uchun ma'lum oraliqlarda to'xtashlari shart.
Oddiy poyga mashinalaridan farqli o'laroq, ular juda tez yura olmaydi.
Ular odatiy tezlik chegaralarida haydashlari kerak.
Haydovchilar poygani tez tugatishni xohlasalar ham, bu asosiy maqsad emas.
Maqsad mashinalar oddiy haydash sharoitida qanchalik yaxshi ishlashini ko'rishdir.
Jahon quyosh musobaqasi tufayli avtomobilsozlik va haydashda yangi davr boshlanmoqda.
Odamlar quyosh mashinalari g'alati ko'ringani uchun ularni masxara qilishlari mumkin, lekin bu yo'qolib ketmaydigan hodisa.
Bu transport vositalaridagi texnologiyadan foydalanib, avtomobil ishlab chiqaruvchilar oxir-oqibat qolganlarimiz uchun ham quyosh mashinalarini yaratishadi.

e4|30.title: The Heirs
paras: Martin, Paul and Tom were brothers. They were very different, but they were consistent about two things. They couldn’t succeed in business, and they never agreed about anything. Martin was a hardworking farmer, growing organic vegetables and raising poultry. But he was disorganized and forgot to pay his bills. Paul owned a textile factory that produced clothes. He was organized, but he was greedy and took too much clothing. His wardrobe was filled with his own products. Tom was once a sergeant in the army. He ran a martial arts school, but his stance on discipline was too strong. He had almost no students.

One day, they received a telegraph saying that their father had died. They were heirs to his old farm. They planned to sell it as soon as possible, so they went to see it even though there was a terrible storm. The house didn’t look great, but there was a lot of land. There was so much, in fact, that they could barely see its boundary.

Suddenly, the storm got worse. The sheer force of the wind almost knocked them over. Martin said, “Look, it’s a typhoon!” Paul said, “No, it’s a cyclone.” Tom said, “No, it’s a tornado!” They argued until Paul began to wail and said, “Whatever it is, it’s coming right at us! We’re doomed!” The three brothers scrambled inside the old house. Martin said, “If we survive, we must stop fighting. This farm could be great if we fixed it up. With my hard work, Paul’s organization and Tom’s discipline, we could run a great business together!” The storm finally ended. And luckily, it didn’t wreck the farm.

“Just think,” Martin said, “it took the chaos of a typhoon to bring us together.” Paul replied, “You mean a cyclone brought us together.” Tom said, “Didn’t I tell you both that it was a tornado?” The brothers never agreed on what kind of storm it was, but by combining their skills, they started a successful farm.

qs.q: The brothers were consistent about what two things?
The brothers were almost knocked down by ___.
o: the sheer force of the wind

qs.q: Why wasn’t Paul’s textile factory successful?
o: He was greedy and took home clothes.
He gave away too much money.

qs.q: Who was the father’s heir?

tr: Martin, Pol va Tom aka-uka edilar.
Ular bir-biridan juda farq qilardi, lekin ikki narsada doim bir xil edilar.
Ular biznesda muvaffaqiyat qozona olmasdilar va hech qachon biror narsada kelisha olmasdilar.
Martin organik sabzavotlar yetishtiradigan va parranda boqadigan mehnatkash fermer edi.
Lekin u tartibsiz edi va hisob-kitoblarini to'lashni unutardi.
Polning kiyim ishlab chiqaradigan to'qimachilik fabrikasi bor edi.
U tartibli edi, lekin ochko'z bo'lib, juda ko'p kiyimni o'zi olib qo'yardi.
Uning kiyim shkafi o'z mahsulotlari bilan to'la edi.
Tom bir paytlar armiyada serjant bo'lgan.
U jang san'atlari maktabini boshqarardi, lekin uning intizomga bo'lgan munosabati haddan tashqari qattiq edi.
Uning deyarli o'quvchilari yo'q edi.
Bir kuni ular otalarining vafot etgani haqida telegramma olishdi.
Ular uning eski fermasining merosxo'rlari edi.
Ular uni imkon qadar tezroq sotishni rejalashtirishdi, shuning uchun dahshatli bo'ron bo'lishiga qaramay uni ko'rgani borishdi.
Uy unchalik yaxshi ko'rinmasdi, lekin yeri juda ko'p edi.
Aslida yer shunchalik ko'p ediki, uning chegarasini zo'rg'a ko'rishardi.
To'satdan bo'ron kuchaydi.
Shamolning zo'ri ularni sal qoldi yiqitib yuborishiga.
Martin dedi: «Qaranglar, bu tayfun!» Pol dedi: «Yo'q, bu siklon». Tom dedi: «Yo'q, bu tornado!»
Ular bahslashishdi, nihoyat Pol nola qilib dedi: «Nima bo'lsa ham, u to'g'ri biz tomon kelyapti!
Halok bo'ladigan bo'ldik!»
Uch aka-uka eski uy ichiga shoshib kirishdi.
Martin dedi: «Agar omon qolsak, janjallashishni bas qilishimiz kerak.
Agar bu fermani ta'mirlasak, u ajoyib bo'lishi mumkin.
Mening mehnatim, Polning tartibliligi va Tomning intizomi bilan biz birga ajoyib biznes yuritishimiz mumkin!»
Nihoyat bo'ron tugadi.
Baxtga, u fermani vayron qilmadi.

«O'ylab ko'ringlar, — dedi Martin, — bizni birlashtirish uchun tayfun to'polonining o'zi kerak bo'ldi». Pol javob berdi: «Ya'ni bizni siklon birlashtirdi demoqchisan». Tom dedi: «Ikkovingizga bu tornado deb aytmaganmidim?»
Aka-ukalar bu qanday bo'ron ekani borasida hech qachon kelisha olishmadi, lekin mahoratlarini birlashtirib, muvaffaqiyatli ferma ochishdi.

e5|1.title: The Little Mice
paras: Beth was a very resourceful and conservative mouse. She knew that winter was coming and that there would soon be a dearth of food. So she decided to make gathering food for winter her primary job. Gathering food was a grueling and mundane activity, but Beth made a deliberate effort because she knew that it was important. She allotted herself a few hours every day to collect beans. By winter, she had collected a massive pile and hid them in a cache.

Beth had a sister named Mary. Mary lacked ambition. She had fanciful ideas about how she would survive winter. She thought that food would just come to her and that she could work at her own convenience. She opted to spend the days playing and dancing, instead of gathering beans. When the final hours of autumn elapsed, Mary had only a paltry amount of food stored away.

Mary realized that her food supply was too small to last through winter. She visited her sister. Mary said, “Beth, I am in a dire situation. I didn’t gather enough food for winter. Will you let me share your beans? Please have some empathy for your sister!”

Beth thought for a moment. Then she replied, “Mary, I am truly sorry for you. But I will not give you any of my beans. Instead, I will let you have my empty bag. You can still work hard and gather enough food for the winter. It will be tedious, but you will learn the value of hard work.”
Beth’s words appalled Mary. Mary cried with outrage, “There is too much work! I won’t have any time to dance or play!”
Beth said, “It is crucial that you gather enough food. You must have sustenance before you have fun. Go now, and rectify your situation.”
Mary griped some more, but she knew that her sister was right. She took the bag and went to work gathering her own beans for the winter.

qs.q: Beth was resourceful and conservative, so she gathered a paltry pile of beans for her cache.
Beth did grueling and mundane work to overcome the dearth of food in the winter.
Beth’s reply appalled Mary and made her reply in outrage.
When the hours of autumn elapsed, Mary had a massive amount of food.

tr: Bet juda tadbirkor va ehtiyotkor sichqon edi.
U qish kelayotganini va tez orada ovqat tanqisligi bo'lishini bilardi.
Shuning uchun u qish uchun ovqat to'plashni o'zining asosiy ishi qilishga qaror qildi.
Ovqat yig'ish mashaqqatli va zerikarli mashg'ulot edi, lekin Bet buning muhimligini bilgani uchun ataylab harakat qildi.
U har kuni loviya yig'ish uchun o'ziga bir necha soat ajratdi.
Qishga kelib u ulkan uyum yig'ib, ularni yashirin omborga yashirdi.
Betning Meri ismli singlisi bor edi.
Merida intilish yo'q edi.
U qishni qanday o'tkazishi haqida xayoliy fikrlarga ega edi.
U ovqat o'z-o'zidan kelaveradi va o'ziga qulay paytda ishlashi mumkin deb o'ylardi.
U kunlarni loviya yig'ish o'rniga o'ynab, raqs tushib o'tkazishni tanladi.
Kuzning so'nggi soatlari o'tib ketganida, Merining zaxirasida juda oz ovqat bor edi.
Meri ovqat zaxirasi qishdan chiqishga yetmasligini angladi.
U opasining oldiga bordi.
Meri dedi: «Bet, men og'ir ahvoldaman.
Qish uchun yetarlicha ovqat yig'madim.
Loviyalaringdan menga ham ulashasanmi?
Iltimos, singlingga hamdardlik ko'rsat!»
Bet bir lahza o'ylab qoldi.
Keyin u javob berdi: «Meri, senga chin dildan achinaman.
Lekin senga loviyalarimdan birontasini ham bermayman.
Buning o'rniga senga bo'sh xaltamni beraman.
Sen hali ham qattiq ishlab, qish uchun yetarlicha ovqat yig'ishing mumkin.
Bu zerikarli bo'ladi, lekin mehnatning qadrini bilib olasan».
Betning so'zlari Merini dahshatga soldi.
Meri g'azab bilan qichqirdi: «Ish juda ko'p!
Raqs tushishga ham, o'ynashga ham vaqtim qolmaydi!»
Bet dedi: «Yetarlicha ovqat yig'ishing juda muhim.
Ko'ngil ochishdan oldin tirikchiliging bo'lishi kerak.
Hozir bor va ahvolingni tuzat».
Meri yana biroz noliydi, lekin opasi haq ekanini bilardi.
U xaltani olib, qish uchun o'z loviyalarini yig'ishga kirishdi.

e5|2.title: The Helpful Abbey
paras: It had not rained on the prairie for several months. Because of the drought, the climate had become very arid. There was no moisture left in the soil. No crops could grow in the dry ground. By wintertime, the people had nothing to eat.
The hungry families heard about an abbey near the mountains where food and water was still abundant. So they traveled inland, across the prairie, to the abbey.
At first only a few families arrived, seeking food and shelter. Then there was ample food. The monks fed them and let them sleep in the small cathedral.

Soon, however, more families were arriving every day. These people had to travel farther, so they were in worse condition. The rugged journey had made their clothes ragged. They were cold and tired. The tiny cathedral was soon full.

Food became scarce. The monks began to grumble. They began to speculate that there would be no food. “If more families come, we won’t make it through the winter,” said a young monk. “We must ask some of them to leave.”

The abbot heard this. “We can not do that,” he said. “It would be wrong to deprive them of food and shelter. We took an oath to help those that need help. All here are in need, so all are eligible to receive our food and shelter.”
“But we won’t have enough,” the monk said.

“That might be true, but we must help them nonetheless. We will fast,” the abbot replied. “Also, we will give our rooms in the abbey to those sleeping outside, and we will sleep in the churchyard that adjoins the cathedral.”

The monks were reluctant at first, but they did what the oldest monk said. By the end of winter, there was still enough food and shelter for everyone. They learned that sometimes helping others means you must give more help than you first expected.

qs.q: The moisture in the soil was gone because a drought made the prairie become arid.
The hungry families traveled inland to an abbey that still had abundant food.
Food was scarce, but the monks had to deprive the families nonetheless.
The rugged journey to the abbey had left many people’s clothing looking ragged.

tr: Dashtga bir necha oydan beri yomg'ir yog'magan edi.
Qurg'oqchilik tufayli iqlim juda quruq bo'lib qolgan edi.
Tuproqda zarracha ham namlik qolmagan edi.
Quruq yerda hech qanday ekin o'smasdi.
Qishga kelib odamlarning yeydigan hech narsasi qolmadi.
Och oilalar tog'lar yaqinida ovqat va suv hali ham mo'l bo'lgan bir abbatlik haqida eshitishdi.
Shuning uchun ular dasht orqali ichkariga, abbatlikka qarab yo'l olishdi.
Avvaliga ovqat va boshpana qidirib faqat bir nechta oila keldi.
O'shanda ovqat yetarli edi.
Rohiblar ularni ovqatlantirib, kichik soborda uxlashlariga ruxsat berishdi.
Biroq tez orada har kuni ko'proq oilalar kela boshladi.
Bu odamlar uzoqroqdan kelishgani uchun ahvoli yomonroq edi.
Og'ir safar ularning kiyimlarini juldur qilib yuborgan edi.
Ular sovqotgan va charchagan edilar.
Kichkina sobor tez orada to'lib ketdi.
Ovqat tanqis bo'lib qoldi.
Rohiblar to'ng'illay boshlashdi.
Ular ovqat qolmaydi deb taxmin qila boshlashdi.
«Agar yana oilalar kelsa, qishdan chiqa olmaymiz, — dedi bir yosh rohib. —
Ulardan ba'zilaridan ketishni so'rashimiz kerak».
Abbat buni eshitdi.
«Biz bunday qila olmaymiz, — dedi u. —
Ularni ovqat va boshpanadan mahrum qilish noto'g'ri bo'lardi.
Biz yordamga muhtojlarga yordam berishga qasamyod qilganmiz.
Bu yerdagilarning hammasi muhtoj, shuning uchun hammasi ovqatimiz va boshpanamizni olishga haqli».
«Lekin bizga yetmaydi-ku», dedi rohib.
«Bu rost bo'lishi mumkin, lekin shunga qaramay ularga yordam berishimiz kerak.
Biz ro'za tutamiz», deb javob berdi abbat.
«Shuningdek, abbatlikdagi xonalarimizni tashqarida uxlayotganlarga beramiz, o'zimiz esa soborga tutash cherkov hovlisida uxlaymiz».
Avvaliga rohiblar istamay turishdi, lekin eng keksa rohib aytganini qilishdi.
Qish oxiriga kelib hamma uchun hali ham yetarlicha ovqat va boshpana bor edi.
Ular ba'zan boshqalarga yordam berish dastlab kutganingizdan ko'proq yordam berishni talab qilishini bilib olishdi.

e5|3.title: The Bachelor’s Lesson
paras: A keen young bachelor had finished his studies at the university. As soon as he had received his diploma, he asserted to everyone he met that he was the smartest person in town.

“I excel at everything I study,” he said, bragging about his knowledge. “I’ve mastered calculus and physiology. I even understand the great theoretical teachings of science, such as relativity. There is nothing that I don’t know. Whether it’s the movements of celestial objects, like planets and stars, or how to harness the power of radioactive substances, I know everything.”

But actually, there was something the bachelor did not know. Though his analytic abilities were great, he failed to notice he was missing something very important in his life. One day while walking through town, the bachelor witnessed a collision between two cars. Both drivers appeared to be injured, but the scholar only stood and watched. He thought to himself, “Those idiots should have been more alert. They really must not be very competent.” He never thought the drivers needed help.
“Please help me,” said the female driver in a weak voice. “Help me, too,” said the male driver. “I’m hurt and can’t move.”
Suddenly the bachelor realized he was the only person near the accident. He quit thinking and ran to help the drivers. He carefully helped them out of their vehicles and then called an ambulance.

The drivers were saved, and the bachelor felt the best he had in his entire life. Studying mythology, sociology, and geology didn’t give him this wonderful feeling. It was the act of helping others, not his cognitive skills, that gave him this great feeling.
He had learned an important lesson. He learned that intellect isn’t everything; being helpful is just as important. “Having only a brain is not enough,” he thought. “You must also have a heart.”

qs.q: The bachelor excelled at calculus, physiology, and theoretical science, such as relativity.
He knew the movements of radioactive materials and how to harness the power of celestial objects.
The bachelor thought the drivers in the collision were not competent.
Studying mythology, sociology, and geology gave the bachelor a wonderful feeling.
The bachelor’s intellect and not his cognitive talents had made him feel this great.

tr: Bir g'ayratli yosh bo'ydoq universitetdagi o'qishini tugatgan edi.
Diplomini olishi bilanoq, u uchratgan har bir kishiga o'zini shahardagi eng aqlli odam deb ta'kidlay boshladi.
«Men o'rgangan hamma narsada ustunman», derdi u bilimi bilan maqtanib.
«Men matematik tahlil va fiziologiyani mukammal o'zlashtirganman.
Hatto nisbiylik kabi ilm-fanning buyuk nazariy ta'limotlarini ham tushunaman.
Men bilmaydigan hech narsa yo'q.
Sayyoralar va yulduzlar kabi samoviy jismlarning harakati bo'ladimi yoki radioaktiv moddalar kuchidan qanday foydalanish bo'ladimi, men hamma narsani bilaman».
Lekin aslida bo'ydoq bilmaydigan bir narsa bor edi.
Uning tahliliy qobiliyatlari zo'r bo'lsa-da, u hayotida juda muhim bir narsa yetishmasligini payqamagan edi.
Bir kuni shahar bo'ylab yurib ketayotib, bo'ydoq ikki mashinaning to'qnashuviga guvoh bo'ldi.
Ikkala haydovchi ham jarohatlanganga o'xshardi, lekin olim faqat qarab turdi.
U ichida o'yladi: «Bu ahmoqlar hushyorroq bo'lishlari kerak edi.
Ular haqiqatan ham unchalik malakali emas shekilli». U haydovchilarga yordam kerakligini xayoliga ham keltirmadi.
«Iltimos, menga yordam bering», dedi ayol haydovchi zaif ovozda.
«Menga ham yordam bering, — dedi erkak haydovchi. —
Men jarohatlandim va qimirlay olmayapman».
To'satdan bo'ydoq halokat yaqinida o'zidan boshqa hech kim yo'qligini angladi.
U o'ylashni bas qilib, haydovchilarga yordam berish uchun yugurdi.
U ularni mashinalaridan ehtiyotkorlik bilan chiqarib oldi va keyin tez yordam chaqirdi.
Haydovchilar qutqarildi va bo'ydoq o'zini butun hayotidagidan ham yaxshiroq his qildi.
Mifologiya, sotsiologiya va geologiyani o'rganish unga bunday ajoyib tuyg'u bermagan edi.
Unga bu ajoyib tuyg'uni bergan narsa uning bilish qobiliyatlari emas, balki boshqalarga yordam berish edi.
U muhim saboq olgan edi.
U aql hamma narsa emasligini, yordam berish ham xuddi shunchalik muhim ekanini bilib oldi.
«Faqat aqlning o'zi yetarli emas, — deb o'yladi u. —
Yurak ham bo'lishi kerak».

e5|4.title: The Corrupt Administrator
paras: Mr. Pig was an administrator at a big factory that made different kinds of merchandise. During a meeting at the company’s headquarters, his bosses said they wanted the factory to make more money.
“If the factory makes more money, then you will too,” his boss, Mr. Horse, told him. It was a great incentive. Pig had always wanted to be as affluent as his bosses.
Mr. Pig returned to the factory and started making changes. However, most were not very nice, and some were not legitimate.

First, he fired all his employees. Then he automated the entire factory. Machines now made everything, and the other animals, Mr. Rabbit, Mr. Sheep, and Mr. Dog had no jobs. Next, he bribed some corrupt senators into legislating special subsidies for the factory. Finally, instead of paying a company to dispose of the factory’s rubbish properly, he violated the law by throwing it into the river to save money.

At first, all the changes to the factory’s infrastructure created more revenue. But soon many stores could no longer sell the factory’s goods at retail. It seemed that the machines couldn’t make products as well as the workers. The customers were disappointed with the factory’s merchandise.

There were other problems, too. The animals had told their friends and family to stop buying the factory’s goods. Officials discovered the factory’s rubbish in the river, and when they audited the company, they discovered that Pig had manipulated the law in order to get more money.

All transactions with Pig’s factory stopped. The factory lost money, and Pig lost his job. He realized his mistakes too late. He had tried to become rich by saving money any way possible, but the cheapest way was not always the best.

qs.q: Mr. Pig bribed some corrupt senators into legislating special subsidies for his factory.
Mr. Pig violated the law by disposing of the factory’s rubbish in the ocean.
At first, changes to the factory’s infrastructure created less revenue.

tr: Mister Cho'chqa turli xil mollar ishlab chiqaradigan katta fabrikada ma'mur edi.
Kompaniyaning bosh qarorgohidagi yig'ilishda boshliqlari fabrikaning ko'proq pul topishini xohlashlarini aytishdi.
«Agar fabrika ko'proq pul topsa, sen ham ko'proq pul topasan», dedi unga boshlig'i mister Ot.
Bu katta rag'bat edi.
Cho'chqa doim boshliqlaridek badavlat bo'lishni xohlardi.
Mister Cho'chqa fabrikaga qaytib, o'zgarishlar qila boshladi.
Biroq ularning ko'pchiligi unchalik yaxshi emas, ba'zilari esa qonuniy ham emasdi.
Avval u barcha xodimlarini ishdan bo'shatdi.
Keyin u butun fabrikani avtomatlashtirdi.
Endi hamma narsani mashinalar yasardi, boshqa hayvonlar — mister Quyon, mister Qo'y va mister It esa ishsiz qolishdi.
So'ng u fabrika uchun maxsus subsidiyalar to'g'risida qonun qabul qilishlari uchun ba'zi poraxo'r senatorlarga pora berdi.
Nihoyat, pul tejash uchun fabrika chiqindilarini to'g'ri yo'q qilish maqsadida kompaniyaga pul to'lash o'rniga, u ularni daryoga tashlab, qonunni buzdi.
Avvaliga fabrika infratuzilmasidagi barcha o'zgarishlar ko'proq daromad keltirdi.
Lekin tez orada ko'plab do'konlar fabrika mollarini chakana sota olmay qolishdi.
Mashinalar mahsulotlarni ishchilarchalik yaxshi yasay olmasdi shekilli.
Xaridorlar fabrika mollaridan hafsalalari pir bo'ldi.
Boshqa muammolar ham bor edi.
Hayvonlar do'stlari va oilalariga fabrika mollarini sotib olmaslikni aytishgan edi.
Mansabdorlar daryoda fabrika chiqindilarini topishdi va kompaniyani tekshirganlarida, Cho'chqa ko'proq pul olish uchun qonunni o'z manfaatiga burganini aniqlashdi.
Cho'chqaning fabrikasi bilan barcha bitimlar to'xtatildi.
Fabrika zarar ko'rdi va Cho'chqa ishidan ayrildi.
U xatolarini juda kech angladi.
U har qanday yo'l bilan pul tejab boyimoqchi bo'lgan edi, lekin eng arzon yo'l har doim ham eng yaxshisi emas edi.

e5|5.title: A Famous Accident
paras: One of the greatest pharmaceutical discoveries happened by accident. In his haste to go on vacation, Alexander Fleming had left his laboratory in a mess. The essence of his ongoing work involved a type of bacteria. An infection caused by the bacteria was often terminal, and he was looking for a remedy. He had left the bacteria out while he was away. When he returned from vacation, he found that his lab was covered in fungus. He started cleaning up the mess. While he was cleaning, he had an impulse to examine the fungus. He saw that whenever the fungus was in close proximity to the bacteria, the bacteria died. Though he was a messy scientist, his experiments were precise. He thought that there might be some significance to the fungus. He immediately commenced an experiment to assess what had happened to the bacteria. It had either died by accident or the fungus had killed it. The subsequent tests proved it was the latter reason.
What he found astonished him. The fungus actually killed the bad bacteria. All this time, he had been looking for a synthetic material to kill the bacteria. Instead, a common fungus did the job.

He knew that something in the fungus had killed the bacteria. His next step was to find those molecules that had done it. When he found them, he extracted them and put them into a pill. The drug proved to be very effective. It also worked against other types of harmful bacteria.

The discovery received a lot of publicity. Soon after, the new drug was being used all over the world. Because of the success, the scientist was able to develop even more fabulous drugs to help people. His accidental discovery changed the world and helped save many people’s lives.

qs.q: One of the most fabulous pharmaceutical discoveries was an accident.
The essence of the scientist’s ongoing work was to find a remedy for a terminal infection.
The infection caused by the bacteria he was working on was not terminal.
Fleming examined the fungus on an impulse.
Whenever the synthetic material was far from the bacteria, the bacteria died.

tr: Eng buyuk farmatsevtik kashfiyotlardan biri tasodifan sodir bo'lgan.
Ta'tilga shoshilib, Aleksandr Fleming laboratoriyasini tartibsiz holda qoldirib ketgan edi.
Uning davom etayotgan ishining mohiyati bakteriyaning bir turi bilan bog'liq edi.
Bu bakteriya keltirib chiqargan infeksiya ko'pincha o'limga olib kelardi va u davo qidirayotgan edi.
U yo'qligida bakteriyani ochiq qoldirib ketgan edi.
Ta'tildan qaytganida, u laboratoriyasini zamburug' qoplab olganini ko'rdi.
U tartibsizlikni tozalay boshladi.
Tozalayotganda unda zamburug'ni tekshirib ko'rish istagi paydo bo'ldi.
U zamburug' bakteriyaga yaqin bo'lgan har bir joyda bakteriya nobud bo'lganini ko'rdi.
U tartibsiz olim bo'lsa-da, tajribalari aniq edi.
U zamburug'ning qandaydir ahamiyati bo'lishi mumkin deb o'yladi.
U darhol bakteriyaga nima bo'lganini baholash uchun tajriba boshladi.
U yo tasodifan nobud bo'lgan, yoki uni zamburug' o'ldirgan edi.
Keyingi sinovlar ikkinchi sabab to'g'ri ekanini isbotladi.
U topgan narsa uni hayratda qoldirdi.
Zamburug' haqiqatan ham zararli bakteriyani o'ldirardi.
Shu vaqtgacha u bakteriyani o'ldirish uchun sintetik modda qidirib kelgan edi.
Buning o'rniga ishni oddiy zamburug' bajardi.
U zamburug'dagi nimadir bakteriyani o'ldirganini bilardi.
Uning keyingi qadami buni qilgan molekulalarni topish edi.
Ularni topgach, u ularni ajratib olib, tabletkaga joyladi.
Dori juda samarali ekani isbotlandi.
U boshqa turdagi zararli bakteriyalarga qarshi ham ta'sir qildi.
Kashfiyot katta shov-shuvga sabab bo'ldi.
Ko'p o'tmay yangi dori butun dunyoda qo'llanila boshlandi.
Bu muvaffaqiyat tufayli olim odamlarga yordam beradigan yanada ajoyib dorilarni ishlab chiqa oldi.
Uning tasodifiy kashfiyoti dunyoni o'zgartirdi va ko'plab odamlarning hayotini saqlab qolishga yordam berdi.

e5|6.title: The Island
paras: “Where am I?” Bob thought to himself when he woke up on a peculiar beach. “I can’t remember what happened.” There had been a bad storm, and Bob’s fishing boat sunk. He washed ashore on a small island, but he had gotten hurt during the storm. He had a terrible migraine, and he had a fracture in his shoulder. He felt awful. But he had a strong desire to make it home to his spouse and children. He had to tolerate all the pain and devise a plan. Bob stood up and looked around. “I’ll walk to a higher altitude, so I can see everything around me,” thought Bob. “Maybe I’ll gain some insight about this island and find something to help me escape.” As he walked along a mountain ridge, he noticed that the tall indigenous trees looked sturdy and thick. Bob got a brilliant idea. He could build a raft! He cut down some leaves and tree limbs. Even though his shoulder injury impaired his ability to carry the materials, he slowly dragged them down the mountain until he reached the coastline. Bob was a proficient builder. He used his building expertise to line up the limbs and tie them together with long vines. When the raft was finished, Bob was happy with his work. “This will bring me home to my family,” he said with a smile.

At last, Bob was ready to implement his escape plan. With all his might, he thrust the raft into the water. He climbed on and began the quest to find his way home. Bob smiled again, and thought, “I’m glad I kept a good attitude. It prevented the pain from deterring me from my plan. Optimism and ambition make anything possible.”
Slowly, he floated out to sea. In a few days, he made it to shore and ran home to see his happy family.

qs.q: Bob had a migraine and a shoulder fracture when he awoke on the peculiar beach.
Bob implemented a plan to bring his spouse and children to the island.
The indigenous tree limbs impaired Bob’s ability to carry the materials.
Bob was proficient in building, and he used his expertise to build the raft.
Bob thrust the raft into the water to begin his quest.

tr: «Men qayerdaman?» deb o'yladi Bob g'alati bir sohilda uyg'onganida.
«Nima bo'lganini eslay olmayapman».
Kuchli bo'ron bo'lgan va Bobning baliq ovlash qayig'i cho'kib ketgan edi.
Uni to'lqin kichik orol sohiliga chiqarib tashladi, lekin u bo'ron paytida jarohatlangan edi.
Uning boshi qattiq og'rirdi va yelkasi singan edi.
U o'zini juda yomon his qildi.
Lekin uning turmush o'rtog'i va bolalari oldiga uyga yetib borish istagi kuchli edi.
U barcha og'riqlarga chidab, reja tuzishi kerak edi.
Bob o'rnidan turib, atrofga qaradi.
«Atrofimdagi hamma narsani ko'rish uchun balandroq joyga chiqaman, — deb o'yladi Bob. —
Balki bu orol haqida biror narsani tushunib, qochishga yordam beradigan narsa topib olarman».
Tog' tizmasi bo'ylab yurarkan, u baland mahalliy daraxtlar mustahkam va yo'g'on ekanini payqadi.
Bobning miyasiga ajoyib fikr keldi.
U sol yasashi mumkin edi!
U bir nechta barg va daraxt shoxlarini kesib oldi.
Yelkasidagi jarohat materiallarni ko'tarishiga xalal bersa-da, u ularni sohilga yetguncha tog'dan sekin-asta sudrab tushdi.
Bob mohir quruvchi edi.
U qurilishdagi mahoratidan foydalanib, shoxlarni bir qatorga terdi va ularni uzun chirmovuqlar bilan bir-biriga bog'ladi.
Sol tayyor bo'lgach, Bob o'z ishidan mamnun bo'ldi.
«Bu meni oilam oldiga olib boradi», dedi u jilmayib.
Nihoyat, Bob qochish rejasini amalga oshirishga tayyor edi.
U bor kuchi bilan solni suvga itarib tushirdi.
U unga chiqib, uyga yo'l topish izlanishini boshladi.
Bob yana jilmayib o'yladi: «Yaxshi kayfiyatni saqlaganimdan xursandman.
Bu og'riq meni rejamdan qaytarishiga yo'l qo'ymadi.
Nekbinlik va intilish har qanday narsani mumkin qiladi».
U asta-sekin dengizga suzib ketdi.
Bir necha kundan keyin u qirg'oqqa yetib keldi va baxtiyor oilasini ko'rish uchun uyiga yugurdi.

e5|7.title: Small World
paras: Even though people can’t see me, I’m an important part of Earth’s biosphere. Scientists who study ecology know that I was the first life form on Earth. There is more of my kind than any other plant or animal in the world. Without me, other plants and animals would not even exist. I am a protist, and my tiny body is made up of one single cell.

In my small world, things can be absolutely bizarre. Unlike most aquatic plants and animals, I don’t need a temperate climate. I have a very high tolerance for extreme conditions. Right now, I’m swimming around in a bucket of boiling water! The temperature is 150 degrees Celsius, but I feel comfortable. I have coarse hairs called cilia that help me swim around in here. I move my cilia in a repetitive motion for the duration of my swim. I can not go very fast, though. It takes me about five minutes to swim a distance of just one millimeter!

When I get hungry, I look for tiny, vulnerable parasites. I swim up to one and swallow it whole. I digest things much like people do. I have an organ that works just like a human stomach. After I eat, I release nitrogen gas. Nitrogen is a prominent gas in the earth’s atmosphere. Other plants and animals need my nitrogen to survive.

My reproductive ability is my most unique trait. I don’t need a companion to mate with. Instead, I undergo a process called fission, where my own nucleus splits in half. An exact copy of my nucleus is made, which forms into another protist. It really is an impressive feat. I can create an infinite number of new protists all by myself!

qs.q: Protists have a high tolerance for temperate conditions.
Things in an aquatic protist’s world can be absolutely bizarre.
A protist splits its companion’s nucleus in fission.
Coarse cilia move in a repetitive motion for the duration of a protist’s swim.
An infinite number of new protists can be created by the impressive feat of fission.

tr: Odamlar meni ko'ra olmasalar ham, men Yer biosferasining muhim qismiman.
Ekologiyani o'rganadigan olimlar Yerdagi birinchi hayot shakli men bo'lganimni bilishadi.
Dunyoda mening turimdagilar boshqa har qanday o'simlik yoki hayvondan ko'ra ko'proq.
Mensiz boshqa o'simliklar va hayvonlar umuman mavjud bo'lmasdi.
Men protistman va mening mitti tanam bitta hujayradan iborat.
Mening kichik dunyomda narsalar mutlaqo g'aroyib bo'lishi mumkin.
Ko'pchilik suv o'simliklari va hayvonlaridan farqli o'laroq, menga mo''tadil iqlim kerak emas.
Men keskin sharoitlarga juda chidamliman.
Hozir men bir chelak qaynoq suvda suzib yuribman!
Harorat 150 daraja Selsiy, lekin men o'zimni qulay his qilyapman.
Mening bu yerda suzib yurishimga yordam beradigan kiprikchalar deb ataladigan dag'al tuklarim bor.
Suzish davomida kiprikchalarimni takroriy harakat bilan qimirlatib turaman.
Lekin men juda tez yura olmayman.
Atigi bir millimetr masofani suzib o'tishim uchun taxminan besh daqiqa kerak bo'ladi!
Qornim ochganda, mayda, himoyasiz parazitlarni qidiraman.
Ulardan biriga suzib borib, uni butunligicha yutib yuboraman.
Men narsalarni xuddi odamlar kabi hazm qilaman.
Menda xuddi inson oshqozoni kabi ishlaydigan a'zo bor.
Ovqatlangandan keyin azot gazini chiqaraman.
Azot Yer atmosferasidagi asosiy gazlardan biri.
Boshqa o'simliklar va hayvonlarga yashash uchun mening azotim kerak.
Ko'payish qobiliyatim mening eng noyob xususiyatim.
Menga juftlashish uchun sherik kerak emas.
Buning o'rniga men bo'linish deb ataladigan jarayonni boshdan kechiraman, bunda o'z yadroim ikkiga bo'linadi.
Yadroimning aynan nusxasi hosil bo'ladi va u boshqa protistga aylanadi.
Bu haqiqatan ham ta'sirli yutuq.
Men yolg'iz o'zim cheksiz miqdorda yangi protistlar yarata olaman!

e5|8.title: Becoming a Healer
paras: Years ago, I worked at a small health clinic in a remote country. I had gone there to treat an obscure syndrome. It attacked people’s lungs, causing them to need a respirator to breathe. I was trying out a new medication to treat these people instead of using a respirator. If I was successful, I would become famous.

Everything was going fine until war broke out in a nearby country. Many people from that country fled the hostile invading army. The army wanted to dominate the people, but the people didn’t want to be oppressed. So they walked hundreds of miles across barren land to get away.

Some of these people came to our clinic for treatment. I talked with them and learned of their difficulties. They did not beg or complain. I was impressed by their dignity. There was one woman I will never forget. Her son suffered from malnutrition and stomach pain, and she didn’t know what to do. Neither did I. I was not adept at treating malnutrition. Nonetheless, when I saw her sadness, I knew I had to help her son.

The woman had been feeding her son bread and water. She had a misconception that it would be enough for him. However, I knew that he needed to eat vegetables, too. So I took her outside and showed her a dense patch of edible plants. I taught her how to dig up the roots, peel them, and cook them for her son. I explained that she should increase her son’s intake of these vegetables. Likewise, she should strive to get him some meat once a week to help him regain his strength.

I sent her off with a prescription for some pain medicine, but she also left my office with some new culinary skills. A few weeks later, she returned to tell me her son was healthy again. As thanks, she gave me a beautiful ceramic bowl.

qs.q: The hostile doctor wanted to dominate and oppress the people.
The doctor was not adept at treating malnutrition before meeting the mother and her son.
The doctor showed the woman a dense patch of barren land.
The woman gave the doctor a ceramic bowl to show off her pottery skills.

tr: Yillar oldin men olis bir mamlakatdagi kichik tibbiyot klinikasida ishlaganman.
Men u yerga noma'lum bir sindromni davolash uchun borgan edim.
U odamlarning o'pkasiga hujum qilib, nafas olishlari uchun respirator kerak bo'lib qolishiga sabab bo'lardi.
Men bu odamlarni respirator o'rniga davolash uchun yangi dorini sinab ko'rayotgan edim.
Agar muvaffaqiyatga erishsam, mashhur bo'lib ketardim.
Qo'shni mamlakatda urush boshlangunga qadar hammasi yaxshi ketayotgan edi.
O'sha mamlakatdan ko'p odamlar bostirib kirgan dushman qo'shinidan qochishdi.
Qo'shin xalqni bo'ysundirmoqchi edi, lekin xalq zulm ostida qolishni xohlamasdi.
Shuning uchun ular qochib qutulish uchun yuzlab mil cho'l yerlarni piyoda kesib o'tishdi.
Bu odamlarning ba'zilari davolanish uchun bizning klinikamizga kelishdi.
Men ular bilan gaplashib, qiyinchiliklari haqida bilib oldim.
Ular tilanchilik ham, shikoyat ham qilishmadi.
Ularning o'zlarini munosib tutishlari meni hayratga soldi.
Hech qachon unutmaydigan bir ayol bor edi.
Uning o'g'li to'yib ovqatlanmaslik va oshqozon og'rig'idan aziyat chekardi va u nima qilishni bilmasdi.
Men ham bilmasdim.
Men to'yib ovqatlanmaslikni davolashda mohir emasdim.
Shunday bo'lsa-da, uning qayg'usini ko'rib, o'g'liga yordam berishim kerakligini bildim.
Ayol o'g'lini non va suv bilan boqayotgan edi.
U bu o'g'li uchun yetarli bo'ladi degan noto'g'ri tushunchada edi.
Biroq men uning sabzavot ham yeyishi kerakligini bilardim.
Shuning uchun men uni tashqariga olib chiqib, yeyiladigan o'simliklarning zich o'sgan joyini ko'rsatdim.
Men unga ildizlarni qanday kovlab olish, tozalash va o'g'li uchun pishirishni o'rgatdim.
Men unga o'g'lining bu sabzavotlarni iste'mol qilishini ko'paytirish kerakligini tushuntirdim.
Xuddi shunday, kuchini tiklashga yordam berish uchun haftada bir marta unga go'sht topishga harakat qilishi kerak edi.
Men uni og'riq qoldiruvchi dori uchun retsept bilan jo'natdim, lekin u kabinetimdan yangi oshpazlik ko'nikmalari bilan ham chiqib ketdi.
Bir necha haftadan keyin u qaytib kelib, o'g'li yana sog'ayganini aytdi.
Minnatdorchilik sifatida u menga chiroyli sopol kosa sovg'a qildi.

e5|9.title: The Weaving Machine
paras: Mr. Joseph Franklin invented a machine that could weave cloth. It wove faster and straighter than anyone could weave by hand. He decided to take it to two cities on a peninsula, Netherton and Wilton. In these cities, a large proportion of the people worked in weaving. Joseph felt sure he could sell his machine there.
Joseph first took his machine to the mayor of Netherton. “Think of the money you will earn from this machine!” Joseph said to him.
But the mayor was a benevolent man. He knew about the people’s dependence on weaving for their livelihood. If he bought the machine, the people would lose their jobs. So he refused to buy it.

Joseph said, “We are no longer in the medieval age! Soon everything will be made by machines. Cloth made by hand will soon be obsolete. If you don’t change your archaic ways, your town’s income will diminish!”
But the mayor said, “I don’t like capitalism. Don’t impose your radical ideas on my town. Go away!”

So Joseph took his machine to the mayor at Wilton. This mayor thought Joseph’s machine was spectacular and spent a long time looking at its different components made of brass. The mayor couldn’t refute the fact that the machine had drawbacks that would affect the people’s jobs. But he realized the machine could bring money and prestige. So he ordered Joseph to build twenty of them.

Within a year, Wilton was a wealthy city, famous for its wonderful cloth. People no longer wove but worked in managerial jobs at cloth factories instead. Nobody bought the cloth from Netherton anymore. The people of Netherton became poor and hungry.

Finally, the mayor of Netherton called Joseph and said, “Now I realize that your machine is not just a passing fad. To succeed in business, we must be willing to change.” He then ordered twenty weaving machines.
After that, both Netherton and Wilton became rich cities, famous throughout the land for their wonderful cloth.

qs.q: Joseph thought the mayor of Netherton’s ideas were medieval and archaic.
The mayor of Wilton refuted the fact that the machine had drawbacks.
In Wilton, the people who used to weave got managerial positions at the factories.
In the end, capitalism brought prestige to both cities.

tr: Mister Jozef Franklin mato to'qiy oladigan mashina ixtiro qildi.
U har qanday odam qo'lda to'qiganidan tezroq va tekisroq to'qirdi.
U uni yarim oroldagi ikki shahar — Neterton va Viltonga olib borishga qaror qildi.
Bu shaharlarda aholining katta qismi to'qimachilikda ishlardi.
Jozef mashinasini u yerda sota olishiga amin edi.
Jozef avval mashinasini Neterton meri oldiga olib bordi.
«Bu mashinadan qancha pul topishingizni o'ylab ko'ring!» dedi Jozef unga.
Lekin mer saxovatli odam edi.
U odamlarning tirikchiligi to'qimachilikka bog'liq ekanini bilardi.
Agar u mashinani sotib olsa, odamlar ishsiz qolardi.
Shuning uchun u uni sotib olishdan bosh tortdi.
Jozef dedi: «Biz endi o'rta asrlarda yashamayapmiz!
Tez orada hamma narsani mashinalar yasaydi.
Qo'lda to'qilgan mato tez orada eskirib qoladi.
Agar eskicha usullaringizni o'zgartirmasangiz, shahringiz daromadi kamayadi!»
Lekin mer dedi: «Men kapitalizmni yoqtirmayman.
O'zingizning radikal g'oyalaringizni mening shahrimga tiqishtirmang.
Keting!»
Shunday qilib, Jozef mashinasini Vilton meri oldiga olib bordi.
Bu mer Jozefning mashinasini ajoyib deb hisobladi va uning jezdan yasalgan turli qismlarini uzoq vaqt ko'zdan kechirdi.
Mer mashinaning odamlar ishiga ta'sir qiladigan kamchiliklari borligini inkor eta olmadi.
Lekin u mashina pul va obro' keltirishi mumkinligini angladi.
Shuning uchun u Jozefga ulardan yigirmatasini yasashni buyurdi.
Bir yil ichida Vilton ajoyib matolari bilan mashhur boy shaharga aylandi.
Odamlar endi to'qimas, balki mato fabrikalarida boshqaruv lavozimlarida ishlashardi.
Netertondan endi hech kim mato sotib olmasdi.
Neterton aholisi kambag'al va och bo'lib qoldi.
Nihoyat, Neterton meri Jozefni chaqirib dedi: «Endi tushundim, sizning mashinangiz shunchaki o'tkinchi moda emas ekan.
Biznesda muvaffaqiyat qozonish uchun o'zgarishga tayyor bo'lishimiz kerak».
Keyin u yigirmata to'quv mashinasiga buyurtma berdi.
Shundan so'ng Neterton ham, Vilton ham ajoyib matolari bilan butun mamlakatga mashhur boy shaharlarga aylandi.

e5|10.title: Life on the Farm
paras: Bill was an excellent capitalist. He financed a large aviation enterprise that made a lot of money. He knew how to maximize monetary gains in every business deal he made. Bill had one big problem, though. He was unhappy all the time. Bill knew that he had to do something about it, or he would be depressed for the rest of his life. One day, Bill was in his office when he heard a knock at the door. “Come in!” Bill said loudly.

His accountant, Jane, walked in. Jane said, “Sir, I haven’t seen you smile in a year. What are you so sad about? Your company is doing very well.” Bill told her, “I’m indifferent about my company’s success. I have contempt toward my job. I just want to do something I enjoy. I’ve always loved growing plants as a hobby. I’m going to quit my job and become a farmer!” “You’re crazy!” Jane said.

“I don’t think so,” Bill replied. “I want the simplicity of a life on a farm. I’m tired of all this stress. Farming will make me happy.” The very next day, Bill carried out the preliminary task of buying land and tools. Then he got to work. He sowed many types of seeds. He planted soy, cabbage, carrots, and onions.

“The upcoming summer is going to be very dry,” thought Bill. “I need to irrigate my crops as a precaution in case it doesn’t rain enough.” He took his spade and dug a ditch down the middle of his farm. “Water from the stream will flow down the ditch and saturate the soil around every plant,” Bill thought.
Bill dedicated himself to farming. After a year, his farm looked exquisite. Most importantly, Bill was happy. He finally had the life he always wanted.

qs.q: Bill could maximize monetary gains in the aviation enterprise that he financed.
Bill was indifferent about the farm’s success.
Bill irrigated his crops as a precaution for the upcoming rain in summer.
Bill dug a ditch with a spade.

tr: Bill zo'r kapitalist edi.
U ko'p pul keltirgan yirik aviatsiya korxonasini moliyalashtirgan edi.
U tuzgan har bir bitimda moliyaviy foydani qanday maksimal darajada oshirishni bilardi.
Biroq Billning bitta katta muammosi bor edi.
U doim baxtsiz edi.
Bill bu borada nimadir qilishi kerakligini bilardi, aks holda umrining oxirigacha tushkunlikda qolardi.
Bir kuni Bill kabinetida o'tirganida, eshik taqillaganini eshitdi.
«Kiring!» dedi Bill baland ovozda.
Uning buxgalteri Jeyn kirib keldi.
Jeyn dedi: «Janob, bir yildan beri jilmayganingizni ko'rmadim.
Nimadan bunchalik g'amginsiz?
Kompaniyangiz juda yaxshi ishlayapti». Bill unga dedi: «Kompaniyamning muvaffaqiyati menga befarq.
Men ishimdan nafratlanaman.
Men shunchaki o'zimga yoqadigan ish qilmoqchiman.
Men doim o'simlik o'stirishni sevimli mashg'ulot sifatida yaxshi ko'rganman.
Ishimdan ketib, fermer bo'laman!»
«Siz aqldan ozibsiz!» dedi Jeyn.
«Menimcha, unday emas, — deb javob berdi Bill. —
Men fermadagi hayotning soddaligini xohlayman.
Bu stresslardan charchadim.
Dehqonchilik meni baxtli qiladi».
Ertasi kuniyoq Bill yer va asboblar sotib olishdek dastlabki vazifani bajardi.
Keyin u ishga kirishdi.
U ko'p turdagi urug'larni sepdi.
U soya, karam, sabzi va piyoz ekdi.
«Kelayotgan yoz juda quruq bo'ladi, — deb o'yladi Bill. —
Yomg'ir yetarlicha yog'masa, ehtiyot chorasi sifatida ekinlarimni sug'orishim kerak».
U belkuragini olib, fermasining o'rtasidan ariq qazidi.
«Soydan kelgan suv ariq bo'ylab oqib, har bir o'simlik atrofidagi tuproqni namga to'yintiradi», deb o'yladi Bill.
Bill o'zini dehqonchilikka bag'ishladi.
Bir yildan keyin uning fermasi juda chiroyli ko'rinardi.
Eng muhimi, Bill baxtli edi.
Nihoyat u doim orzu qilgan hayotiga erishdi.

e5|11.title: Beethoven’s Gift
paras: Beethoven was a great composer of classical music in the 1800s. Many biographies have been written that narrate his dominance in the music world. But do you know what really makes him special? Even though millions of people got to hear his multiple masterpieces, he never did. Beethoven wrote his best pieces after he went completely deaf!

His partiality toward classical music developed when he was very young. He wasn’t interested in anything else as a child. When he was five, he learned how to play the piano. From then, nothing could stop his passion for writing and playing music.

When Beethoven was twenty, he began to lose his hearing. He got acute, spontaneous pains in his ears. His hearing kept getting worse over time. It was inevitable that he would eventually lose it altogether. It was very hard for him to keep writing music. He lost the virtue of patience, and he became notorious for his aggression. Still, he never stopped trying. His passion for music compelled him to keep performing even after he went deaf. He couldn’t hear himself play, but he knew that his creations sounded gorgeous.

His final concert was held at a huge banquet. He gave the musicians a cue, and they began to play. He directed the concert with all his heart. He couldn’t hear the music, but he said that he could feel it. Overall, the performance was one of the finest in history. When it was over, he turned to the crowd. They clapped and cheered wildly. In that beautiful moment, the applause boosted his emotions, and he began to cry.
In 1827, he suffered from lead poisoning. He didn’t survive the sickness, but his music did because great music never becomes outdated. Even though Beethoven is gone, his legacy will live on forever.

qs.q: People have narrated biographies about Beethoven’s dominance.
Beethoven created multiple masterpieces that sounded gorgeous.
It was inevitable that Beethoven would lose his virtue altogether.
Beethoven became notorious for his aggression.
Beethoven’s legacy lives on because great music is outdated.

tr: Betxoven 1800-yillardagi buyuk klassik musiqa bastakori edi.
Uning musiqa olamidagi ustunligi haqida hikoya qiluvchi ko'plab tarjimai hollar yozilgan.
Lekin uni haqiqatan ham nima alohida qilishini bilasizmi?
Millionlab odamlar uning ko'plab durdona asarlarini eshitgan bo'lsa-da, uning o'zi ularni hech qachon eshitmagan.
Betxoven o'zining eng yaxshi asarlarini butunlay kar bo'lib qolganidan keyin yozgan!
Uning klassik musiqaga moyilligi juda yoshligida shakllangan.
Bolaligida u boshqa hech narsaga qiziqmasdi.
Besh yoshida u pianino chalishni o'rgandi.
Shundan beri musiqa yozish va ijro etishga bo'lgan ishtiyoqini hech narsa to'xtata olmadi.
Betxoven yigirma yoshga to'lganida eshitish qobiliyatini yo'qota boshladi.
Uning quloqlarida to'satdan o'tkir og'riqlar paydo bo'lardi.
Vaqt o'tishi bilan eshitishi tobora yomonlashib bordi.
Oxir-oqibat uni butunlay yo'qotishi muqarrar edi.
Uning uchun musiqa yozishni davom ettirish juda qiyin edi.
U sabr fazilatini yo'qotdi va tajovuzkorligi bilan mashhur bo'lib ketdi.
Shunday bo'lsa-da, u hech qachon urinishdan to'xtamadi.
Musiqaga bo'lgan ishtiyoqi uni kar bo'lib qolganidan keyin ham ijro etishda davom etishga majbur qildi.
U o'zining chalayotganini eshita olmasdi, lekin yaratganlari ajoyib yangrashini bilardi.
Uning so'nggi konserti katta ziyofatda o'tkazildi.
U musiqachilarga ishora berdi va ular chala boshlashdi.
U konsertni butun qalbi bilan boshqardi.
U musiqani eshita olmasdi, lekin uni his qila olishini aytardi.
Umuman olganda, bu ijro tarixdagi eng zo'rlaridan biri bo'ldi.
U tugagach, u olomonga o'girildi.
Ular qarsak chalib, qizg'in olqishlashdi.
O'sha go'zal lahzada olqishlar uning his-tuyg'ularini qo'zg'atib yubordi va u yig'lay boshladi.
1827-yilda u qo'rg'oshindan zaharlandi.
U kasallikdan omon qolmadi, lekin uning musiqasi omon qoldi, chunki buyuk musiqa hech qachon eskirmaydi.
Betxoven bu dunyodan o'tgan bo'lsa ham, uning merosi abadiy yashaydi.

e5|12.title: Brothers
paras: John and Mark were brothers, but they were quite different people. Mark looked very masculine. He had a mustache and was very muscular. He was a sculptor. He made things out of stone. Mark was a good artist, but he was not very intelligent.

John looked nothing like his brother. He was small and weak, but he was very smart. John was an undergraduate in college, and he studied anthropology and history. He knew a lot about ancient cultures. The brothers loved each other very much, but they thought they had nothing in common.

One day, the mayor appointed Mark to build a monument: a statue of Egyptian Pharaoh, Tut. Mark agreed to do the job, but he had a problem. He had no idea who Pharaoh Tut was! However, he thought he had the competence to build a good statue anyway. He made some crude measurements and sculpted a statue of a very old man with a tattoo on his chest. Mark was proud of his work, but when John saw the statue, he laughed aloud. “What’s so funny?” Mark asked.

John replied, “Your ignorance makes me laugh. Don’t you know that Tut was only a teenager when he was pharaoh? Let me help you. I’ll supervise your work. I’ll give you feedback, and we’ll make this a great monument.”
Mark got another cube of stone. John told him what Tut looked like. “Make him tall with good posture,” John said. “And make sure there is symmetry in his body.”

Mark conferred with John about every detail. For ten consecutive hours, the brothers worked. At last, the finished statue was situated in front of the museum. Everyone applauded the brothers’ good work.
“We worked together very well. I guess we are compatible after all,” Mark said. John replied, “I agree! When we combine our talents, we are capable of greatness.”

qs.q: Mark’s masculine features included a mustache and a muscular body.
John laughed at Pharaoh Tut’s ignorance.
John appointed himself to supervise Mark’s work and give him feedback about posture and symmetry.
Mark made crude measurements and situated a tattoo on his original monument’s chest.
John was an undergraduate who studied sculpture and anthropology.

tr: Jon va Mark aka-uka edilar, lekin ular bir-biridan ancha farq qiladigan odamlar edi.
Mark juda erkakshoda ko'rinardi.
Uning mo'ylovi bor edi va juda muskulli edi.
U haykaltarosh edi.
U toshdan buyumlar yasardi.
Mark yaxshi rassom edi, lekin unchalik aqlli emasdi.
Jon akasiga umuman o'xshamasdi.
U kichkina va zaif edi, lekin juda aqlli edi.
Jon kollejda bakalavriat talabasi edi va antropologiya hamda tarixni o'rganardi.
U qadimiy madaniyatlar haqida ko'p narsa bilardi.
Aka-ukalar bir-birini juda yaxshi ko'rishardi, lekin ularning hech qanday umumiyligi yo'q deb o'ylashardi.
Bir kuni mer Markni yodgorlik — Misr fir'avni Tut haykalini yasashga tayinladi.
Mark bu ishni qilishga rozi bo'ldi, lekin uning bir muammosi bor edi.
U fir'avn Tut kim ekanini umuman bilmasdi!
Biroq u baribir yaxshi haykal yasashga qobiliyati yetadi deb o'yladi.
U bir nechta qo'pol o'lchovlar oldi va ko'kragida tatuirovkasi bor juda keksa odamning haykalini yo'ndi.
Mark o'z ishi bilan faxrlanardi, lekin Jon haykalni ko'rganida, ovoz chiqarib kulib yubordi.
«Nimasi kulgili?» deb so'radi Mark.
Jon javob berdi: «Sening bilimsizliging meni kuldiryapti.
Tut fir'avn bo'lganida endigina o'smir bo'lganini bilmaysanmi?
Kel, senga yordam beray.
Men ishingni nazorat qilaman.
Senga fikr bildirib turaman va biz buni ajoyib yodgorlikka aylantiramiz».
Mark yana bir kub tosh oldi.
Jon unga Tut qanday ko'rinishda bo'lganini aytib berdi.
«Uni qaddi-qomati kelishgan, baland bo'yli qilib yasa, — dedi Jon. —
Va tanasida simmetriya bo'lishiga e'tibor ber».
Mark har bir tafsilot bo'yicha Jon bilan maslahatlashdi.
Aka-ukalar ketma-ket o'n soat ishlashdi.
Nihoyat, tayyor haykal muzey oldiga o'rnatildi.
Hamma aka-ukalarning yaxshi ishini olqishladi.
«Biz birga juda yaxshi ishladik.
Menimcha, biz bir-birimizga mos ekanmiz», dedi Mark.
Jon javob berdi: «Qo'shilaman!
Iste'dodlarimizni birlashtirsak, buyuk ishlarga qodirmiz».

e5|13.title: The Old Hound
paras: Elvis was a dog that loved to run. He possessed all the criteria to be a great racing dog. He had long legs, lean muscles, and a strong heart. He was so good that he never lost a race in the northern hemisphere. Spectators who bet on dog races always picked Elvis to win.

After ten years of racing, however, Elvis was getting old. His faculties were not as strong as they used to be. His owner got upset when Elvis started losing. Elvis’s owner wasn’t a considerate person. He degraded the dog all the time. Finally, his owner decided to get rid of him. He threw Elvis in his car and took him to the middle of the forest. He tossed him out and drove away. Elvis was cold and scared. He decided to follow a brook into the city. Elvis soon found out that the city was a big and impersonal place. Everywhere he went, he saw signs that said, “No Dogs Allowed.” Pedestrians yelled at him. He was sad and hungry and was ready to give up when he heard a soft voice say, “What a beautiful hound!” Elvis looked up and saw an old woman. She said, “You’re entitled to a better life than this. I can take you to a sanctuary for old dogs like you. I’ll cater to all your needs. Would you like to come with me?”

The woman escorted Elvis to a beautiful facility. There was a sign on the external door that said, “Dogs Welcome!” The interior of the building was painted blue, and shiny ornaments hung from the ceiling. There was a heap of tasty bones and bread crusts for consumption. Elvis learned there were kind people in the world after all.

qs.q: Elvis possessed the criteria to be a spectator.
Elvis’s owner was not considerate, and he degraded the dog.
Elvis followed the brook to the big, impersonal city where pedestrians yelled at him.
In the interior of the facility, there was a heap of ornaments and bread crusts for consumption.
The old woman wanted to cater to Elvis’s needs at the sanctuary for old hounds.

tr: Elvis yugurishni yaxshi ko'radigan it edi.
Unda zo'r poyga iti bo'lishning barcha mezonlari bor edi.
Uning oyoqlari uzun, muskullari pishiq va yuragi baquvvat edi.
U shunchalik zo'r ediki, shimoliy yarimsharda birorta ham poygada yutqazmagan edi.
It poygalariga pul tikadigan tomoshabinlar doim g'olib sifatida Elvisni tanlashardi.
Biroq o'n yillik poygadan keyin Elvis qarib qolayotgan edi.
Uning qobiliyatlari avvalgidek kuchli emasdi.
Elvis yutqaza boshlaganida, egasining jahli chiqdi.
Elvisning egasi o'ylovchi odam emasdi.
U itni doim kamsitardi.
Nihoyat, egasi undan qutulishga qaror qildi.
U Elvisni mashinasiga tashlab, o'rmonning o'rtasiga olib bordi.
U uni uloqtirib tashladi va mashinasini haydab ketdi.
Elvis sovqotgan va qo'rqib ketgan edi.
U shaharga soy bo'ylab borishga qaror qildi.
Elvis tez orada shahar katta va befarq joy ekanini bilib oldi.
U qayerga bormasin, «Itlar kirishi mumkin emas» degan yozuvlarni ko'rdi. Piyodalar unga baqirishardi.
U g'amgin va och edi va «Qanday chiroyli ov iti!» degan mayin ovozni eshitganda, taslim bo'lishga tayyor edi.
Elvis boshini ko'tarib, bir kampirni ko'rdi.
U dedi: «Sen bundan yaxshiroq hayotga haqlisan.
Seni senga o'xshagan qari itlar uchun boshpanaga olib bora olaman.
Barcha ehtiyojlaringni qondiraman.
Men bilan borishni xohlaysanmi?»
Ayol Elvisni chiroyli bir muassasaga olib bordi.
Tashqi eshikda «Itlar, xush kelibsiz!» degan yozuv bor edi.
Binoning ichi ko'k rangga bo'yalgan va shiftdan yaltiroq bezaklar osilib turardi.
Yeyish uchun bir uyum mazali suyaklar va non qobiqlari bor edi.
Elvis dunyoda baribir mehribon odamlar borligini bilib oldi.

e5|14.title: Day Without Sight
paras: On Friday afternoon, Sam’s teacher had a special assignment.

“Next week, we’ll be studying humanitarian efforts around the world since the time of the Renaissance, including those to help the blind,” she said. “Over the weekend, I want each of you to wear a blindfold for an entire day. The premise of this experiment is that it will help you understand what it’s like to be blind,” she said.

Sam was a skeptic. He really didn’t think the assignment would be too challenging. On Saturday morning, Sam took a piece of cloth and tied it around his head to cover his eyes. Then he went into the kitchen for breakfast. He heard the voices of his parents and brothers but couldn’t specify where each voice was coming from. He thought about how important hearing is for blind people.

“Could you pass me the newspaper, please?” he asked. Just then, he remembered he couldn’t see the words on the page. He wondered if Braille newspapers were ever made. After finishing breakfast, his brothers asked him to play soccer. As he followed them, he accidentally walked into the baker’s rack. He also found that he couldn’t play soccer. He wouldn’t be able to coordinate his actions without being able to see. Without his optic senses, he had no spatial awareness. Furthermore, he couldn’t do simultaneous activities because he had to make sure he was safe first.

He sat on the lawn. Suddenly, he realized that though he couldn’t see, his other senses worked perfectly fine. In fact, he began to realize new and different aspects of common objects. For example, he took a flower bud and felt it with his finger. He realized for the first time that it seemed to be covered with wax.

His hypothesis about being blind was disproved. The informative experiment had an imprint on him. It showed him sight was an asset that should be appreciated and taught him to revere the talents of blind people.

qs.q: Sam’s teacher asked the students to wear a blindfold for a whole day.
Sam thought the assignment would be very hard.
Sam walked into the baker’s rack.
Sam played soccer with his brothers.
The experiment taught Sam to respect blind people.

tr: Juma kuni tushdan keyin Semning o'qituvchisi maxsus topshiriq berdi.
«Kelasi hafta biz Uyg'onish davridan beri dunyo bo'ylab amalga oshirilgan insonparvarlik sa'y-harakatlarini, jumladan ko'zi ojizlarga yordam berishga qaratilganlarini o'rganamiz», dedi u.
«Dam olish kunlari har biringiz butun bir kun ko'zingizni bog'lab yurishingizni xohlayman.
Bu tajribaning asosiy g'oyasi shundaki, u sizga ko'zi ojiz bo'lish qanday ekanini tushunishga yordam beradi», dedi u.
Sem shubhachi edi.
U topshiriq unchalik qiyin bo'ladi deb o'ylamagan edi.
Shanba kuni ertalab Sem bir parcha mato olib, ko'zlarini yopish uchun boshiga bog'ladi.
Keyin u nonushta qilish uchun oshxonaga kirdi.
U ota-onasi va akalarining ovozlarini eshitdi, lekin har bir ovoz qayerdan kelayotganini aniqlay olmadi.
U ko'zi ojizlar uchun eshitish qanchalik muhim ekani haqida o'yladi.

Aynan shu payt u sahifadagi so'zlarni ko'ra olmasligini esladi.
U Brayl yozuvidagi gazetalar umuman chiqarilganmikan, deb o'yladi.
Nonushtani tugatgandan keyin akalari uni futbol o'ynashga chaqirishdi.
Ularning ortidan borayotib, u bexosdan novvoyning javoniga urilib ketdi.
U futbol ham o'ynay olmasligini bildi.
U ko'rmasdan harakatlarini muvofiqlashtira olmasdi.
Ko'rish sezgisi bo'lmagani uchun u fazoni idrok eta olmasdi.
Bundan tashqari, u bir vaqtning o'zida bir nechta ish qila olmasdi, chunki avval xavfsizligiga ishonch hosil qilishi kerak edi.

To'satdan u ko'ra olmasa ham, boshqa sezgilari mutlaqo yaxshi ishlayotganini angladi.
Aslida u oddiy narsalarning yangi va boshqacha jihatlarini anglay boshladi.
Masalan, u gul g'unchasini olib, barmog'i bilan paypasladi.
U ilk bor u mum bilan qoplanganga o'xshashini angladi.
Uning ko'zi ojiz bo'lish haqidagi farazi rad etildi.

U unga ko'rish qadrlanishi kerak bo'lgan boylik ekanini ko'rsatdi va ko'zi ojiz odamlarning iste'dodlarini hurmat qilishni o'rgatdi.

e5|15.title: The Big Ship
paras: Ernest looked at his fleet of ships. Usually, he used them for his firm, which imported marble statues from other countries. But today he was going fishing. And the ship he chose was his favorite. It had an elaborate painting on the side that showed a naval battle. It also had some new updates to its computer system. His favorite ship’s latest acquisition was a device with a small grid to show the ship’s exact location. This new accessory kept Ernest from getting lost.

At daybreak, Ernest happily sailed the temperate waters until he was far from land. Then he saw a small boat in the distance. There was an old man standing next to its mast. He was waving his arms in the air. There was also a boy with his head hanging over the boat’s edge. Ernest inferred that the boy was suffering from nausea. Both of their clothes were saturated with sea water. Ernest assumed that they were in trouble. Most people never realized, but Ernest had an innate desire to help people. He began sailing toward them, eager to facilitate their rescue and thus solve their dilemma.

As he got closer to the boat, he was shocked by its simplicity. The boat’s wood looked no stronger than cardboard, and the equipment was old. Still, there were several large fish in a pouch in the boat.
Ernest threw a large package onto the boat. He yelled, “Here! You can inflate this boat to get you back to land.”
“Get out of here!” screamed the old man.
Ernest was confused. “Don’t you need help?” he asked. “Your ship doesn’t seem adequate enough to sail so far away from land.”
“You’ve just scared away a huge fish,” the boy said. “We waved to let you know you were too close to us.”
Ernest turned around and headed home. He learned that it’s better not to help unless asked to. Otherwise, you might not help anyone at all.

qs.q: Ernest usually used his fleet for his firm that imported marble statues from other countries.
His favorite ship had updated accessories like a new grid.
When Ernest saw the old man standing next to the mast, he decided to go home.
Ernest offered the man and the boy a boat that inflates to facilitate their rescue.
Ernest had the innate desire to make a lot of money.

tr: Ernest o'zining kemalar flotiga qaradi.
Odatda u ulardan boshqa mamlakatlardan marmar haykallar olib keladigan firmasi uchun foydalanardi.
Lekin bugun u baliq oviga ketayotgan edi.
U tanlagan kema esa uning eng sevimlisi edi.
Uning yon tomonida dengiz jangi tasvirlangan murakkab rasm bor edi.
Uning kompyuter tizimida ham bir nechta yangilanishlar bor edi.
Sevimli kemasiga so'nggi qo'shilgan narsa kemaning aniq joylashuvini ko'rsatuvchi kichik to'rli qurilma edi.
Bu yangi moslama Ernestning adashib qolishidan saqlardi.
Tong otganda Ernest quruqlikdan ancha uzoqlashguncha mo''tadil suvlarda xursand suzib bordi.
Keyin u uzoqda kichik qayiqni ko'rdi.
Uning machtasi yonida bir chol turardi.
U qo'llarini havoda silkitayotgan edi.
Boshi qayiq chetidan osilib turgan bir bola ham bor edi.
Ernest bolaning ko'ngli aynayotganini taxmin qildi.
Ikkalasining ham kiyimlari dengiz suviga shilta bo'lgan edi.
Ernest ularni muammoga duch kelgan deb o'yladi.
Ko'pchilik buni hech qachon sezmagan, lekin Ernestda odamlarga yordam berishga tug'ma ishtiyoq bor edi.
U ularni qutqarishga ko'maklashish va shu tariqa muammolarini hal qilishga intilib, ular tomon suzib keta boshladi.
Qayiqqa yaqinlashganda, uning soddaligidan hayratda qoldi.
Qayiqning yog'ochi kartondan mustahkamroq ko'rinmasdi va jihozlari eski edi.
Shunday bo'lsa-da, qayiqdagi xaltada bir nechta katta baliq bor edi.
Ernest qayiqqa katta bir tugunni otdi.
U qichqirdi: «Mana!
Quruqlikka qaytish uchun bu qayiqni damlab olishingiz mumkin».
«Yo'qol bu yerdan!» deb qichqirdi chol.
Ernest gangib qoldi.
«Sizga yordam kerak emasmi? — deb so'radi u. —
Qayig'ingiz quruqlikdan bunchalik uzoqqa suzish uchun yetarli emasga o'xshaydi».
«Siz hozirgina ulkan baliqni qo'rqitib yubordingiz, — dedi bola. —
Biz sizga juda yaqin kelib qolganingizni bildirish uchun qo'l silkitgandik».
Ernest burilib, uyiga yo'l oldi.
U so'ralmaguncha yordam bermagan ma'qul ekanini bilib oldi.
Aks holda, umuman hech kimga yordam bermasligingiz mumkin.

e5|16.title: The History of Parachutes
paras: Scientists who study archeology say that there may be some evidence of prehistoric parachutes. But the first written history of the device comes from China about 2,100 years ago. Scientists cite an ancient book that describes parachutes. However, there is no archeological evidence that proves that an actual parachute was ever made. Later, people from northern Africa and Italy also had ideas about a similar invention. In fact, a Leonardo Da Vinci’s drawing corresponds closely with the modern parachute design!

In 1783, French scientist Sebastian Lenormand invented the first modern parachute. Sebastian brainstormed with other scientists to come up with a way to help people jump safely out of burning buildings. He thought the solution was to give people an object to restrict their speed while they traveled toward the ground. Many people thought that he was up to some kind of fraud, but Sebastian had a lot of integrity.

His budget was limited, so he first tested his theory by using two umbrellas. He jumped out of a tree and found that the umbrellas worked. Next, he refined his invention. Rather than using umbrellas, he knit a large parachute. Finally, he jumped off a tall building on a French estate and landed safely in the courtyard.

Sebastian’s work gave another man an idea. Jean-Pierre Blanchard had a different outlook than Sebastian. He was a hot air balloon addict. He was one of the first people to ride in a hot air balloon powered by hydrogen gas. He was a proponent of using parachutes to exit from hot air balloons. Starting in 1785, he used his dog to show that animals could land safely from hot air balloons by using parachutes.

Then, in 1793, he was faced with a chaotic experience. The hot air balloon he was riding in burst and started to fall. He was forced to use a parachute himself. And much to his relief, it saved his life.

qs.q: Archeological evidence shows there were prehistoric parachutes in China.
Archeology experts cite an old Chinese book that describes a parachute that corresponds with modern parachutes.
Sebastian brainstormed with scientists to invent a device that would allow people to jump from buildings safely.
On Sebastian’s first jump, he used a large blanket to restrict his speed as he traveled to the ground.
Jean-Pierre was a hot air balloon addict.

tr: Arxeologiyani o'rganadigan olimlar tarixdan oldingi parashyutlarning ba'zi dalillari bo'lishi mumkinligini aytishadi.
Lekin bu moslamaning birinchi yozma tarixi taxminan 2100 yil oldin Xitoydan kelgan.
Olimlar parashyutlarni tasvirlagan qadimiy kitobga iqtibos keltirishadi.
Biroq haqiqiy parashyut qachondir yasalganini isbotlaydigan arxeologik dalil yo'q.
Keyinchalik Shimoliy Afrika va Italiyadan bo'lgan odamlarda ham shunga o'xshash ixtiro haqida g'oyalar bo'lgan.
Aslida Leonardo da Vinchining chizmasi zamonaviy parashyut tuzilishiga juda mos keladi!
