Sebastyan odamlarga yonayotgan binolardan xavfsiz sakrashga yordam beradigan usulni topish uchun boshqa olimlar bilan fikr almashdi.
U yechim odamlarga yerga tushayotganda tezligini cheklaydigan narsa berishdir deb o'yladi.
Ko'p odamlar uni qandaydir firibgarlik qilyapti deb o'ylashdi, lekin Sebastyan juda halol odam edi.
Uning mablag'i cheklangan edi, shuning uchun u avval nazariyasini ikkita soyabon yordamida sinab ko'rdi.
U daraxtdan sakradi va soyabonlar ish berganini ko'rdi.
Keyin u ixtirosini takomillashtirdi.
Soyabonlar o'rniga u katta parashyut to'qidi.
Nihoyat, u Fransiyadagi bir mulkdagi baland binodan sakrab, hovliga eson-omon tushdi.
Sebastyanning ishi boshqa bir odamga g'oya berdi.
Jan-Pyer Blanshar Sebastyandan boshqacha qarashga ega edi.
U havo shariga mukkasidan ketgan edi.
U vodorod gazi bilan ishlaydigan havo sharida uchgan birinchi odamlardan biri edi.
U havo sharlaridan chiqish uchun parashyutlardan foydalanish tarafdori edi.
1785-yildan boshlab u hayvonlar parashyut yordamida havo sharlaridan eson-omon tusha olishini ko'rsatish uchun itidan foydalandi.
Keyin, 1793-yilda u to's-to'polon voqeaga duch keldi.
U uchayotgan havo shari yorilib, pastga qulay boshladi.
U parashyutdan o'zi foydalanishga majbur bo'ldi.
Va uni yengil torttirib, parashyut uning hayotini saqlab qoldi.

e5|17.title: “I Didn’t Do It!”
paras: Billy was in big trouble. The day before, a donor gave the school a painting with a sports theme. It showed a referee congratulating two athletes. The principal hung the painting in front of the office, hoping that it would be a stimulus for students to play sports. The next morning, however, the painting was destroyed. There was graffiti on it, and it had many holes in it. The worst part was that one of Billy’s fellow students said she thought she saw Billy do it!

But Billy didn’t do it. The principal called Billy’s parents and said, “Billy won’t tell us the truth. He’s a chronic liar, and he ruined the painting. If you don’t pay for it, we’ll terminate his education here.”

Billy’s parents didn’t have enough money to pay for the painting and for his tuition. But Billy’s parents had an idea. That afternoon, they went to see Mr. Meyers, an attorney. “Mr. Meyers, my son has been implicated in a crime he says he didn’t do,” Billy’s father said. “Everybody believes the gossip. Even some of our own kin think he did it!” “I believe you. My suspicion is that the tape from the security cameras will show who really did it,” said Mr. Meyers.

The next day, Mr. Meyers received a packet with the videotape from the school. It showed another student who resembled Billy walking up to the painting and writing on it. Then the student took a knife by the shaft and started to stab large holes in it. Finally, he severed the rope that held up the painting, and it fell to the floor.
Mr. Meyers showed the tape to the principal. “Clearly, that’s not Billy,” he said. “This boy is actually responsible and needs some discipline.”
Billy was happy that someone believed him. He said to Mr. Meyers, “When I graduate and go to university, I will major in law, so I can be a guardian of justice like you!”

qs.q: A donor gave the school a painting with a sports theme as a stimulus for students to play sports.
The painting showed a referee congratulating two athletes.
Billy was implicated in the crime because a fellow student received a packet with a videotape showing him doing it.
The principal threatened to terminate Billy’s education if his parents didn’t pay his tuition.

tr: Billi katta muammoga duch kelgan edi.
Bir kun oldin bir homiy maktabga sport mavzusidagi rasm sovg'a qilgan edi.
Unda hakam ikki sportchini tabriklayotgani tasvirlangan edi.
Direktor rasmni o'quvchilarni sport bilan shug'ullanishga undaydi degan umidda idora oldiga osib qo'ydi.
Biroq ertasi kuni ertalab rasm vayron qilingan edi.
Unga graffiti chizilgan va unda ko'plab teshiklar bor edi.
Eng yomoni, Billining sinfdoshlaridan biri buni Billi qilganini ko'rgandek bo'lganini aytdi!
Lekin buni Billi qilmagan edi.
Direktor Billining ota-onasiga qo'ng'iroq qilib dedi: «Billi bizga rostini aytmayapti.
U surunkali yolg'onchi va rasmni u buzgan.
Agar uning pulini to'lamasangiz, uning bu yerdagi o'qishini to'xtatamiz».
Billining ota-onasida rasm uchun ham, o'qish puli uchun ham to'lashga yetadigan pul yo'q edi.
Lekin Billining ota-onasida bir fikr bor edi.
O'sha kuni tushdan keyin ular advokat mister Mayersning oldiga borishdi.
«Mister Mayers, o'g'lim o'zi qilmaganini aytayotgan jinoyatga aralashtirilmoqda», dedi Billining otasi.
«Hamma g'iybatga ishonyapti.
Hatto ba'zi qarindoshlarimiz ham buni u qilgan deb o'ylashyapti!»
«Men sizga ishonaman.
Mening gumonimcha, xavfsizlik kameralari yozuvi buni aslida kim qilganini ko'rsatadi», dedi mister Mayers.
Ertasi kuni mister Mayers maktabdan videoyozuv solingan paket oldi.
Unda Billiga o'xshagan boshqa bir o'quvchining rasm oldiga kelib, unga yozayotgani ko'rinardi.
Keyin o'quvchi pichoqni sopidan ushlab, unda katta teshiklar ocha boshladi.
Nihoyat, u rasmni ushlab turgan arqonni kesdi va rasm polga tushdi.
Mister Mayers yozuvni direktorga ko'rsatdi.
«Ko'rinib turibdiki, bu Billi emas, — dedi u. —
Aslida bu bola aybdor va unga biroz tarbiya kerak».
Billi kimdir unga ishonganidan xursand bo'ldi.
U mister Mayersga dedi: «Maktabni bitirib, universitetga kirganimda huquqshunoslik yo'nalishini tanlayman, toki sizdek adolat posboni bo'lay!»

e5|18.title: The Soldier’s Decision
paras: A soldier was captured while fighting in an enemy king’s land. It was well known that this king would make captives fight one another. This was commonplace during his reign. For these fights, the king had built several large arenas. He often awarded the winners by setting them free or even having them join his elite army corps.

The soldier, however, decided he had seen too much violence. He now felt that all life was sacred. The night before his first match, he made a risky decision. He decided that he would not engage in combat. He knew he may never be set free, but it was a decision that he was willing to accept.
In the morning, he was led from the prisoners’ compound to one of the king’s arenas. A gate coated in rust stood between him and the auditorium’s floor. He was worried, but he knew what he had to do.

When the gate opened, he calmly walked to the center of the arena and sat. He started to meditate. His foe Darius, who was skilled in the realm of sword fighting and was typically not very aggressive, would not fight the quiet soldier until he attacked Darius first. Darius tried to provoke him by hacking at the air close to his head with his sword. But the soldier was not distracted. He sat quietly, as if he were dumb, and looked calmly up at the sky. Even when Darius nicked him on the cheek with the edge of his sword, the soldier did not move.
At last he threw down his sword and shield and gave up.
“I can’t fight someone who refuses to fight me!” Darius shouted to the king.
The king was very impressed with the soldier.

Never in any battle had he seen someone so brave. As a result, he gave the peaceful soldier amnesty. The soldier’s actions proved to the king and everyone in the arena that peace was more powerful than fighting.

qs.q: The prisoner was led from the arena to the compound.
While he meditated, the soldier was distracted by his opponent.
The king gave the brave soldier amnesty and made him join his elite army corps.
The quiet soldier felt that all life was sacred.

tr: Bir askar dushman qirolning yurtida jang qilayotganda asirga tushdi.
Bu qirol asirlarni bir-biri bilan jang qildirishi hammaga ma'lum edi.
Uning hukmronligi davrida bu odatiy hol edi.
Bu janglar uchun qirol bir nechta katta arena qurdirgan edi.
U ko'pincha g'oliblarni ozod qilib yoki hatto o'zining saralangan qo'shin korpusiga qo'shib taqdirlardi.
Biroq askar o'zi juda ko'p zo'ravonlik ko'rganiga qaror qildi.
Endi u har qanday hayot muqaddas deb hisoblardi.
Birinchi jangidan oldingi kechasi u xavfli qaror qabul qildi.
U jangga kirishmaslikka qaror qildi.
U hech qachon ozod qilinmasligi mumkinligini bilardi, lekin bu u qabul qilishga tayyor bo'lgan qaror edi.
Ertalab uni asirlar qo'rg'onidan qirolning arenalaridan biriga olib borishdi.
U bilan tomoshagoh maydoni o'rtasida zang bosgan darvoza turardi.
U xavotirda edi, lekin nima qilishi kerakligini bilardi.
Darvoza ochilganda, u bamaylixotir arena markaziga borib o'tirdi.
U meditatsiya qila boshladi.
Qilichbozlik sohasida mohir va odatda unchalik tajovuzkor bo'lmagan raqibi Doro jim askar o'ziga birinchi hujum qilmaguncha u bilan jang qilmasdi.
Doro qilichi bilan uning boshi yonidagi havoni chopib, uni g'azablantirmoqchi bo'ldi.
Lekin askarning diqqati chalg'imadi.
U xuddi soqovdek jim o'tirar va osmonga xotirjam qarab turardi.
Hatto Doro qilichining tig'i bilan uning yonog'ini tirnab qo'yganida ham askar qimirlamadi.
Nihoyat u qilichi va qalqonini tashlab, taslim bo'ldi.
«Men bilan jang qilishdan bosh tortgan odam bilan jang qila olmayman!» deb qichqirdi Doro qirolga.
Qirol askardan juda ta'sirlandi.
U hech bir jangda bunchalik jasur odamni ko'rmagan edi.
Natijada u tinchliksevar askarga avf berdi.
Askarning xatti-harakati qirolga va arenadagi hammaga tinchlik jangdan qudratliroq ekanini isbotladi.

e5|19.title: Jane’s Pride
paras: Jane and her father, Mike, owned a secondhand boat. They called it “High Hopes.” The two loved to spend time together on the ocean and would often go on long fishing trips. Mike taught Jane how to perform important tasks. Jane learned how to steer the boat and adjust the sails. She learned how to put grease on the intricate gears of the motor. She learned how to submerge the anchor and secure it by putting a rope in a slot. Jane liked helping her father, but she thought that she wasn’t very good at it. Sometimes, she omitted important steps and made frequent mistakes. Jane thought she wasn’t capable of manual labor.

Mike wanted to prove to her that she was indeed capable and important. He thought of a tactic to test Jane’s skills in the context of a catastrophe. He hid under the deck and pretended to be trapped. He shouted, “Jane, I can’t get out! You have to get back to the dock and find help!”

Jane began to panic. She thought she might make her usual mistakes, which would precipitate a disaster. However, she had to listen to her dad and act accordingly. She pulled up the anchor with all of her might. She remembered to overlap the sails to offset the wind. She steered the boat around buoys where the water was shallow.
When they got to shore, Mike came out from under the deck.
Jane said, “I thought you were trapped!”
Mike laughed. He said, “It wasn’t a genuine emergency. I distorted the truth to test your abilities. Look at what a great job you did getting the boat home safely! I knew you could do it.”
To honor his daughter, Mike decided to rename his boat.
He designated it “Jane’s Pride” and painted the name on the fore of the ship. Jane finally had something to be proud of.

qs.q: Jane and her father owned a new boat called “High Hopes.”
Jane thought she wasn’t very good at helping her father.
Mike was really trapped under the deck.
Jane steered the boat around buoys where the water was shallow.
Mike renamed the boat “Jane’s Pride.”

tr: Jeyn va uning otasi Maykning ishlatilgan qayig'i bor edi.
Ular uni «Katta umidlar» deb atashardi.
Ikkalasi okeanda birga vaqt o'tkazishni yaxshi ko'rishardi va tez-tez uzoq baliq oviga chiqishardi.
Mayk Jeynga muhim ishlarni qanday bajarishni o'rgatdi.
Jeyn qayiqni boshqarishni va yelkanlarni sozlashni o'rgandi.
U motorning murakkab tishli g'ildiraklariga moy surtishni o'rgandi.
U langarni suvga tushirib, arqonni teshikka o'tkazib mahkamlashni o'rgandi.
Jeynga otasiga yordam berish yoqardi, lekin u buni unchalik yaxshi uddalay olmaydi deb o'ylardi.
Ba'zan u muhim qadamlarni tashlab ketar va tez-tez xato qilardi.
Jeyn o'zini qo'l mehnatiga qodir emas deb hisoblardi.
Mayk unga haqiqatan ham qodir va muhim ekanini isbotlamoqchi edi.
U falokat sharoitida Jeynning mahoratini sinash uchun bir usul o'ylab topdi.
U paluba ostiga yashirinib, o'zini qamalib qolgandek ko'rsatdi.
U qichqirdi: «Jeyn, men chiqa olmayapman!
Iskalaga qaytib, yordam topishing kerak!»
Jeyn vahimaga tusha boshladi.
U odatdagi xatolarini qilib, falokatni tezlashtirib qo'yishim mumkin deb o'yladi.
Biroq u dadasining gapiga quloq solib, shunga mos harakat qilishi kerak edi.
U bor kuchi bilan langarni tortib chiqardi.
U shamolni muvozanatlash uchun yelkanlarni bir-birining ustiga tushirishni esladi.
U qayiqni suv sayoz bo'lgan joylardagi buyalar atrofidan aylantirib boshqardi.
Ular qirg'oqqa yetganlarida, Mayk paluba ostidan chiqdi.
Jeyn dedi: «Men sizni qamalib qolgan deb o'ylagandim!»
Mayk kulib yubordi.
U dedi: «Bu haqiqiy favqulodda holat emasdi.
Qobiliyatlaringni sinash uchun haqiqatni biroz buzib ko'rsatdim.
Qara, qayiqni uyga eson-omon olib kelishda qanday zo'r ish qilding!
Men sen buni uddalay olishingni bilardim».
Qizini sharaflash uchun Mayk qayig'ining nomini o'zgartirishga qaror qildi.
U uni «Jeynning faxri» deb atadi va nomni kemaning old qismiga bo'yab yozdi.
Nihoyat Jeynning faxrlanadigan narsasi bor edi.

e5|20.title: Microchips
paras: The bond between humans and computers is becoming more intimate than ever before. Scientists are now putting microchips inside people’s bodies. They are made up of compressed electrical circuits that can detect and record data about the body. They are tiny, but they hold the equivalent amount of data as most computers.

A microchip is put to use inside a person with a simple procedure. First, a doctor must put data about the patient onto a chip. Input about the person’s age, race, gender, and medical history is stored on the chip. The second phase of the process involves putting it in the person’s skin. The doctor pinches a piece of skin and cuts a tiny hole with a tool shaped like a spiral. The chip is inserted, and the skin is allowed to heal. At last, it begins the task of putting data into its database.

Microchips scan the patient’s body to record what is happening on the quantum level. They can find problems with the person’s metabolism and organs. They can also detect viral infections. They can find the aggregate number of immune and infected cells and present the results in a ratio. They can even tell doctors what type of antibiotic to give to the patient!

To recover the chip’s data, the doctor uses a special magnet that copies it. This way, the doctor can put the information from the chip onto a computer. Then they can find out exactly what is wrong with the person.

The idea of putting chips in humans is still very new. However, it is now becoming more prevalent. Scientists and doctors are hopeful about the future uses of microchips. Someday, all new babies might get a microchip soon after they are born. Doctors will be able to know about any problems from the very beginning. It is obvious that medicine and computers complement each other well.

qs.q: Microchips are made up of compressed electrical circuits.
Chips express the aggregate number of immune and intimate cells in a ratio.
Chips detect viral infections and problems with people’s metabolism.
A doctor pinches the skin and cuts a hole with a tool shaped like a spiral.
Putting antibiotics in humans is becoming more prevalent.

tr: Inson va kompyuter o'rtasidagi bog'liqlik avvalgidan ham yaqinroq bo'lib bormoqda.
Olimlar endi odamlarning tanasiga mikrochiplar joylashtirmoqda.
Ular tana haqidagi ma'lumotlarni aniqlab, yozib oladigan zichlashtirilgan elektr sxemalaridan iborat.
Ular mitti, lekin ko'pchilik kompyuterlar sig'diradigan miqdordagi ma'lumotni saqlaydi.
Mikrochip odam tanasiga oddiy muolaja orqali joylashtiriladi.
Avval shifokor bemor haqidagi ma'lumotlarni chipga yozishi kerak.
Odamning yoshi, irqi, jinsi va kasallik tarixi haqidagi ma'lumotlar chipda saqlanadi.
Jarayonning ikkinchi bosqichi uni odamning terisiga joylashtirishdan iborat.
Shifokor terining bir qismini chimchilab ushlaydi va spiral shaklidagi asbob bilan mitti teshik ochadi.
Chip kiritiladi va terining bitishiga imkon beriladi.
Nihoyat, u ma'lumotlarni o'z bazasiga kiritish vazifasini boshlaydi.
Mikrochiplar kvant darajasida nima sodir bo'layotganini yozib olish uchun bemorning tanasini skanerlaydi.
Ular odamning moddalar almashinuvi va a'zolaridagi muammolarni topa oladi.
Ular virusli infeksiyalarni ham aniqlay oladi.
Ular immun va zararlangan hujayralarning umumiy sonini topib, natijalarni nisbat ko'rinishida taqdim eta oladi.
Ular hatto shifokorlarga bemorga qanday antibiotik berish kerakligini ham aytib bera oladi!
Chip ma'lumotlarini olish uchun shifokor ularni ko'chirib oladigan maxsus magnitdan foydalanadi.
Shu tariqa shifokor chipdagi ma'lumotni kompyuterga o'tkaza oladi.
Keyin ular odamda aynan nima muammo borligini aniqlay olishadi.
Odamlarga chip joylashtirish g'oyasi hali juda yangi.
Biroq u endi tobora keng tarqalmoqda.
Olimlar va shifokorlar mikrochiplardan kelajakda foydalanishga umid bilan qarashmoqda.
Qachondir barcha chaqaloqlarga tug'ilganidan ko'p o'tmay mikrochip qo'yilishi mumkin.
Shifokorlar har qanday muammo haqida boshidanoq bila olishadi.
Tibbiyot va kompyuterlar bir-birini yaxshi to'ldirishi aniq.

e5|21.title: The Twins
paras: Katie and Alice were twins. They were so alike that few people could tell the siblings apart. They were almost like clones. They even used the same colloquial language as each other. They were best friends.

But the twins’ attributes were not all identical. Alice liked humanities, and Katie was a good linguist. One summer, Katie decided to be a participant at a summer camp in France. Alice wasn’t interested in the French language, so she didn’t go. But she felt angry that Katie wanted to spend the summer away from her.

Two months later, Katie returned. Alice dashed to the airport to greet her sister. But when Alice saw Katie, she was astounded. Katie was now bilingual, and she looked completely different! She was wearing nice clothes, cosmetics and looked skinnier. Alice felt very messy next to her. She was just wearing a fluorescent t-shirt, and her hair had knots in it. When Alice asked Katie about France, Katie was vague and didn’t say much. It made Alice furious and filled her with disgust because in the past they’d always told each other everything. Now there was a huge gulf between them. Over the weeks, the sisters spoke even less.

Two months later, it was the twins’ birthday. All their lives, they’d had a ritual. Before their birthday, they’d talk all night long. That night, Alice came into Katie’s bedroom. “I’m sorry I haven’t spoken much lately,” Katie said.
“I understand. You have new friends now,” said Alice, angrily.

Katie said, “My French friends don’t write much nowadays. For a while, I thought they were more exciting than my friends at home. But I was wrong. You’re my sister, and you’ll always be my best friend.”

Alice said, “I’m sorry, too. I wanted our relationship to stay the same forever. But it’s totally plausible for twins to have different interests. We can still be best friends without being together all the time.”

qs.q: The girls looked like clones, but they used different colloquial language.
The twins’ attributes were different in that Katie was bilingual and Alice liked humanities.
Alice’s hair was in knots when she dashed to the airport to meet her sister.
Alice was astounded when she saw Katie wearing a fluorescent t-shirt.

tr: Keyti va Elis egizak edilar.
Ular shunchalik o'xshash ediki, opa-singilni kamdan-kam odam ajrata olardi.
Ular deyarli klonlardek edilar.
Ular hatto bir xil so'zlashuv tilidan foydalanishardi.
Ular eng yaqin dugonalar edilar.
Lekin egizaklarning xususiyatlari to'liq bir xil emasdi.
Elis gumanitar fanlarni yoqtirardi, Keyti esa yaxshi tilshunos edi.
Bir yozda Keyti Fransiyadagi yozgi lagerda qatnashishga qaror qildi.
Elis fransuz tiliga qiziqmasdi, shuning uchun bormadi.
Lekin Keyti yozni undan uzoqda o'tkazmoqchi bo'lganidan uning jahli chiqdi.
Ikki oydan keyin Keyti qaytib keldi.
Elis singlisini kutib olish uchun aeroportga yugurdi.
Lekin Elis Keytini ko'rganida, hang-mang bo'lib qoldi.
Keyti endi ikki tilni bilardi va butunlay boshqacha ko'rinardi!
U chiroyli kiyim kiygan, pardoz qilgan va ozg'inroq ko'rinardi.
Elis uning yonida o'zini juda tartibsiz his qildi.
U shunchaki yarqiroq rangli futbolka kiygan edi va sochlari chigallashib ketgan edi.
Elis Keytidan Fransiya haqida so'raganida, Keyti noaniq javob berib, ko'p gapirmadi.
Bu Elisni g'azablantirdi va unda nafrat uyg'otdi, chunki ilgari ular bir-biriga doim hamma narsani aytishardi.
Endi ular o'rtasida katta jarlik paydo bo'lgan edi.
Haftalar o'tib, opa-singil yanada kamroq gaplashadigan bo'lishdi.
Ikki oydan keyin egizaklarning tug'ilgan kuni keldi.
Butun umri davomida ularning bir odati bor edi.
Tug'ilgan kunlaridan oldin ular tun bo'yi gaplashib chiqishardi.
O'sha kechasi Elis Keytining yotoqxonasiga kirdi.
«Kechirasan, oxirgi paytlarda kam gaplashdim», dedi Keyti.
«Tushunaman.
Endi yangi do'stlaring bor», dedi Elis jahl bilan.
Keyti dedi: «Fransuz do'stlarim hozir kam yozishadi.
Bir muddat ularni uydagi do'stlarimdan qiziqroq deb o'ylagandim.
Lekin xato qilgan ekanman.
Sen mening opamsan va doim eng yaqin dugonam bo'lib qolasan».
Elis dedi: «Men ham kechirim so'rayman.
Munosabatimiz abadiy o'zgarmay qolishini xohlagandim.
Lekin egizaklarning turli qiziqishlari bo'lishi mutlaqo tabiiy.
Biz doim birga bo'lmasak ham, eng yaqin dugonalar bo'lib qola olamiz».

e5|22.title: The New Bioco
paras: Jack got a new job at a biotechnology company called Bioco. Bioco manufactured drugs to treat diabetes and high cholesterol. Jack’s job was to use a tiny mechanism to get nectar from flowers. The nectar was a main ingredient in the drugs. Jack liked his job, and he thought that Bioco was a caring company. However, Jack soon learned that the company wasn’t as kind as he first thought.

Bioco’s motto was “Make the Earth a Better Place.” However, this motto was deceptive. The company actually did a number of really bad things to the environment. The company produced a lot of smog and harmful acid. Bioco poured the acid in a nearby river, which caused erosion and made fish prone to illness.

After a few weeks at the new job, Jack saw all the bad things Bioco was doing. He had always had strong ethics, and he knew he had to do something. One day, while the Bioco workers were eating in the cafeteria, Jack stood up and gave a speech. He said, “My fellow coworkers, I know you have all seen the evil things our company is doing. I have a notion that we can fix them if we form a coalition. We can go to the administration and tell them we’ll quit if they don’t eliminate the problems. They’ll have no choice but to listen to us.” Jack explained what they were to do. His coworkers liked his explicit plan. They went to the administrative offices and demanded that Bioco stop damaging the environment, or they all would quit. One supervisor said to them, “Thank you for being straightforward about this issue. Since I can’t afford to lose all of you workers, I guess we’ll just have to fix things.”

Jack, his supervisor, and his coworkers spent the next month designing a new framework for the company. They cleaned up the acid from the river and minimized the amount of air pollution the company released. At last, the company motto became apt.

qs.q: Bioco was a biotechnology company that manufactured diabetes and high cholesterol.
Jack used a mechanism to get nectar from flowers.
The waste acid caused erosion and made fish prone to illness.
After the company minimized Jack’s ethics, the motto became apt.

tr: Jek Bioko degan biotexnologiya kompaniyasida yangi ishga kirdi.
Bioko qandli diabet va yuqori xolesterinni davolash uchun dorilar ishlab chiqarardi.
Jekning ishi mitti mexanizm yordamida gullardan nektar olish edi.
Nektar dorilarning asosiy tarkibiy qismi edi.
Jekka ishi yoqardi va u Biokoni g'amxo'r kompaniya deb o'ylardi.
Biroq Jek tez orada kompaniya u dastlab o'ylaganchalik mehribon emasligini bilib oldi.
Biokoning shiori «Yerni yaxshiroq joyga aylantiraylik» edi.
Biroq bu shior aldamchi edi.
Kompaniya aslida atrof-muhitga juda ko'p yomon ishlar qilardi.
Kompaniya ko'p smog va zararli kislota chiqarardi.
Bioko kislotani yaqindagi daryoga to'kardi, bu esa eroziyaga sabab bo'lib, baliqlarni kasallikka moyil qilib qo'ygandi.
Yangi ishda bir necha hafta ishlagach, Jek Bioko qilayotgan barcha yomon ishlarni ko'rdi.
Uning axloqiy tamoyillari doim mustahkam edi va u nimadir qilishi kerakligini bildi.
Bir kuni Bioko ishchilari oshxonada ovqatlanayotganda, Jek o'rnidan turib nutq so'zladi.
U dedi: «Hurmatli hamkasblar, kompaniyamiz qilayotgan yovuz ishlarni hammangiz ko'rganingizni bilaman.
Menimcha, agar ittifoq tuzsak, ularni tuzata olamiz.
Biz ma'muriyatga borib, agar muammolarni bartaraf etishmasa, ishdan ketishimizni aytishimiz mumkin.
Ularda bizni tinglashdan boshqa iloj qolmaydi». Jek ular nima qilishlari kerakligini tushuntirdi.
Hamkasblariga uning aniq rejasi yoqdi.
Ular ma'muriy idoralarga borib, Bioko atrof-muhitga zarar yetkazishni to'xtatishini, aks holda hammalari ishdan ketishlarini talab qilishdi.
Bir rahbar ularga dedi: «Bu masalada ochiq gapirganingiz uchun rahmat.
Sizlarning hammangizni yo'qotishga qurbim yetmagani uchun, shekilli, ishlarni tuzatishimizga to'g'ri keladi».
Jek, uning rahbari va hamkasblari keyingi oyni kompaniya uchun yangi tuzilma ishlab chiqishga sarflashdi.
Ular daryoni kislotadan tozalashdi va kompaniya chiqaradigan havo ifloslanishini kamaytirishdi.
Nihoyat, kompaniya shiori o'z ma'nosiga mos keldi.

e5|23.title: How Comet Got His Tail
paras: A solitary rock roamed through the cold gloom of outer space. It slowly drifted through the debris of broken asteroids with a feeling of sadness. In the vast and beautiful galaxy, it was only a tiny rock. It felt like an insignificant atom. In its journeys it encountered many amazing objects. It flew by beautiful crescent moons that were covered with craters and moon dust. “Why can’t I be as beautiful as them?” it thought. The rock passed a gigantic planet. The sphere had a circumference hundreds of times larger than the breadth of the small rock. “Why can’t I be as large as that?” it wondered. The rock was filled with despair. It was surrounded by beauty and greatness, yet it was just a small and ugly fragment of rock.
One day, it approached the area of an astronomical star.
“What’s wrong?” the star asked.
“Oh, I wish I had a higher status in the galaxy. All the other objects are so beautiful and large,” the rock replied. “But I’m just an ugly rock.”
The star considered the problem.

At last it said, “You don’t have to worry anymore. I think I can help.” The star radiated its light brighter and hotter than it had ever done before. “Come a little closer,” the star said to the rock.
The rock drifted closer to the star.

Suddenly, the ice that was embedded in the rock’s tiny cracks melted and became steam. Then the steam extended behind the comet to form a brilliant tail. The tail shined with all the colors of the spectrum.

The little rock had become a beautiful comet. It looked so amazing. It realized that the star helped it change its appearance. “Thank you,” the comet said and then flew away with its new beautiful tail following behind it like a galactic cape.

qs.q: The little rock drifted through the debris of broken atoms.
The gigantic planet was in the shape of a sphere.
The ice embedded in the little rock bubbled with all the colors of the spectrum.
The star radiated its light hotter and brighter than ever before.
The little rock wished it had a higher status in the galaxy.

tr: Yolg'iz bir tosh koinotning sovuq qorong'iligida kezib yurardi.
U singan asteroidlarning qoldiqlari orasidan g'amginlik bilan sekin suzib borardi.
Ulkan va go'zal galaktikada u shunchaki mitti tosh edi.
U o'zini arzimas atomdek his qilardi.
Sayohatlarida u ko'plab ajoyib jismlarga duch keldi.
U kraterlar va oy changi bilan qoplangan go'zal o'roqsimon oylar yonidan uchib o'tdi.
«Nega men ham ulardek go'zal bo'la olmayman?» deb o'yladi u.
Tosh ulkan bir sayyora yonidan o'tdi.
Sharning aylanasi kichik toshning enidan yuzlab marta katta edi.
«Nega men ham shunday katta bo'la olmayman?» deb o'yladi u.
Toshni umidsizlik qamrab oldi.
Uning atrofi go'zallik va ulug'vorlikka to'la edi, u esa shunchaki kichik va xunuk tosh parchasi edi.
Bir kuni u ulkan yulduz hududiga yaqinlashdi.
«Nima bo'ldi?» deb so'radi yulduz.
«Oh, galaktikada maqomim balandroq bo'lishini istardim.
Boshqa barcha jismlar shunchalik go'zal va katta, — deb javob berdi tosh. —
Men esa shunchaki xunuk toshman».
Yulduz muammo haqida o'ylab ko'rdi.
Nihoyat u dedi: «Endi tashvishlanishing shart emas.
Menimcha, yordam bera olaman».
Yulduz nurini avvalgi har qandaydan ham yorqinroq va issiqroq taratdi.
«Biroz yaqinroq kel», dedi yulduz toshga.
Tosh yulduzga yaqinroq suzib bordi.
To'satdan toshning mayda yoriqlarida qotib qolgan muz erib, bug'ga aylandi.
Keyin bug' kometa ortidan cho'zilib, porloq dum hosil qildi.
Dum spektrning barcha ranglarida jilolanardi.
Kichik tosh go'zal kometaga aylandi.
U juda ajoyib ko'rinardi.
U yulduz unga tashqi ko'rinishini o'zgartirishga yordam berganini angladi.
«Rahmat», dedi kometa va ortidan galaktik yopinchiqdek ergashgan yangi go'zal dumi bilan uchib ketdi.

e5|24.title: The Resourceful Landlord
paras: A kind landlord was afraid that he would lose his apartment building. He needed to make some mandatory repairs to the old building, or his tenants would have to leave by the end of the month. Without tenants to lease the rooms, the landlord would be unable to pay his mortgage. He’d be bankrupt, and the bank would take his building. But he didn’t have the money whereby he could employ the personnel he needed to make the repairs. It would seem like he did not want to conform to the city’s codes before the forthcoming inspection. He had requested an extension, but it was denied by the city.
He held a meeting with his tenants and explained the unfortunate situation. “If the building does not meet the appropriate standards for safety and hygiene,” he said, “the city will expel everyone.”
The tenants were all sad for the kind old man. “Maybe we can help,” the hairdresser who lived on the first floor stated. The other tenants agreed.

One tenant had worked for the city’s utilities. He knew a lot about plumbing, so that’s how he helped. Another tenant was a carpenter; he mended the holes in the floor and walls. Others cleaned the building from top to bottom so that it was more hygienic. They even furnished some of the apartments with new beds, dressers, and chairs. When they were done, all of the people dispersed, and the landlord went home to rest. When the deadline of the inspection arrived, the apartment building was hygienic and safe. The landlord couldn’t believe it. His old building now looked like one of the trendiest buildings in town.
The building passed its inspection, and the landlord and the tenants had a big party.
“Thank you all so much,” the landlord said during the party. “I could never have done it by myself. But by working together, we now all have a beautiful place to live.”

qs.q: If the tenants didn’t pay the mortgage, the landlord could not pay his lease and would be bankrupt.
The landlord did not have money whereby he could employ personnel.
The city would expel everyone if the building did not pass the inspection for safety and hygiene.
The hairdresser mended the holes in the floors and walls.
After everyone helped to fix it, the building looked like one of the trendiest buildings in town.

tr: Bir mehribon uy egasi ko'p qavatli uyini yo'qotib qo'yishidan qo'rqardi.
U eski binoda majburiy ta'mirlash ishlarini o'tkazishi kerak edi, aks holda ijarachilari oy oxirigacha ko'chib ketishlariga to'g'ri kelardi.
Xonalarni ijaraga oladigan ijarachilar bo'lmasa, uy egasi ipoteka to'lovini to'lay olmasdi.
U bankrot bo'lardi va bank uning binosini olib qo'yardi.
Lekin uning ta'mirlash uchun kerakli xodimlarni yollashga puli yo'q edi.
Go'yo u bo'lajak tekshiruvdan oldin shahar qoidalariga rioya qilishni xohlamayotgandek tuyulardi.
U muddatni uzaytirishni so'ragan edi, lekin shahar rad etdi.
U ijarachilari bilan yig'ilish o'tkazib, noxush vaziyatni tushuntirdi.
«Agar bino xavfsizlik va gigiyena bo'yicha tegishli me'yorlarga javob bermasa, — dedi u, — shahar hammani chiqarib yuboradi».
Ijarachilarning hammasi mehribon cholga achinishdi.
«Balki biz yordam bera olarmiz», dedi birinchi qavatda yashovchi sartarosh.
Boshqa ijarachilar ham rozi bo'lishdi.
Bir ijarachi shahar kommunal xizmatida ishlagan edi.
U santexnika haqida ko'p narsa bilardi, shuning uchun shu yo'l bilan yordam berdi.
Yana bir ijarachi duradgor edi; u pol va devorlardagi teshiklarni tuzatdi.
Boshqalar binoni yanada gigiyenik qilish uchun tepadan pastgacha tozalashdi.
Ular hatto ba'zi kvartiralarni yangi karavotlar, komodlar va stullar bilan jihozlashdi.
Ular tugatganlaridan keyin hamma tarqalib ketdi va uy egasi dam olish uchun uyiga ketdi.
Tekshiruv muddati kelganida, ko'p qavatli uy toza va xavfsiz edi.
Uy egasi bunga ishona olmadi.
Uning eski binosi endi shahardagi eng zamonaviy binolardan biriga o'xshardi.
Bino tekshiruvdan o'tdi va uy egasi bilan ijarachilar katta bazm qilishdi.
«Hammangizga katta rahmat», dedi uy egasi bazm paytida.
«Men buni hech qachon yolg'iz o'zim uddalay olmasdim.
Lekin birgalikda ishlab, endi hammamizning yashash uchun go'zal joyimiz bor».

e5|25.title: The Man and the Monkey
paras: While flying over a jungle, a wealthy executive’s private plane crashed. Some of the crew were hurt, so the pilot decided to stay with them and wait for help. The arrogant executive, though, didn’t care about the welfare of the pilot and crew. Rather, he thought he could walk out of the jungle and find a town to stay in.

He followed a trail through a canyon and along a creek. The jungle was actually very stunning. If the arrogant executive had stopped to look around, he might have perceived the jungle’s beauty. But he was in a nasty mood and had no care for the aesthetic value of the jungle. He continued to walk up the steep incline of the jungle’s hills. Soon, he was lost. Several days passed, and fatigue and hunger weakened him. He was very tired and afraid.

Just then, a monkey came out of the trees. It was carrying a twig covered in honey. It walked up to a mound where termites lived. He then used the twig like a drill to make a hole in the mound. Then very carefully, it removed the twig from the hole. The sticky twig was covered with termites.
Instead of eating the bugs, the monkey offered them to the executive, but he didn’t want what the monkey offered. He shouted at the monkey, “Get away from me, you stupid primate!”

The executive’s stereotype of the monkey was wrong. The monkey was not stupid. It knew how to find food, whereas the executive did not. He refused the help of the monkey, thereby leaving himself to starve.

When the executive was finally found, he was very skinny and sick. He had not eaten for a very long time. Because he held a bias against the primitive ways of the monkey, he had gone hungry and almost died. The executive didn’t understand that it was his arrogant attitude that had caused all of his problems.

qs.q: The executive only cared about the welfare of his pilot and crew.
The executive followed a trail through a canyon and along a creek.
The executive was in a nasty mood, so he did not see the aesthetic value of the jungle.
The executive walked up the small incline of the jungle’s hills.
The executive’s stereotype of the primate was correct.

tr: O'rmon ustidan uchib ketayotganda boy bir rahbarning shaxsiy samolyoti halokatga uchradi.
Ekipajning ba'zilari jarohatlandi, shuning uchun uchuvchi ular bilan qolib, yordam kutishga qaror qildi.
Biroq kibrli rahbarga uchuvchi va ekipajning ahvoli befarq edi.
Aksincha, u o'rmondan piyoda chiqib, qolish uchun biror shahar topa olaman deb o'yladi.
U kanyon orqali va soy bo'ylab o'tgan so'qmoqdan bordi.
O'rmon aslida juda go'zal edi.
Agar kibrli rahbar to'xtab, atrofga qaraganida, o'rmonning go'zalligini sezishi mumkin edi.
Lekin uning kayfiyati juda yomon edi va o'rmonning nafis go'zalligi unga qiziq emasdi.
U o'rmon tepaliklarining tik qiyaligi bo'ylab yuqoriga chiqishda davom etdi.
Ko'p o'tmay, u adashib qoldi.
Bir necha kun o'tdi va charchoq hamda ochlik uni holdan toydirdi.
U juda charchagan va qo'rqib ketgan edi.
Aynan shu payt daraxtlar orasidan bir maymun chiqib keldi.
U asalga belangan xivich ko'tarib kelayotgan edi.
U termitlar yashaydigan uyum oldiga bordi.
Keyin u xivichni parmadek ishlatib, uyumda teshik ochdi.
So'ng juda ehtiyotkorlik bilan xivichni teshikdan chiqarib oldi.
Yopishqoq xivich termitlar bilan qoplangan edi.
Maymun hasharotlarni yeyish o'rniga ularni rahbarga taklif qildi, lekin u maymun taklif qilgan narsani xohlamadi.
U maymunga qichqirdi: «Yo'qol mendan, ahmoq primat!»
Rahbarning maymun haqidagi qolipli tasavvuri noto'g'ri edi.
Maymun ahmoq emasdi.
U ovqat topishni bilardi, rahbar esa bilmasdi.
U maymunning yordamidan bosh tortib, shu bilan o'zini ochlikka mahkum etdi.
Rahbar nihoyat topilganida, u juda ozib, kasal bo'lib qolgan edi.
U juda uzoq vaqtdan beri hech narsa yemagan edi.
Maymunning ibtidoiy usullariga nisbatan xurofoti tufayli u och qoldi va sal qoldi o'lishiga.
Rahbar barcha muammolariga aynan o'zining kibrli munosabati sabab bo'lganini tushunmadi.

e5|26.title: Cosmo’s Flight
paras: When Cosmo woke up, he was crying. He had a dream that he was falling. This dream had recurred for the previous five nights. Cosmo was scared that his dreams were a preview of what was going to happen on his flight the next day.

Cosmo was a supernatural being who was about to turn 15 years old. In his culture, boys of his age were required to participate in an important rite. They were given wings and instructed to orbit the Earth. After successful flights, the boys officially became men. Cosmo certainly wanted to be a man, but he was scared. He went to the oracle of a god named Dano. Cosmo said, “I’m not sure I can make such a long trip. What if I get tired? What if my strength stalls, and I can’t stay in the air. I’ll crash and die!”

Dano replied, “Don’t be afraid. You have all the relevant skills in your personal inventory that have been building up over the years. To ease your worry, let me tell you a little about what will happen tomorrow. You’ll begin over Africa. You’ll keep flying north until you come to the Himalayas. The mountain tops will look like small loaves of bread at such a high distance. The rivers of the world will look like pieces of blue string that cross the globe. Keep your body horizontal when flying against the winds of the Pacific Ocean. Keep your eyes open and enjoy the beauty of the Earth. You will be fine, you’ll see.”
Cosmo replied, “Thanks for the overview of my journey, I’ll do my best.”

The next morning, Cosmo was provided with a divine set of wings and sent on his way. He flapped his wings and went high above the Earth. He flew over mountains, oceans, and glaciers. After a while, his inward thoughts were no longer about falling. He was actually having fun! He began to hum a song as he enjoyed the view. When he reached home, his tribe was there to greet him.
The chief said, “On behalf of the tribe, I declare you a man. We’re proud of you, Cosmo!” Cosmo was proud of himself, too.

qs.q: Cosmo was scared that his recurring dreams of the previous nights were a preview of what would happen.
Supernatural boys of Cosmo’s age participated in an important rite.
In Dano’s summary, he told Cosmo to keep his body horizontal against the winds of the Indian Ocean.
Dano flapped the wings he was provided with and orbited the globe.
Cosmo sang a tune while he flew and enjoyed the view.

tr: Kosmo uyg'onganida yig'layotgan edi.
U tushida yiqilib tushayotganini ko'rgan edi.
Bu tush oldingi besh kecha davomida takrorlangan edi.
Kosmo tushlari ertangi parvozida nima bo'lishining oldindan ko'rinishi deb qo'rqardi.
Kosmo 15 yoshga to'lish arafasida turgan g'ayritabiiy mavjudot edi.
Uning madaniyatida uning yoshidagi o'g'il bolalar muhim marosimda qatnashishlari shart edi.
Ularga qanot berilib, Yer atrofida aylanib uchish buyurilardi.
Muvaffaqiyatli parvozlardan keyin o'g'il bolalar rasman erkak bo'lishardi.
Kosmo, albatta, erkak bo'lishni xohlardi, lekin qo'rqardi.
U Dano ismli xudoning bashoratgo'yi oldiga bordi.
Kosmo dedi: «Bunday uzoq safarni uddalay olishimga ishonchim yo'q.
Agar charchab qolsam-chi?
Agar kuchim tugab, havoda tura olmasam-chi?
Yiqilib, o'lib ketaman!»
Dano javob berdi: «Qo'rqma.
Yillar davomida shakllangan barcha kerakli ko'nikmalar senda bor.
Xavotiringni yengillatish uchun ertaga nima bo'lishi haqida biroz aytib beray.
Sen Afrika ustidan boshlaysan.
Himolay tog'lariga yetguncha shimolga uchaverasan.
Shunday baland masofadan tog' cho'qqilari kichkina non bo'laklaridek ko'rinadi.
Dunyo daryolari yer sharini kesib o'tgan ko'k ip bo'laklaridek ko'rinadi.
Tinch okeani shamollariga qarshi uchganingda tanangni gorizontal tut.
Ko'zlaringni ochiq tut va Yerning go'zalligidan zavqlan.
Hammasi yaxshi bo'ladi, ko'rasan».
Kosmo javob berdi: «Safarim haqidagi umumiy ma'lumot uchun rahmat, qo'limdan kelganini qilaman».
Ertasi kuni ertalab Kosmoga ilohiy qanotlar berildi va u yo'lga jo'natildi.
U qanotlarini qoqib, Yerdan baland ko'tarildi.
U tog'lar, okeanlar va muzliklar ustidan uchdi.
Bir muncha vaqtdan keyin uning ichki o'ylari endi yiqilish haqida emasdi.
U haqiqatan ham maza qilayotgan edi!
U manzaradan zavqlanib, qo'shiq xirgoyi qila boshladi.
U uyga yetib kelganida, qabilasi uni kutib olish uchun u yerda edi.
Boshliq dedi: «Qabila nomidan seni erkak deb e'lon qilaman.
Biz sen bilan faxrlanamiz, Kosmo!»
Kosmo ham o'zi bilan faxrlandi.

e5|27.title: The First Organ Transplant
paras: In 1954, a man named Richard was dying of kidney disease. He wouldn’t survive for long unless he got a new kidney right away. Richard’s twin brother, Robert, was willing to donate one of his kidneys to his dying brother. At the time, however, no doctor had ever performed a successful internal organ transplant. The idea of taking an organ out of one person and putting it into another was just a fantasy. But the brothers decided to be brave and found a doctor who could make organ transplants a reality.

Since Richard and Robert were twins, their heredity was identical. They had the exact same biological traits. Even their kidneys were identical on the cellular level. Therefore, Robert’s working kidney could be substituted for Richard’s bad one. Richard’s body could adapt to the new organ if the operation was done correctly.

The twins went to Dr. Murray, who was a pioneer of new surgical methods. His dynamic team of surgeons performed the transplant. Dr. Murray made sure his surgeons followed a rigid sequence of directions so that no mistakes were made. First, they made a minimal cut in Richard’s side and removed the bad kidney. Then, they made another small cut in Robert’s side, removed his kidney, and transferred it into Richard’s body. Finally, they sewed up the respective cuts. The entire operation only took about one hour. After the surgery, it was clear that both brothers were going to be OK. The operation was confirmed a success. Richard’s new kidney worked great! Doctors prescribed medicine for the pain caused by the surgery. Since Richard was still weak, he used physical therapy to revive his strength. At last, Richard’s transition into a healthy, happy person was complete.
Dr. Murray became a hero in the medical world. His success gave other doctors confidence to try organ transplants themselves.
Now, doctors perform life-saving transplants and surgeries every day.

qs.q: Internal organ transplants were a fantasy after 1954.
Robert was a pioneer of new surgical procedures.
The twins’ kidneys were identical on the cellular level because of their heredity.
The dynamic surgeons followed a rigid sequence of directions to avoid mistakes.
Richard’s body adapted to the kidney that was transferred from his brother.

tr: 1954-yilda Richard ismli bir odam buyrak kasalligidan o'lim to'shagida yotardi.
Agar u zudlik bilan yangi buyrak olmasa, uzoq yashamasdi.
Richardning egizak akasi Robert o'layotgan ukasiga buyraklaridan birini berishga tayyor edi.
Biroq o'sha paytda hech bir shifokor ichki a'zoni muvaffaqiyatli ko'chirib o'tkazmagan edi.
Bir odamdan a'zoni olib, boshqasiga joylashtirish g'oyasi shunchaki xayol edi.
Lekin aka-ukalar jasorat ko'rsatishga qaror qilishdi va a'zo ko'chirib o'tkazishni haqiqatga aylantira oladigan shifokorni topishdi.
Richard va Robert egizak bo'lgani uchun ularning irsiyati bir xil edi.
Ularning biologik xususiyatlari aynan bir xil edi.
Hatto buyraklari ham hujayra darajasida bir xil edi.
Shuning uchun Robertning sog'lom buyragini Richardning kasal buyragi o'rniga qo'yish mumkin edi.
Agar operatsiya to'g'ri bajarilsa, Richardning tanasi yangi a'zoga moslasha olardi.
Egizaklar yangi jarrohlik usullarining kashshofi bo'lgan doktor Myurreyning oldiga borishdi.
Uning g'ayratli jarrohlar jamoasi ko'chirib o'tkazishni amalga oshirdi.
Doktor Myurrey hech qanday xato bo'lmasligi uchun jarrohlari ko'rsatmalarning qat'iy ketma-ketligiga amal qilishlarini ta'minladi.
Avval ular Richardning biqinida juda kichik kesik ochib, kasal buyrakni olib tashlashdi.
Keyin ular Robertning biqinida yana bir kichik kesik ochib, uning buyragini olishdi va uni Richardning tanasiga ko'chirishdi.
Nihoyat, ular har ikki kesikni tikishdi.
Butun operatsiya atigi bir soatcha davom etdi.
Operatsiyadan keyin ikkala aka-uka ham yaxshi bo'lishi aniq bo'ldi.
Operatsiya muvaffaqiyatli deb tasdiqlandi.
Richardning yangi buyragi a'lo ishladi!
Shifokorlar jarrohlik keltirib chiqargan og'riq uchun dori yozib berishdi.
Richard hali zaif bo'lgani uchun kuchini tiklash maqsadida fizioterapiyadan foydalandi.
Nihoyat, Richardning sog'lom, baxtli odamga aylanishi yakunlandi.
Doktor Myurrey tibbiyot olamida qahramonga aylandi.
Uning muvaffaqiyati boshqa shifokorlarga ham a'zo ko'chirib o'tkazishni sinab ko'rishga ishonch berdi.
Endi shifokorlar har kuni hayotni saqlab qoluvchi ko'chirib o'tkazish va jarrohlik amaliyotlarini bajarishadi.

e5|28.title: The Lottery
paras: Joe was watching television when he heard a knock at the door. He thought, “Who could that be? It’s probably one of the naughty neighborhood children.” Joe stood up and walked to the door. When he opened it, he saw a beautiful woman.
She said, “Good morning, Joe! I have great news. You’re the recipient of this check for one million dollars! You won the lottery!”
Joe couldn’t believe it. His mind was overloaded with emotions. Joe said, “Thank you! Thank you!”

After he calmed down, Joe made a photocopy of the check in case he misplaced the original one. He sat and thought about what he wanted to do with the money. He didn’t want to spend it in an arbitrary way. Joe thought, “I know there are others who need this money more than I do. I’ve always loved animals, so I think I’ll buy things for the zoo!” Joe knew that the zoo was in bad shape. The cages were too small, and they weren’t insulated from the cold. Animals couldn’t thrive in such conditions.

He took out some stationery and wrote a letter to the zoo. He offered to help the zoo buy huge cages for the large mammals and reptiles. He offered to buy healthy food for the orangutans to increase their longevity. He even said that he would buy new glass walls for the aquarium because the old ones were cracked.

Joe’s act of philanthropy intrigued the zoo keeper. He probed Joe to learn why he spent his money to improve the zoo. It wasn’t a social convention for a person to be so gracious. Joe told the zoo keeper, “I know it’s not the norm, but my ultimate decision to help these animals is better than anything I could have done for myself. If I ever write an autobiography, I will write that this was the happiest day of my life.”

qs.q: Joe was the recipient of a check because he won the lottery.
He wanted to buy new glass walls for the aquarium because the old ones were cracked.
If Joe wrote an autobiography, he would write about the norms of the overloaded aquarium.
Joe made a photocopy of the check in case he misplaced the original one.
When Joe opened the door, he saw one of the naughty neighborhood children.

tr: Jo televizor ko'rayotganida eshik taqillaganini eshitdi.
U o'yladi: «Bu kim bo'lishi mumkin?
Ehtimol, mahalladagi sho'x bolalardan biridir».
Jo o'rnidan turib, eshik oldiga bordi.
Uni ochganida, u go'zal bir ayolni ko'rdi.
Ayol dedi: «Xayrli tong, Jo!
Menda ajoyib yangilik bor.
Siz bir million dollarlik ushbu chekning egasisiz!
Siz lotereyada yutdingiz!»
Jo bunga ishonolmadi.
Uning xayoli his-tuyg'ularga to'lib-toshib ketdi.
Jo dedi: «Rahmat!
Rahmat!»
Tinchlangandan keyin Jo asl nusxasini yo'qotib qo'ysa deb chekning nusxasini ko'chirib oldi.
U o'tirib, pulni nima qilishni xohlashi haqida o'yladi.
U uni tasodifiy yo'l bilan sarflashni xohlamadi.
Jo o'yladi: «Bilaman, bu pulga mendan ko'ra ko'proq muhtoj bo'lganlar bor.
Men doim hayvonlarni yaxshi ko'rganman, shuning uchun hayvonot bog'i uchun narsalar sotib olaman shekilli!»
Jo hayvonot bog'ining ahvoli yomon ekanini bilardi.
Qafaslar juda kichik edi va ular sovuqdan himoyalanmagan edi.
Bunday sharoitda hayvonlar yaxshi rivojlana olmasdi.
U bir nechta xat qog'ozi olib, hayvonot bog'iga xat yozdi.
U hayvonot bog'iga yirik sutemizuvchilar va sudralib yuruvchilar uchun ulkan qafaslar sotib olishda yordam berishni taklif qildi.
U orangutanlarning umrini uzaytirish uchun ularga sog'lom ovqat sotib olishni taklif qildi.
U hatto akvarium uchun yangi shisha devorlar sotib olishini aytdi, chunki eskilari yorilgan edi.
Joning xayriya ishi hayvonot bog'i xodimini qiziqtirib qoldi.
U Jo nega o'z pulini hayvonot bog'ini yaxshilashga sarflaganini bilish uchun undan so'rab-surishtirdi.
Odamning bunchalik saxiy bo'lishi odatiy ijtimoiy hol emasdi.
Jo hayvonot bog'i xodimiga dedi: «Bilaman, bu odatiy emas, lekin bu hayvonlarga yordam berish haqidagi yakuniy qarorim o'zim uchun qila oladigan har qanday narsadan yaxshiroq.
Agar qachondir tarjimai holimni yozsam, bu hayotimdagi eng baxtli kun bo'lganini yozaman».

e5|29.title: Jen’s New Job
paras: The history museum needed to recruit a new tour guide. The director interviewed dozens of applicants before he decided to hire Jen. She was chosen because she was friendly, punctual and had a great attitude.

On her first day, Jen got to work and prepared to give her first tour. She looked at the names on the register. She saw that the Queen of England and a diplomat were visiting the museum. She thought, “It’s my very first day, and I have to impress a monarch! I hope I don’t humiliate myself in front of a person of such renown!”

Jen was nervous. She took a deep breath and said, “Hello, everyone! I’m going to talk to you about the chronology of ancient Egypt.” As she turned around to show the group some artifacts, she bumped into a fossil of an authentic elephant tusk. It fell to the ground and broke into a million pieces! “Oh no!” said Jen in a subtle voice. “I sure hope the rest of the tour goes better than this!”
The rest of the tour did not go any better. She tripped over an antique vase and broke a piece off of it. As she was reading an excerpt from a lyric poem, she sneezed and tore a page of the epic.

After the tour, Jen approached the queen to apologize. She said, “I’m sorry, Your Majesty. I was a terrible tour guide. Let me give you a refund for the money you spent.” The queen laughed. She said, “I don’t want my money back, Jen. I loved the tour. You just have to be a little more careful and work hard to become the best at your job. Hard work precedes success.”
Jen smiled and thanked the queen. She decided to be extra careful from then on. She was persistent and worked hard. In time, Jen became the best tour guide at the museum.

qs.q: The museum director interviewed dozens of applicants when he recruited a new tour guide.
Jen did not want to humiliate herself in front of the diplomat and the monarch.
The queen bumped into the fossil of an authentic elephant tusk.
Jen was chosen for the job because she was friendly, punctual, and had a register.
Jen broke artifacts, including an antique vase.

tr: Tarix muzeyiga yangi gid yollash kerak edi.
Direktor Jenni ishga olishga qaror qilishdan oldin o'nlab nomzodlar bilan suhbat o'tkazdi.
U do'stona, vaqtga rioya qiladigan va ajoyib munosabatli bo'lgani uchun tanlandi.
Birinchi kuni Jen ishga kelib, birinchi ekskursiyasini o'tkazishga tayyorlandi.
U ro'yxatdagi ismlarga qaradi.
U muzeyga Angliya qirolichasi va bir diplomat tashrif buyurayotganini ko'rdi.
U o'yladi: «Bu mening eng birinchi kunim va men monarxni hayratga solishim kerak!
Umid qilamanki, bunchalik mashhur odam oldida sharmanda bo'lmayman!»
Jen hayajonda edi.
U chuqur nafas olib dedi: «Hammaga salom!
Men sizlarga qadimgi Misr xronologiyasi haqida gapirib beraman».
Guruhga bir nechta qadimiy buyumni ko'rsatish uchun burilganida, u haqiqiy fil tishining qazilma qoldig'iga urilib ketdi.
U yerga tushib, mayda-mayda bo'lib sindi!
«Voy, yo'q!» dedi Jen past ovozda.
«Umid qilamanki, ekskursiyaning qolgan qismi bundan yaxshiroq o'tadi!»
Ekskursiyaning qolgan qismi ham yaxshiroq o'tmadi.
U qadimiy guldonga qoqilib, undan bir bo'lagini sindirib qo'ydi.
Lirik she'rdan parcha o'qiyotganda u aksirib, dostonning bir sahifasini yirtib yubordi.
Ekskursiyadan keyin Jen kechirim so'rash uchun qirolichaning oldiga bordi.
U dedi: «Kechirasiz, Janobi Oliylari.
Men dahshatli gid bo'ldim.
Sarflagan pulingizni qaytarib beray». Qirolicha kulib yubordi.
U dedi: «Pulimni qaytarishingni xohlamayman, Jen.
Ekskursiya menga juda yoqdi.
Sen shunchaki biroz ehtiyotkorroq bo'lishing va ishingda eng zo'ri bo'lish uchun qattiq mehnat qilishing kerak.
Qattiq mehnat muvaffaqiyatdan oldin keladi».
Jen jilmayib, qirolichaga rahmat aytdi.
U bundan buyon o'ta ehtiyotkor bo'lishga qaror qildi.
U qat'iyatli edi va qattiq mehnat qildi.
Vaqt o'tib, Jen muzeydagi eng zo'r gidga aylandi.

e5|30.title: The Demon’s Bridge
paras: A young woman’s cow had crossed the river in the morning when the water level was moderate. But when the woman returned with her dog to get the cow, she was overwhelmed by how high the water had risen. Even if she crossed, she still couldn’t tow her cow back through the river.
“What am I going to do?” she wondered.
Suddenly, a man appeared across the river. “A fragile young lady like you shouldn’t have to struggle across a river,” he said. “I’ll build you a bridge.”
The man was an enigma. The young woman’s perception of him was that he was a sociable person. He was talkative, yet something was strange about him.
“I don’t want to be a burden to you, sir,” the woman replied.
“Don’t worry,” he told her as he began crafting a bridge. He merged the pieces of the bridge together with amazing speed. Soon, it was finished.
“Oh, but how can I pay you for your work? Let’s compromise. I am sure that we can find a fair solution. What do you think?” The woman asked.

“The only currency I need is the first living thing that crosses the bridge,” the man replied. She thought, “This deal sounds weird. Maybe he’s actually a river demon.” She shivered because she realized that he had taken advantage of her innocence and rigged the deal somehow. But she had a plan of her own. She pulled a piece of bread from her pocket and threw it across the bridge. Her dog ran after it.

“The dog is the first living thing across the bridge,” she said to the man. The man was angry. He suddenly changed into a hybrid of a human and a fish. “You crook!” he shouted. “You tricked me. I have no use for your dog!” He screamed and dove into the river. The woman tramped across the bridge to the other side and had a happy reunion with her dog and cow.

qs.q: The woman’s perception was that though the man was talkative and sociable, he was also an enigma.
When the young woman returned, she was overwhelmed by the moderate water level.
The fragile young woman thought she might be a burden to the man.
While crafting the bridge, the man merged the pieces with amazing speed.
The woman tramped across the bridge and had a happy reunion with the man.

tr: Bir yosh ayolning sigiri ertalab suv sathi o'rtacha bo'lganida daryoni kechib o'tgan edi.
Lekin ayol sigirni olib kelish uchun iti bilan qaytib kelganida, suv qanchalik baland ko'tarilganidan esankirab qoldi.
U kechib o'tgan taqdirda ham, sigirini daryodan sudrab qaytara olmasdi.
«Endi nima qilaman?» deb o'yladi u.
To'satdan daryoning narigi tomonida bir odam paydo bo'ldi.
«Senga o'xshagan nozik yosh xonim daryodan qiynalib o'tmasligi kerak, — dedi u. —
Senga ko'prik qurib beraman».
Bu odam jumboq edi.
Yosh ayolning unga bo'lgan taassuroti — u xushmuomala odam degan fikr edi.
U gapdon edi, lekin unda nimadir g'alati edi.
«Sizga yuk bo'lishni xohlamayman, janob», deb javob berdi ayol.
«Xavotir olma», dedi u ko'prik yasashga kirisharkan.
U ko'prik qismlarini hayratlanarli tezlikda bir-biriga biriktirdi.
Tez orada u tayyor bo'ldi.
«Oh, lekin mehnatingiz uchun sizga qanday haq to'layman?
Keling, kelishaylik.
Ishonamanki, adolatli yechim topa olamiz.
Siz nima deysiz?» deb so'radi ayol.
«Menga kerak bo'lgan yagona to'lov — ko'prikdan birinchi o'tadigan tirik jon», deb javob berdi odam.
Ayol o'yladi: «Bu kelishuv g'alati tuyulyapti.
Balki u aslida daryo devidir».
U qaltirab ketdi, chunki u uning soddaligidan foydalanib, kelishuvni qandaydir yo'l bilan o'z foydasiga burganini angladi.
Lekin uning ham o'z rejasi bor edi.
U cho'ntagidan bir burda non olib, uni ko'prik bo'ylab otdi.
Iti uning ortidan yugurdi.
«Ko'prikdan birinchi o'tgan tirik jon — it», dedi u odamga.
Odamning jahli chiqdi.
U to'satdan yarim odam, yarim baliq qiyofasiga kirdi.
«Firibgar! — deb qichqirdi u. —
Meni aldading.
Sening iting menga kerak emas!» U qichqirib, daryoga sho'ng'idi.
Ayol ko'prikdan narigi tomonga og'ir qadamlar bilan o'tdi va iti hamda sigiri bilan xursand bo'lib qayta ko'rishdi.

e6|1.title: The North Star
paras: Among the multitude of stars in the universe, there are a couple that are of great importance to people on Earth. The sun, of course, is one of them. The other is known as Polaris, the North Star. Polaris is special because it is the only star that always appears to be in the same place in the sky. Therefore, Polaris is a great compass. When people in the northern hemisphere of Earth look toward Polaris, they can be certain that they are facing north. The permanence of Polaris in the north sky has helped countless people find their destinations.

Before the invention of modern navigation tools, mariners relied on Polaris. From the top of their hulls, sailors would look for Polaris to figure out their place at sea. They figured out the angle between the star and the horizon to determine their latitude. As long as the equations weren’t erroneous, the results were very reliable. Polaris also let sailors determine North, South, East, and West. By knowing directions and their location, mariners could easily navigate their ships.

To those who sail at night, volatile storms and dark clouds were more than nuisances. They could disrupt entire journeys by blocking the view of Polaris. A captain could err and make an inadvertent wrong turn. The ship could become stranded at sea, and the frantic captain would have no way to improvise to get the ship back on the right course. The mariner’s fears wouldn’t be soothed until the clouds cleared and Polaris came back into view. Even today, sailors sometimes opt to navigate by using Polaris on clear nights.

It’s not difficult to differentiate Polaris from other stars. The Big Dipper, a constellation that is well known in astrology, appears to revolve around Polaris. The handle of the Big Dipper always points to the North Star. When people get lost, it’s comforting to know that their problems can be alleviated by looking at the sky.

qs.q: Even today, sailors opt to improvise by using Polaris on clear nights.
A ship could become stranded if a captain erred and made an inadvertent wrong turn.
People who are lost can be alleviated by gazing up at a frantic sky.
Volatile storms were more than nuisances because they disrupted entire journeys.
It is not difficult to differentiate Polaris from the multitude of other stars in the universe.

tr: Koinotdagi son-sanoqsiz yulduzlar orasida Yerdagi odamlar uchun katta ahamiyatga ega bo'lgan bir-ikkitasi bor.
Albatta, Quyosh ulardan biri.
Ikkinchisi Qutb yulduzi — Polyaris nomi bilan mashhur.
Polyaris alohida, chunki u osmonda doim bir joyda turgandek ko'rinadigan yagona yulduzdir.
Shuning uchun Polyaris ajoyib kompas.
Yerning shimoliy yarimsharidagi odamlar Polyarisga qaraganlarida, shimolga qarab turganliklariga amin bo'lishlari mumkin.
Polyarisning shimoliy osmonda doimiy turishi son-sanoqsiz odamlarga manzillarini topishga yordam bergan.
Zamonaviy navigatsiya asboblari ixtiro qilinishidan oldin dengizchilar Polyarisga tayanishgan.
Dengizchilar dengizdagi o'rnini aniqlash uchun kema korpusining tepasidan Polyarisni qidirishardi.
Ular kenglikni aniqlash uchun yulduz bilan ufq orasidagi burchakni hisoblashardi.
Tenglamalar xato bo'lmasa, natijalar juda ishonchli edi.
Polyaris dengizchilarga Shimol, Janub, Sharq va G'arbni aniqlashga ham imkon berardi.
Yo'nalishlar va o'z joylashuvini bilgan holda dengizchilar kemalarini osongina boshqara olishardi.
Kechasi suzadiganlar uchun o'zgaruvchan bo'ronlar va qora bulutlar shunchaki noqulaylikdan ko'proq narsa edi.
Ular Polyarisni to'sib qo'yib, butun safarni izdan chiqarishi mumkin edi.
Kapitan xato qilib, bilmagan holda noto'g'ri burilishi mumkin edi.
Kema dengizda qolib ketishi mumkin edi va sarosimaga tushgan kapitanda kemani to'g'ri yo'lga qaytarish uchun biror chora topishning iloji bo'lmasdi.
Bulutlar tarqalib, Polyaris yana ko'rinmaguncha dengizchining qo'rquvi bosilmasdi.
Hatto bugun ham dengizchilar ba'zan ochiq tunlarda Polyaris yordamida yo'l topishni afzal ko'rishadi.
Polyarisni boshqa yulduzlardan ajratish qiyin emas.
Munajjimlikda yaxshi ma'lum bo'lgan Katta Ayiq yulduz turkumi Polyaris atrofida aylanayotgandek ko'rinadi.
Katta Ayiqning dastasi doim Qutb yulduziga qarab turadi.
Odamlar adashib qolganda, muammolarini osmonga qarab yengillatish mumkinligini bilish taskin beradi.

e6|2.title: The Fossil Hunters
paras: Tim and Dean were great fossil hunters. They were the very best at finding dinosaur bones. Although Tim and Dean were quite similar, they were outright enemies. The two men got into vicious arguments all the time. They couldn’t coexist peacefully because their egos were too large. Tim thought he was the best fossil hunter, while Dean was sure that he was much better than Tim.

One day, Tim was searching for fossils on the periphery of the city when he discovered a huge bone. He had never seen anything like it! He took his shovel and carefully excavated the dirt around it. As he dug, he uncovered more jagged bones. He realized that he had found an entire dinosaur skeleton! Tim couldn’t conceive a plan to remove the huge skeleton all by himself. Such an endeavor would be too arduous. He needed help. He tried to think of people who would be capable of helping him remove the skeleton without breaking it. The only person Tim could think of was Dean, his enemy.
Tim ran into the city to find Dean. Tim found him and said, “Dean, I’ve found the skeletal remains of a huge terrestrial animal. But I can’t get the skeleton out by myself. Will you please help me?”
Dean thought that Tim’s claim might be dubious. He replied, “If you’re serious about the skeleton, I’ll help.”

Tim excitedly showed Dean the skeleton’s locale. They worked together to carefully remove each bone. And to keep the bones together, they tied them with elastic strips. When they were finished, they had attained a perfect skeleton. They used plaster to make a mold of the dinosaur’s skull. They engraved their initials into it and gave it to the curator of a local museum.
Tim and Dean found out that they could work very well together. They decided to end their feud and become friends. By combining their talents, the men became even greater than they were before.

qs.q: Tim and Dean were outright enemies who got into vicious arguments.
Tim and Dean removed the jagged bones and used elastic to attain them.
Tim couldn’t conceive a plan to remove the bones because the endeavor would be too arduous.
Dean thought that Tim’s ego might be dubious.
When Tim excavated the land, he uncovered many engraved bones.

tr: Tim va Din zo'r qazilma qidiruvchilar edi.
Ular dinozavr suyaklarini topishda eng zo'rlari edi.
Tim va Din bir-biriga ancha o'xshash bo'lsa-da, ular ochiqdan-ochiq dushman edilar.
Ikkalasi doim qattiq janjallashishardi.
Ularning manmanligi haddan tashqari katta bo'lgani uchun ular tinch-totuv yashay olishmasdi.
Tim o'zini eng zo'r qazilma qidiruvchi deb hisoblardi, Din esa Timdan ancha yaxshiroq ekaniga amin edi.
Bir kuni Tim shahar chekkasida qazilma qidirayotib, ulkan suyak topdi.
U hech qachon bunday narsani ko'rmagan edi!
U belkuragini olib, uning atrofidagi tuproqni ehtiyotkorlik bilan qazib oldi.
Qazigan sari u yana ko'proq qirrali suyaklarni ochdi.
U butun bir dinozavr skeletini topganini angladi!
Tim ulkan skeletni yolg'iz o'zi chiqarib olish rejasini o'ylab topa olmadi.
Bunday urinish juda mashaqqatli bo'lardi.
Unga yordam kerak edi.
U skeletni sindirmasdan chiqarib olishga yordam bera oladigan odamlarni o'ylab ko'rdi.
Timning xayoliga kelgan yagona odam uning dushmani Din edi.
Tim Dinni topish uchun shaharga yugurdi.
Tim uni topib dedi: «Din, men ulkan quruqlik hayvonining skelet qoldiqlarini topdim.
Lekin skeletni yolg'iz o'zim chiqara olmayman.
Iltimos, menga yordam berasanmi?»
Din Timning da'vosi shubhali bo'lishi mumkin deb o'yladi.
U javob berdi: «Agar skelet haqida jiddiy gapirayotgan bo'lsang, yordam beraman».
Tim hayajon bilan Dinga skelet joylashgan joyni ko'rsatdi.
Ular har bir suyakni ehtiyotkorlik bilan chiqarib olish uchun birga ishlashdi.
Suyaklarni bir joyda saqlash uchun ularni elastik tasmalar bilan bog'lashdi.
Ular tugatganlarida, mukammal skeletga ega bo'lishdi.
Ular dinozavr bosh suyagining qolipini yasash uchun gipsdan foydalanishdi.
Ular unga ismlarining bosh harflarini o'yib yozishdi va uni mahalliy muzey kuratoriga topshirishdi.
Tim va Din birga juda yaxshi ishlay olishlarini bilib olishdi.
Ular adovatlariga chek qo'yib, do'st bo'lishga qaror qilishdi.
Iste'dodlarini birlashtirib, bu odamlar avvalgidan ham buyukroq bo'lishdi.

e6|3.title: Dressed to Excess
paras: If you traveled back in time to the 1700s in Europe, you would laugh when you saw how the aristocracy dressed. Soon you’d realize, though, that the aristocrats of Europe were very serious about their appearance.

The predominant style in women’s attire was enormous dresses. They were often three times larger than the wearer. Ladies even used pads to enlarge the appearance of their hips and shoulders. On the other extreme, the aristocratic women made their waists appear extremely thin. It took several maids stretching fabric and pulling straps in order to get a lady’s waist to the proper thinness. These ladies could barely breathe and often fainted.

Pale skin was also a craze, yet this too was done in excess. One could not simply be pale. Instead, she needed to look as if she had anemia. In order to look paler, ladies actually cut themselves daily, so they would bleed.

The hairstyles, however, were the hallmark of women’s fashion. These stood a meter high on the ladies’ heads. The columns of hair were a ridiculous tangle of wigs, jewels, flowers, and even stuffed birds.

Men’s fashion was similarly absurd. Today it would probably seem very feminine. Reputable men wore wigs of long curly hair. Their shoes had large soles or high heels so that they could walk high above the filth on the streets. Furthermore, just like the ladies, the men wore lipstick and put rouge on their cheeks.

Their clothes were brightly colored, often purple and pink. They were made from the finest of fabrics and decorated with jewels and lace. The men vied with one another to see who wore the more expensive clothes, for the clothing signified his wealth and status.

Both men and women spent huge amounts of money and time on how they looked. Though such vanity would seem vulgar today, three hundred years from now, the fashions of our time might also seem completely ridiculous.

qs.q: Ladies used pads to enlarge their hips and shoulders.
Only the ladies wore lipstick and rouge.
The aristocracy’s vanity would seem vulgar today.
Women’s hair was a tangle of wigs, straps, flowers, and stuffed birds.
Men’s fashion was absurd and feminine.

tr: Agar vaqt bo'ylab 1700-yillar Yevropasiga sayohat qilsangiz, aslzodalar qanday kiyinganini ko'rib kulib yuborgan bo'lardingiz.
Biroq tez orada Yevropa aslzodalari tashqi ko'rinishlariga juda jiddiy qaraganini tushungan bo'lardingiz.
Ayollar kiyimidagi asosiy uslub ulkan ko'ylaklar edi.
Ular ko'pincha kiygan odamdan uch baravar katta bo'lardi.
Xonimlar hatto son va yelkalarini kattaroq ko'rsatish uchun yostiqchalardan foydalanishardi.
Boshqa tomondan esa, zodagon ayollar bellarini nihoyatda ingichka qilib ko'rsatishardi.
Xonimning belini kerakli darajada ingichka qilish uchun bir nechta xizmatkor matoni tortib, tasmalarni siqishi kerak edi.
Bu xonimlar zo'rg'a nafas olishardi va tez-tez hushdan ketishardi.
Oqargan teri ham urf edi, lekin bu ham haddan oshirib yuborilardi.
Shunchaki oqarib turishning o'zi yetmasdi.
Buning o'rniga ayol kamqonligi bordek ko'rinishi kerak edi.
Oqroq ko'rinish uchun xonimlar haqiqatan ham har kuni qon chiqishi uchun o'zlarini kesishardi.
Biroq ayollar modasining eng asosiy belgisi soch turmaklari edi.
Ular xonimlarning boshida bir metr balandlikda turardi.
Soch ustunlari pariklar, javohirlar, gullar va hatto to'ldirilgan qushlardan iborat kulgili chigal edi.
Erkaklar modasi ham xuddi shunday bema'ni edi.
Bugun u, ehtimol, juda ayollarga xos tuyulardi.
Obro'li erkaklar uzun jingalak sochli pariklar kiyishardi.
Ularning poyabzallarida qalin taglik yoki baland poshna bo'lardi, toki ular ko'chalardagi iflosliklardan baland yura olsinlar.
Bundan tashqari, xuddi xonimlar kabi erkaklar ham lab bo'yog'i surtib, yonoqlariga upa-elik qo'yishardi.
Ularning kiyimlari yorqin rangli, ko'pincha binafsha va pushti edi.
Ular eng nozik matolardan tikilib, javohirlar va to'r bilan bezatilardi.
Erkaklar kim qimmatroq kiyim kiyishi borasida bir-biri bilan bellashishardi, chunki kiyim uning boyligi va maqomini bildirardi.
Erkaklar ham, ayollar ham tashqi ko'rinishlariga juda ko'p pul va vaqt sarflashardi.
Bunday manmanlik bugun qo'pol tuyulsa-da, uch yuz yildan keyin bizning davrimiz modasi ham mutlaqo kulgili ko'rinishi mumkin.

e6|4.title: The Butler’s Bad Day
paras: The Superintendent of Civic Projects was a busy man. He worked every day of the week and had fancy parties at his house every night.

However, if there was someone busier than him, it was his butler. He worked all day organizing the superintendent’s parties and then cleaned up after them late at night. Hence, while the superintendent slept soundly, snoring loudly in his bed, the butler was still awake.

Sadly, though the butler was always overworked, his profession’s intrinsic nature demanded he never be outspoken. Therefore, his employer never knew the butler hadn’t slept for several days. On any day the butler might make a mistake.
One day, the superintendent said, “This particular party is important. People from the ministry are coming. Everything must be perfect.”

The butler began preparing at once. First he went to the attic to get more chairs and tables. But on his descent, he realized he needed to make the food. A gourmet dinner was necessary for such a party. He boiled water in a kettle for soup and chopped some beef into chunks. Just as he was starting the soup, he remembered that he had to sweep the veranda. As he was sweeping the veranda, he realized that he had to clean the sauna.

By this time, the first guests had arrived. The veranda was still dirty. There were not enough chairs for the guests to sit on, and the soup tasted too pungent. Some guests were dissatisfied. They started to make a fuss, and the party was filled with a din of complaints. The superintendent’s party was a disaster. He wondered why his butler had made so many mistakes. At last, the butler admitted to being exhausted. His boss felt pity for the butler. He had no idea the butler was so tired. He said, “You should have told me earlier, then we could have avoided this whole ordeal.”

qs.q: The Superintendent of Civic Projects cleaned late at night; hence, he was busier than his butler.
Though the butler was outspoken, his job’s intrinsic nature made him never become overworked.
This particular party was important because people from the ministry were coming.
The butler boiled caffeine in a kettle and chopped beef into chunks.
The soup for the gourmet dinner tasted too pungent.

tr: Shahar loyihalari boshlig'i band odam edi.
U haftaning har kuni ishlar va har kecha uyida dabdabali ziyofatlar berardi.
Biroq undan ham band odam bo'lsa, bu uning mulozimi edi.
U kun bo'yi boshliqning ziyofatlarini tashkil qilib, keyin kechalari ularning ortidan yig'ishtirardi.
Shuning uchun boshliq to'shagida baland ovozda xurrak otib qattiq uxlayotganda, mulozim hali ham uyg'oq bo'lardi.
Afsuski, mulozim doim haddan tashqari ko'p ishlasa-da, kasbining tabiati undan hech qachon ochiq gapirmaslikni talab qilardi.
Shuning uchun ish beruvchisi mulozimning bir necha kundan beri uxlamaganini hech qachon bilmasdi.
Mulozim istalgan kuni xato qilib qo'yishi mumkin edi.
Bir kuni boshliq dedi: «Aynan bu ziyofat muhim.
Vazirlikdan odamlar kelishadi.
Hamma narsa mukammal bo'lishi kerak».
Mulozim darhol tayyorgarlik ko'ra boshladi.
Avval u ko'proq stul va stol olish uchun chordoqqa chiqdi.
Lekin pastga tushayotganda, u ovqat tayyorlashi kerakligini angladi.
Bunday ziyofat uchun nozik kechki ovqat zarur edi.
U sho'rva uchun choynakda suv qaynatdi va mol go'shtini bo'laklarga to'g'radi.
Sho'rvani endi boshlaganida, u ayvonni supurishi kerakligini esladi.
Ayvonni supurayotganda, u saunani tozalashi kerakligini angladi.
Bu vaqtga kelib birinchi mehmonlar kelib qolgan edi.
Ayvon hali ham iflos edi.
Mehmonlar o'tirishi uchun stullar yetarli emasdi va sho'rvaning ta'mi juda achchiq edi.
Ba'zi mehmonlar norozi bo'lishdi.
Ular janjal ko'tara boshlashdi va ziyofat shikoyatlar shovqiniga to'ldi.
Boshliqning ziyofati halokat bilan yakunlandi.
U mulozimi nega bunchalik ko'p xato qilganiga hayron bo'ldi.
Nihoyat, mulozim holdan toyganini tan oldi.
Boshlig'i mulozimga achindi.
U mulozimning bunchalik charchaganini umuman bilmagan edi.
U dedi: «Menga oldinroq aytishing kerak edi, shunda bu butun mashaqqatning oldini olgan bo'lardik».

e6|5.title: A Bet
paras: Russell finished running a relay and joined his friend Becky in the cafeteria. He asked, “What’s for lunch?”
“Sesame chicken. It’s OK, except the meat’s charred. Oh, and watch out for the chili peppers,” Becky said.
“Chilies don’t bother me!” said Russell.
“My stepmother says you should be careful with them,” replied Becky.
An argument ensued about eating chilies. “Chilies aren’t so bad. I bet I can take more bites of this chili than you,” Russell said.

Becky was wary of eating the pepper. Despite her reluctance, she didn’t want to say no to the bet. She wavered about whether to do it or not. She negotiated the details. “What will the winner get?” she asked.

“The loser has to carry the winner’s books for a year! I’ll even let you go first.” Becky replied, “Fine, but to clarify, you’ll carry my books for the entire school year, right?” Russell restated the agreement, “That’s right. I’ll carry your books all year if you win—which you won’t!”

His dogged persuasion convinced her. The chili looked benign, but Becky knew it could cause a lot of pain. She bit the bottom of the pepper. Surprisingly, she felt nothing. “My turn,” said Russell. He bit the middle of the chili. Immediately, he seemed to be in distress. He gasped and his face alternated between brave and pained expressions. He experienced an overdose of spice. He was on the verge of tears and finally let out a horrible cry.
“Take this,” said Becky, handing him her drink.
“That was awful!” he said, continuing to sip from the glass.

That night, Becky researched chilies. The next day she said in an apologetic voice, “I read that the hot part of chilies is in the middle, where the seeds are. I’m sorry—I feel like I cheated by going first.”
Russell was relieved, not only did he learn something new about chilies, but he learned that Becky was a good friend.

qs.q: Becky was having charred sesame chicken for lunch.
The argument ensued because Becky wavered about whether to run the relay.
After Russell and Becky negotiated the bet, they decided that whoever lost would carry the winner’s books for a year.
Russell was wary about eating the pepper even if it looked benign.
Becky was apologetic because of her choice to take the first bite of the pepper.

tr: Rassell estafetani yugurib bo'lib, oshxonada dugonasi Bekiga qo'shildi.
U so'radi: «Tushlikka nima bor?»
«Kunjutli tovuq.
Yomon emas, faqat go'shti kuyib qolgan.
Ha, aytgancha, qalampirlardan ehtiyot bo'l», dedi Beki.
«Qalampir menga ta'sir qilmaydi!» dedi Rassell.
«O'gay onam ulardan ehtiyot bo'lish kerak deydi», deb javob berdi Beki.
Qalampir yeyish haqida bahs boshlandi.
«Qalampirlar unchalik yomon emas.
Garov o'ynayman, men bu qalampirni sendan ko'proq tishlay olaman», dedi Rassell.
Beki qalampir yeyishdan cho'chirdi.
Istamasa ham, u garovga yo'q deyishni xohlamadi.
U buni qilish-qilmaslik haqida ikkilanib qoldi.
U tafsilotlarni kelishib oldi.
«G'olib nima oladi?» deb so'radi u.
«Yutqazgan bir yil davomida g'olibning kitoblarini ko'tarib yuradi!
