Rassell kelishuvni yana bir bor takrorladi: «To'g'ri.
Agar sen yutsang, butun yil kitoblaringni ko'taraman — lekin sen yutmaysan!»
Uning qaysar ko'ndirishi uni rozi qildi.
Qalampir zararsiz ko'rinardi, lekin Beki u kuchli og'riq keltirishi mumkinligini bilardi.
U qalampirning pastki qismini tishladi.
Ajablanarlisi, u hech narsa sezmadi.
«Endi mening navbatim», dedi Rassell.
U qalampirning o'rtasini tishladi.
Darhol u qiynalayotganga o'xshab qoldi.
U nafasi qaytib, yuzi goh jasur, goh og'riqli ifoda olardi.
U haddan tashqari ko'p achchiq yeb qo'ygan edi.
Uning ko'zlari yoshlanib, nihoyat dahshatli qichqiriq chiqardi.
«Mana, ol», dedi Beki unga ichimligini uzatib.
«Dahshat edi!» dedi u stakandan ho'plashda davom etib.
O'sha kechasi Beki qalampir haqida ma'lumot qidirdi.
Ertasi kuni u uzr so'ragan ohangda dedi: «O'qishimcha, qalampirning achchiq qismi o'rtasida, urug'lari bor joyda bo'larkan.
Kechirasan, birinchi bo'lib aldagandek his qilyapman».
Rassell yengil tortdi: u nafaqat qalampir haqida yangi narsa bilib oldi, balki Beki yaxshi do'st ekanini ham bildi.

e6|6.title: Amazing Komodo Dragons
paras: Once, a British gazette had an unusual story. Scientists at a zoo made a discovery about komodo dragons. Komodo dragons are giant lizards that grow up to two and a half meters long. A female lizard at the zoo had babies. However, it had never been around a male lizard in its entire life. After the scientists publicized their discovery, many people thought it was fictitious.
But it was true. It was discovered that female komodo dragons can have babies without the help of their male counterparts. This contradicts what scientists know about how most animals have babies.

In most cases, there are many things that can obstruct this type of reproduction. For example, adult males and females carry different genes needed to make an embryo. If the genes are homogeneous, the babies are weaker and have genetic problems. Over time, the weakened species dies out completely. This makes it necessary for the male to be involved. However, scientists verified that when Komodo babies are born, their genes aren’t the exact same genes as their mother. Also, they are devoid of any genetic problems.

Scientists theorize that Komodo dragons developed the ability because it helps the species fend off extinction. If a volcano erupts, lava can kill all of the komodo dragons on an island. However, as long as one female eludes death, she can prolong the survival of the species. Luckily, Komodo dragons are vigorous swimmers. So the surviving female can plunge into the ocean and swim to another island. When she comes ashore, she can reproduce by herself. Over time, the genes within the population diverge. Then, the sparse population increases. Once again there is a surplus of lizards on one island. Scientists think that this may be how the lizards took over all of the islands in that area.

qs.q: People thought that the story publicized in the gazette about the komodo dragons was fictitious.
Female komodo dragons can have babies without their male counterparts.
Scientists verified that baby komodo dragons have homogeneous genes if they don’t have fathers, which leads to genetic problems.
Scientists theorize that the special ability of komodo dragons help them elude predators.
A female komodo dragon can increase a sparse population so that there are surplus lizards on one island.

tr: Bir paytlar bir Britaniya gazetasida g'ayrioddiy maqola chiqdi.
Hayvonot bog'idagi olimlar komodo varanlari haqida kashfiyot qilishdi.
Komodo varanlari ikki yarim metrgacha o'sadigan ulkan kaltakesaklardir.
Hayvonot bog'idagi urg'ochi kaltakesak bolaladi.
Biroq u butun umri davomida hech qachon erkak kaltakesak bilan birga bo'lmagan edi.
Olimlar kashfiyotlarini e'lon qilganlaridan keyin ko'p odamlar buni to'qima deb o'ylashdi.
Lekin bu rost edi.
Urg'ochi komodo varanlari erkak juftining yordamisiz bola tug'a olishi aniqlandi.
Bu olimlarning ko'pchilik hayvonlar qanday ko'payishi haqidagi bilimlariga zid keladi.
Ko'p hollarda bu turdagi ko'payishga to'sqinlik qiladigan ko'p narsalar bor.
Masalan, voyaga yetgan erkak va urg'ochilar embrion hosil qilish uchun kerakli turli genlarni tashiydi.
Agar genlar bir xil bo'lsa, bolalar zaifroq bo'ladi va genetik muammolarga ega bo'ladi.
Vaqt o'tishi bilan zaiflashgan tur butunlay yo'q bo'lib ketadi.
Shuning uchun erkakning ishtiroki zarur bo'ladi.
Biroq olimlar komodo bolalari tug'ilganda ularning genlari onasinikiga aynan bir xil emasligini tasdiqlashdi.
Shuningdek, ularda hech qanday genetik muammo yo'q.
Olimlarning nazariyasiga ko'ra, komodo varanlari bu qobiliyatni rivojlantirgan, chunki u turga yo'q bo'lib ketishdan himoyalanishga yordam beradi.
Agar vulqon otilsa, lava oroldagi barcha komodo varanlarini o'ldirishi mumkin.
Biroq bitta urg'ochi o'limdan qochib qutulsa, u turning yashashini davom ettira oladi.
Baxtga, komodo varanlari baquvvat suzuvchilardir.
Shuning uchun omon qolgan urg'ochi okeanga sho'ng'ib, boshqa orolga suzib o'ta oladi.
Qirg'oqqa chiqqach, u o'zi yolg'iz ko'paya oladi.
Vaqt o'tishi bilan populyatsiya ichidagi genlar farqlana boradi.
Keyin siyrak populyatsiya ko'payadi.
Yana bir orolda kaltakesaklar ko'payib ketadi.
Olimlarning fikricha, kaltakesaklar o'sha hududdagi barcha orollarni shu yo'l bilan egallab olgan bo'lishi mumkin.

e6|7.title: Greek Magical Papyri
paras: The Greek Magical Papyri is a collection of writing about magic. After it was found in the Egyptian desert, it took experts years to decipher it. The text was written in at least three different ancient languages. After many years, experts realized it contained a number of spells that varied greatly in scope.

The most common types of magic in the collection dealt with healing illnesses like pneumonia. Some spells also gave advice for treating people with mental illnesses, such as those who became psychotic. Some spells asked for unusual things, like crocodile dung. But botany was an important part of the magic. Many healing spells gave instructions on how to use herbs and plants that were believed to be therapeutic. For example, in order to cure arthritis, the book says that the magician should build an ornate altar. Then he should mash different types of herbs and place them on top of it. At dusk, he is supposed to say a spell, so the gods would be gratified.

Other parts of the collection describe how to hone one’s psychic abilities and how to give credible descriptions of the future. Often, the book advised people how to use different objects to tell the future, including tea leaves. Also, one part of the book tells what different dreams might mean. It gives advice for using dreams to tell the future.

A small part of the book, however, is more sinister than the rest. It is meant to cause strife and deception. For example, one tells how to give someone warts, while another will make all of the victim’s farm animals die. However, if someone’s farm animals died as a result of a curse, he could ask a magician to perform magic that makes the deceased come back to life.

qs.q: The Greek Magical Papyri was hard to decipher because it was too large in scope.
The book is about botany.
A spell is spoken at dusk to become more credible.
The book had instructions for honing one’s psychic powers.

tr: «Yunon sehrli papiruslari» — sehr haqidagi yozuvlar to'plami.
U Misr cho'lida topilgandan keyin mutaxassislarga uni o'qib chiqish uchun yillar kerak bo'ldi.
Matn kamida uchta turli qadimiy tilda yozilgan edi.
Ko'p yillardan keyin mutaxassislar unda ko'lami jihatidan bir-biridan juda farq qiladigan ko'plab duolar borligini anglashdi.
To'plamdagi eng keng tarqalgan sehr turlari zotiljam kabi kasalliklarni davolash bilan bog'liq edi.
Ba'zi duolar ruhiy kasalliklarga chalinganlarni, masalan, aqldan ozganlarni davolash bo'yicha maslahatlar ham berardi.
Ba'zi duolar timsoh go'ngi kabi g'ayrioddiy narsalarni talab qilardi.
Lekin botanika sehrning muhim qismi edi.
Ko'plab shifobaxsh duolar shifobaxsh deb hisoblangan o'tlar va o'simliklardan qanday foydalanish haqida ko'rsatmalar berardi.

Keyin u turli xil o'tlarni ezib, ularni uning ustiga qo'yishi kerak.
Kech kirganda u xudolar mamnun bo'lishi uchun duo o'qishi kerak.
To'plamning boshqa qismlarida g'aybni bilish qobiliyatini qanday charxlash va kelajakni qanday ishonarli tasvirlash bayon qilingan.
Ko'pincha kitob odamlarga kelajakni aytish uchun turli narsalardan, jumladan choy barglaridan qanday foydalanishni maslahat berardi.
Shuningdek, kitobning bir qismida turli tushlar nimani anglatishi mumkinligi aytilgan.
U kelajakni aytish uchun tushlardan foydalanish bo'yicha maslahatlar beradi.
Biroq kitobning kichik bir qismi qolganidan ko'ra dahshatliroq.
U nizo va aldovga sabab bo'lishga mo'ljallangan.

Biroq agar kimningdir uy hayvonlari qarg'ish natijasida o'lsa, u sehrgardan o'liklarni tiriltiradigan sehr qilishni so'rashi mumkin edi.

e6|8.title: Watch Out!
paras: Kevin stepped off the tram and walked toward the ship, holding a package tightly in his hands. He had been hired as a courier for an important broker. All he needed to do was deliver a package to an office in New York City; the ship would take him there. When he boarded, the ship was congested with people. As Kevin walked to his cabin, he saw the exclusive first-class section. Everybody inside was wearing fancy garments. He would have liked to socialize with the people inside, but it was against proper etiquette. People paid a premium for the privilege to ride in first-class.

Instead, he went to his cabin next to the freight section of the boat. His room smelled bad, and the floorboards were warped and deformed in some areas. He could also hear the motor humming as it waited to propel the ship forward. Suddenly, Kevin was unsettled by something, but he wasn’t sure why.

He took a short walk on the ship’s deck, but he still felt strange. That night, he suffered from insomnia—he couldn’t suppress his obsessing over how strange he felt. Kevin went back on deck. It was cold and dark outside. He looked overboard, but it seemed that everything was all right. “Just go back inside,” he thought. Then Kevin saw it. A giant iceberg was sticking out of the ocean in the distance!
“Help!” he yelled.
People looked at him as if he was crazy, but he continued to shout until he saw the captain.
“There’s an iceberg out there,” Kevin said to him. “If the ship doesn’t move, we’re liable to crash,” he said, pointing toward the iceberg.

The captain saw it and immediately instructed the crew to change the ship’s direction. “Without your help, we would have definitely hit the iceberg. That would have been a terrible disaster!” he said to Kevin.
Kevin felt relieved. Now he knew to always trust his intuitive sense.

qs.q: In order to get the privilege to be in the exclusive section, one had to wear fancy garments.
Kevin didn’t socialize with the people in the exclusive section because it was too congested.
Kevin could not sleep because he had insomnia.
If Kevin hadn’t seen the iceberg, the ship was liable to have crashed into it.

«Sizning yordamingiz bo'lmaganida, biz albatta aysbergga urilgan bo'lardik.
Bu dahshatli falokat bo'lardi!» dedi u Kevinga.

e6|9.title: Dangerous Bites
paras: There are many animals with dangerous bites in the world, but which one is the worst? Some would say that the elusive short-tailed mamushi has the worst bite. The snake only goes into homes to chase pests such as mice. Otherwise, it stays in the fields, where it’s dangerous to people who forage for food there. If someone stuns it by accidentally stepping on it, it bites to protect itself. At first, the effects of the bite may seem negligible because it doesn’t cause a lot of bleeding. However, after a few moments, the venom induces paralysis in the area where the individual was bitten. Furthermore, the venom can also impede respiration. If the person doesn’t go to the doctor, they are susceptible to kidney deterioration.

Others would argue that tigers have the worst bite. Mother tigers are inseparable from their babies and seem to be the gentlest creatures when they are around their young. However, if the babies are threatened, the mother tiger’s savage nature prevails. With strong jaws and the ability to move quickly, the tiger can kill someone with one bite. That’s because it always tries to bite an important artery when it attacks. If the artery is ruptured, the victim will bleed to death.

In the mainstream, animal bites are seen as the most dangerous. But some scientists think this idea is invalid. In fact, the most dangerous bite might be the human bite. When scientists magnified the contents in human saliva, they found about three hundred different microbes in it. A human bite can be dangerous if the bacteria enters the body through a cut, which can make people very sick. Furthermore, most people don’t clean a human bite right away.

qs.q: The elusive mamushi attacks humans if it is bothered by pests in houses.
The consequences of a mamushi bite are negligible.
Mother tigers are inseparable from their babies.
When tigers attack, they try to rupture an important artery.
Scientists think that the mainstream idea that human bites are the most dangerous is invalid.

tr: Dunyoda chaqishi xavfli bo'lgan hayvonlar ko'p, lekin ulardan qaysi biri eng yomoni?
Ba'zilar tutqich bermaydigan qisqa dumli mamushi ilonining chaqishi eng yomoni deyishadi.
Bu ilon uylarga faqat sichqon kabi zararkunandalarni quvish uchun kiradi.
Aks holda u dalalarda qoladi va u yerda ovqat qidirib yurgan odamlar uchun xavfli bo'ladi.
Agar kimdir bexosdan uni bosib olib, gangitib qo'ysa, u o'zini himoya qilish uchun chaqadi.
Avvaliga chaqishning oqibatlari arzimasdek tuyulishi mumkin, chunki u ko'p qon ketishiga sabab bo'lmaydi.
Biroq bir necha daqiqadan keyin zahar odam chaqilgan joyda falajlikni keltirib chiqaradi.
Bundan tashqari, zahar nafas olishga ham to'sqinlik qilishi mumkin.
Agar odam shifokorga bormasa, uning buyraklari ishdan chiqishi mumkin.
Boshqalar yo'lbarslarning tishlashi eng yomoni deb bahslashadi.
Ona yo'lbarslar bolalaridan ajralmaydi va bolalari yonida eng yuvosh maxluqlardek ko'rinadi.
Biroq agar bolalariga xavf tug'ilsa, ona yo'lbarsning yovvoyi tabiati ustun keladi.
Kuchli jag'lari va tez harakatlana olishi tufayli yo'lbars odamni bir tishlashda o'ldirishi mumkin.
Buning sababi, u hujum qilganda doim muhim arteriyani tishlashga harakat qiladi.
Agar arteriya yorilsa, jabrlanuvchi qon yo'qotib o'ladi.
Umumiy fikrga ko'ra, hayvonlarning tishlashi eng xavfli hisoblanadi.
Lekin ba'zi olimlar bu fikrni noto'g'ri deb hisoblashadi.

Olimlar inson so'lagidagi narsalarni kattalashtirib ko'rganlarida, unda uch yuzga yaqin turli mikrob topishdi.
Agar bakteriya kesik orqali tanaga kirsa, inson tishlashi xavfli bo'lishi mumkin, bu esa odamlarni og'ir kasal qilib qo'yishi mumkin.
Bundan tashqari, ko'pchilik odamlar inson tishlagan joyni darhol tozalashmaydi.

e6|10.title: The Avalanche
paras: Randy was a forest ranger. Because of his job, he was secluded in a cabin in the wilderness.

One day, the radio reported, “Convection in the atmosphere is causing a lot of clouds to form. A serious storm...” Suddenly, the radio went silent. The signal was lost. He went outside and looked at the overcast sky. Anybody else would have taken the dark sky as an omen of a very bad storm, but not Randy. His upbringing had taught him consistency. He had done this job for years, and nothing could stop him. Besides, he thought nothing could hurt him.

Today, he had a very important task to do. The snow was starting to pile up high on the mountain. If too much accumulated, it could cause an avalanche. But Randy had an apparatus to get rid of the snow. It used dynamite to shake the snow and make the top layer of snow come down.

As the snow started falling, he thought about returning to the office until the storm stopped, but he decided not to. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise behind him. It was an avalanche! He started to run, but within seconds, he was knocked sideways and buried by the snow and rubble from an old cabin that had been destroyed. An aerial rescue team came quickly. Randy was just a speck amongst the great pile of snow, but the team found him thanks to his brightly colored jacket. They quickly took him to a hospital. After a few hours, Randy woke up in the hospital. He looked at the sober faces of the doctors and saw his wife sobbing.
“What’s wrong?” he asked. He didn’t remember what had happened.
“You were almost killed!” his wife said.
“You broke several ribs. But the rest of you is still reasonably intact. You are really lucky to be alive,” the doctor said.
After five days, Randy was discharged from the hospital. The experience had taught him a poignant lesson: he was a mortal, and nature was much more powerful than him.

qs.q: Randy’s job as a ranger had taught him consistency.
Randy had an apparatus that moved snow sideways to help avoid avalanches.
Randy was seen by the aerial rescue team thanks to his brightly colored jacket.
According to the doctor, Randy was lucky to be alive after the avalanche.

Ishi tufayli u yovvoyi tabiatdagi kulbada yolg'iz yashardi.
Bir kuni radio xabar berdi: «Atmosferadagi konveksiya ko'plab bulutlar hosil bo'lishiga sabab bo'lmoqda.
Kuchli bo'ron...»
To'satdan radio jim bo'lib qoldi.
Signal yo'qolgan edi.
U tashqariga chiqib, bulut qoplagan osmonga qaradi.
Boshqa har qanday odam qorong'i osmonni juda kuchli bo'ronning alomati deb bilardi, lekin Rendi emas.

Bu qor ko'chkisi edi!
U yugura boshladi, lekin bir necha soniya ichida uni yonboshga uloqtirib yuborishdi va qor hamda vayron bo'lgan eski kulbaning siniqlari ostida qolib ketdi.
Havodan qutqaruv guruhi tezda yetib keldi.
Rendi ulkan qor uyumi orasida shunchaki bir nuqta edi, lekin guruh uni yorqin rangli kurtkasi tufayli topdi.
Ular uni tezda kasalxonaga olib borishdi.
Bir necha soatdan keyin Rendi kasalxonada uyg'ondi.
U shifokorlarning jiddiy yuzlariga qaradi va xotinining ho'ngrab yig'layotganini ko'rdi.
«Nima bo'ldi?» deb so'radi u.
U nima bo'lganini eslay olmadi.
«Sal qoldi o'lib ketishingga!» dedi xotini.
«Bir nechta qovurg'angiz singan.
Lekin qolgan joylaringiz ancha butun.
Tirik qolganingiz haqiqatan ham omad», dedi shifokor.
Besh kundan keyin Rendi kasalxonadan chiqarildi.
Bu voqea unga ta'sirli saboq berdi: u o'lishi mumkin bo'lgan oddiy inson edi va tabiat undan ancha qudratliroq edi.

e6|11.title: The Lydian King
paras: King Croesus was once one of the richest kings in the world. He ruled over Lydia, an ancient empire located near modern-day Turkey and controlled a valuable commodity: gold. Many people were very envious of him.

One day, a messenger disclosed some interesting news: political unrest in Persia had weakened the empire. Before then, the Persians had taken over many countries. Many leaders were scared of the Persian conquest. But King Croesus understood the dynamics of war better than most. He decided that it would be a good time to try to beat the Persians while they were weak.

He advocated starting war, but nobody shared his sentiment. Then he asked a wise member of the senate who was visiting from Athens. The sage didn’t say whether he should attack the Persians or not. He only warned him that his good luck wouldn’t last. Finally, King Croesus sent a messenger to visit the Oracle, a special lady who could see the future. The messenger gave the Oracle jugs of wine and baskets of lentils in order to make her happy.
When the messenger came back, he was in a festive mood.
“What was the Oracle’s prophecy?” asked King Croesus.
The jolly messenger responded, “She said that if you attack Persia, you will destroy a great empire.”

The news filled Croesus with euphoria. After hearing the Oracle’s prophecy, many civilians enrolled in the Lydian army. The king marshaled his troops and prepared them for a war with Persia. Their morale was high because they were sure they would win. Soon, King Croesus authorized an attack against the Persians.

However, the Persian army was still very strong. After a few months of fighting, it was obvious that the Oracle’s prophecy had come true: by attacking the Persians, King Croesus had destroyed a great empire—his own! King Croesus should have considered the advice more carefully.

qs.q: People were envious of King Croesus because he understood the dynamics of war better than anybody else.
The messenger disclosed that the Persians were in a state of unrest.
The sage man from the senate was the only one that shared the king’s sentiment.
The messenger gave the Oracle jugs of wine and baskets of lentils to make her happy.
The Oracle’s prophecy was that the Lydian conquest of Persia would be successful.

tr: Qirol Krez bir paytlar dunyodagi eng boy qirollardan biri bo'lgan.
U hozirgi Turkiya yaqinida joylashgan qadimiy imperiya Lidiyani boshqargan va qimmatbaho mol — oltinni nazorat qilgan.
Ko'p odamlar unga juda hasad qilishardi.
Bir kuni bir xabarchi qiziq yangilikni ma'lum qildi: Forsdagi siyosiy notinchlik imperiyani zaiflashtirgan edi.
Ungacha forslar ko'plab mamlakatlarni bosib olgan edi.
Ko'plab hukmdorlar forslarning istilosidan qo'rqishardi.
Lekin qirol Krez urush qonuniyatlarini ko'pchilikdan yaxshiroq tushunardi.
U forslar zaif paytida ularni yengishga urinish uchun qulay vaqt deb qaror qildi.
U urush boshlash tarafdori edi, lekin hech kim uning fikriga qo'shilmadi.
Keyin u Afinadan tashrif buyurgan senatning dono bir a'zosidan so'radi.
Donishmand u forslarga hujum qilishi kerakmi yoki yo'qmi, aytmadi.
U faqat uning omadi uzoqqa bormasligidan ogohlantirdi.
Nihoyat, qirol Krez kelajakni ko'ra oladigan alohida ayol — Bashoratgo'yning oldiga xabarchi yubordi.
Xabarchi Bashoratgo'yni xursand qilish uchun unga ko'zachalarda sharob va savatlarda yasmiq berdi.
Xabarchi qaytib kelganida, uning kayfiyati bayramona edi.
«Bashoratgo'yning bashorati qanday bo'ldi?» deb so'radi qirol Krez.
Quvnoq xabarchi javob berdi: «U agar siz Forsga hujum qilsangiz, buyuk bir imperiyani vayron qilasiz, dedi».
Bu xabar Krezni behad xursand qildi.
Bashoratgo'yning bashoratini eshitgach, ko'plab tinch aholi Lidiya qo'shiniga yozilishdi.
Qirol qo'shinlarini to'plab, ularni Fors bilan urushga tayyorladi.
Ularning ruhi baland edi, chunki g'alaba qozonishlariga amin edilar.
Tez orada qirol Krez forslarga qarshi hujumga ruxsat berdi.
Biroq Fors qo'shini hali ham juda kuchli edi.
Bir necha oylik janglardan keyin Bashoratgo'yning bashorati amalga oshgani ayon bo'ldi: forslarga hujum qilib, qirol Krez buyuk imperiyani — o'zinikini vayron qilgan edi!
Qirol Krez maslahatni diqqat bilan o'ylab ko'rishi kerak edi.

e6|12.title: The Butler
paras: Greta was an elderly lady who lived alone in a huge, dilapidated mansion. The mansion was in terrible condition. It was covered with filth, and most of the furniture was broken. Plus, the kitchen sink leaked water all over the floor. Greta was too old to do housekeeping and repairs herself, so she hired a butler named Gordon.

Gordon was a young, muscular man. His muscles were a testament to his strong work ethic. He believed that if he worked hard, great things would happen for him. On his first day, he worked for hours cleaning and making repairs. He swept up mounds of dirt. He tightened the valve underneath the kitchen faucet to stop the leak. He even bought timber to build new stools for the kitchen. He worked so hard that his fingers went numb, and he got cramps in his shoulders.

Gordon worked hard every day. Even when tasks were boring, he was never reckless. He made sure there were no flaws in his work. Gordon was worried, however, that Greta wasn’t pleased. She never expressed thanks or said that he did a good job. The lack of appreciation evoked unhappy feelings in Gordon. He even thought about quitting. But he decided the right thing to do was to keep working hard.

One day, while Gordon was sweeping, Greta said, “Gordon! I have a surprise for you!” He went to Greta’s room and saw a beautiful slate statue. It looked just like him! It was adorned with a banner that read: “Welcome home.”
Greta said, “You’ve made this ugly old mansion look new again. I’m so thankful for your hard work that I want you to have it. I’ll move into a smaller house.”
He grinned and gave Greta a big hug. He said, “I’m in bliss! My hard work really paid off!”
The two said their farewells, and Gordon spent the afternoon admiring his beautiful new home.

qs.q: The dilapidated mansion was covered in filth.
Gordon’s muscles were a testament to his flaws.
Gordon was never reckless even when tasks were boring.
The mound of dirt evoked unhappy feelings in Gordon.
Gordon tightened the valve under the kitchen faucet and bought timber to build stools.

tr: Greta ulkan, xaroba qasrda yolg'iz yashaydigan keksa xonim edi.
Qasrning ahvoli dahshatli edi.
U iflosliklarga to'la edi va mebellarning ko'pi singan edi.
Buning ustiga, oshxona rakovinasidan suv sizib, butun polga yoyilardi.
Greta uy ishlarini va ta'mirlashni o'zi qilish uchun juda qarib qolgan edi, shuning uchun Gordon ismli mulozimni yolladi.
Gordon yosh, muskulli yigit edi.
Uning muskullari mehnatsevarligining isboti edi.
U agar qattiq ishlasa, uning hayotida ajoyib narsalar yuz berishiga ishonardi.
Birinchi kuni u soatlab tozalash va ta'mirlash ishlarini qildi.
U uyum-uyum axlatni supurib tashladi.
U oqishni to'xtatish uchun oshxona jo'mragi ostidagi ventilni mahkamladi.
U hatto oshxona uchun yangi kursilar yasash maqsadida taxta sotib oldi.
U shunchalik qattiq ishladiki, barmoqlari uvishib, yelkalari tortishib qoldi.
Gordon har kuni qattiq ishladi.
Hatto vazifalar zerikarli bo'lganda ham, u hech qachon beparvolik qilmasdi.
U ishida hech qanday nuqson bo'lmasligiga ishonch hosil qilardi.
Biroq Gordon Greta mamnun emas deb xavotirlanardi.
U hech qachon minnatdorlik bildirmas yoki yaxshi ishlading demasdi.
Qadrlanmaslik Gordonda noxush tuyg'ular uyg'otdi.
U hatto ishdan ketishni ham o'yladi.
Lekin u to'g'ri yo'l qattiq ishlashda davom etish ekanini qaror qildi.
Bir kuni Gordon supurayotganda, Greta dedi: «Gordon!
Senga bir syurprizim bor!»
U Gretaning xonasiga bordi va chiroyli shifer haykalni ko'rdi.
U xuddi unga o'xshardi!
U «Uyingizga xush kelibsiz» degan yozuvli banner bilan bezatilgan edi.
Greta dedi: «Sen bu xunuk eski qasrni yana yangidek qilding.
Mehnating uchun shunchalik minnatdormanki, uning seniki bo'lishini xohlayman.
Men kichikroq uyga ko'chib o'taman».
U tirjayib, Gretani mahkam quchoqladi.
U dedi: «Men baxtdan mast bo'ldim!
Mehnatim haqiqatan ham o'z samarasini berdi!»
Ikkalasi xayrlashishdi va Gordon tushdan keyin go'zal yangi uyiga mahliyo bo'lib o'tkazdi.

e6|13.title: The End of Smallpox
paras: Smallpox was once the most deadly disease in the world. During the 1800s, more than 20 million people got the disease every year. Of those, nearly half died. At the onset of smallpox, people suffered from high fevers, headaches, vomiting, and aching muscles. Yet the worst symptom of all was an intolerable rash that caused irritation on the entire body. Those who survived the disease were often rendered blind or left with gross scars on their face and body.

Today, however, cases of smallpox are very rare due to the work of many countries during the late 1900s. This federation of countries collaborated to completely destroy smallpox. Early in the century, wealthy countries in Europe and North America had developed a substance that made the body immune to smallpox. They had required all their citizens to get this vaccine to counteract the disease. Hence, the people of these countries no longer had to worry about smallpox.
However, many of the needy people in poorer parts of the world still suffered from the disease. Their countries could not afford the vaccine nor supply enough doctors to curb the spread of smallpox.

In 1950, the wealthier countries of the world vowed to free the world of the disease. They pledged to supply the vaccine to any country that could not afford it. Scientists compiled lists of areas where the disease still thrived. Then doctors diagnosed people who had the disease in these areas. They enacted laws that prohibited people with smallpox from mixing with those who did not. In this way, they could not transmit the disease to others. Then the doctors gave all of them the vaccine.

It took a long time and a lot of work. But nearly thirty years later, on December 9, 1979, a group of scientists certified that smallpox had been successfully stopped. The humane efforts of people from all over the world had accomplished a great task.

qs.q: Smallpox was once the most deadly disease in the world.
Wealthy countries first developed the vaccine in the late 1900s.
Poorer countries could not afford the vaccine.
People with smallpox were allowed to mix with healthy people.
Scientists certified that smallpox had been stopped in 1979.

tr: Chechak bir paytlar dunyodagi eng halokatli kasallik bo'lgan.
1800-yillarda har yili 20 milliondan ortiq odam bu kasallikka chalingan.
Ulardan qariyb yarmi vafot etgan.
Chechak boshlanishida odamlar yuqori isitma, bosh og'rig'i, qusish va mushak og'riqlaridan aziyat chekishgan.
Biroq eng yomon alomat butun tanada qichishish keltirib chiqaradigan chidab bo'lmas toshma edi.
Kasallikdan omon qolganlar ko'pincha ko'r bo'lib qolishgan yoki yuzi va tanasida xunuk chandiqlar qolgan.
Biroq bugungi kunda 1900-yillar oxirida ko'plab mamlakatlarning qilgan ishlari tufayli chechak holatlari juda kam uchraydi.
Mamlakatlarning bu ittifoqi chechakni butunlay yo'q qilish uchun hamkorlik qildi.
Asr boshida Yevropa va Shimoliy Amerikadagi boy mamlakatlar tanani chechakka qarshi immunitetli qiladigan modda ishlab chiqishgan edi.
Ular kasallikka qarshi kurashish uchun barcha fuqarolaridan bu vaksinani olishni talab qilishgan edi.
Shu sababli bu mamlakatlar aholisi endi chechak haqida tashvishlanmasdi.
Biroq dunyoning qashshoqroq hududlaridagi ko'plab muhtoj odamlar hamon bu kasallikdan aziyat chekardi.
Ularning mamlakatlari na vaksina sotib olishga qodir edi, na chechak tarqalishini jilovlash uchun yetarlicha shifokor ta'minlay olardi.
1950-yilda dunyoning boyroq mamlakatlari dunyoni bu kasallikdan xalos etishga va'da berishdi.
Ular vaksinani sotib olishga qurbi yetmaydigan har qanday mamlakatga yetkazib berishga ahd qilishdi.
Olimlar kasallik hamon avj olgan hududlar ro'yxatini tuzishdi.
Keyin shifokorlar bu hududlarda kasallikka chalingan odamlarga tashxis qo'yishdi.
Ular chechak bilan og'riganlarning kasal bo'lmaganlar bilan aralashishini taqiqlaydigan qonunlar qabul qilishdi.
Shu tariqa ular kasallikni boshqalarga yuqtira olmasdilar.
Keyin shifokorlar ularning hammasiga vaksina qilishdi.
Bu ko'p vaqt va mehnat talab qildi.
Lekin qariyb o'ttiz yildan keyin, 1979-yil 9-dekabrda bir guruh olimlar chechak muvaffaqiyatli to'xtatilganini tasdiqlashdi.
Butun dunyo odamlarining insonparvarlik sa'y-harakatlari buyuk vazifani amalga oshirgan edi.

e6|14.title: The Coward’s Lesson
paras: Tom was easily frightened. He enlisted in the army because he thought the military would teach him courage. And though he needed courage, he never imagined how he would learn it.

During a march across a tract of wilderness near his country’s frontier, Tom strayed from his squad. He had stopped to gaze at a splendid view of a lush valley. When he turned around, his squad was gone. He searched for them, but because their outfits had camouflage, he couldn’t find them.

It was getting dark, and Tom grew weary. All he had was a knife, a boomerang, and his handbook. He made a camp for the night. It was cold, and the ground was hard. He wished he had his cot and a blanket. Instead, he made a fire, wrapped himself tightly in his jacket, and fell asleep.

A loud noise roused him from his sleep. “What was that?” he wondered. Then he noticed it. An animal of substantial size had left a print from its paw in the dirt. He sat closer to the fire and looked into the darkness. He imagined a large beast jumping from the gloom and attacking him. He shook so much from fear that it felt like the marrow in his bones quivered.
Tom contemplated many different plans. He was hesitant to act. He decided to stay by the fire, but during his vigil, he heard more noises.

He couldn’t contend with his fear any longer. He knew what he had to do. He made a torch and followed the prints. He heard a twig snap very close ahead, but he bravely went on. Seconds later, he discovered what had scared him. It was only a kangaroo.
Tom went back to his camp and slept. In the morning, he found his squad. He had finally learned courage. He learned that he had to confront his fear in order to conquer it.

qs.q: Tom joined the army because he wanted to learn courage.
Tom left his squad to look for food.
Tom had a knife, a boomerang, and his handbook.
Tom stayed by the fire all night and never left his camp.
The animal that scared Tom was a kangaroo.

tr: Tom tez qo'rqib ketardi.
U harbiy xizmat unga jasoratni o'rgatadi deb o'ylab armiyaga yozildi.
Unga jasorat kerak bo'lsa-da, uni qanday o'rganishini hech qachon tasavvur qilmagan edi.
Mamlakati chegarasi yaqinidagi yovvoyi hudud bo'ylab yurish paytida Tom o'z bo'linmasidan adashib qoldi.
U yam-yashil vodiyning ajoyib manzarasiga tikilish uchun to'xtagan edi.
U orqasiga o'girilganida, bo'linmasi yo'q edi.
U ularni qidirdi, lekin kiyimlari niqobli bo'lgani uchun topa olmadi.
Qorong'i tusha boshladi va Tom holdan toydi.
Uning bor-yo'g'i pichog'i, bumerangi va qo'llanmasi bor edi.
U tunash uchun joy qildi.
Havo sovuq, yer esa qattiq edi.
U yig'ma karavoti va adyoli bo'lishini istardi.
Buning o'rniga u gulxan yoqdi, kurtkasiga mahkam o'ralib oldi va uxlab qoldi.
Kuchli shovqin uni uyqusidan uyg'otdi.
«Bu nima edi?» deb o'yladi u.
Keyin u uni payqadi.
Ancha katta bir hayvon tuproqda panjasining izini qoldirgan edi.
U gulxanga yaqinroq o'tirib, qorong'ilikka tikildi.
U zulmatdan katta bir yirtqich sakrab chiqib, unga hujum qilayotganini tasavvur qildi.
U qo'rquvdan shunchalik qaltirardiki, go'yo suyaklarining iligi titrayotgandek tuyuldi.
Tom ko'plab turli rejalarni o'ylab ko'rdi.
U harakat qilishga ikkilanardi.
U gulxan yonida qolishga qaror qildi, lekin bedor o'tirgan paytida yana shovqinlarni eshitdi.
U endi qo'rquviga bardosh bera olmadi.
U nima qilishi kerakligini bildi.
U mash'al yasab, izlarning ortidan bordi.
U juda yaqinda oldinda xivich qarsillab singanini eshitdi, lekin jasorat bilan oldinga yurdi.
Bir necha soniyadan keyin u uni nima qo'rqitganini aniqladi.
Bu shunchaki kenguru edi.
Tom lageriga qaytib, uxladi.
Ertalab u bo'linmasini topdi.
U nihoyat jasoratni o'rgandi.
U qo'rquvini yengish uchun unga yuzma-yuz chiqishi kerakligini bildi.

e6|15.title: Epidemic in Zimbabwe
paras: In August of 2008, a deadly cholera epidemic manifested in Zimbabwe. A severe health hazard caused the outbreak. There was an extreme lack of clean drinking water in the overcrowded urban cities. Garbage and chemicals got into the public water supplies and contaminated them. Since people did not have access to other sources, they had to drink the dirty water.

The outbreak spread rapidly and infected almost 16,000 people. The illness caused extreme pain in people’s intestines. It also caused a deficiency of important fluids in sick people’s bodies. Without the proper fluids and minerals, metabolic processes stopped working correctly. People were unable to digest food properly or replenish their lost nutrients. If they had not received viable treatment, they would have been likely to die. It was imperative for help to come soon.

However, the government of Zimbabwe was unable to provide help to its people. The government didn’t have a plan to stop the spread of cholera. In addition, the country was too poor to get clean water or medication for the sick. The people seemed to be doomed. Luckily, many other countries recognized the paramount need to contain the outbreak. Dozens of voluntary practitioners from Britain, France, the United States, and other countries went to Zimbabwe to treat the disease. Through the provision of sterile drinking water and medication, people finally got the treatment they badly needed. The compassionate doctors were able to save the lives of thousands. By January of 2009, the epidemic was almost completely contained.

Today, the Zimbabwean government is working with other countries to prevent future epidemics. They are cleaning up the water supply and learning how to avoid health hazards. The system used to filter water is being upgraded. The government now administers the water supply plants and makes sure that they adhere to strict safety guidelines. Hopefully, future instances of cholera will be treated before they start deadly epidemics.

qs.q: The health hazard was a lack of sterile drinking water in overcrowded urban cities.
A deficiency of contaminated water caused metabolic processes to stop working correctly.
It was imperative that people received viable treatment quickly.
The government now administers water supply plants to make sure they adhere to guidelines.

tr: 2008-yil avgustida Zimbabveda halokatli vabo epidemiyasi namoyon bo'ldi.
Kasallik tarqalishiga jiddiy sog'liq xavfi sabab bo'ldi.
Aholisi haddan tashqari ko'p shaharlarda toza ichimlik suvi o'ta yetishmasdi.
Axlat va kimyoviy moddalar jamoat suv ta'minotiga tushib, uni ifloslantirdi.
Odamlarning boshqa manbalardan foydalanish imkoni bo'lmagani uchun ular iflos suv ichishga majbur edilar.
Kasallik tez tarqalib, qariyb 16 000 kishiga yuqdi.
Kasallik odamlarning ichaklarida qattiq og'riq keltirib chiqardi.
U bemorlar tanasida muhim suyuqliklar yetishmovchiligiga ham sabab bo'ldi.
Kerakli suyuqlik va minerallar bo'lmagani uchun moddalar almashinuvi jarayonlari to'g'ri ishlamay qoldi.
Odamlar ovqatni to'g'ri hazm qila olmas va yo'qotilgan ozuqa moddalarini to'ldira olmasdi.
Agar ular samarali davolanishmaganida, o'lishlari ehtimoli yuqori edi.
Yordam tezda kelishi shart edi.
Biroq Zimbabve hukumati o'z xalqiga yordam bera olmadi.
Hukumatda vabo tarqalishini to'xtatish rejasi yo'q edi.
Bundan tashqari, mamlakat bemorlar uchun toza suv yoki dori-darmon olishga juda qashshoq edi.
Odamlar halokatga mahkumdek tuyulardi.
Baxtga, ko'plab boshqa mamlakatlar kasallik tarqalishini cheklash o'ta muhim ekanini tan olishdi.
Britaniya, Fransiya, AQSh va boshqa mamlakatlardan o'nlab ko'ngilli shifokorlar kasallikni davolash uchun Zimbabvega borishdi.
Steril ichimlik suvi va dori-darmon bilan ta'minlash orqali odamlar nihoyat o'zlariga juda zarur bo'lgan davolanishni olishdi.
Rahmdil shifokorlar minglab odamlarning hayotini saqlab qolishga muvaffaq bo'lishdi.
2009-yil yanvariga kelib epidemiya deyarli butunlay to'xtatildi.
Bugun Zimbabve hukumati kelajakdagi epidemiyalarning oldini olish uchun boshqa mamlakatlar bilan hamkorlik qilmoqda.
Ular suv ta'minotini tozalab, sog'liq uchun xavflardan qanday saqlanishni o'rganishmoqda.
Suvni filtrlash uchun ishlatiladigan tizim yangilanmoqda.
Hukumat endi suv ta'minoti inshootlarini boshqaradi va ular qat'iy xavfsizlik qoidalariga rioya qilishini ta'minlaydi.
Umid qilamizki, kelajakda vabo holatlari halokatli epidemiyalar boshlanishidan oldin davolanadi.

e6|16.title: The Brute and the Billionaire
paras: Hundreds of people had come to see a popular satire, but during the performance a fire started in the theater. The audience and actors evacuated the building. Luckily, no one was hurt, and the fire was soon put out. Immediately, the audience assembled into an angry mob and demanded to know what had happened.

It was soon revealed that the fire had started backstage, and only two people were in the area at the time. One was the husband of the play’s star actress, the billionaire Henry Rich. The other was the theater’s janitor, Bill, a large and strong man who looked like a brute. The crowd segregated the two men and demanded to know who the culprit was. Most of the crowd thought that Bill was to blame. They felt that he had started the fire without ever subjecting him to any scrutiny. Bill resented this but said nothing.

Luckily, the billionaire’s wife testified in his defense. “Your decision is premature,” she told the crowd. “I fell down amid the tumult while everyone fled the fire. Bill rescued me and carried me out of the building. I think you underestimate his character. Besides, in order to be close enough to save me, he couldn’t have been near the place where the fire began.”
The crowd then turned their eyes to the billionaire. “He did it!” they shouted. “Make him pay!”

“Wait,” the billionaire said over the uproar. “I admit that I started the fire, but it was an accident. I was going backstage to see my wife and was clumsy. I collided with a lamp, and it fell to the floor. The floor was flammable. A fire started, and I fled.”

The mob was surprised. The man they blamed was innocent, and the billionaire was guilty. To pay for his error, the billionaire not only repaired the theater but had it remade to be better than before.

qs.q: The billionaire and the play’s star actress were the only two people backstage.
Because Henry looked like a brute, the crowd underestimated his character.
The billionaire fell down amid the tumult while everyone fled the fire.
The crowd made an uproar when they learned who had started the fire.

tr: Yuzlab odamlar mashhur satirani ko'rgani kelgan edi, lekin tomosha paytida teatrda yong'in chiqdi.
Tomoshabinlar va aktyorlar binodan evakuatsiya qilindi.
Baxtga, hech kim jarohat olmadi va yong'in tez orada o'chirildi.
Darhol tomoshabinlar g'azablangan olomonga aylanib, nima bo'lganini bilishni talab qilishdi.
Tez orada yong'in sahna ortida boshlangani va o'sha paytda u yerda faqat ikki kishi bo'lgani ma'lum bo'ldi.
Ulardan biri spektaklning bosh aktrisasining eri, milliarder Genri Rich edi.
Ikkinchisi teatr farroshi Bill edi — u yirtqichga o'xshagan katta, baquvvat odam edi.
Olomon ikki erkakni ajratib, aybdor kim ekanini bilishni talab qildi.
Olomonning ko'pchiligi Billni aybdor deb o'yladi.
Ular uni hech qanday tekshiruvdan o'tkazmay turib, yong'inni u chiqargan deb hisoblashdi.
Bill bundan ranjidi, lekin hech narsa demadi.
Baxtiga, milliarderning xotini uning himoyasiga guvohlik berdi.
«Sizning qaroringiz shoshilinch», dedi u olomonga.
«Hamma yong'indan qochayotgan to'polon paytida men yiqilib tushdim.
Bill meni qutqarib, binodan ko'tarib chiqdi.
Menimcha, siz uning fe'l-atvorini past baholayapsiz.
Bundan tashqari, meni qutqarish uchun yetarlicha yaqin bo'lgan bo'lsa, u yong'in boshlangan joy yaqinida bo'la olmasdi».
Keyin olomon nigohini milliarderga qaratdi.
«Buni u qilgan! — deb qichqirishdi ular. —
Uni jazolash kerak!»
«To'xtanglar», dedi milliarder shovqin-suronni bosib.
«Tan olaman, yong'inni men chiqardim, lekin bu tasodif edi.
Men xotinimni ko'rish uchun sahna ortiga ketayotgan edim va beo'xshovlik qildim.
Men chiroqqa urilib ketdim va u polga tushdi.
Pol tez yonadigan edi.
Yong'in boshlandi va men qochib ketdim».
Olomon hayratda qoldi.
Ular ayblagan odam aybsiz, milliarder esa aybdor edi.
Xatosining evaziga milliarder nafaqat teatrni ta'mirladi, balki uni avvalgidan ham yaxshiroq qilib qayta qurdirdi.

e6|17.title: The Tenacious Inventor
paras: A young student of meteorology was having a difficult time with an experiment. He was attempting to duplicate lightning in clouds. He had made a device that could simulate lightning. It worked by releasing an electromagnetic pulse into the cloud. This pulse, in turn, stimulated the electrons in the cloud’s particles. Then the electrons produced lightning.
But his meteorological experiment had a major defect. He couldn’t get the device into the sky.
He had tied it to balloons, but they had burst. He had shot the device from a cannon, but the force of the cannon had damaged it.

“You should give up,” his friends told him. “You’ll never get that thing into the air.” But his friends’ criticisms only spurred him to try again. The student was very innovative, and at last, he thought that he had an innovation that would work. He attached wings to the device, and on one dreary day, when clouds blocked the light of the sun, he started his experiment anew.

He placed the device on a rocket and launched it into the sky. The propulsion of the rocket carried the device high into the air. The rocket accelerated into the clouds and then released the device. It glided on its wings through the clouds, and when it penetrated the center of a large black cloud, it emitted the electromagnetic pulse. And just as he had predicted, lightning shot from the cloud!
He called his professors, and the next day they came to watch. He successfully duplicated the experiment. His teachers were extremely impressed and called the student and his invention ingenious.
The student was given many awards and became a famous inventor. He had not given up. He had remained tenacious and succeeded.

qs.q: The student of meteorology had bought a device that simulated lightning in clouds.
The electromagnetic pulse stimulated the electrons in the cloud’s particles.
The student’s friends’ criticisms spurred him to try his experiment anew.
It was a dreary day when the device glided into the clouds.
The propulsion of the rocket accelerated the speed of the lightning.

tr: Meteorologiyani o'rganayotgan bir yosh talaba tajriba bilan qiynalayotgan edi.
U bulutlarda chaqmoqni takrorlashga urinayotgan edi.
U chaqmoqni sun'iy ravishda hosil qila oladigan qurilma yasagan edi.
U bulutga elektromagnit impuls yuborish orqali ishlardi.
Bu impuls, o'z navbatida, bulut zarrachalaridagi elektronlarni qo'zg'atardi.
Keyin elektronlar chaqmoq hosil qilardi.
Lekin uning meteorologik tajribasida jiddiy nuqson bor edi.
U qurilmani osmonga chiqara olmasdi.
U uni sharlarga bog'lagan edi, lekin ular yorilib ketgan edi.
U qurilmani to'pdan otgan edi, lekin to'pning zarbi unga shikast yetkazgan edi.
«Voz kechishing kerak, — deyishdi do'stlari unga. —
U narsani hech qachon havoga chiqara olmaysan».
Lekin do'stlarining tanqidi uni yana urinib ko'rishga undadi, xolos.
Talaba juda ixtirochi edi va nihoyat u ish beradigan yangilik topdim deb o'yladi.
U qurilmaga qanotlar biriktirdi va bulutlar quyosh nurini to'sib qo'ygan bir g'amgin kunda tajribasini qaytadan boshladi.
U qurilmani raketaga joylashtirib, osmonga uchirdi.
Raketaning tortish kuchi qurilmani havoga baland ko'tardi.
Raketa tezlashib bulutlarga kirdi va keyin qurilmani bo'shatdi.
U qanotlarida bulutlar orasidan sirpanib uchdi va katta qora bulutning markaziga kirib borganida, elektromagnit impuls chiqardi.
Va u bashorat qilganidek, bulutdan chaqmoq chaqnadi!
U professorlariga qo'ng'iroq qildi va ertasi kuni ular tomosha qilgani kelishdi.
U tajribani muvaffaqiyatli takrorladi.
O'qituvchilari juda hayratlanib, talabani va uning ixtirosini zukko deb atashdi.
Talabaga ko'plab mukofotlar berildi va u mashhur ixtirochiga aylandi.
U taslim bo'lmagan edi.
U qat'iyatli bo'lib qoldi va muvaffaqiyatga erishdi.

e6|18.title: The Nurse’s Lesson
paras: One of the children in the nursery was sick. The child’s mother, who was usually quite vivacious and chattered constantly, was quiet and worried. She knew that if she did not act quickly, the child’s condition would deteriorate.

She summoned the children’s nurse and said to her, “The monks make a medicine that can cure my child’s sickness. Please, hurry tonight to the monastery and get it.” The nurse immediately hurried from the manor to get the medicine. The monastery was far away by Rabbit Cove, and there was no freeway leading to it. The only way there was to walk along a dark and winding trail.

The temperature was close to zero degrees centigrade, and it was raining. Luckily, the nurse had grabbed her raincoat beforehand. She zipped it up and pulled the hood over her head. “I’ll never make it there,” she thought. “Perhaps I should return and go in the morning.” But she remembered the sick child and decided to continue.

Finally, she arrived at the monastery. It was very late. She feared the monks would not be hospitable. But she approached the door and knocked anyway. The rain had condensed on the exterior of the windows by the door. All she could see was the profile of a large man coming to answer the door. Again, she was filled with fear.

But the monk smiled at her when he opened the door. He took her outstretched hand and welcomed her with a hearty voice. The place was warm, and she heard a concerto playing in another room. She relaxed.

“How can I help you?” the monk asked, and the nurse explained the situation. He instantly knew what to do. He grabbed a parcel of medicine and took her back to the manor in a carriage. The medicine worked. The nurse was happy she had persevered through the bad weather and found the monastery.
Now the boy would be able to live a long natural life.

qs.q: The nurse was usually a vivacious woman who constantly chattered.
The nursery was far from the freeway that was near Rabbit Cove.
The temperature was close to zero degrees centigrade.
When the nurse heard a concerto playing in another room, she became hospitable.

tr: Bolalar xonasidagi bolalardan biri kasal edi.
Odatda ancha sho'x va tinimsiz gapiradigan bolaning onasi jim va xavotirda edi.
U tez harakat qilmasa, bolaning ahvoli yomonlashishini bilardi.
U bolalar enagasini chaqirib, unga dedi: «Rohiblar bolamning kasalligini davolaydigan dori tayyorlashadi.
Iltimos, bu kecha shoshilib monastirga borib, uni olib kel».
Enaga darhol dori olish uchun qo'rg'ondan shoshilib chiqdi.
Monastir uzoqda, Quyon ko'rfazi yonida edi va unga olib boradigan katta yo'l yo'q edi.
U yerga borishning yagona yo'li qorong'i va egri-bugri so'qmoq bo'ylab yurish edi.
Harorat nol daraja Selsiyga yaqin edi va yomg'ir yog'ayotgan edi.
Baxtiga, enaga oldindan yomg'irpo'shini olib olgan edi.
U uning chaqmog'ini tortib, kapyushonini boshiga tortdi.
«U yerga hech qachon yetib bora olmayman», deb o'yladi u.
«Balki qaytib, ertalab borishim kerakdir».
Lekin u kasal bolani eslab, yo'lida davom etishga qaror qildi.
Nihoyat, u monastirga yetib keldi.
Juda kech bo'lgan edi.
U rohiblar mehmondo'st bo'lmasligidan qo'rqdi.
Lekin baribir eshik oldiga borib, taqillatdi.
Eshik yonidagi derazalar sirtida yomg'ir tomchilari to'planib qolgan edi.
U faqat eshikni ochish uchun kelayotgan katta bir odamning qorasini ko'ra oldi.
Yana uni qo'rquv qamrab oldi.
Lekin rohib eshikni ochganida, unga jilmaydi.
U uning cho'zilgan qo'lini olib, samimiy ovoz bilan uni kutib oldi.
U yer iliq edi va u boshqa xonada konsert chalinayotganini eshitdi.
U yengil tortdi.
«Sizga qanday yordam bera olaman?» deb so'radi rohib va enaga vaziyatni tushuntirdi.
U darhol nima qilishni bildi.
U bir tugun dorini olib, uni aravada qo'rg'onga qaytarib olib bordi.
Dori ta'sir qildi.
Enaga yomon ob-havoga qaramay sabr-toqat bilan yo'l bosib, monastirni topganidan xursand edi.
Endi bola uzoq, tabiiy umr ko'ra olardi.

e6|19.title: Seizures Then and Now
paras: If a person who lived 200 years ago was treated for a seizure today, they would be surprised by the treatment’s novelty. That’s because doctors in the 1800s were influenced more by primal medical beliefs than science.

Rather than thinking the brain caused seizures, people in the 1800s still thought they were the result of strange forces. They equated seizures with the work of evil spirits. Others felt that the seizures had a cosmic or lunar cause. They believed that the cycles of the moon and constellations could make someone have a seizure.

During a session to treat a patient who had seizures, doctors would force the patient to invoke the grace of the Almighty. They thought if the patient did this, then the patient would rid themselves of the evil spirits causing the seizures.

The advent of modern psychiatry occurred during the 1800s. At that time people who suffered from seizures were placed in psychiatric hospitals. They were treated like they were insane. However, none of the outmoded treatments worked.

It wasn’t until the late 1850s that the causes of seizures were understood. We know today that these causes pertain to the brain. Misfired signals from the brain cause a jerking reflex in the body. These usually occur when someone is very tired.

Once the causes of seizures were known, definitive treatments were developed. Today, treatments range from taking pills to having surgery. Treatment is personalized according to the type of seizure the patient has.

Even today, some people are unsure about seizures. Their most common mistake is thinking that a person having a seizure will swallow their tongue. They often shove some utensil in the person’s mouth. However, this doesn’t help. The utensil often blocks the airway and prevents the person from inhaling. Yet most of the public no longer fear people who have seizures. Instead, they can now help and comfort a person if they have a seizure.

qs.q: Doctors who treated patients for seizures in the 1800s were influenced by primal medical beliefs.
Doctors still used outmoded treatments even after definitive treatments were developed.
The cause of seizures used to be equated to the work of the Almighty.
Today, care for people with seizures is better because treatment sessions are more personalized.
The cause of seizures pertain to misfired signals in the brain that cause a jerking reflex in the body.

tr: Agar 200 yil oldin yashagan odam bugun tutqanoq uchun davolansa, davolashning yangiligidan hayratda qolardi.
Buning sababi, 1800-yillardagi shifokorlar ilm-fandan ko'ra ibtidoiy tibbiy e'tiqodlar ta'sirida bo'lishgan.
1800-yillardagi odamlar tutqanoqni miya keltirib chiqaradi deb o'ylash o'rniga, hamon uni g'alati kuchlarning natijasi deb hisoblashgan.
Ular tutqanoqni yovuz ruhlarning ishi bilan tenglashtirishgan.
Boshqalar tutqanoqning sababi koinot yoki oy bilan bog'liq deb hisoblashgan.
Ular oy va yulduz turkumlarining davrlari kimnidir tutqanoqqa olib kelishi mumkin deb ishonishgan.
Tutqanoq bilan og'rigan bemorni davolash seansida shifokorlar bemorni Qodir Tangrining marhamatini so'rab duo qilishga majbur qilishardi.
Ular agar bemor shunday qilsa, tutqanoqqa sabab bo'layotgan yovuz ruhlardan xalos bo'ladi deb o'ylashardi.
Zamonaviy psixiatriya 1800-yillarda paydo bo'ldi.
O'sha paytda tutqanoqdan aziyat chekkan odamlar psixiatrik shifoxonalarga joylashtirilardi.
Ularga aqldan ozganlardek munosabatda bo'lishardi.
Biroq eskirgan davolash usullarining hech biri ish bermadi.
Faqat 1850-yillarning oxiriga kelib tutqanoqning sabablari tushunildi.
Bugun biz bu sabablar miya bilan bog'liq ekanini bilamiz.
Miyadan noto'g'ri yuborilgan signallar tanada silkinish refleksini keltirib chiqaradi.
Ular odatda odam juda charchaganida yuz beradi.
Tutqanoq sabablari ma'lum bo'lgach, aniq davolash usullari ishlab chiqildi.
Bugun davolash tabletka ichishdan tortib jarrohlik amaliyotigacha bo'lishi mumkin.
Davolash bemordagi tutqanoq turiga qarab alohida belgilanadi.
Hatto bugun ham ba'zi odamlar tutqanoq haqida aniq tasavvurga ega emas.
Ularning eng keng tarqalgan xatosi tutqanog'i tutgan odam tilini yutib yuboradi deb o'ylashdir.
Ular ko'pincha odamning og'ziga biror buyumni tiqishadi.
Biroq bu yordam bermaydi.
Buyum ko'pincha nafas yo'lini to'sib, odamning nafas olishiga to'sqinlik qiladi.
Shunga qaramay, jamoatchilikning ko'pchiligi endi tutqanoq bilan og'rigan odamlardan qo'rqmaydi.
Buning o'rniga ular endi tutqanog'i tutgan odamga yordam berib, unga taskin bera olishadi.

e6|20.title: The Greedy Bee
paras: A young bee had passed his intermediate level exams. He now knew everything about flowers. He understood how they used photosynthesis to make oxygen and which ones produced the best pollen. Bees had an important dependency on pollen. From the beginning of time, bees’ eternal task was to gather pollen and make honey with it.

Since he passed his exams, the little bee had earned his inclusion in the swarms that gathered pollen. He was excited because he was finally allowed to leave the hive. He left with the next swarm and was determined to find the perfect flower. Soon he saw a large, vibrant flower full of pollen. He landed on a petal and walked toward the pollen at the flower’s center.

Immediately, he began rolling in the pollen, gathering it on his legs and wings. The fine texture of the pollen tickled when it stuck to his body. It was the best experience the little bee had ever had. He gathered as much as he could.

But when he was flying back home, he realized that all the pollen had an adverse effect. He had no control over his flight. The intermittent wind fluctuated in power. He was blown to and fro. One minute he was flying straight, and the next minute the wind had reversed his course.
He tried to dump some of the pollen, but it acted as an adhesive. He couldn’t get it off. He became tired and fell to the ground.
“What am I going to do now?” he thought. Just then, his mentor landed next to him and began cleaning the excess pollen off the little bee. “You shouldn’t have taken so much,” his mentor said.

Finally, with the pollen off of him, the bee easily regained his strength, and like a phoenix, the young bee flew back into the air. When he returned to the hive, he turned to his mentor and said, “I learned an important lesson today. I will never be greedy again.”

qs.q: The bees had an important dependency on pollen.
The texture of the petals in the vibrant flower tickled.
The little bee was blown to and fro and reversed in his direction.
Because the pollen acted like an adhesive, the little bee couldn’t dump it.
After his mentor helped him regain his strength, the little bee lost his ambitions and fell to the ground like a phoenix.

tr: Bir yosh asalari o'rta darajadagi imtihonlardan o'tgan edi.
Endi u gullar haqida hamma narsani bilardi.
U ular kislorod hosil qilish uchun fotosintezdan qanday foydalanishini va qaysilari eng yaxshi chang berishini tushunardi.
Asalarilar changga juda bog'liq edilar.
Azaldan asalarilarning abadiy vazifasi chang yig'ish va undan asal tayyorlash bo'lgan.
Imtihonlardan o'tgani uchun kichkina asalari chang yig'adigan to'dalar safiga qo'shilishga loyiq bo'lgan edi.
U hayajonda edi, chunki nihoyat unga uyadan chiqishga ruxsat berilgan edi.
U navbatdagi to'da bilan uchib chiqdi va mukammal gulni topishga qat'iy ahd qildi.
Tez orada u changga to'la, katta, yorqin gulni ko'rdi.
U gulbargga qo'nib, gul markazidagi chang tomon yurdi.
Darhol u changda dumalay boshladi va uni oyoqlari va qanotlariga yig'di.
Changning mayin tuzilishi tanasiga yopishganda qitiqlardi.
Bu kichkina asalari boshidan kechirgan eng zo'r tajriba edi.
U imkon qadar ko'p chang yig'di.
Lekin uyga uchib qaytayotganida, bu chang salbiy ta'sir ko'rsatganini angladi.
U parvozini boshqara olmay qoldi.
Uzuq-uzuq esayotgan shamolning kuchi o'zgarib turardi.
U u yoqdan bu yoqqa uloqtirilardi.
Bir daqiqa u to'g'ri uchardi, keyingi daqiqada esa shamol uning yo'nalishini teskarisiga burib yuborardi.
U changning bir qismini tashlab yubormoqchi bo'ldi, lekin u yelimdek yopishib qoldi.
U uni ko'chira olmadi.
U charchab, yerga tushib qoldi.
«Endi nima qilaman?» deb o'yladi u.
Aynan shu payt ustozi uning yoniga qo'nib, kichkina asalaridan ortiqcha changni tozalay boshladi.
«Bunchalik ko'p olmasliging kerak edi», dedi ustozi.
Nihoyat, ustidan chang tozalangach, asalari kuchini osongina tikladi va xuddi Qaqnus qushidek yosh asalari yana havoga ko'tarildi.
U uyaga qaytgach, ustoziga o'girilib dedi: «Bugun muhim saboq oldim.
Boshqa hech qachon ochko'zlik qilmayman».

e6|21.title: The Mayor of Sherman
paras: The cosmopolitan city of Sherman needed to elect a new mayor. Two men aspired to become mayor: Mr. Jones and Mr. Webb. Mr. Jones was a tall, handsome man. He was a phenomenal speaker, and the citizens loved him. However, Mr. Jones didn’t know much about running a city. He was a pathological liar who merely flattered people with his words. Mr. Webb was very different. He was a small, unattractive man. He was lame and limped when he walked. But he was an expert on politics and knew what was best for the people. The citizens of Sherman didn’t care about what the politicians had to say. No one listened to Mr. Webb, even though he had great ideas. They cheered when Mr. Jones spoke, although he didn’t talk about important things. His pretty words put people in a trance. All the polls predicted that Mr. Jones would win the election.

When the votes were totaled, Mr. Jones won easily. But when he took office, he didn’t know what to do! He tried to hide his ignorance by working in secrecy. He added a law to the city’s constitution that prevented citizens from seeing the mayor. He even censored newspapers that tried to disseminate information about his inability to help the people.
Soon, however, Mr. Jones became infamous for his poor leadership.
There was an outburst of anger among the citizens. They were full of remorse for their misguided decision to elect an ignorant mayor. They voted to remove Mr. Jones and let Mr. Webb take over.

Immediately, Mr. Webb proved that he was a great mayor. He abolished Mr. Jones’s law, and he was willing to talk openly with everyone. He tackled important issues and amended unfair laws in the city’s charter.
The citizens learned that a pleasant appearance and nice words do not make a good leader.
The most important qualities are intelligence and a desire to help others.

qs.q: Two men aspired to be mayor of the cosmopolitan city of Sherman.
Mr. Jones was a pathological speaker who flattered people with his words.
Mr. Webb was lame, so he limped when he walked.
Mr. Webb tackled important issues and amended unfair laws in the city charter.
Mr. Jones censored newspapers that tried to disseminate outbursts of anger.

tr: Ko'p millatli Sherman shahri yangi mer saylashi kerak edi.
Ikki kishi mer bo'lishga intilardi: mister Jons va mister Vebb.
Mister Jons baland bo'yli, kelishgan odam edi.
U ajoyib notiq edi va fuqarolar uni yaxshi ko'rishardi.
Biroq mister Jons shaharni boshqarish haqida ko'p narsa bilmasdi.
U so'zlari bilan odamlarga shunchaki xushomad qiladigan, yolg'on gapirishga mukkasidan ketgan odam edi.
Mister Vebb esa juda boshqacha edi.
U kichkina, xunukroq odam edi.
U cho'loq edi va yurganda oqsoqlanardi.
Lekin u siyosat bo'yicha mutaxassis edi va xalq uchun nima eng yaxshi ekanini bilardi.
Sherman fuqarolari siyosatchilar nima deyishiga e'tibor bermasdilar.
Mister Vebbning ajoyib g'oyalari bo'lsa-da, hech kim uni tinglamasdi.
Mister Jons muhim narsalar haqida gapirmasa ham, u gapirganda hamma olqishlardi.
Uning chiroyli so'zlari odamlarni sehrlab qo'yardi.
Barcha so'rovnomalar saylovda mister Jons g'alaba qozonishini bashorat qildi.
Ovozlar sanab chiqilganda, mister Jons osongina g'alaba qozondi.
Lekin u lavozimga kirishganida, nima qilishni bilmadi!
U o'z bilimsizligini maxfiy ishlash orqali yashirmoqchi bo'ldi.
U shahar konstitutsiyasiga fuqarolarning merni ko'rishini taqiqlaydigan qonun qo'shdi.
U hatto uning xalqqa yordam bera olmasligi haqida ma'lumot tarqatmoqchi bo'lgan gazetalarni senzura qildi.
Biroq tez orada mister Jons yomon rahbarligi bilan nom chiqardi.
Fuqarolar orasida g'azab portlashi yuz berdi.
Ular bilimsiz merni saylash haqidagi noto'g'ri qarorlari uchun afsus-nadomatga to'la edilar.
Ular mister Jonsni lavozimdan chetlatib, o'rniga mister Vebbni qo'yish uchun ovoz berishdi.
Mister Vebb darhol o'zining ajoyib mer ekanini isbotladi.
U mister Jonsning qonunini bekor qildi va hamma bilan ochiq gaplashishga tayyor edi.
U muhim masalalarni hal qildi va shahar nizomidagi adolatsiz qonunlarga o'zgartirish kiritdi.
Fuqarolar yoqimli tashqi ko'rinish va chiroyli so'zlar yaxshi rahbar qilmasligini bilib olishdi.
Eng muhim fazilatlar aql va boshqalarga yordam berish istagidir.

e6|22.title: The Editor’s Choice
paras: A newspaper editor sat at his desk and stared at the flashing cursor on his computer’s screen. He didn’t know if he should delete the article he had just written or go ahead and publish it. He was scared and filled with doubt.

The empire had passed a new law stating that citizens could only use the imperial language. The editor disagreed with the law and decided to write an article about why it was wrong. He felt that the new law excluded people of different nationalities and racial and ethnic backgrounds. He had firsthand knowledge of what it feels like not to be fluent in the imperial language because he was from a remote part of the empire.

He felt that the empire shouldn’t be monolingual and should be more inclusive. Yet he was afraid that he would get in trouble for having this belief. Many would say that he was not a patriot—that he didn’t love the empire. But he didn’t wish to undermine the authority of the empire. He wanted to argue that the empire could be stronger if it accepted people of various cultures and beliefs.

At last, he decided to stop being a coward and to be earnest about how he felt. He wrote the article. It wasn’t rude or angry, but rather, very solemn and intelligent. The next day it was published in all the papers.

Everyone was impressed by his tact and showed solidarity with his ideas. He expected to be arrested any day, but the police never came. Surprisingly, instead of being prosecuted, he became a hero. The legislature changed the law, and people from many linguistic backgrounds praised him.

qs.q: The editor felt the imperial law excluded people of different nationalities and racial and ethnic backgrounds.
The legislature prosecuted the editor for undermining the authority of the empire.
The editor was not fluent in the empire’s language.
Everyone was impressed by the editor’s tact and showed solidarity with his ideas.
The article wasn’t solemn and intelligent, but rather rude and angry.

tr: Bir gazeta muharriri stolida o'tirib, kompyuter ekranidagi miltillayotgan kursorga tikilib turardi.
U hozirgina yozgan maqolasini o'chirishi kerakmi yoki chop etaverishi kerakmi, bilmasdi.
U qo'rqardi va ikkilanishga to'la edi.
Imperiya fuqarolar faqat imperiya tilidan foydalanishlari mumkinligi haqida yangi qonun qabul qilgan edi.
Muharrir qonunga qo'shilmadi va u nega noto'g'ri ekani haqida maqola yozishga qaror qildi.
U yangi qonun turli millat, irq va etnik kelib chiqishga ega odamlarni chetga surib qo'yadi deb hisoblardi.
U imperiyaning olis bir qismidan bo'lgani uchun imperiya tilini erkin bilmaslik qanday ekanini o'z boshidan kechirgan edi.
U imperiya bir tilli bo'lmasligi va ko'proq odamlarni qamrab olishi kerak deb hisoblardi.
Shunga qaramay, u bunday e'tiqodi uchun boshi balolarga qolishidan qo'rqardi.
Ko'pchilik uni vatanparvar emas — imperiyani sevmaydi deyishi mumkin edi.
Lekin u imperiyaning hokimiyatini zaiflashtirishni xohlamasdi.
U imperiya turli madaniyat va e'tiqoddagi odamlarni qabul qilsa, kuchliroq bo'lishi mumkinligini isbotlamoqchi edi.
Nihoyat, u qo'rqoqlikni bas qilib, o'z his-tuyg'ulari haqida samimiy bo'lishga qaror qildi.
U maqolani yozdi.
U qo'pol yoki g'azabli emas, aksincha, juda jiddiy va oqilona edi.
Ertasi kuni u barcha gazetalarda chop etildi.
Hamma uning odobidan ta'sirlandi va uning g'oyalariga birdamlik bildirdi.
U har kuni hibsga olinishini kutdi, lekin politsiya hech qachon kelmadi.
Ajablanarlisi shundaki, u jinoiy javobgarlikka tortilish o'rniga qahramonga aylandi.
Qonun chiqaruvchi organ qonunni o'zgartirdi va turli til vakillari uni maqtashdi.

e6|23.title: The Ice House
paras: Last year, Erik constructed one of the world’s strangest houses in the glacial landscape of northern Sweden. He called it the Ice House: a house made entirely of ice and snow. All of the beds, chairs, tables, and walls are cold, hard sculptures of ice.

A group of architects and volunteers from all over the world traveled to the site of the Ice House and began its construction. The multicultural group journeyed through blizzards and frigid temperatures to reach the site. Once the builders arrived, there was an interchange of ideas, and tools were allocated to each worker. An expert was selected to oversee the building process to make sure there was no discord between the workers. Once a plan was generated, they got right to work. The design was very unique; the builders couldn’t replicate the design from normal houses.

The first step was to build the walls and ceiling. The builders used a metal frame to help them build the structure. After the ice was in place, the frame was removed. The builders then created furniture and art pieces. Designs were carved into each piece. One worker carved big wavy lines, and another made tiny clockwise, concentric circles. Finally, the workers carved small cavities in the roof and inserted colored lights. When the work was finished, the beautiful house was ready for a resident to enjoy.

Living in the Ice House is an experience like no other. Erik stores his belongings in an ice locker and lays out a sleeping bag on his ice bed. At dinner, he dines on a delicious salad with crisp toppings. And for the main course, he enjoys appetizing fish caught from a nearby river. The fish are pierced with icicles and served on ice plates. After dinner, he gets ready for a cold night. The omission of heaters can be too much for his visitors sometimes. Luckily, there are warm rooms nearby, as a courtesy to guests.

qs.q: A multicultural group traveled through blizzards and frigid temperatures to reach the site.
Erik dines on crisp, appetizing fish that are pierced with icicles.
The expert who oversaw the process made sure there wasn’t discord in the glacial landscape.
One worker carved big wavy lines, and another made tiny clockwise, concentric circles.
The builders replicated the design from normal houses.

tr: O'tgan yili Erik Shimoliy Shvetsiyaning muzlik manzarasida dunyodagi eng g'alati uylardan birini qurdi.

Barcha karavotlar, stullar, stollar va devorlar muzdan yasalgan sovuq, qattiq haykallardir.
Dunyoning turli burchaklaridan bir guruh me'morlar va ko'ngillilar Muz uy joyiga kelib, uning qurilishini boshlashdi.
Ko'p madaniyatli guruh u yerga yetib borish uchun qor bo'ronlari va qahraton sovuqlar orqali yo'l bosishdi.
Quruvchilar yetib kelgach, g'oyalar almashildi va har bir ishchiga asboblar taqsimlandi.
Ishchilar o'rtasida kelishmovchilik bo'lmasligi uchun qurilish jarayonini nazorat qilishga bir mutaxassis tanlandi.
Reja tuzilgach, ular darhol ishga kirishishdi.
Loyiha juda noyob edi; quruvchilar oddiy uylarning loyihasini takrorlay olmasdilar.
Birinchi qadam devorlar va shiftni qurish edi.
Quruvchilar inshootni qurishga yordam berish uchun metall karkasdan foydalanishdi.

Bir ishchi katta to'lqinsimon chiziqlar o'ydi, boshqasi esa soat mili yo'nalishidagi mayda konsentrik doiralar yasadi.

Ish tugagach, go'zal uy unda yashovchi zavqlanishi uchun tayyor bo'ldi.

Kechki ovqatda u qarsildoq qo'shimchali mazali salat yeydi.
Asosiy taomga esa yaqindagi daryodan tutilgan ishtahani ochadigan baliqdan bahramand bo'ladi.
Baliqlar muz sumalaklariga sanchilib, muz likopchalarda tortiladi.
Kechki ovqatdan keyin u sovuq tunga tayyorlanadi.
Isitgichlarning yo'qligi ba'zan uning mehmonlari uchun haddan tashqari og'irlik qiladi.
Baxtga, mehmonlarga hurmat belgisi sifatida yaqin atrofda iliq xonalar bor.

e6|24.title: Preparing for the Future
paras: Overpopulation is a big problem in the world today. Too many people are crammed into cities and towns around the globe. Earth’s population is about 6.5 billion people. This number is growing every day. In just 50 years, the population will be almost 9 billion. Many people worry that the Earth won’t have enough resources to support so many people. One major reason for this is that wasting resources and polluting have become habitual behaviors. Industrial output results in polluting the air with dangerous fumes. Also, cars and machines waste a ton of important natural resources like oil and water. It’s possible that the Earth may become so damaged that it can not support a large population of humans.

Another issue is the lack of useful land for cultivating crops. Even today, many people subsist on mere scraps of food and little water. In 50 years, many experts worry that huge numbers of people will starve to death. So what is being done to prepare for the future? People are realizing they can no longer justify their wasteful behavior or defer action to fix it. Many car companies already have patents on prototypes for very efficient cars. Such cars waste no resources and produce no pollution. A conversion to clean cars means that petroleum can be saved for the future. In addition, the environmental sectors of many governments are setting strict rules for industries that pollute too much. If companies do not abide by the standards, they are penalized with higher taxes. In some cases, their operations might be suspended altogether.

Food is also an issue that is being tackled. Many countries are now subscribing to the point of view that immediate action is needed. They are determining ways to export goods to people in need, so that no one goes hungry. Experts will continue to come up with ideas for the future, and a synthesis of these ideas will help to support the growing population.

qs.q: Because of overpopulation, too many people are crammed into cities and towns.
The environmental sectors of many governments are deferring strict standards.
Some car companies have patents on prototypes.
A conversion to clean cars means petroleum can be used right now for people.
Companies that don’t abide by standards are penalized or their operations might be suspended.

tr: Aholining haddan tashqari ko'payishi bugungi dunyoda katta muammo.
Dunyo bo'ylab shahar va qishloqlarga juda ko'p odam tiqilib qolgan.
Yer aholisi taxminan 6,5 milliard kishi.
Bu raqam har kuni o'sib bormoqda.
Atigi 50 yil ichida aholi qariyb 9 milliardga yetadi.
Ko'p odamlar Yerda shuncha odamni ta'minlash uchun resurslar yetarli bo'lmasligidan xavotirda.
Buning asosiy sabablaridan biri resurslarni isrof qilish va atrof-muhitni ifloslantirish odatiy xatti-harakatga aylanib qolganidir.
Sanoat ishlab chiqarishi havoni xavfli tutunlar bilan ifloslantiradi.
Shuningdek, mashinalar va uskunalar neft va suv kabi muhim tabiiy resurslarni juda ko'p isrof qiladi.
Yer shunchalik zarar ko'rishi mumkinki, u ko'p sonli aholini ta'minlay olmay qolishi mumkin.
Yana bir muammo ekin yetishtirish uchun yaroqli yerlarning yetishmasligidir.
Hatto bugun ham ko'p odamlar arzimagan ovqat qoldiqlari va oz suv bilan kun kechirishadi.
Ko'plab mutaxassislar 50 yildan keyin juda ko'p odam ochlikdan o'lishidan xavotirda.
Xo'sh, kelajakka tayyorgarlik ko'rish uchun nima qilinmoqda?
Odamlar endi isrofgarchilikni oqlay olmasliklarini yoki uni tuzatish choralarini kechiktira olmasliklarini anglab yetmoqdalar.
Ko'plab avtomobil kompaniyalarida juda tejamkor mashinalar prototiplari uchun allaqachon patentlar bor.
Bunday mashinalar hech qanday resursni isrof qilmaydi va ifloslanish chiqarmaydi.
Toza mashinalarga o'tish neftni kelajak uchun saqlab qolish mumkinligini anglatadi.
Bundan tashqari, ko'plab hukumatlarning atrof-muhit bo'limlari haddan tashqari ko'p ifloslantiradigan sanoat korxonalari uchun qat'iy qoidalar o'rnatmoqda.
Agar kompaniyalar me'yorlarga rioya qilmasa, ular yuqoriroq soliqlar bilan jazolanadi.
Ba'zi hollarda ularning faoliyati butunlay to'xtatilishi mumkin.
Oziq-ovqat ham hal qilinayotgan muammolardan biri.
Ko'plab mamlakatlar endi zudlik bilan chora ko'rish kerak degan nuqtai nazarga qo'shilmoqda.
Ular hech kim och qolmasligi uchun muhtojlarga mahsulot eksport qilish yo'llarini belgilamoqda.
Mutaxassislar kelajak uchun g'oyalar o'ylab topishda davom etadilar va bu g'oyalarning uyg'unlashuvi o'sib borayotgan aholini ta'minlashga yordam beradi.

e6|25.title: Hundred Plays
paras: Over two thousand years ago, Chinese farmers had a problem. Even though they were very industrious, the weather became too cold outside to plant their staple food, rice. So what did they do? Since they had so much free time during the long, cold winters, the inventive farmers started performing tricks to entertain themselves. They used their farm tools and anything they could find to make their tricks more spectacular. They even twisted their bodies into crazy shapes and performed awesome jumps. Over time, they became great acrobats, and their art form came to be known as “Hundred Plays.”

Hundred Plays involves doing many kinds of tricks. For example, in Mandarin-speaking parts of China, performers do the lion dance. They wear costumes and mimic the animal’s movements. Early performers also did tricks on ropes and vines that were high above the ground.
Even though the acrobats’ fluid movements may have looked easy, they took a lot of work.

Learning Hundred Plays is a communal event. A veteran of the acrobatic arts usually teaches younger people in the village. They spend a lot of time rehearsing. The young performers also learn an old philosophy. The teachings help them harmonize the sensory aspects of acrobatics with mental aspects. In other words, it teaches them to use their physical and mental strength together.

Since the art has its origins with poor farmers, rich people used to scorn acrobats. They thought acrobats were villains. The rich people thought the acrobats just wanted to trick them. But later, their misguided opinions changed. Acrobats came to be respected in Chinese society. They were invited to perform in metropolitan areas as well as in small villages. They performed for important people, including judicial officers. Arts advocacy groups convinced the government to support Chinese acrobatics. As a result, there is now a statute that made several villages the center of training future acrobats.

qs.q: The Chinese farmers became great acrobats while planting staple crops like rice.
The version of the lion dance in Mandarin-speaking areas involves performers mimicking the movements of the lion.
Chinese acrobats gain their fluid motions by rehearsing often.
The art form of Hundred Plays harmonizes the sensory and mental aspects of acrobatics.
Advocacy groups worked to get a statute that would protect acrobats from being scorned.

tr: Ikki ming yildan ko'proq vaqt oldin xitoylik dehqonlarning bir muammosi bor edi.
Ular juda mehnatkash bo'lishsa-da, tashqarida asosiy oziq-ovqatlari — guruch ekish uchun havo juda sovib ketardi.
Xo'sh, ular nima qilishdi?
Uzoq, sovuq qishlarda bo'sh vaqtlari juda ko'p bo'lgani uchun zukko dehqonlar o'zlarini ovuntirish uchun turli fokuslar ko'rsata boshlashdi.
Ular fokuslarini yanada ajoyibroq qilish uchun dehqonchilik asboblari va topa olgan har qanday narsadan foydalanishdi.
Ular hatto tanalarini aql bovar qilmas shakllarga solib, ajoyib sakrashlar qilishardi.
Vaqt o'tib, ular zo'r akrobatlarga aylanishdi va ularning san'at turi «Yuz o'yin» nomi bilan mashhur bo'ldi.

Masalan, Xitoyning mandarin tilida so'zlashadigan hududlarida ijrochilar sher raqsini ijro etishadi.

«Yuz o'yin»ni o'rganish jamoaviy tadbirdir.
